questions.q: What opened every rehearsal and every audition?
options: The conductor's speech
The same A played by the oboist
A trumpet fanfare
The applause of the audience
questions.explain: 第8句 "the same A that opened every rehearsal and every audition"，双簧管的标准音 A。

questions.q: What happened when the strings and the winds finally agreed?
options: The conductor stopped the rehearsal
Every chord turned soft and consonant
The trumpet player left the stage
The hall started to empty
questions.explain: 第20句 "every chord turned soft and consonant"，每个和弦都变得柔和、和谐。

questions.q: In 第10句, the trumpet practiced until the "dissonance dissolved." The root son means sound and dis- means apart, so dissonance is . . .
options: sounds that clash and do not agree
sounds played together in tune
a kind of dance
a ticket for the concert
questions.explain: 第10句的 dissonance（不和谐音）与第20句的 consonant（和谐）相对：dis-（分开）+ son（声音）→ 相互打架的声音。

questions.q: Why did Lin forget to press record for the first five minutes?
options: She was too nervous to move
The music passed through her like weather and carried her away in deep listening
Her recorder was broken again
The cellist told her not to record
questions.explain: 第15-16句：音乐“像天气一样从她身上穿过”，头五分钟她“干脆忘了”——她听得入了迷，忘了录音的任务。

title: 《城市的声音地图》· 市场的清晨

sentences.en: At five in the morning, Lin carried her microphone into the market by the river.
sentences.zh: 清晨五点，林带着麦克风走进河边的市场。

sentences.en: The sky was still the color of ink mixed with water, and the lamps made small yellow islands on the wet stone.
sentences.zh: 天还是墨水兑了水的颜色，灯在湿漉漉的石板上照出一座座黄色小岛。

sentences.en: Vendors were shouting prices over each other in a wild, bright cacophony.
sentences.zh: 摊贩们互相压着嗓子报价，喧闹成一片刺耳又鲜亮的杂音。

sentences.en: An old radio on the noodle stand played opera, losing gracefully to everyone.
sentences.zh: 面条摊上一台老收音机放着歌剧，心服口服地输给了所有人。

sentences.en: A fish seller used a megaphone, and his voice boomed across the stone floor with a metallic resonance.
sentences.zh: 一个鱼贩子用扩音器吆喝，声音带着金属般的共鸣，在石板地上滚过来。

sentences.en: Lin stood still in the middle of it and recorded layer after layer of the waking noise.
sentences.zh: 林站在市场正中一动不动，一层一层录下这清晨的喧哗。

sentences.en: Her headphones filled with it, and for a moment she was not a listener but part of the noise itself.
sentences.zh: 耳机里灌满了它，有一瞬间她不再是听者，而是噪音本身的一部分。

sentences.en: A dog barked at her microphone, decided it was harmless, and went back to sleep under a cabbage table.
sentences.zh: 一条狗对着她的麦克风叫了两声，判定它无害，又钻回白菜桌下睡了。

sentences.en: At first the market sounded like pure disorder, a wall of noise without any shape.
sentences.zh: 一开始，市场听起来纯粹是乱的，一堵没有任何形状的声墙。

sentences.en: The sounds ran into each other like paint colors mixed by an angry child.
sentences.zh: 各种声音互相撞在一起，像被一个生气的孩子搅混的颜料。

sentences.en: But when she listened longer, patterns began to rise slowly out of the noise.
sentences.zh: 但听得久了，规律开始慢慢从噪音里浮上来。

sentences.en: Each vendor had a rhythm, a pitch, a personal melody for every kind of vegetable.
sentences.zh: 每个摊贩都有自己的节奏、音高，还有专属每样蔬菜的小调。

sentences.en: The shouting repeated itself every few seconds, like waves that followed a hidden formula.
sentences.zh: 吆喝声每隔几秒重复一次，像追随某个隐藏公式的波浪。

sentences.en: She timed one seller with her watch: three seconds, pause, three seconds, pause, like a heartbeat in disguise.
sentences.zh: 她用表给一个摊贩计时：三秒，停顿，三秒，停顿，像一颗化了妆的心跳。

sentences.en: An old woman selling tofu sang her price in a soft, steady euphony.
sentences.zh: 一位卖豆腐的老婆婆用轻柔平稳的调子唱出价钱。

sentences.en: Her prices were songs, her thanks were songs, even her sneeze had a small melody to it.
sentences.zh: 她的报价是歌，道谢是歌，连打个喷嚏都自带一点小旋律。

sentences.en: Her quiet call wove through the loud voices around her like a silver thread.
sentences.zh: 她轻轻的叫卖穿过四周的喧哗，像一根银线。

sentences.en: Lin recorded her for a whole minute, because some sounds are worth more than their weight.
sentences.zh: 林整整录了她一分钟，因为有些声音的价值远超它的分量。

sentences.en: The tofu seller noticed her recording and sang her price one extra time, for the city's sake.
sentences.zh: 豆腐婆婆注意到她在录音，特意又把价钱多唱了一遍——就当唱给这座城市。

sentences.en: By seven, the market had found its sonic shape; it was not chaos but an orchestra without a conductor.
sentences.zh: 到七点，市场找到了它声音的形状；它不是混乱，而是一支没有指挥的乐团。

sentences.en: Every player knew their part, and nobody had ever printed the score.
sentences.zh: 每个乐手都记得自己的声部，只是从没有人印过总谱。

sentences.en: A phone rang behind the fruit stalls, a cheap electronic melody, nearly lost inside the crowd.
sentences.zh: 水果摊后一部手机响了，廉价的电子铃声，几乎淹没在人声里。

sentences.en: It was audible for only a second before the noise folded it back in like the sea folding a coin.
sentences.zh: 它只听得见一秒钟，随即被喧哗收了回去，像大海收回一枚硬币。

sentences.en: The owner answered it anyway, shouting happily above three different kinds of fish advertisement.
sentences.zh: 摊主照样接了电话，快活地喊着话，压过三种鱼广告。

sentences.en: Nobody minded the shouting; in this market, shouting was simply how neighbors said good morning.
sentences.zh: 没人介意喊叫；在这个市场里，喊叫就是街坊们互道早安的方式。

sentences.en: Lin drank a bowl of hot soy milk, and even the spoon had a small percussion solo against the bowl.
sentences.zh: 林喝了一碗热豆浆，连勺子都碰着碗来了一段小小的打击乐独奏。

sentences.en: Lin realized that the city was never quiet; it was only sometimes listened to.
sentences.zh: 林忽然明白：城市从来不是安静的，只是有时没人在听。

sentences.en: In her notebook she wrote: noise is just information we have not learned to read.
sentences.zh: 她在笔记本上写：噪音只是我们还没学会解读的信息。

sentences.en: That evening she drew a third circle and wrote inside it: the market, conductorless.
sentences.zh: 当晚，她画下第三个圈，在里面写：市场，无指挥。

questions.q: What tool did the fish seller use to shout?
options: A bell
A megaphone
A microphone
A whistle
questions.explain: 第5句 "A fish seller used a megaphone"，鱼贩子用的是扩音器。

questions.q: How did the vendors' shouting repeat itself?
options: Randomly, without any rule
Every few seconds, like waves following a hidden formula
Only when it rained
Once an hour
questions.explain: 第13句 "repeated itself every few seconds, like waves that followed a hidden formula"，第14句她还用表量出三秒一停顿。

questions.q: How did the old tofu seller call her price?
options: In an angry voice
Through a megaphone
In a soft, steady euphony
In a whisper nobody heard
questions.explain: 第15句 "sang her price in a soft, steady euphony"，轻柔平稳的调子。

questions.q: In 第15句, the tofu seller sang in a "euphony" — the opposite of 第3句's "cacophony." The root phon means sound, so euphony is . . .
options: pleasant, sweet-sounding sound
a loud argument between vendors
a cheap electronic ringtone
a kind of vegetable
questions.explain: 第3句 cacophony（刺耳的杂音）与第15句 euphony 相对：eu-（好）+ phon（声音）→ 好听悦耳的声音。

questions.q: Why did Lin label her third circle "the market, conductorless" (第29句)?
options: The market had fired its conductor
Like an orchestra, every vendor knew their part and rhythm, but no single leader directed it
Nobody in the market could read music
The market was closed on weekends
questions.explain: 第20-21句：市场“是一支没有指挥的乐团”，“每个乐手都记得自己的声部，只是从没有人印过总谱”。

title: 《城市的声音地图》· 唱片店的一九二六

sentences.en: On a rainy afternoon, Lin discovered a record shop at the end of Maple Street.
sentences.zh: 一个下雨的下午，林在枫树街尽头发现了一家唱片店。

sentences.en: The shop was so narrow that the shelves seemed to hold the walls apart.
sentences.zh: 店面窄得可怜，架子仿佛是撑住两面墙的支柱。

sentences.en: They were filled with old vinyl records, each one in a uniform paper sleeve, gray as school uniforms.
sentences.zh: 架上摆满旧黑胶唱片，每一张都装在式样一致的纸套里，灰得像校服。

sentences.en: Handwritten labels divided them by decade, and the handwriting got older as the shelves went higher.
sentences.zh: 手写的标签按年代分格，架子越高，字迹越老。

sentences.en: The owner, Mr. Hua, was repairing a brass gramophone nearly a hundred years old.
sentences.zh: 店主华先生正在修一台黄铜留声机，快一百年了。

sentences.en: He was sixty-something, with reading glasses pushed far up his nose and cotton in one ear.
sentences.zh: 他六十多岁，老花镜推得高高的，一只耳朵里塞着棉花。

sentences.en: He wound the handle, lowered the needle, and the machine coughed, then began to sing.
sentences.zh: 他上好发条，落下唱针，机器咳嗽了一声，随即唱了起来。

sentences.en: A woman's voice from 1926 filled the shop, thin as rain beneath the crackle.
sentences.zh: 一段一九二六年的女声灌满小店，细得像雨，压在噼啪声之下。

sentences.en: It was a love song, or perhaps a song about leaving; at this distance, Lin thought, they are the same thing.
sentences.zh: 那是一首情歌，或者一首关于离别的歌；隔了这么远，林想，它们本来就是同一回事。

sentences.en: The crackle came first, Lin noticed, and the voice learned to live inside it.
sentences.zh: 林注意到，噼啪声先来，那声音是后来才学会住在里面的。

sentences.en: "Some people call it a phonograph, some a gramophone," Mr. Hua said. "I call it my grandmother."
sentences.zh: “有人叫它phonograph，有人叫它gramophone，”华先生说，“我叫它我外婆。”

sentences.en: "Every groove on this record is a tiny valley that carries sound," he told her.
sentences.zh: “唱片上每一道纹路，都是一条驮着声音的小山谷。”他告诉她。

sentences.en: "The needle walks through the valley like an old man through his hometown."
sentences.zh: “唱针走在山谷里，就像老人走在自己的家乡。”

sentences.en: Lin touched the groove and felt it, a frozen river of sound.
sentences.zh: 林摸了摸那道纹路——一条冻住的声音之河。

sentences.en: Lin borrowed his spare microphone and pressed it gently against the horn.
sentences.zh: 林借来他那支备用麦克风，轻轻抵住喇叭口。

sentences.en: The audio she captured was rough, but it carried the warmth of another century.
sentences.zh: 录下的音频很粗糙，却带着另一个世纪的体温。

sentences.en: Somewhere in the hiss she could hear a tram, a baby, and a door closing forever.
sentences.zh: 嘶嘶声深处，她听得见一辆电车、一个婴儿，和一扇永远关上的门。

sentences.en: Mr. Hua showed her the same song saved in four different formats.
sentences.zh: 华先生又给她看同一首歌的四种不同格式。

sentences.en: Wax, vinyl, tape, and file: the format had transformed four times, but the voice stayed the same.
sentences.zh: 蜡盘、黑胶、磁带、音频文件——格式变了四次，那个声音没变。

sentences.en: "Technology is a long train," he said, "and the voice is the passenger who never changes seats."
sentences.zh: “技术是一列长火车，”他说，“声音是那个从不换座位的乘客。”

sentences.en: Lin asked whether he missed the old formats; he said the formats missed each other, but the songs did not care.
sentences.zh: 林问他想不想那些旧格式；他说，格式们彼此想念，歌才不在乎。

sentences.en: He played her a street musician from 1950, and a wedding from 1973, and one extraordinary thunderstorm.
sentences.zh: 他放给她听一九五〇年的街头艺人、一九七三年的一场婚礼，还有一场了不起的雷雨。

sentences.en: On her way out, she bought an old audiobook, a poet reading his own poems.
sentences.zh: 临走时，她买了一盘旧有声书，一位诗人读自己的诗。

sentences.en: Mr. Hua wrapped it in yesterday's newspaper and charged her almost nothing.
sentences.zh: 华先生用昨天的报纸把它包好，几乎没要她钱。

sentences.en: He also gave her a needle, a real steel one, "so you remember that sound is physical."
sentences.zh: 他还送了她一根唱针，真钢的——“好让你记得，声音是有形状的实物。”

sentences.en: That night she played it twice, and the poet's pauses felt like a second language.
sentences.zh: 那晚她听了两遍，诗人的停顿像另一种语言。

sentences.en: The voice on the tape had been silent for forty years, yet it was not dead, only waiting.
sentences.zh: 磁带上的声音沉默了四十年，却没有死，只是在等。

sentences.en: She thought of the subway rails, the market's hidden formula, the concert hall: all of them, pressed grooves of time.
sentences.zh: 她想起地铁的铁轨、市场那隐藏的公式、音乐厅——全都是时间压出的纹路。

sentences.en: In her notebook she wrote: a record is a voice that refused to disappear.
sentences.zh: 她在笔记本上写：唱片，是一种拒绝消失的声音。

sentences.en: Beside the sentence she drew a small circle, the fourth on her growing map.
sentences.zh: 这句话旁边，她画下一个小圈——地图上的第四个。

questions.q: What was Mr. Hua repairing when Lin arrived?
options: A radio
A brass gramophone nearly a hundred years old
A broken telephone
A grand piano
questions.explain: 第5句 "repairing a brass gramophone nearly a hundred years old"，一台快一百年的黄铜留声机。

questions.q: What did the four formats — wax, vinyl, tape, and file — have in common?
options: The same cover art
The same length
The same recorded voice stayed the same
The same price
questions.explain: 第19句 "the format had transformed four times, but the voice stayed the same"，格式在变，录下的声音没变。

questions.q: What did Lin buy on her way out of the shop?
options: A brass gramophone
An old audiobook of a poet reading his own poems
A stack of vinyl records
A steel needle
questions.explain: 第23句 "she bought an old audiobook, a poet reading his own poems"，一盘诗人自读诗集的有声书。

questions.q: In 第11句, "phonograph" and "gramophone" both name the old machine. The root phon means sound and graph means writing, so a phonograph literally . . .
options: writes sound down so it can be played again
amplifies the human voice
broadcasts news by radio
measures musical pitches
questions.explain: 第11-12句：唱针走过“驮着声音的小山谷”——phon（声音）+ graph（写）→ 把声音“写”下来、可以重放的机器。

questions.q: What does "Technology is a long train, and the voice is the passenger who never changes seats" (第20句) suggest?
options: Trains will replace recording technology
However the format changes, what is recorded — the human voice — stays constant and is what truly matters
Old passengers should keep their seats on trains
The voice needs a new format every decade
questions.explain: 第19-20句：格式变了四次，声音没变——变的是载体，不变的是被录下的人声与情感。

title: 《城市的声音地图》· 会发声的地图

sentences.en: Lin spent a whole year walking the city with her recorder and her growing map.
sentences.zh: 林用一整年时间，带着录音笔和那张越画越满的地图走遍城市。

sentences.en: She recorded buses and bells, rain on iron roofs, the last tram at midnight, and two arguing chess players in the park.
sentences.zh: 她录公交车和钟声、铁皮屋顶上的雨、午夜的末班电车，还有公园里两个吵架的棋手。

sentences.en: By the following spring, she had collected four hundred sonic fragments, from traffic to birdsong.
sentences.zh: 到第二年春天，她已收集了四百段声音碎片，从车流到鸟鸣。

sentences.en: Some fragments lasted a second; others, like the storm recording, filled an entire afternoon.
sentences.zh: 有的碎片只有一秒钟；有的，比如那场雷雨，装满了整整一个下午。

sentences.en: Each fragment lived in a labeled folder, and the folders were alphabetized like a strange, breathing library.
sentences.zh: 每段声音住在一个贴了标签的文件夹里，文件夹按字母排好，像一座会呼吸的怪图书馆。

sentences.en: Her headphones had grown soft at the edges, worn the way old shoes are worn.
sentences.zh: 她的耳机边缘已经磨软了，像一双穿旧的鞋。

sentences.en: Her school informed her that the auditorium was free for one evening in June.
sentences.zh: 学校通知她，六月的某个晚上礼堂是空的。

sentences.en: She asked for the chance the way one asks for a heartbeat: quietly, and with everything she had.
sentences.zh: 她争取这个机会的方式，像人争取一次心跳：安安静静，却用上了全部。

sentences.en: Her teacher signed the form and added one sentence: give the walls something to say.
sentences.zh: 老师在表格上签了字，还添了一句：给这些墙一点话说。

sentences.en: She spent a month turning the hall into a map that could sing.
sentences.zh: 她花了一个月，把大厅变成一张会唱歌的地图。

sentences.en: She printed a huge paper map of the city and hid small speakers under its surface.
sentences.zh: 她印了一张巨大的城市纸质地图，在纸面下藏进一个个小喇叭。

sentences.en: She wired each district to its own recorded voice, and tested every connection twice with her microphone and her ears.
sentences.zh: 她把每个街区接上它自己的录音，用麦克风和耳朵把每条线路测了两遍。

sentences.en: When a visitor touched a district, the district answered with its own recorded sound.
sentences.zh: 参观者碰到哪个街区，哪个街区就用自己录下的声音作答。

sentences.en: If someone pressed two places together, the two sounds blended into something new that no mayor had ever approved.
sentences.zh: 如果有人同时按住两个地方，两种声音便混合成新的东西——市长可从没批准过。

sentences.en: On the opening night, three hundred people came, and the auditorium fell completely silent.
sentences.zh: 开幕那晚来了三百人，整个礼堂安静得彻底。

sentences.en: For a moment nobody breathed; three hundred hands hovered above the paper like birds deciding where to land.
sentences.zh: 有一瞬间没人呼吸；三百只手悬在纸面上，像一群正在决定落在哪里的鸟。

sentences.en: A boy touched the subway line and heard the rails' resonance under his fingers.
sentences.zh: 一个男孩按住地铁线，指尖下响起铁轨的共鸣。

sentences.en: He pressed his whole hand against it, as if trying to hold the city's hand.
sentences.zh: 他把整只手掌压上去，像想握一握城市的手。

sentences.en: An old woman touched the market street and recognized a morning from forty years ago.
sentences.zh: 一位老太太按在市场那条街，忽然认出了四十年前的某个早晨。

sentences.en: She stood there for a long time, her hand flat on the paper, listening to a market that had since been rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 她在那儿站了很久，手掌平平地贴着纸，听一个早已拆掉的市场。

sentences.en: People began to walk from district to district, following sounds instead of streets.
sentences.zh: 人们开始从一个街区走到另一个街区，循着声音，而不是街道。

sentences.en: Children ran; grandparents walked slowly; a bus driver, still in uniform, pressed his route and found it singing.
sentences.zh: 孩子们跑着，老人慢慢走；一个还穿着制服的公交司机按住自己的线路，发现它在唱歌。

sentences.en: A whole crowd moved in a slow unison, leaning toward whatever was singing under the paper.
sentences.zh: 一大群人以缓慢的整齐移动着，身体朝纸下正在唱歌的地方倾过去。

sentences.en: In the last row, a music student wrote in his notebook: the city is an unwritten symphony.
sentences.zh: 最后一排，一个音乐学生写下：这座城市是一部没写出来的交响乐。

sentences.en: Lin watched her audience and understood that a map could also have a voice.
sentences.zh: 林望着她的听众，明白了一张地图也可以有嗓音。

sentences.en: Even the silence of the crowd, she noticed, had a shape: the shape of attention.
sentences.zh: 她注意到，连人群的安静都有形状：那形状叫专注。

sentences.en: The city had not changed, but the way she heard it had been completely transformed.
sentences.zh: 城市没有变，但她听见城市的方式被彻底改变了。

sentences.en: Her grandmother's old recording machine stood by the exit, still working, like a small, proud relative.
sentences.zh: 外婆那台旧录音机立在出口，还在工作，像一位小小的、骄傲的亲戚。

sentences.en: In the last line of her notebook she wrote: listen long enough, and every place becomes music.
sentences.zh: 笔记本最后一行她写：听得够久，每个地方都会成为音乐。

sentences.en: After that night, the map stayed in the auditorium, and the city kept singing, whether anyone listened or not.
sentences.zh: 那晚之后，地图留在礼堂里，而城市继续唱着——无论有没有人在听。

questions.q: How many sonic fragments had Lin collected by the following spring?
options: Forty
Four hundred
Four thousand
Fourteen
questions.explain: 第3句 "four hundred sonic fragments, from traffic to birdsong"，四百段声音碎片。

questions.q: How did visitors make the map speak?
options: By speaking into a microphone
By touching a district on the paper map
By calling a phone number
By reading the labels aloud
questions.explain: 第13句 "When a visitor touched a district, the district answered with its own recorded sound"，摸到哪个街区，哪个街区就用录音作答。

questions.q: What did the old woman recognize when she touched the market street?
options: A song from the radio
A morning from forty years ago
Her daughter's voice
An old friend's laugh
questions.explain: 第19句 "recognized a morning from forty years ago"，她认出了四十年前的某个早晨。

questions.q: In 第24句, a music student calls the city "an unwritten symphony." The root phon means sound and sym- means together, so a symphony is literally . . .
options: many sounds sounding together as one piece
a very quiet song
a map of the city
a bus route that sings
questions.explain: 第24句：sym-（共同）+ phon（声音）→ 众声合奏；全书多次出现的 symphony 都源自这一词根。

questions.q: What does 第26句 "the silence of the crowd had the shape of attention" tell us about the exhibition?
options: The audience was bored and waiting to leave
The silence was not emptiness but three hundred people listening together — exactly what Lin wanted
The speakers had stopped working
The crowd was afraid to make noise
questions.explain: 第25-27句：地图有了嗓音、安静有了“专注”的形状、林听城市的方式被彻底改变——这三百人真正学会了听。

title: 《爷爷的果园年历》· 剪枝与堆肥

sentences.en: In early spring, Xiao took the slow train back to her grandfather's orchard, carrying an empty notebook and a head full of city noise.
sentences.zh: 早春，晓坐慢车回到爷爷的果园，带着一个空本子和满脑子的城市噪音。

sentences.en: Grandpa Chen was waiting at the gate with two pairs of pruning shears, one large and one small.
sentences.zh: 陈爷爷提着两把修枝剪等在园门口，一把大，一把小。

sentences.en: "A tree is like a sentence," Grandpa said. "If a branch does not help the meaning, you cut it out."
sentences.zh: “树就像一个句子，”爷爷说，“哪根枝帮不上句子的意思，就把它剪掉。”

sentences.en: Xiao followed him between rows of pear trees that had fruited for sixty years.
sentences.zh: 晓跟着他在梨树间穿行，这些树已经结了六十年的果。

sentences.en: Their trunks were gray and bent, like old men who had learned to bow before weather.
sentences.zh: 树干灰而弯曲，像学会了在天气面前低头的老人。

sentences.en: They were perennial trees, he explained; they woke up every spring without being told, and they remembered winter in their rings.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，这些是多年生的树：每年春天不用谁提醒就会醒来，把冬天记在自己的年轮里。

sentences.en: Pruning, he said, was not destruction but direction: you removed the crowded branches so light and air could reach the inside.
sentences.zh: 他说，剪枝不是破坏，是指方向：剪掉过密的枝条，光和空气才进得去树心。

sentences.en: The terrain of the orchard rose in soft steps, and each step held a different kind of tree.
sentences.zh: 果园的地势一级级缓缓抬升，每一级台阶种着不同的树。

sentences.en: On the lowest step the soil was heavy and wet, so the apples there grew slowly and kept longest.
sentences.zh: 最低一级的土又黏又湿，那儿的苹果长得慢，却存得最久。

sentences.en: On the south-facing shelf of the hill, the pears turned sweet weeks before the others.
sentences.zh: 朝南的山坡上，梨比别人早几个星期就甜了。

sentences.en: "Read the land like a page," he said. "It has been writing to us for sixty years."
sentences.zh: “把土地当书页来读，”他说，“它已经写了六十年给我们看。”

sentences.en: Xiao had grown up in the city and never read a hill this way before.
sentences.zh: 晓在城里长大，从没这样读过一座山。

sentences.en: By noon the ground was covered with fallen twigs.
sentences.zh: 到中午，地上落满了剪下的细枝。

sentences.en: Everything went into the compost pit at the lower edge of the orchard, where last year's leaves were already becoming next year's soil.
sentences.zh: 所有的细枝都进了果园下坡处的堆肥坑，去年的落叶在那儿正慢慢变成明年的土。

sentences.en: "Everything here is biodegradable," Grandpa said. "The leaves, the fruit, even the rope. Give them time and they will all turn back into earth."
sentences.zh: “这儿样样都可降解，”爷爷说，“叶子、果子，连绳子都是。给它们时间，它们都会变回泥土。”

sentences.en: Compost had a formula, he insisted: three parts brown, one part green, and a certain amount of patience.
sentences.zh: 他坚持说堆肥有配方：三份褐色，一份绿色，再加一定分量的耐心。

sentences.en: Xiao dug her fingers in and found the compost warm, crawling with beetles and threads of white fungus.
sentences.zh: 晓把手指插进去，堆肥是暖的，爬满甲虫和白色的菌丝。

sentences.en: "That is biology at its most patient," Grandpa said. "Nothing is wasted, and everything is transformed."
sentences.zh: “这就是最耐心的生物学，”爷爷说，“没有废物，一切都在转化。”

sentences.en: She took off her gloves and let the warm earth hold her hands for a while.
sentences.zh: 她摘掉手套，让暖烘烘的泥土握了会儿她的手。

sentences.en: She helped him turn the pile with a wooden fork, and the steam that rose smelled of rain and sweetness.
sentences.zh: 她帮他用木叉翻堆，升起的蒸汽闻起来像雨，又带点甜。

sentences.en: In the evening, his knees cracked like the ladders, and he laughed at the sound.
sentences.zh: 傍晚，他的膝盖像木梯一样咔咔响，他自己被这声音逗笑了。

sentences.en: Inside the house, they ate noodles with the last jar of pickled pears, and the kitchen smelled like every winter of her childhood.
sentences.zh: 屋里，他们吃面条，就着最后一罐糖渍梨，厨房的味道像她童年的每一个冬天。

sentences.en: He opened a worn notebook with a green cover and wrote one line in it: spring, pruning done.
sentences.zh: 他翻开一本绿皮的旧笔记，写下一行：春，剪枝毕。

sentences.en: The pages were soft and brown at the edges, like the leaves they described.
sentences.zh: 纸页边缘又软又黄，像它们描写的那些叶子。

sentences.en: He had kept this annual record for forty years, one thin page for every spring.
sentences.zh: 这样的年度记录他记了四十年，每年春天薄薄一页。

sentences.en: "A notebook is a formation," he told her. "One year is a word. Forty years make a sentence."
sentences.zh: “本子是一种构造，”他告诉她，“一年是一个词，四十年连成一个句子。”

questions.q: What does Grandpa compare a tree to?
options: A building
A sentence
A river
A machine
questions.explain: 第3句 "A tree is like a sentence... If a branch does not help the meaning, you cut it out."，他把树比作一个句子。

questions.q: What was Grandpa's compost formula?
options: Equal parts of everything
Three parts brown, one part green, and patience
Only green leaves
Half soil and half water
questions.explain: 第16句 "three parts brown, one part green, and a certain amount of patience"，三份褐色、一份绿色，再加耐心。

questions.q: How long has Grandpa kept his annual record?
options: Six years
Twenty years
Forty years
Sixty years
questions.explain: 第25句 "He had kept this annual record for forty years, one thin page for every spring."，四十年，每年一页。

questions.q: In 第15句, Grandpa says everything in the orchard is "biodegradable." The root bio means life, so biodegradable things are things that . . .
options: can be broken down by living things and return to the earth
can be sold at the market
grow only in spring
must be burned in winter
questions.explain: 第15句：给它们时间，叶子和果子都会“变回泥土”；bio（生命）+ degrade（分解）→ 能被生物分解的。

questions.q: What does Grandpa mean by "Read the land like a page" (第11句)?
options: The hill is good for reading books outdoors
The terrain carries information — where to plant, what to expect — learned from sixty years of farming
He wants Xiao to write poems about the hill
The land must be flattened before planting
questions.explain: 第8-11句：每一级台阶种不同的树、朝南的坡最甜——地形象一页写满经验的书，告诉他们怎么种树。

title: 《爷爷的果园年历》· 不打药的夏天

sentences.en: In July the orchard hummed like a small engine, and every day became a biology lesson.
sentences.zh: 七月，果园嗡嗡响得像一台小发动机，每天都成了一堂生物课。

sentences.en: Xiao came back for two weeks of her summer holiday and slept in the room that still had her childhood drawings on the wall.
sentences.zh: 晓回来过两周暑假，睡在墙上还贴着她童年涂鸦的房间。

sentences.en: One morning she found the young shoots covered with aphids, small green insects moving like slow rain.
sentences.zh: 一天早晨，她发现新梢爬满蚜虫，绿色的小虫像慢镜头的雨一样挪动。

sentences.en: She ran to Grandpa with a bottle of spray from the shop in town.
sentences.zh: 她拿着从镇上小店买的一瓶药水跑去找爷爷。

sentences.en: He refused it the way he refused loud arguments, gently and completely.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝它，像拒绝大声吵架一样：温和，而彻底。

sentences.en: "A healthy orchard does not fight its pests," he said. "It balances them."
sentences.zh: “健康的果园不跟虫开战，”他说，“它只跟虫保持平衡。”

sentences.en: Years ago he had bought one antibiotic spray, used it once, and regretted it for three seasons.
sentences.zh: 多年前他买过一瓶抗生素药水，用了一次，后悔了三个季节。

sentences.en: The spray killed the aphids, he explained, but it also killed the small hunters that kept the aphids down.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，药杀了蚜虫，也把压制蚜虫的小小猎手们一起杀了。

sentences.en: Instead, he planted flowers between the rows to invite wasps and hoverflies, natural hunters of aphids.
sentences.zh: 于是他在树行间种花，请来蚜虫的天敌——胡蜂和食蚜蝇。

sentences.en: Within two weeks the green shoots were clean again, and the flowers looked like small yellow flags of victory.
sentences.zh: 两周之内，绿梢又干净了，那些花像一面面黄色的小小胜利旗帜。

sentences.en: Ladybugs patrolled the leaves, and spiders set up small territorial webs between the branches.
sentences.zh: 瓢虫在叶面上巡逻，蜘蛛在枝头织出各自划地盘的小网。

sentences.en: A wren scolded them from the fence, then went back to its own hunting.
sentences.zh: 一只鹪鹩在篱笆上骂了他们几句，又回去忙自己的猎事。

sentences.en: Each spider defended its own corner, and Grandpa never pulled a web down.
sentences.zh: 每只蜘蛛守着自己的角落，爷爷从不拆掉任何一张网。

sentences.en: Below the grass, earthworms rebuilt the soil; he called them his subterranean engineers, quiet workers of the dark.
sentences.zh: 草皮之下，蚯蚓翻修着泥土；他叫它们“地下工程师”，黑暗里安静的工人。

sentences.en: "What we have here is symbiosis," he said one evening, pointing with his teacup.
sentences.zh: “我们这儿有的是共生，”一天傍晚他举着茶杯指点着说。

sentences.en: "Different lives helping each other stay alive. The flowers feed the hunters, the hunters guard the fruit, the fruit feeds us."
sentences.zh: “不同的生命互相帮衬着活下去：花喂养猎手，猎手守护果子，果子养活我们。”

sentences.en: Grandpa called the whole hillside a small biosphere, a world that fed and guarded itself.
sentences.zh: 爷爷管整面山坡叫一个小生物圈——一个自己养活自己、自己守卫自己的世界。

sentences.en: He read the terrain like a newspaper he had been subscribing to for sixty years.
sentences.zh: 他读地形，像读一份订了六十年的报纸。

sentences.en: The south-facing slope always grew the sweetest fruit, because the sun spent more hours there.
sentences.zh: 朝南的坡上果子最甜，因为太阳在那儿待的钟头最多。

sentences.en: The north side was colder and damper, so he had planted the hardier trees there, and they thanked him in their quiet way every autumn.
sentences.zh: 北坡又冷又潮，他就把更耐活的树种在那边；每年秋天，树都用自己的方式悄悄道谢。

sentences.en: That summer Xiao counted eleven kinds of birds, six kinds of bees, and one shy hedgehog that came for water at dusk.
sentences.zh: 那个夏天，晓数出十一种鸟、六种蜜蜂，还有一只怕生的刺猬，黄昏时分来喝水。

sentences.en: She gave the hedgehog a name, Mo, and Mo came every evening at the same time, punctual as a train.
sentences.zh: 她给刺猬起了个名字，叫“小墨”；小墨每天同一时刻到，准得像火车。

sentences.en: She wrote the numbers in her notebook and drew small, serious diagrams of spider webs.
sentences.zh: 她把数字记进本子，还画下一张张认真严肃的蛛网图。

sentences.en: "Biodiversity is not a word for books," Grandpa said. "It is this orchard's immune system."
sentences.zh: “生物多样性不是书上的词，”爷爷说，“是这片果园的免疫系统。”

sentences.en: "When one kind of life has trouble, another kind stands up and covers for it."
sentences.zh: “哪一种日子不好过了，另一种日子就站起来替它顶班。”

sentences.en: No tree was sprayed that year, and still almost every apple survived.
sentences.zh: 那年一棵树也没打药，苹果却几乎个个保住了。

sentences.en: The apples were smaller that year, Grandpa admitted, but they tasted like apples, not like fear.
sentences.zh: 爷爷承认，那年的苹果小了些，可它们吃起来是苹果味，不是害怕的味道。

sentences.en: In the city, Xiao had thought nature was a park you visited; here she learned it was a family you belonged to.
sentences.zh: 在城里，晓以为自然是一座去逛的公园；在这里她明白，自然是一个你从属的家。

questions.q: Why did Grandpa regret using the antibiotic spray years ago?
options: It was too expensive
It killed the aphids but also killed the small hunters that kept the aphids down
It made the fruit taste sweet
The shop refused to sell it again
questions.explain: 第7-8句：他用了一次就后悔了三个季节——药也“把压制蚜虫的小小猎手们一起杀了”。

questions.q: What did Grandpa plant between the rows, and why?
options: Vegetables, to sell at the market
Flowers, to invite wasps and hoverflies that hunt aphids
Young trees, to replace the old ones
Grass, to keep the soil dry
questions.explain: 第9句 "he planted flowers between the rows to invite wasps and hoverflies, natural hunters of aphids"，种花是为了请来蚜虫的天敌。

questions.q: How did Grandpa explain symbiosis?
options: A war between species that ends with one winner
A chemical process inside the soil
Different lives helping each other stay alive
A way to make fruit sweeter
questions.explain: 第15-16句 "Different lives helping each other stay alive"，共生就是不同的生命互相帮衬着活下去。

questions.q: In 第14句, the earthworms are called "subterranean engineers." The root terr means earth or land, so subterranean means . . .
options: high up in the mountains
under the ground
from another planet
near the seaport
questions.explain: 第14句：sub-（在下面）+ terr（土地）→ 地面之下；蚯蚓就是黑暗里的“地下工程师”。

questions.q: What did Xiao learn about nature by the end of that summer?
options: Nature is a park people visit on weekends
Nature is a family you belong to, where lives help each other
Farming always needs chemical sprays
City life is healthier than orchard life
questions.explain: 第28句：在城里她以为自然“是一座去逛的公园”，在这里她明白自然“是一个你从属的家”。

title: 《爷爷的果园年历》· 百年老树

sentences.en: October arrived, and the whole orchard leaned toward the ground with the weight of fruit.
sentences.zh: 十月一到，满园的果树被果子压得向地面弯下腰。

sentences.en: Xiao came back on the night train, and the smell of ripe pears met her at the station.
sentences.zh: 晓坐夜车回来，熟梨的香味在车站就迎上了她。

sentences.en: Wooden ladders stood along the rows like a small formation waiting for orders.
sentences.zh: 木梯沿树行排开，像一支待命的小小队列。

sentences.en: She picked with both hands, and her basket filled faster than she could count.
sentences.zh: 她两只手一起摘，篮子装得比她数得还快。

sentences.en: The terrain was gentle at the bottom of the hill and steep near the top.
sentences.zh: 山脚的地势平缓，山顶附近却陡了起来。

sentences.en: On the steep rows they picked slowly, passing the fruit hand to hand like a bucket chain.
sentences.zh: 陡坡上他们摘得慢，果子手递手地传下来，像一条传水桶的长队。

sentences.en: By noon the whole hillside smelled like jam that had not been cooked yet.
sentences.zh: 到中午，整面山坡闻起来像还没下锅的果酱。

sentences.en: Grandpa Chen moved along the branches with the patience of a man reading his own handwriting.
sentences.zh: 陈爷爷在枝间移动，带着一个人读自己笔迹的耐心。

sentences.en: At the hilltop stood the oldest tree, planted by Grandpa's grandfather in 1921.
sentences.zh: 山顶上立着最老的那棵树，是爷爷的祖父一九二一年种下的。

sentences.en: It had passed its centennial years ago; its trunk was wide as a door, and its roots held half the hill.
sentences.zh: 这棵树的百岁生日早已过去；树干有一扇门那么宽，根抓住半座山。

sentences.en: Grandpa called it the family's annals, because its rings recorded every hard and generous year.
sentences.zh: 爷爷叫它“家里的编年史”——每一圈年轮都记着荒年与丰年。

sentences.en: "This one remembers the dry summer of 1972 and the great storm of 1998," he said, touching the bark like an old friend's shoulder.
sentences.zh: “它记得一九七二年的旱夏，也记得一九九八年的那场大风，”他拍着树皮，像拍老朋友的肩膀。

sentences.en: "A hundred years is nothing for a tree," he added. "Give it a millennium and it is still a young one."
sentences.zh: “一百年对树来说不算什么，”他又说，“给它一千年，它也还算年轻。”

sentences.en: Below them, the valley had been transformed from summer green to harvest gold.
sentences.zh: 山下，谷地已经从夏天的绿变成了收获的金。

sentences.en: Smoke rose from the village, and a radio played news that nobody listened to.
sentences.zh: 村子里升起炊烟，收音机播着没人听的新闻。

sentences.en: Under the old tree they ate lunch with pears, bread, and cold tea in a thermos.
sentences.zh: 他们在老树下吃午饭：梨、面包，还有保温壶里的凉茶。

sentences.en: "Your great-grandmother sat here too," Grandpa said, "with the same view of the valley and probably the same appetite."
sentences.zh: “你的太奶奶也在这儿坐过，”爷爷说，“看的是同一片谷地，胃口估计也一样。”

sentences.en: The words made Xiao quiet; the tree connected her to people she had never met.
sentences.zh: 这句话让晓安静下来；这棵树把她和从未见过面的人连在了一起。

sentences.en: She pressed her palm against the bark and felt sixty years of family shade.
sentences.zh: 她把手掌贴上树皮，摸到了六十年家族的荫凉。

sentences.en: For the family photo that afternoon, Grandpa put on his formal jacket, the brown one with two buttons missing.
sentences.zh: 下午拍全家福，爷爷换上他那件正式的旧外套，棕色的，少了两颗扣子。

sentences.en: The photo shows the whole hill: twenty people, one dog, and the old tree filling the sky behind them.
sentences.zh: 照片里是整面山坡：二十个人，一条狗，老树在身后撑满整个天空。

sentences.en: The neighbors laughed and said he dressed like the tree was getting married.
sentences.zh: 邻居们笑说，他这打扮，像这棵树要结婚了。

sentences.en: A cold current came down the hill at dusk, and Grandpa called it winter's precursor.
sentences.zh: 黄昏，一股冷风顺坡而下，爷爷说，那是冬天的先遣。

sentences.en: "The first frost is three weeks away," he said. "The pears know it already; they always ripen before the warning."
sentences.zh: “初霜还有三个星期，”他说，“梨早就知道了；它们总在警告之前就熟透。”

sentences.en: That evening the neighbors helped load ninety-six boxes, the best harvest in ten years.
sentences.zh: 当晚邻居们来帮忙装车，九十六箱，十年里最好的收成。

sentences.en: The neighbors took boxes home in exchange for laughter and promises to return for the cider.
sentences.zh: 邻居们抱着箱子回家，留下满院子笑声，还有回来喝苹果酒的承诺。

sentences.en: In his ledger, Grandpa wrote the annual total in his careful, patient hand: 96 boxes, best year since 2019.
sentences.zh: 爷爷在账本里用工整耐心的笔迹写下年度总数：九十六箱，二〇一九年以来最好的一年。

sentences.en: Then he went out and, standing in the dark, thanked the hill in a voice too low for anyone to hear.
sentences.zh: 然后他走到屋外，站在黑暗里，用低得谁也听不见的声音谢了谢这座山。

questions.q: Who planted the oldest tree at the top of the hill?
options: Grandpa himself
Grandpa's grandfather in 1921
The neighbors together
Xiao's great-grandmother
questions.explain: 第9句 "planted by Grandpa's grandfather in 1921"，是爷爷的祖父一九二一年种下的。

questions.q: Why did Grandpa call the old tree the family's annals?
options: Because it was worth a lot of money
Because its rings recorded every hard and generous year
Because it was planted on his birthday
Because it grew the sweetest pears
questions.explain: 第11句 "because its rings recorded every hard and generous year"，年轮记着荒年与丰年。

questions.q: What did Grandpa call the cold current that came down the hill at dusk?
options: Autumn's greeting
Winter's precursor
The orchard's breath
A sign of rain
questions.explain: 第23句 "A cold current came down the hill at dusk, and Grandpa called it winter's precursor"，那是冬天的先遣。

questions.q: In 第13句, Grandpa says, "Give it a millennium and it is still a young one." How long is a millennium?
options: Ten years
A hundred years
A thousand years
A million years
questions.explain: 第13句：centennial（第10句）是百年，millennium 是它的十倍——一千年；词根 ann 意为“年”。

questions.q: Why did Xiao go quiet under the old tree?
options: She was tired from picking fruit all morning
The tree connected her to family members she had never met, and she felt part of their long line
She did not like the cold tea
Grandpa asked her to be quiet
questions.explain: 第17-19句：太奶奶也坐过这里，树“把她和从未见过面的人连在了一起”，她摸着树皮感受到六十年家族的荫凉。

title: 《爷爷的果园年历》· 地窖与账本

sentences.en: When the first snow came, the orchard went quiet, and the work moved underground.
sentences.zh: 初雪落下，果园静了，活计转到了地下。

sentences.en: Grandpa's cellar was a subterranean room, cool, dark, and smelling of earth, apples, and time.
sentences.zh: 爷爷的地窖是一间地下屋，又凉又暗，满是泥土、苹果和时间的气味。

sentences.en: They carried the best fruit down the stone steps and laid it in wooden trays, one careful layer at a time.
sentences.zh: 他们把最好的果子抱下石阶，一层层小心码进木盘。

sentences.en: The trays were numbered, and the numbers had their own history; number seven, he told her, had survived three floods and one fox.
sentences.zh: 木盘都编了号，号码各有自己的历史；他告诉她，七号盘挺过三场洪水和一只狐狸。

sentences.en: "Cold slows the clock of the fruit," Grandpa said. "Spring will find them still fresh, and surprised about it."
sentences.zh: “低温会把果子的时钟调慢，”爷爷说，“春天来找它们时还新鲜着，自己都要吃一惊。”

sentences.en: On the cellar wall hung a thermometer and, next to it, forty years of small pencil notes.
sentences.zh: 地窖墙上挂着一支温度计，旁边是四十年用铅笔写下的小记录。

sentences.en: The notes were uniform: date, temperature, how many trays, one line each winter evening.
sentences.zh: 这些记录格式统一：日期、温度、几盘果，每个冬夜一行。

sentences.en: Xiao copied one line into her notebook just to feel the shape of the habit.
sentences.zh: 晓往自己本子上抄了一行，只为摸一摸这习惯的形状。

sentences.en: Every winter evening, Grandpa opened his ledger and recorded the day in the same format.
sentences.zh: 每个冬夜，爷爷都翻开账本，用同一种格式记下这一天。

sentences.en: His pen was slow and exact, and he never used a ruler, but every line came out straight.
sentences.zh: 他的笔又慢又准，从不用尺，可每一行都写得笔直。

sentences.en: He had started it in 1986, the year her mother was born, and had never missed a single annual page.
sentences.zh: 这本记录他从一九八六年、晓妈妈出生那年记起，一页年度都没落下。

sentences.en: Each page held one year: rainfall, blossom dates, boxes sold, birds seen, small accidents, and small jokes.
sentences.zh: 每页装着一年：雨量、花期、卖出的箱数、见过的鸟、小小的事故，还有小小的玩笑。

sentences.en: Some pages carried a small star; those were the hard years when the orchard still got its water first.
sentences.zh: 有些页上画着一颗小星；那些是紧巴的年头，可果园还是第一个分到水。

sentences.en: "It is not a diary," he said. "A diary talks about feelings. This is the annals of the hill."
sentences.zh: “这不是日记，”他说，“日记谈感受，这是这座山的编年史。”

sentences.en: "The hill has feelings too," he added, "but it prefers numbers."
sentences.zh: “山也有感受，”他补了一句，“只是它更喜欢数字。”

sentences.en: Xiao read the pages like a novel, with a flashlight under the blankets.
sentences.zh: 晓躲在被窝里打着手电，像读小说一样翻这些纸页。

sentences.en: In them she found droughts, storms, broken ladders, and patient recoveries.
sentences.zh: 纸页里有旱灾、风暴、摔坏的梯子，还有一次次耐心的恢复。

sentences.en: In 1998 a late frost had taken every blossom, and the whole page held only one line: nothing this year.
sentences.zh: 一九九八年一场倒春寒卷走了每一朵花，整页只写了一行：今年无收。

sentences.en: The next line, 1999, began quietly: the trees came back on their own, no help asked, no thanks given.
sentences.zh: 一九九九年那一行开头很平静：树自己缓了过来，不求人，也不道谢。

sentences.en: Information like this, Grandpa said, was an inheritance that no bank could hold and no thief could steal.
sentences.zh: 爷爷说，这样的信息，是哪家银行都存不下、哪个小偷都偷不走的家产。

sentences.en: "A bank keeps your money for you," he said. "This keeps your years."
sentences.zh: “银行替你存钱，”他说，“这个替你存年头。”

sentences.en: Outside, the perennial trees stood in the snow, dark branches forming letters against the sky.
sentences.zh: 屋外，多年生的树静静立在雪里，深色的枝桠在天幕上排成一个个字母。

sentences.en: Grandpa pointed at them with his pipe and read the shapes like a man reading a familiar alphabet.
sentences.zh: 爷爷用烟斗指着它们，像读一套熟悉的字母表一样读着那些形状。

sentences.en: Snow covered the hill like a page waiting to be written on.
sentences.zh: 雪盖住山坡，像一页等着被写字的纸。

sentences.en: The orchard in winter was not empty, he explained; it was a sentence that had lost its leaves but kept its grammar.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，冬天的果园并不空；它是一个掉了叶子、却留着语法的句子。

sentences.en: That night, the cellar lamp transformed the shelves into small gold streets.
sentences.zh: 那天夜里，地窖的灯把木架照成一条条金色的小街。

sentences.en: Xiao chose one line from 1986 and copied it into her own new notebook, the first of many.
sentences.zh: 晓从一九八六年那页上选了一行，抄进自己的新本子——这是许多行里的第一行。

sentences.en: Under it she wrote a small heading in careful letters: volume one.
sentences.zh: 在下面，她用一笔一划写下一个小标题：第一卷。

questions.q: What was Grandpa's cellar like?
options: A warm kitchen
A subterranean room, cool, dark, smelling of earth and apples
A wooden shed behind the house
A garage full of empty boxes
questions.explain: 第2句 "a subterranean room, cool, dark, and smelling of earth, apples, and time"，又凉又暗的地下屋。

questions.q: Since when had Grandpa kept his ledger, and had he ever missed a page?
options: Since 1986, and never a single annual page missed
Since 1998, only in good years
Since 2020, on his phone
Since 1970, only harvest totals
questions.explain: 第9、11句：从一九八六年记起，每晚同一格式，“一页年度都没落下”。

questions.q: What did the page for 1998 hold?
options: A long story about the storm
Only one line: nothing this year
A star and a joke
The 96-box record
questions.explain: 第18句 "the whole page held only one line: nothing this year"，倒春寒卷走所有花，整页只有一行“今年无收”。

questions.q: The word "annals" (第14句) comes from the root ann, meaning year. Annals are . . .
options: year-by-year records of what happened
a kind of winter apple
songs sung at harvest
bank accounts for farmers
questions.explain: 第14句：日记谈感受，账本却是“这座山的编年史”——一年一页按年记录的史册；词根 ann = 年。

questions.q: What does "A bank keeps your money for you. This keeps your years" (第21句) suggest about the ledger?
options: The ledger should be stored in a bank
The information in it is an inheritance more precious than money
Grandpa does not trust banks with money
The ledger can be sold for a good price
questions.explain: 第20-21句：这些信息“是哪家银行都存不下、哪个小偷都偷不走的家产”——比钱更贵重的传家之宝。

title: 《爷爷的果园年历》· 新的年历

sentences.en: In her last winter break, Xiao asked Grandpa if she could borrow the ledgers for a school project.
sentences.zh: 最后一个寒假，晓问爷爷能不能为学校的一个项目把账本借她。

sentences.en: He carried them out of the cellar like sleeping children and told her to be careful with the corners.
sentences.zh: 他把它们从地窖里抱出来，像抱熟睡的孩子，嘱咐她小心纸角。

sentences.en: She scanned four hundred pages, one thin annual page for every year since 1986.
sentences.zh: 她扫描了四百页纸——从一九八六年起，每年薄薄一页。

sentences.en: Some pages were soft with age, and one had a tea stain shaped like a small island.
sentences.zh: 有的纸页软得发旧，有一页上的茶渍像一座小小的岛。

sentences.en: She typed the numbers into her laptop and watched forty years rearrange themselves on the screen.
sentences.zh: 她把数字敲进笔记本电脑，看四十年在屏幕上重新排队。

sentences.en: Grandpa sat beside her for an hour, saying nothing, which for him was a long speech.
sentences.zh: 爷爷在她身边坐了一个钟头，一言不发——对他来说，这已经是一篇长篇演说。

sentences.en: The numbers told a story that no single year could show: the springs were coming earlier, and the rains were arriving harder.
sentences.zh: 数字讲出一个单年看不出的故事：春天来得更早，雨下得更凶。

sentences.en: Blossom dates had crept forward eleven days across the decades, like a slow, invisible parade.
sentences.zh: 几十年间，花期悄悄提前了十一天，像一场缓慢而看不见的游行。

sentences.en: She built charts of blossom dates, harvest weights, and the first song of the oriole each spring.
sentences.zh: 她做了花期的曲线、收成的重量、还有每年春天黄鹂第一声歌的图表。

sentences.en: She added a chart of biodiversity too: the bees and birds returning year by year, in a shy, rising line.
sentences.zh: 还加了一张生物多样性的图：蜜蜂和鸟一年一年回来，连成一条羞怯上扬的线。

sentences.en: Grandpa looked at that line longer than at any other.
sentences.zh: 爷爷看那条线，看得比哪张图都久。

sentences.en: "The bees signed their names again," he said quietly.
sentences.zh: “蜜蜂又签上自己的名字了。”他轻声说。

sentences.en: Forty years of small notes passed through a quiet transformation and became a book.
sentences.zh: 四十年的小记录经历了一场安静的转变，变成了一本书。

sentences.en: Xiao designed it herself: one spread for every month, and a blank page at the end, waiting for next year.
sentences.zh: 晓亲自设计版式：每月一对页，末尾留一页空白，等着来年。

sentences.en: She kept the format simple, the way Grandpa's ledger was simple: numbers, dates, one line a day.
sentences.zh: 她把格式保持得简单，像爷爷的账本一样简单：数字、日期，每天一行。

sentences.en: On the cover she printed the title: Grandpa's Orchard Almanac, 1986 to 2026.
sentences.zh: 封面上印着书名：《爷爷的果园年历，1986—2026》。

sentences.en: Grandpa turned the pages slowly, and his thumb stopped at 2021, the old tree's centennial.
sentences.zh: 爷爷慢慢翻页，拇指停在二〇二一年——老树的百岁之年。

sentences.en: "You have turned my numbers into information that can speak," he said, and then he had to look out the window for a while.
sentences.zh: “你把我这些数字，变成了会说话的信息。”他说完，只好朝窗外望了好一会儿。

sentences.en: That winter had been formative for Xiao; she filled in her university forms and wrote "agriculture" without hesitating.
sentences.zh: 那个冬天是晓的成形之冬；她填大学志愿表时，毫不犹豫写下“农业”。

sentences.en: Her parents had expected economics; her grandfather had expected nothing, and was therefore never disappointed.
sentences.zh: 她父母盼的是经济；爷爷什么都不盼，所以从不失望。

sentences.en: The almanac was printed in a hundred copies, one for every neighbor on the hill.
sentences.zh: 年历印了一百本，山上的邻居每家一本。

sentences.en: Mrs. Luo from the next hill ordered two more, one for each of her sons in the city.
sentences.zh: 隔壁山的罗太太又订了两本，给城里的两个儿子一人一本。

sentences.en: The neighbors read it at breakfast and argued about it over fences, which Grandpa said was the sincerest form of reading.
sentences.zh: 邻居们早餐时读它，隔着篱笆为它争论；爷爷说，这是最真诚的阅读。

sentences.en: Grandpa kept the first copy in the cellar, between the thermometer and the apple trays.
sentences.zh: 爷爷把第一本放进地窖，搁在温度计和苹果盘之间。

sentences.en: Under the old tree, the first snow of the new year lay evenly on the perennial branches.
sentences.zh: 老树下，新年的第一场雪均匀地落在多年生的枝条上。

sentences.en: "Not the end of the annals," Xiao wrote on the last page, "only its newest page."
sentences.zh: “这不是编年史的结束，”晓在最后一页写道，“只是它最新的一页。”

sentences.en: Grandpa read the last page twice and signed it with his pruning-callused thumb.
sentences.zh: 爷爷把最后一页读了两遍，用剪枝磨出茧的拇指按了个印。

sentences.en: Then she sharpened her pencil, because the hill, patient as ever, had already begun next year's first line.
sentences.zh: 然后她削尖铅笔——因为这座耐心如常的山，已经开始写来年的第一行了。

questions.q: What story did forty years of numbers tell?
options: Nothing changed on the hill at all
Springs were coming earlier and rains arriving harder
The harvests grew smaller every single year
The birds had all left the hill
questions.explain: 第7句 "the springs were coming earlier, and the rains were arriving harder"，春天更早，雨更凶。

questions.q: Where did Grandpa's thumb stop while reading the new almanac?
options: At 1986, the first page
At 2021, the old tree's centennial
At the biodiversity chart
At the blank last page
questions.explain: 第17句 "his thumb stopped at 2021, the old tree's centennial"，停在老树百岁的二〇二一年。

questions.q: How many copies of the almanac were printed, and for whom?
options: Ten, for family members only
A hundred, one for every neighbor on the hill
A thousand, for the whole county
Four, one for each season
questions.explain: 第21句 "printed in a hundred copies, one for every neighbor on the hill"，一百本，山上邻居每家一本。

questions.q: In 第19句, that winter was "formative" for Xiao. The root form means shape, so a formative experience is one that . . .
options: shapes who you become
costs a lot of money
happens every winter
makes you feel tired
questions.explain: 第19句：那个冬天决定了她填志愿时“毫不犹豫写下农业”——formative 即“塑造人的、定型的”。

questions.q: Why did Grandpa say the neighbors' arguing over fences was "the sincerest form of reading"?
options: Because arguing is louder than reading
Because people only argue about a book when they have truly read it and care about it
Because the neighbors could not read very well
Because he wanted them to stop arguing
questions.explain: 第23句：邻居们早餐读它、隔着篱笆为它争论——只有真正读过、真正在意的人才会争论，所以这是最真诚的阅读。

title: 《水的旅程：从雪山到水龙头》· 雪线之上：一滴水的出生地

sentences.en: Every drop of water in your glass began its journey long before anyone thought of building a faucet, long before the first fishermen raised their huts beside its rivers, and long before any human language had a word for a river.
sentences.zh: 你杯子里的每一滴水，早在有人想到造水龙头之前，早在第一批渔夫在河边搭起棚屋之前，早在任何人类语言为河流造出一个词之前，就已经开始了旅程。

sentences.en: The water we drink today belongs to a hydrosphere that has circulated the planet for over four billion years, falling as rain onto stone-age deserts, sliding under glaciers that came and went, and passing again and again through the bodies of animals nobody has ever named.
sentences.zh: 我们今天喝的水，属于一个已在地球上循环四十多亿年的水圈：它曾作为雨落进石器时代的荒漠，曾在来来去去的冰川下潜行，也曾一次次穿过那些从未被命名的动物的身体。

sentences.en: In each molecule, two hydrogen atoms bond with one oxygen atom in a bent shape that behaves like a tiny magnet, and that small magnetic character explains almost everything about water: why it climbs, why it dissolves, and why it refuses to behave like nearly every other liquid on Earth.
sentences.zh: 在每个水分子里，两个氢原子与一个氧原子结合成一个弯曲的形状，像一枚微小的磁铁；正是这点磁性解释了水的几乎一切：它为什么会攀爬、为什么会溶解、为什么执意不肯像地球上几乎所有其他液体那样安分。

sentences.en: That hydrogen is older than the Earth itself, because it was forged in the first minutes after the Big Bang, long before the first star was born; the oxygen in each molecule arrived much later, cooked inside dying stars and scattered across space by the explosions that ended them.
sentences.zh: 那些氢比地球本身更古老——它们在大爆炸后的最初几分钟里铸成，比第一颗恒星的诞生还要早；每个分子里的氧则姗姗来迟，是在垂死的恒星内部烹制，又随终结那些恒星的爆炸撒遍太空。

sentences.en: Most of the planet's freshwater is stored not in rivers, where people imagine it, but in glaciers and ice sheets above the snow line; if you could melt every mountain of that ancient ice at once, sea levels would climb higher than a ten-storey building in most coastal cities.
sentences.zh: 地球上的淡水大部分并不存于人们想象中的河流，而在雪线之上的冰川和冰盖之中；如果你能把那一片片古老冰山一次性融化，多数沿海城市的海平面会涨得比十层楼还高。

sentences.en: A glacier is not a frozen statue but a slow river of ice, transferring the winter snow of high peaks toward the valleys at speeds of a few centimetres or, in rare cases, a few metres per day; sheep could outwalk the fastest of them, yet nothing in the landscape can stop their patient, grinding journey.
sentences.zh: 冰川并非一尊冻住的雕像，而是一条缓慢的冰河：它以每天几厘米、个别情况几米的速度，把高峰的冬雪运往山谷。羊都走得比最快的冰川快，可这片山水中，没有什么能拦住它们耐心碾磨的行程。

sentences.en: Each spring, melting snow produces a white current of meltwater that feeds the rivers below and refills the groundwater under the fields, so that wells dug by grandfathers continue to offer their cool water in August; farmers refer to this gift as the white season, the quiet engine of the valleys.
sentences.zh: 每年春天，融雪产出一股白色的融水径流，滋养山下的河流，也灌满田野之下的地下水；于是祖父们打下的井，到了八月仍能献上凉水。农民把这份馈赠称作"白色的季节"——山谷安静的动力。

sentences.en: Scientists refer to the lowest altitude where snow survives the summer as the snow line, and that line is climbing year after year; where grandfathers learned to ski as boys, their grandchildren now walk among grass and black stones, and the maps drawn a century ago quietly turn into fiction.
sentences.zh: 科学家把积雪能熬过夏天而不化的最低海拔称为雪线，而这条线正在一年年上移；祖父们小时候学滑雪的地方，孙辈如今走在草丛与黑石之间，一百年前绘制的地图正悄悄变成小说。

sentences.en: In the Alps and the Himalayas, glaciers are now retreating at speeds absent from the written chronicle of human history; monks who have photographed the same ice face every summer for fifty years offer the clearest record, and their pictures differ from each other more with every passing decade.
sentences.zh: 在阿尔卑斯山和喜马拉雅山，冰川正以人类文字记载中从未见过的速度消退。五十年来每个夏天都拍摄同一面冰壁的修道院，留下了最清晰的记录——而照片之间的差异，每过十年就更大一些。

sentences.en: Communities that depend on glacier-fed rivers will suffer shortages during the dry months long before the ice disappears completely, because the dangerous years are not the final ones but the peak-melt ones, when the sick glacier produces a flood of extra water and everyone mistakes the warning for a gift.
sentences.zh: 依赖冰川补水的社区，早在冰完全消失之前就会在旱季吃缺水的苦头；因为危险的年头并不是最后的年头，而是融水峰值期——那时病弱的冰川产出额外的洪水，人人却把警报错当成礼物。

sentences.en: The melting also reduces the bright white surface that once reflected sunlight back into space and kept the planet cooler; every square kilometre of ice that turns to dark rock or blue water absorbs heat instead, so the melting produces more melting, a circle that scientists can measure but not switch off.
sentences.zh: 融化还削减了那层曾把阳光反射回太空、让地球更凉快白色地表；每有一平方公里冰变成暗色的岩石或蓝色的海水，就多吸收一分热量——于是融化催生更多融化，一个科学家能测量、却关不掉的循环。

sentences.en: Hydroelectric stations, which prefer steady flows, must adjust their output as the rhythm of the seasons grows less predictable, and planners who once referred to "average years" now admit that no such year will occur again; the currency of mountain water, once so reliable, has turned speculative.
sentences.zh: 偏爱稳定水流的水电站，不得不随着季节节律日益难测而调整出力；规划者们过去常提"平均年份"，如今承认这样的年份再也不会出现了——山区之水这份一度可靠的货币，已经变成投机品。

sentences.en: Our journey begins here, where a single drop sits inside a crack of ancient blue ice, compressed by decades of snowfall, waiting for a morning sun that is arriving earlier and striking harder than any morning in the long memory of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 我们的旅程从这里开始：一滴水正待在古老蓝冰的一道裂缝里，被几十年的落雪压实，等待一个清晨的太阳——而在大山漫长的记忆里，从来没有哪轮朝阳来得这么早、晒得这么狠。

questions.q: Where is most of the planet's freshwater stored?
options: In rivers and lakes
In glaciers and ice sheets above the snow line
In clouds and rainfall
In underground city pipes
questions.explain: 第5句明确说淡水大部分"并不存于人们想象中的河流，而在雪线之上的冰川和冰盖之中"。

questions.q: When was the hydrogen in water molecules formed?
options: Inside ancient glaciers
During the first minutes after the Big Bang
By modern treatment plants
In the Earth's core
questions.explain: 第4句：氢在大爆炸后的最初几分钟里铸成，比地球和第一颗恒星都古老。

questions.q: What is happening to the snow line?
options: It stays fixed year after year
It is moving downward
It is climbing higher year after year
It has completely vanished
questions.explain: 第8句："这条线正在一年年上移"，孙辈只能在草丛与黑石间行走。

questions.q: Why does the author call the peak-melt years "the dangerous ones"?
options: Because the glacier finally disappears then
Because the extra water looks like a gift but is really a warning of coming shortages
Because floods destroy all the maps
Because sheep can no longer outwalk the ice
questions.explain: 第10句：病弱的冰川在融水峰值期产出额外的洪水，"人人却把警报错当成礼物"——旱季的缺水还在后头（推断）。

questions.q: The words refer and transfer both derive from the Latin root fer ("to carry"). Which sentence pairs them naturally?
options: Farmers refer to the meltwater as the white season, while the glacier transfers snow toward the valleys
Monks refer to maps, while photographs transfer heat
Planners refer to currency, while stations transfer sheep
Scientists refer to fiction, while rivers transfer magnets
questions.explain: 第6句冰川"把高峰的冬雪运往山谷"（transfer），第7句农民把融水称作"白色的季节"（refer）——两个词同属词根 fer（带来、搬运）。

title: 《水的旅程：从雪山到水龙头》· 高架渠：引水的文明

sentences.en: Long before pumps existed, engineers discovered that gravity alone could conduct water across hills and valleys without any engine; if the source sat a little higher than the city, the water would walk downhill forever, patient as a mule and far cheaper to feed.
sentences.zh: 在水泵问世很久之前，工程师就发现：仅凭重力，不用任何机器，就能引导水翻山越谷。只要水源比城市高那么一点，水就会永远往低处走——像头有耐心的骡子，而且喂养成本低得多。

sentences.en: Ancient Rome eventually operated eleven aqueducts, whose combined channels stretched more than five hundred kilometres toward the city, and their construction occupied generations of surveyors, stone-cutters and bricklayers whose names never entered any chronicle, although their work still stands in the Italian sun.
sentences.zh: 古罗马最终运转着十一条高架渠，渠道总长超过五百公里，一路通向城里；修筑它们耗尽了测量员、凿石匠与砌砖匠的几代人——他们的名字从未进入任何编年史，作品却至今立在意大利的阳光下。

sentences.en: Most of that distance ran underground, because open channels would suffer heavy losses from evaporation, mud, and theft along the way; a buried channel keeps its water cool, clean and honest, and the same argument is used today by engineers who prefer tunnels to canals.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分路段在地下，因为明渠会因蒸发、淤泥和沿途偷水而损失惨重；埋在地下的水渠让水保持凉爽、洁净、诚实——而今天更偏爱隧道而非明渠的工程师，用的还是这套理由。

sentences.en: Where a valley was too wide to cross, builders erected arched bridges that we now call viaducts, close cousins of the water channels themselves; the arch transferred every load downward into its own legs, turning gravity from an enemy into a partner and letting every stone squeeze its neighbours into one self-supporting curve.
sentences.zh: 遇到过宽的山谷，工匠便架起拱桥——也就是我们今天所说的高架桥，与水渠本身是近亲；拱把每一分荷载都传进自己的双腿，把重力从敌人变成盟友，让每块石头都把邻石挤成一个自撑的弧。

sentences.en: The Pont du Gard in southern France, nearly fifty metres tall, conducted water across the Gardon valley for centuries with a slope so gentle that the eye cannot see it — barely twenty-four centimetres of fall along its top tier, a precision achieved with plumb lines, water clocks and endless patience.
sentences.zh: 法国南部的加尔桥高近五十米，曾有几个世纪之久引水跨过加尔东河谷，坡度平缓到肉眼无法察觉——顶层全程落差仅约二十四厘米，靠铅垂线、水钟和无尽的耐心达到这样的精度。

sentences.en: The Romans did not invent the aqueduct — earlier versions occurred in Assyria, Greece and Egypt — but they introduced standard designs that spread with their armies across the empire, so that a bathhouse in Spain and a fountain in Syria often conducted water through channels built to exactly the same imperial plan.
sentences.zh: 高架渠并非罗马人发明——更早的样式已在亚述、希腊和埃及出现过——但罗马人引入了标准设计，随军团传遍帝国；于是西班牙的浴场与叙利亚的喷泉，常常按同一份帝国图纸铺设的渠道引水。

sentences.en: In the capital, the water was conducted into public baths, ornamental fountains, and the private houses of a privileged few, and it arrived under enough pressure to play in the gardens; ordinary citizens collected their share at public basins, where the queue offered news, gossip and a thin kind of politics.
sentences.zh: 在都城，水被引入公共浴场、观赏喷泉，以及少数特权者的私宅，抵达时的压力足以在花园里喷涌嬉戏；普通市民则在公共水盆前接自己的一份——排队的队伍里附送新闻、闲话，和一种薄薄的政治。

sentences.en: Frontinus, the official appointed to run Rome's water supply, wrote a technical handbook so careful that it still survives, and in it he referred to the aqueducts as the most solemn testimony of the empire's greatness — he counted every pipe, exposed every illegal connection, and never once doubted that water was worth the arithmetic.
sentences.zh: 弗龙蒂努斯受命管理罗马供水，他写下一部严谨到今天仍有传本的技术手册；书里他把高架渠称作"帝国伟大最庄严的证词"。他清点每一根管道，揪出每一处私接，且从不怀疑水值得这份算术。

sentences.en: Modern megacities face the same ancient problem, though their materials and scales differ enormously from cut stone and lead pipe; a metropolis of twenty million people cannot drink from a river that runs beside it, and so it must introduce water from reservoirs hundreds of kilometres away.
sentences.zh: 现代特大城市面对的是同一个古老问题，尽管材料与规模早已和条石铅管天差地别；一座两千万人的都市没法只靠身旁流过的那条河解渴，于是必须从几百公里外的水库引水。

sentences.en: China's South-to-North Water Diversion Project has transferred more than sixty billion cubic metres of water since operations began in 2014, conducting it through pipes and channels that offer the dry north a share of the wet south; the scheme remains, by any measure, the largest plumbing work in human history.
sentences.zh: 自2014年通水以来，中国南水北调工程已调水超过六百亿立方米，通过管渠把湿润南方的一份水分给干旱的北方；无论以什么尺度衡量，它都是人类历史上最大的"管道工程"。

sentences.en: Pipes, tunnels, pumps and enormous pumping stations now conduct water across distances and up heights that Roman engineers could not have imagined; water climbs over mountain ranges in the Andes and the California Sierras, pushed by machines that never sleep, and it arrives in taps a thousand kilometres from any natural spring.
sentences.zh: 如今管道、隧道与巨型泵站输送水的高度与距离，远超罗马工程师的想象；在安第斯山与加州内华达山脉，水被从不睡觉的机器推着翻过分水岭，抵达离任何天然泉上千公里外的水龙头。

sentences.en: The principle, however, has not changed at all: move water from where it occurs naturally to where people prefer to live, and let the city grow where the view is good rather than where the water is; every civilization, from the Assyrians to the engineers of Beijing, has concurred on this single sentence.
sentences.zh: 但原则丝毫未变：把水从它自然出现的地方送到人们更愿意居住的地方，让城市长在风景好、而不是水源好的位置——从亚述人到北京的工程师，每一种文明都赞成这句话。

sentences.en: Our drop, now travelling through a steel pipe wider than a Roman road, has joined that long human argument; it occurs in one place, is wanted in another, and the distance between the two is crossed at the speed of a modern pump.
sentences.zh: 我们这滴水，此刻正行进在一条比罗马道路还宽的钢管里，加入了这场漫长的人类争论：它出现在此地，被需要于彼方，而两地之间的距离，正以现代水泵的速度跨越。

questions.q: How many aqueducts did ancient Rome eventually operate?
options: Five
Eight
Eleven
Twenty
questions.explain: 第2句给出史实："十一条高架渠，渠道总长超过五百公里"。

questions.q: Why did most Roman channels run underground?
options: To hide them from enemies
To avoid losses from evaporation, mud, and theft along the way
Because arches were forbidden
Because Romans feared floods
questions.explain: 第3句：明渠会"因蒸发、淤泥和沿途偷水而损失惨重"，所以大部分路段埋在地下。

questions.q: How much water has the South-to-North project transferred since 2014?
options: More than six billion cubic metres
More than sixty billion cubic metres
More than six hundred billion cubic metres
Less than one billion cubic metres
questions.explain: 第10句："中国南水北调工程已调水超过六百亿立方米"，自2014年通水起算。

questions.q: Frontinus counted every pipe and exposed every illegal connection. What can we infer about how Rome managed its water?
options: Water supply was run with meticulous seriousness, worth careful records and enforcement
Rome relied on luck and prayer
Nobody in Rome was interested in water accounts
Illegal connections were encouraged among the rich
questions.explain: 第8句：他的手册流传至今，他称高架渠为"帝国伟大最庄严的证词"，"从不怀疑水值得这份算术"——可见罗马以严谨的记录与执法管理供水（推断）。

questions.q: The Latin root duct ("to lead") appears in conduct, aqueduct and viaduct. In sentence 1, what does gravity's power to "conduct water" mean?
options: To perform music about water
To lead and guide water along a path downhill
To boil water safely
To sell water to a city
questions.explain: 第1句：重力"就能引导水翻山越谷"，conduct 在此意为引导、输送——duct（引导）这一词根同样出现在第2句 aqueducts 和第4句 viaducts 中。

title: 《水的旅程：从雪山到水龙头》· 净水厂：一杯自来水的诞生

sentences.en: Before it reaches your tap, the drop passes through a treatment plant built to remove whatever the river carried with it — leaves, silt, the quiet chemistry of farms, and a long list of smaller trespassers; the plant is a factory whose product happens to be one of the oldest substances in the universe.
sentences.zh: 在抵达你家水龙头之前，这滴水会穿过一座净水厂，去除河水随身带来的一切——树叶、淤泥、农田里安静的化学，还有一长串更细小的不速之客；这座厂是一家工厂，而它的产品恰好是宇宙中最古老的物质之一。

sentences.en: In the first stage, coagulant chemicals are introduced into the raw water, making tiny mud particles cling together into clumps heavy enough to sink; the dose is not guessed but calculated, because an overdose would simply produce new problems while the old ones were still waiting.
sentences.zh: 第一步向原水投加混凝剂，让细小的泥粒彼此吸附，结成足以沉降的大絮团；投加量不靠猜而靠算，因为药剂一旦过量，旧问题还没解决，新问题已经先冒出来了。

sentences.en: In wide, silent basins, these clumps settle slowly to the bottom, a stage that engineers call sedimentation; the water just sits there for hours, like a student revising before an exam, and by the end of its long stillness most of its dirt has quietly given up.
sentences.zh: 在宽阔而安静的水池里，絮团缓缓沉到池底，工程师把这个阶段叫作沉淀；水就那样静坐几个小时，像考前复习的学生——漫长的静止结束时，它大部分的污浊都已悄悄缴械。

sentences.en: The water then drains downward through beds of sand and anthracite, where filtration removes particles far too small for the eye; each grain of sand offers its own tiny surface, and a cloud of clean water is the reduced, concentrated result of a million small refusals.
sentences.zh: 随后水向下穿过砂床与无烟煤滤层，过滤掉肉眼根本看不见的微粒；每一粒砂都献出自己小小的表面，而一杯清亮的出水，正是无数次细小拒绝之后被浓缩、被简化的结果。

sentences.en: At last a measured dose of chlorine, or a flash of ultraviolet light, disinfects the water, reducing the risk of waterborne disease to nearly nothing; children drink from fountains, hospitals run on taps, and nobody in the city recites a prayer before breakfast, which is exactly what the disinfection stage earned for them.
sentences.zh: 最后，定量投加的氯，或者紫外线的短暂一闪，完成消毒，把水源疾病的风险降到几乎为零；孩子们对着饮水器喝，医院全靠水龙头运转，城里没人在早餐前默念祷文——这正是消毒环节为他们挣来的日常。

sentences.en: Plant inspectors do not sip the water to test it; instead they measure how easily it conducts an electrical current, because an instrument is cheaper than a stomach and far more willing to repeat its opinion a thousand times a day.
sentences.zh: 厂里的检验员并不靠品尝来检测水质，而是测量水传导电流的难易——毕竟仪器比胃便宜，而且一天愿意把同一意见重复一千次。

sentences.en: Nearly pure water is a poor conductor, so a sudden jump in conductivity suggests that dissolved salts have entered the supply — perhaps from a broken seal, perhaps from a farm upstream — and the sensors refer that jump to a control room within seconds.
sentences.zh: 接近纯的水是不良导体，因此电导率骤升往往说明有溶解盐混进了供水——也许来自一处破损的密封，也许来自上游的农田——传感器会在几秒内把这一跳上报给控制室。

sentences.en: Every hour, samples are transferred to laboratories, where analysts test for metals, bacteria and acidity before the water is released; the results are reduced to plain numbers on a public report that any citizen can read online for free, because a treatment plant that nobody understands cannot be trusted by anybody.
sentences.zh: 每小时都有水样被送往实验室，放行之前，分析员要检测金属、细菌与酸碱度；检测结果最终浓缩成公开报告上的几个数字，任何市民都能在网上免费查阅——因为一座没人看得懂的净水厂，也就没人信得过。

sentences.en: What leaves the plant is a manufactured product, no longer the river water that first entered through the intake gates; the difference is not philosophical but chemical, and it can be written as a list of substances the plant removed one by one from the drop's long cargo.
sentences.zh: 从厂里流出的是一件加工过的产品，不再是当初从取水口进来的河水；这差别不是玄学而是化学，可以写成一张清单——净水厂从这滴水的漫长行李中，一样一样取走了那些东西。

sentences.en: Educating the public about these steps matters, because trust in tap water decides whether people drink it or buy bottles; a city can produce excellent water and still watch its citizens prefer plastic, which is why many plants now offer open days, school visits and honest tours of the basins.
sentences.zh: 向公众讲清楚这些步骤很重要，因为对自来水的信任，决定了人们是喝它，还是去买瓶装水；一座城市可以把水做得非常好，却眼看着市民更偏爱塑料瓶——所以如今许多水厂开始提供开放日、学校参观，以及诚实的池体导览。

sentences.en: In the Netherlands, some plants produce drinking water without any chlorine at all, letting the water filter naturally through dunes for weeks instead; the slow sand does the work that chemicals would do faster, and many Dutch customers refer to the result, only half joking, as dune champagne.
sentences.zh: 在荷兰，有些水厂完全不用氯，而是让水在沙丘中自然过滤数周来产出饮用水；慢吞吞的砂做了化学药剂本可以更快做完的事，而许多荷兰用户半开玩笑地把成品叫作"沙丘香槟"。

sentences.en: Other countries experiment with membranes, ultraviolet arrays and slow carbon beds, but every process offers the same quiet promise: whatever the river offers us in the morning, the evening tap will not offer it back unaltered, and the plant is the translator between those two sentences.
sentences.zh: 别的国家试验膜滤、紫外阵列与慢速碳床，但每种工艺许下的都是同一句安静的承诺：早晨河流送来什么，傍晚的水龙头都不会原样奉还——而净水厂，就是这两句话之间的翻译。

sentences.en: Our drop, now crystal clear and faintly chlorinated, leaves the basins behind and enters the dark network of pipes that runs beneath the streets of the city, where it will travel for hours toward a kitchen it has never seen.
sentences.zh: 这滴水如今清澈透亮、带着淡淡的氯味，告别水池，钻进城市街道底下那片幽暗的管网——它将在那里走上几个小时，去往一间它从未见过的厨房。

questions.q: What happens during sedimentation?
options: Coagulant chemicals are added to the water
Clumps settle to the bottom of wide, silent basins for hours
Chlorine kills the remaining bacteria
Sand beds remove the finest particles
questions.explain: 第3句：絮团在宽阔安静的水池里"缓缓沉到池底"，水静坐数小时，工程师称之为沉淀。加药是第一步（第2句），过滤在其后（第4句）。

questions.q: Why do inspectors measure conductivity instead of sipping the water?
options: Nearly pure water is a poor conductor, so a jump reveals dissolved salts in the supply
To check the temperature of the water
To measure how fast the water flows
To count bacteria in each sample
questions.explain: 第6句检验员不品尝，改测导电性；第7句："接近纯的水是不良导体"，电导率骤升即说明溶解盐混入。

questions.q: How do some Dutch plants avoid chlorine entirely?
options: They boil the water for hours
They let it filter naturally through dunes for weeks
They add chlorine only at night
They import bottled water instead
questions.explain: 第11句：荷兰有些水厂"让水在沙丘中自然过滤数周"，成品被戏称为"沙丘香槟"。

questions.q: Why do many plants now offer open days, school visits and tours of the basins?
options: Because a plant that nobody understands cannot be trusted, and trust decides tap versus bottles
Because the law requires public lectures
Because they need more workers
Because tourists pay well
questions.explain: 第10句："一座城市可以把水做得非常好，却眼看着市民更偏爱塑料瓶"，因此向公众讲清工艺、赢得信任（推断其动机）。

questions.q: The Latin root duct ("to lead") plus pro- ("forward") gives product — literally something led forth. In sentence 9, what is the plant's product?
options: The river's raw water at the intake gates
The manufactured, treated water that leaves the plant
The mud removed from the basins
The plastic bottles in the shops
questions.explain: 第9句："从厂里流出的是一件加工过的产品"，第1句也说净水厂是一家工厂，产品恰好是宇宙中最古老的物质之一——pro-（向前）+ duct（引导）→ 引出来的东西 → 产品。

title: 《水的旅程：从雪山到水龙头》· 管网深处：漏与灌

sentences.en: Beneath the streets, the drop travels through hundreds of kilometres of pipe, much of it older than the people it serves; some networks contain sections laid in the nineteenth century, and a few of those iron veterans still conduct water to taps that did not exist when they were buried.
sentences.zh: 街道之下，这滴水要穿过数百公里的管道，其中不少管龄比它所服务的人还老；有些管网里还留着十九世纪铺的管段，几条铁铸的老兵至今仍把水送到它们下葬时不曾存在的水龙头。

sentences.en: In many aging networks, more than a quarter of the treated water is lost before it ever reaches a single customer; the city pays to filter, pump and disinfect every drop, and then watches a considerable fraction of that expensive product seep quietly back into the ground.
sentences.zh: 在许多老旧管网里，超过四分之一的成品水还没送到任何一户人家，就已经漏掉了；城市花钱过滤、加压、消毒每一滴水，然后眼睁睁看着这份昂贵产品里相当大的一部分，悄悄渗回地底。

sentences.en: Some leaks announce themselves as flooded basements and sudden holes in the road, but far more occur silently for years, wasting water that nobody counts; a broken pipe under a park can lose a swimming pool a day and never once appear on any bill or map.
sentences.zh: 有的漏水会以地下室进水、路面突现大洞的方式宣告自己，但更多的漏水默默发生多年，浪费着无人统计的水；公园地下一根破裂的管道，一天能漏掉一整座游泳池，却从不出现在任何账单或地图上。

sentences.en: Utilities now infer the location of hidden leaks from data gathered by pressure sensors and acoustic loggers fixed to the pipes; at three in the morning, when honest households sleep and dishonest meters sit still, the loggers listen for the thin hiss of water escaping into the dark.
sentences.zh: 水务公司如今靠数据推断暗漏的位置——贴在管壁上的压力传感器和听漏仪昼夜采集；凌晨三点，诚实的住户已入睡，不老实的水表也安静下来，听漏仪正竖着耳朵，捕捉水逃进黑暗时那细细的嘶声。

sentences.en: When night-time flow in one district does not match what the meters predicted, the difference itself becomes evidence of a crack, and a crew is transferred to the spot before the street above it learns anything; the inference is rarely perfect, but it is far cheaper than digging up the whole city on suspicion.
sentences.zh: 一旦某片区深夜的流量与水表模型预测不符，这个差额本身就成为裂隙的证据，抢修队会在头顶的街道察觉任何动静之前就被调往现场；这样的推断不总是精准，却远比凭怀疑把全城刨个遍便宜。

sentences.en: Above ground, the picture differs completely, because irrigation consumes roughly seventy percent of the freshwater humanity withdraws each year; every litre that runs through a city tap is dwarfed, in the global ledger, by the litres that pour across fields of wheat, rice and cotton.
sentences.zh: 地面之上则是另一番景象：人类每年抽取的淡水中，约七成都耗在了农业灌溉上；翻开全球的账本，城市水龙头里流过的每一升，都被倾泻在麦田、稻田与棉田上的公开数压得抬不起头。

sentences.en: Drip systems can reduce waste dramatically compared with fields flooded from open canals, where much of the water simply evaporates before any root can prefer it; the difference between a damp stem and a drowned field is worth entire reservoirs in a dry summer.
sentences.zh: 与靠明渠漫灌、任水还没等任何根偏爱它就大量蒸发的田地相比，滴灌能把浪费大幅减少；在旱夏，"湿润的茎秆"与"淹死的田"之间的差别，抵得上好几座水库。

sentences.en: The world's most fertile plains, from the Nile delta to the Punjab, were built by rivers that transferred silt season after season; the same floods that suffered a bad reputation among town-dwellers were quietly producing the soil that fed them, a bargain nobody designed and nobody can now afford to end.
sentences.zh: 世界上最肥沃的平原，从尼罗河三角洲到旁遮普，都是河流一季又一季搬来淤泥堆成的；那些在城里人心里名声很坏的洪水，正悄悄造出养活他们的土壤——一桩没人设计、如今也没人赔得起去终止的交易。

sentences.en: Farmers apply fertilizer to sustain high yields, but the same rain that offers the fields a drink can transfer the surplus into rivers, where it feeds toxic blooms of algae; the water suffers twice, once in the field and once in the channel, and the bill is offered downstream.
sentences.zh: 农民施用肥料来维持高产，可同一场给田地送水的雨，也能把多余的部分搬进河流，喂出有毒的藻华；水受了两次苦——一次在田里，一次在河道里——而账单被递到下游。

sentences.en: Such blooms recur every warm summer, and they are occurring more often as the climate keeps warming; each bloom consumes the river's oxygen at night, and each morning can offer the shore a carpet of dead fish as a kind of receipt.
sentences.zh: 这样的藻华每个暖夏都会重现，而且随着气候持续变暖，出现得愈发频繁；每场藻华都会在夜里耗尽河水的氧气，而每一个早晨，都可能把一滩死鱼铺上河岸，像某种回执。

sentences.en: In dry regions, the question of whose preference for water should prevail returns to the courts every single decade, because every river is a conference of competing claims — cities against farms, fish against turbines, the present against the future — and the referee owns a wooden desk rather than a hydrological model.
sentences.zh: 在干旱地区，谁对水的偏好应当优先的问题，每隔十年就会重新回到法庭；因为每条河都是一场各执一词、彼此竞争的主张大集会——城市对农田、鱼对水轮机、现在对未来——而裁判手里握的是一张木桌，而不是水文模型。

sentences.en: Hydrologists largely concur on the diagnosis: fixing leaks is the cheapest new source of water available to any city, cheaper than a new reservoir, cheaper than a desalination plant, and far cheaper than waiting until the dry years occur; the disagreement, where it exists, is only about who should pay for the repair.
sentences.zh: 水文学家们对诊断基本一致：修好漏水，就是任何一座城市能找到的最便宜的新水源——比新建水库便宜，比海水淡化厂便宜，更比干等到旱年到来便宜得多；就算有分歧，也只是该由谁掏修理费。

sentences.en: Our drop leaves the pipe network and joins a sewer, beginning the last stage of its long excursion through the city; what it conducted on the way in — cleanliness, pressure, trust — it will now hand over, downstream and in the dark, to a different kind of plant.
sentences.zh: 这滴水离开管网，汇入下水道，开始它穿越这座城市的漫长旅程的最后一段；它一路引来的东西——洁净、压力、信任——如今要在下游的黑暗里，移交给另一种工厂。

questions.q: How much treated water is lost in many aging networks?
options: Less than one percent
More than a quarter
About half of it
Nearly all of it
questions.explain: 第2句："超过四分之一的成品水还没送到任何一户人家，就已经漏掉了"。

questions.q: How do utilities locate hidden leaks?
options: Divers inspect every pipe by hand
They infer locations from sensor data and night-time flow mismatches
Customers must report every leaking tap
They replace the entire network each year
questions.explain: 第4句：靠压力传感器与听漏仪的数据"推断暗漏的位置"；第5句：深夜流量的差额"本身就成为裂隙的证据"。

questions.q: Roughly what share of humanity's withdrawn freshwater goes to irrigation?
options: About ten percent
About thirty percent
About seventy percent
About ninety-five percent
questions.explain: 第6句："人类每年抽取的淡水中，约七成都耗在了农业灌溉上"。

questions.q: What can we infer about the floods from the Nile and Punjab example?
options: They were pure disasters with no benefit
Despite their bad reputation among town-dwellers, they quietly built the fertile soil that fed those towns
They were first designed by ancient engineers
They stopped transferring silt decades ago
questions.explain: 第8句：洪水"在城里人心里名声很坏"，却"正悄悄造出养活他们的土壤"——名声与功用相反，这是需要推断的关系。

questions.q: "Such blooms recur every warm summer" — the word recur means:
options: To happen for the first time
To happen again and again
To disappear completely
To move to another river
questions.explain: 第10句：藻华"每个暖夏都会重现"（recur），前缀 re-（再次）+ 词根 cur（跑、发生）→ 反复发生。

title: 《水的旅程：从雪山到水龙头》· 归海：最后一程与水的重现

sentences.en: The sewer carries our drop not away but around, toward a treatment plant that most citizens will never see and would prefer not to discuss; yet this unloved building conducts the most important recycling on the planet, and its work begins the moment your bath stops singing.
sentences.zh: 下水道载着这滴水并非去往远方，只是绕行，去一座大多数市民永远不会看见、也宁愿不谈的污水处理厂；然而这座不受待见的建筑，主持着地球上最重要的循环，而它的工作，从你浴缸停止唱歌的那一刻开始。

sentences.en: There, bacteria are offered a banquet of dissolved waste, and they spend hours digesting it inside vast aerated tanks that bubble like grey champagne; the plant feeds its guests oxygen so that they never suffer for appetite, and in return they remove nearly everything the city put into the water.
sentences.zh: 在那里，细菌获得一场溶解态废弃物的盛宴，在冒着灰色香槟般气泡的巨大曝气池里，花上几个小时把它吃干净；厂子给客人们供足氧气，让它们的胃口从不受委屈，作为回报，客人们几乎吃掉城市倒进水里的一切。

sentences.en: Solids settle out, pathogens are disinfected with the same care a drinking plant would use, and the cleaned water is finally conducted back toward the river or the sea; in well-run systems the discharge is cleaner than the river that receives it, a fact that surprises people every single time.
sentences.zh: 固体沉降，病原以饮用水厂级别的细致被消灭，净化后的水最终被引回河流或大海；在运转良好的系统里，出厂水比接纳它的河水更干净——这个事实每一次都让人吃惊。

sentences.en: In Singapore, a program called NEWater purifies treated sewage into drinking water so carefully that it meets up to forty percent of national demand; the city-state refers to every drop as precious, not because its engineers differ from others, but because it has no rivers wide enough to be careless with.
sentences.zh: 在新加坡，名为NEWater的项目把处理后的污水净化成饮用水，精细到最高满足全国四成的用水需求；这个城市国家称每一滴水都珍贵，不是因为它的工程师与别人有何不同，而是因为它没有一条河宽到容得下粗心。

sentences.en: Public resistance to reused water is cultural rather than chemical, because the product is often cleaner than the river it returns to; the difficulty occurs in the imagination, where a drop retains the memory of its journey long after any laboratory can offer evidence that the memory is gone.
sentences.zh: 公众对再生水的抗拒来自文化而非化学，因为这产品往往比它要回归的河流更干净；难处发生在想象里——在那里，一滴水始终保留着对旅程的记忆，哪怕实验室早已拿出证据，证明那记忆已荡然无存。

sentences.en: Whatever its route, every drop sooner or later rejoins the ocean, where sunlight will dehydrate it back into invisible vapour; the same energy that lifts it from the waves once lifted it from the skin of a dinosaur, and will lift it again from a puddle outside a school.
sentences.zh: 无论走哪条路，每一滴水迟早汇入海洋，阳光会把它重新脱水成看不见的水汽；这份把它从浪尖托起的能量，曾从一只恐龙的皮肤上托起过它，将来也会从学校外的水洼里再次托起它。

sentences.en: Winds carry the vapour for days across oceans and continents, and when it cools over land, the water is returned as rain; farmers who refer to the weather as bad luck are, without knowing it, describing a delivery service that never closes and almost never misses a coast.
sentences.zh: 风带着水汽在大洋与大陆上空走上数日，一旦在内陆上空遇冷，水便以雨的形式归还大地；把天气说成倒霉的农民，其实正在不知不觉地描述一家从不打烊、几乎从不误送海岸的快递。

sentences.en: Water is the planet's oldest currency, circulating endlessly among clouds, rivers, oceans and living bodies without ever losing value; no bank prints it, no government debases it, and every transaction in four billion years has occurred at a perfectly stable exchange rate of one drop for one drop.
sentences.zh: 水是这颗行星最古老的货币，在云、河、海与活着的身体之间无尽流通，从不贬值；没有银行印刷它，没有政府让它掺水贬值，四十亿年来的每一笔交易，都按一滴兑一滴的完美固定汇率成交。

sentences.en: This cycle has recurred for four billion years, which means almost no water molecule on Earth is truly new; the hydrosphere is closed, nothing truly leaves it, and nothing new is added in any meaningful amount, so the glass you hold tonight is a second-hand shop of very old goods.
sentences.zh: 这个循环已重演四十亿年，意味着地球上几乎没有一个水分子是真正"新"的；水圈是封闭的：没有什么真正离开它，也没有什么以有意义的量被新添进来——所以你今夜举起的杯子，是一家装满陈年旧货的二手店。

sentences.en: It is a strange but sound inference: in your glass, some molecules almost certainly passed through a living dinosaur, and others through the boiling springs where life first occurred; drinking water is therefore a kind of family reunion, although the relatives never send cards.
sentences.zh: 这是一个奇怪却站得住的推断：你杯中的水，几乎必然有一些曾流过某只活着的恐龙，另一些曾流过生命最初涌现的那几处滚烫的温泉；因此，喝水是一场家族团圆——只是亲戚们从不寄贺卡。

sentences.en: The same closed circle explains why hydration is never a purchase but always a borrowing: when you hydrate after a long run, you are rejoining a cycle older than every mountain range on Earth, and the loan will be repaid, with interest, within about ten days.
sentences.zh: 同一个闭环也解释了为什么补水从来不是购买，而永远是借贷：当你长跑后补水，你正重新加入一个比地球上任何山脉都古老的循环，而这笔贷款连本带息，大约十天内就会还清。

sentences.en: Whatever a city conducts through its aqueducts, pipes and taps, the hydrosphere remains the only true owner of the goods, and it lends them to every civilization at the same gentle interest rate it charged the Assyrians and will charge whoever comes after us.
sentences.zh: 无论一座城市用高架渠、管道和水龙头输送什么，水圈始终是这批货物唯一真正的主人；它以当年对亚述人收取的同一种温和利率，把水借给每一种文明，也将借给在我们之后到来的任何人。
