sentences.en: The journey of water is not a line but a circle, and your glass is simply where the circle passes today; tomorrow the same drop may occur in a cloud above the Pacific, in a rice field, or in the tears of somebody who has never heard of your city — and it will not remember you, which is perhaps the gentlest fact in all of science.
sentences.zh: 水的旅程不是一条直线，而是一个圆；你的杯子，不过是这个圆今天恰好经过的地方。明天，同一滴水也许出现在太平洋上空的云里、一片稻田里、或某个从没听说过你这座城的人的泪水中——而它不会记得你，这也许是全部科学里最温柔的一个事实。

questions.q: What happens inside the vast aerated tanks of a treatment plant?
options: Bacteria digest the dissolved waste, fed with oxygen so their appetite never suffers
Chlorine is added to the water
Sand filters the last particles
The water is pumped to Singapore
questions.explain: 第2句：细菌"获得一场溶解态废弃物的盛宴"，厂子供足氧气，"作为回报，客人们几乎吃掉城市倒进水里的一切"。

questions.q: NEWater can meet up to how much of Singapore's water demand?
options: Four percent
Fourteen percent
Forty percent
Eighty percent
questions.explain: 第4句：NEWater把处理后的污水净化成饮用水，"最高满足全国四成的用水需求"。

questions.q: Why is public resistance to reused water called cultural rather than chemical?
options: Because the product is often cleaner than the river it returns to; the difficulty occurs in the imagination
Because reused water contains more salt
Because chemists refuse to test it
Because the law forbids drinking it
questions.explain: 第5句：再生水"往往比它要回归的河流更干净"，难处"发生在想象里"——一滴水在想象中保留旅程的记忆。

questions.q: Why does the author call the dinosaur claim a sound inference?
options: Because dinosaurs were recently rediscovered
Because the hydrosphere is closed and the cycle has recurred for four billion years, so old molecules must circulate among all drinkers
Because laboratories found dinosaur DNA in water
Because the Bible mentions it
questions.explain: 第9句："循环已重演四十亿年"且水圈封闭；第10句据此推断："你杯中的水，几乎必然有一些曾流过某只活着的恐龙"。

questions.q: "Sunlight will dehydrate it back into invisible vapour" — the word dehydrate means:
options: To fill something with water
To remove water from something
To freeze something solid
To heat a bath
questions.explain: 第6句：阳光把海水"脱水成看不见的水汽"；前缀 de-（去掉）+ 词根 hydro（水）→ 除去水分。同根词还有第9句的 hydrosphere（水圈）。

title: 《时间档案馆》· 影子与秩序：计时的开端

sentences.en: Before humans learned to count hours, they learned to watch shadows crawl slowly across the ground, because a shadow never argues, never sleeps, and repeats its whole performance every single day of the year without once asking for wages — for a species just learning to count, the perfect employee.
sentences.zh: 在学会数小时之前，人类先学会了看影子在地上缓慢爬行；影子从不抬杠、从不睡觉，一年里的每一天都原样重演全场演出，而且从不开口要工钱——对一个刚学数数的物种来说，这是最完美的雇员。

sentences.en: In ancient Egypt, priests tracked the sun with obelisks whose moving shadows marked the seasons of the Nile's annual flood; when the shadow touched the carved line, the river would follow within weeks, and the priests who read the stone were the most indispensable men in the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 在古埃及，祭司用方尖碑追踪太阳，碑影的移动标出了尼罗河一年一度泛滥的季节；影子一旦触到刻线，几周之内河水必至——而能读懂那块石头的祭司，是王国里最不可或缺的人。

sentences.en: By around 1500 BC, Egyptian astronomers had built portable shadow clocks that divided the working day into measurable parts; a simple bar with a raised crosspiece could be carried from temple to temple, so the day's shape travelled with its owner instead of staying nailed to the palace floor.
sentences.zh: 约公元前1500年，埃及天文学家已造出可携带的影钟，把白昼切成可以计量的段落；一根装着抬高横杆的木条就能从一座神庙带到另一座，于是"一天的形状"跟着主人走南闯北，而不必钉死在宫殿的地面上。

sentences.en: Babylonian astronomers later divided daylight into twelve hours, a scheme that survives inside our clocks today, and their reason was arithmetic rather than astronomy: twelve divides cleanly by two, by three, by four and by six, which made it the friendliest number the ancient world owned.
sentences.zh: 巴比伦的天文学家后来把白昼分作十二个小时，这套方案至今仍活在我们的钟表里；他们的理由与其说来自天文学，不如说来自算术——十二能被二、三、四、六整除，是古代世界所拥有的最好相处的一个数。

sentences.en: Those early hours were unequal, because each was simply one twelfth of the daylight, longer in summer than in winter; a summer afternoon hour might contain ninety of our modern minutes, while a winter one hurried past in fifty, and nobody in Babylon found this strange enough to complain.
sentences.zh: 那些小时并不等长——每个小时只是白昼的十二分之一，夏天长，冬天短；夏日午后的一小时可能装下今天我们的九十分钟，而冬天的一小时五十分钟就匆匆跑完，巴比伦却没人觉得这事怪到值得抱怨。

sentences.en: To compensate, Egyptian water-clock makers marked different scales for the different months of the year, understanding that time is not one thing but several, and that a clock must bend toward the calendar it serves rather than the other way around, a lesson several modern software companies have yet to learn.
sentences.zh: 为了补偿这一点，埃及的水钟匠为一年中不同的月份刻下不同的刻度；他们明白，时间不是一种东西而是好几种，钟必须迁就它所服务的历法，而不是反过来——这一课，几家现代软件公司至今还没学会。

sentences.en: Timekeeping grew from a desire for order: kings wanted chronologies to legitimize their reigns, priests wanted calendars to schedule their gods, and farmers wanted planting dates simple enough to bet a harvest on; the three demands produced three professions — scribe, astronomer and almanac-maker — and all three still exist.
sentences.zh: 计时源于对秩序的渴望：君王要编年来证明王位的正当，祭司要历法来安排众神的日程，农夫要简单到敢拿一季收成下注的播种日期；三种需求造出三种职业——书吏、天文学家、历书匠——而三种职业至今都还活着。

sentences.en: Egyptian scribes recorded each year of every reign, producing annals that historians still consult three thousand years later; a drought year, a war year, a year of strange birds — all were entered with the same patient brush, because a chronicle that selects is a chronicle that lies.
sentences.zh: 埃及书吏记下每位君王在位的每一年，留下三千年后史家仍在查考的编年史册；旱年、战年、怪鸟出现的年份——全都用同样耐心的笔触录入，因为挑挑拣拣的编年史，就是撒谎的编年史。

sentences.en: To keep such records in chronological order, they invented king lists that let later generations count backward through the centuries, dynasty by dynasty, like climbing down a staircase whose every step was carved with a name; whenever a list and a monument disagreed, the argument could last a hundred years.
sentences.zh: 为了让记载按时间顺序排列，他们发明了王表，让后人能一朝一代地顺着世纪向前回数，像走下一道每一级都刻着一个名字的楼梯；而每当王表与某块碑铭对不上，那场争吵可以吵上一百年。

sentences.en: Chinese astronomers were equally careful chroniclers, and their chronicles of comets and eclipses still help scientists date ancient events; when a modern astronomer needs to know which night in 1054 a star exploded, it is a Song-dynasty clerk's entry, not a European archive, that offers the answer.
sentences.zh: 中国的天文学家同样是笔耕不辍的编年者，他们关于彗星与日月食的记载至今仍在帮科学家为古代事件断代；当代天文学家想知道1054年那颗星爆发的具体是哪一夜时，给出答案的是一位宋代小吏的条目，而不是任何一座欧洲档案馆。

sentences.en: In every city, markets and city gates slowly synchronized their schedules to the public shadow clock in the square, so that opening and closing no longer depended on a gatekeeper's mood or a merchant's guess; the town had, without naming it, invented the deadline.
sentences.zh: 在每一座城市，市集与城门都渐渐依照广场上那面公共日晷来同步作息，开门关门不再取决于守门人的心情或商人的估摸；这座城在不知其名的情况下，发明了"截止时间"。

sentences.en: Yet every sundial shared one fatal weakness: at night, under clouds, and in rain it fell completely silent, and the town that trusted it had to endure whole evenings of clockless dark; the shadow served the sun, and when the sun refused to appear, so did the hour.
sentences.zh: 然而所有日晷都有同一个致命弱点：入夜、阴天、下雨时，它便彻底沉默，信任它的城镇只能硬挨整晚没有钟的黑暗；影子是太阳的仆人——太阳不肯露面的时候，钟点也不肯。

sentences.en: To modern eyes, a smartphone beside an obelisk is an anachronism, yet both answer the same very old question — what part of the day is it, and how long until the thing I am waiting for occurs — and the twenty-first century answers it with a battery instead of a shadow.
sentences.zh: 在今人眼里，方尖碑旁放一部手机是时代错置；但两者回答的是同一个古老的问题——现在是一天里的什么时辰，我等的那个东西还要多久才来——只是二十一世纪用来作答的，是一块电池，而不是一道影子。

questions.q: Why were the early twelve hours of daylight unequal?
options: Each hour was simply one twelfth of the daylight, varying with the season
The clocks were badly built
Priests adjusted them every month
The sun moved at an irregular speed
questions.explain: 第5句：每个小时"只是白昼的十二分之一，夏天长，冬天短"，夏午后一小时可达九十分钟，冬日一小时仅五十分钟。

questions.q: Why did Egyptian water clocks carry different scales for different months?
options: To compensate for the unequal length of hours
Purely for decoration
To honor different gods
To confuse potential thieves
questions.explain: 第6句开头 "To compensate"——为补偿小时随季节不等长的问题，钟必须迁就历法。

questions.q: What did king lists allow later generations to do?
options: Count backward through the centuries in chronological order
Predict the flooding of the Nile
Record taxes and trade
Measure the length of shadows
questions.explain: 第9句：王表"让后人能一朝一代地顺着世纪向前回数"，让记载保持时间顺序。

questions.q: "A chronicle that selects is a chronicle that lies." What does this tell us about the scribes' method?
options: They recorded everything with the same patient brush, good years and bad
They only wrote about wars and droughts
They erased strange events on purpose
They wrote only what the kings ordered
questions.explain: 第8句：旱年、战年、怪鸟之年"全都用同样耐心的笔触录入"——不挑拣、不遮掩，才是不撒谎的编年（推断其方法）。

questions.q: The Greek root chron ("time") appears in chronology, chronicle, chronological and anachronism. In sentence 13, why is a smartphone beside an obelisk an anachronism?
options: Because it belongs to a different time than the obelisk
Because it is too heavy to carry
Because it has no battery
Because obelisks are clocks
questions.explain: 第13句：两者回答同一个古老问题，但手机属于另一个时代——ana-（错）+ chron（时间）→ 时代错置之物。

title: 《时间档案馆》· 钟摆与机械钟：摇摆驯服了时间

sentences.en: In 1583, a nineteen-year-old student named Galileo watched a lamp swinging in the cathedral of Pisa, dragged there by his father to study medicine, and found the medicine that would occupy him for a lifetime hanging from the ceiling instead.
sentences.zh: 1583年，一位十九岁的学生伽利略，被父亲拽到比萨大教堂去学医，结果却发现那将占用他一生的"药"，挂在头顶的天花板上。

sentences.en: Timing the swings against his own pulse, he found that each swing took the same duration whether the arc was wide or narrow; four hundred heartbeats for the long journeys, four hundred for the short, as if the lamp politely refused to hurry.
sentences.zh: 他用自己的脉搏计时，发现无论弧线宽窄，每摆一次所持续的时间完全相同：大弧四百次心跳，小弧也是四百次——仿佛那盏灯客气地拒绝了赶时间这回事。

sentences.en: This property, later named isochronism, meant that a pendulum could become the beating heart of a clock, because a machine that repeats itself perfectly is a machine you can count on, and a machine you can count on is a machine you can ask the time.
sentences.zh: 这个后来被称作"等时性"的性质，意味着钟摆可以成为一座钟跳动的心脏：一台能完美重复自己的机器，才是一台靠得住的机器；而靠得住的机器，才是一台可以向它问时间的机器。

sentences.en: It took another seventy years before Christiaan Huygens, in 1656, built the first pendulum clock that ran reliably, depending on little more than gravity, good oil and a patient owner; almost overnight, daily errors fell from roughly fifteen minutes to about fifteen seconds.
sentences.zh: 又过了七十多年，直到1656年，惠更斯才造出第一座可靠运转的摆钟，所依赖的无非重力、好机油和一位有耐心的主人；几乎一夜之间，日误差从约十五分钟降到了约十五秒。

sentences.en: For the first time, the hour could be divided into minutes on which everyone could agree, and the minutes into seconds; a sermon, a market price, a sunrise over a battlefield — all could now be pinned to a number that meant the same thing in every town in Europe.
sentences.zh: 小时第一次可以被切分成人人都能认同的分钟，分钟再切成秒；一场布道、一个市价、战场上空的一次日出——从此都能钉在一个全欧洲每个城镇都同义的数字上。

sentences.en: Clockmakers learned to suspend the pendulum from a thin flexible spring and to keep it moving with the gentlest pushes, because force enough to speed a swing is force enough to spoil it; the craft became one of small kindnesses applied to metal.
sentences.zh: 钟表匠学会用一枚纤细柔韧的簧片悬吊钟摆，用最轻的推力让它不停摆动——因为足以催快摆的力，也正是足以毁掉摆的力；这门手艺由此变成一门"对金属施加小小善意"的手艺。

sentences.en: A pendulum's rate depends only on gravity and on its length: shorten it, and the whole clock runs faster; lengthen it toward a metre, and the swings slow until one metre marks one second, a relationship that follows directly from the laws of mechanics and cannot be bribed.
sentences.zh: 钟摆的快慢只取决于重力与摆长：调短它，整座钟就走得更急；放长到一米，摆动就慢到恰好一米对应一秒——这个关系直接从力学定律推出，贿赂不动。

sentences.en: Sailors at sea could not share this luxury, for a rolling deck swings a pendulum into chaos; aboard ships the clocks slowed, raced, and finally stopped, and a navigator who depended on them for longitude was depending on a drunk.
sentences.zh: 海上的水手却享受不到这份奢侈：颠簸的甲板会把钟摆甩进一片混沌。在船上，钟忽慢忽快，最后干脆停摆——靠这种钟定经度的领航员，等于靠一个醉汉指路。

sentences.en: An ocean's worth of longitude could be read from a clock accurate to a few seconds a day, so the race to build a motion-proof timekeeper became a race for empire; the British parliament offered a fortune — twenty thousand pounds, a king's ransom — to the first person who could endure the challenge.
sentences.zh: 一座日差仅几秒的钟，就能读出一整片大洋的经度，于是"造出不受晃动影响的钟"成了一场帝国竞赛；英国议会悬下重金——两万英镑，一笔够赎国王的巨款——奖给第一个能扛住这项挑战的人。

sentences.en: The winner was not a court astronomer but a Yorkshire carpenter's son, John Harrison, whose marine chronometers — wooden gears and self-lubricating parts, durable enough to shrug off salt and storm — held time at sea well enough to fix longitude within a few miles.
sentences.zh: 赢的人不是宫廷天文学家，而是一位约克郡木匠之子：约翰·哈里森。他的船用精密计时器——木齿轮、自润滑部件，结实到对盐雾与风暴耸耸肩就过去——在海上守时到能把经度确定在几英里之内。

sentences.en: During the sea trials of the 1760s, his instruments lost only a few seconds in months of rolling weather, a performance that ships' captains, a famously unsentimental audience, described with something close to love; one of them reportedly asked whether a second instrument could be bought, in case the first ever needed a holiday.
sentences.zh: 在1760年代的海上实测中，他的计时器在数月的颠簸天气里只慢了几秒——这份成绩，让船长们这个出了名的没有感情的人群，用近乎爱慕的语气描述它；据报告，其中一位还问过能不能再买一台，以防头一台想休假。

sentences.en: By the nineteenth century, railways had synchronized their stations by telegraph, and towns that had kept their own slightly different noons for centuries gave them up in a single decade; the company timetable, not the sun, now decided when the working day began.
sentences.zh: 到十九世纪，铁路公司已用电报把各站时钟对齐，几个世纪以来各守一套"正午"的城镇，在短短十年里集体放弃；如今决定一天从何时开始的，是公司的时刻表，而不是太阳。

sentences.en: Standard time was at first a private convenience of the railway companies rather than a public law, a reminder that many of our most durable institutions begin life as somebody's bookkeeping; governments wrote the arrangement into law only after decades of comfortable confusion.
sentences.zh: 标准时起初只是铁路公司的私利方便，而非公共法律——这提醒我们，许多最经久的制度，出生时不过是某人的记账簿；政府是在几十年舒舒服服的糊涂之后，才把这套安排写进法律。

sentences.en: Time, once a shadow cast by the sun and readable only while the sun consented, had become a mechanism ticking steadily on a wall — independent of weather, independent of mood, and almost, though not yet entirely, independent of the sky that had invented it.
sentences.zh: 时间，曾是太阳投下、只在太阳肯赏脸时才可读的影子，如今成了墙上嘀嗒作响的机械——不问阴晴，不看心情，而且，几乎（尽管还不完全）独立于那片发明了它的天空。

questions.q: What did young Galileo discover about the swinging lamp?
options: Each swing took the same duration whether the arc was wide or narrow
Heavier lamps always swing faster
Swings grow longer like rolling balls
The human pulse is a better clock
questions.explain: 第2句：他借脉搏计时，发现"无论弧线宽窄，每摆一次所持续的时间完全相同"。

questions.q: How much did daily clock errors fall once pendulum clocks ran reliably?
options: From fifteen hours to fifteen minutes
From fifteen minutes to about fifteen seconds
From fifteen seconds to one second
They did not change at all
questions.explain: 第4句：惠更斯造出可靠的摆钟后，"日误差从约十五分钟降到了约十五秒"。

questions.q: What does a pendulum's rate depend on?
options: Only gravity and its length
The temperature of the room
The weight of the lamp
The skill of the owner
questions.explain: 第7句："钟摆的快慢只取决于重力与摆长"，调短则快，一米恰好对应一秒。

questions.q: What can we infer about how standard time spread across countries?
options: It began as the railway companies' private convenience and only later became public law
It was imposed by astronomers immediately
Every town kept its own noon until the twentieth century
The sun was consulted at each step
questions.explain: 第12句："如今决定一天从何时开始的，是公司的时刻表"；第13句："标准时起初只是铁路公司的私利方便"，政府几十年后才写进法律（推断）。

questions.q: The word chronometer joins chron ("time") with meter ("measure"). According to sentence 10, what did Harrison's marine chronometers achieve?
options: They held time at sea well enough to fix longitude within a few miles
They predicted the tides for a decade
They replaced the pendulum in every church
They rang the hours more loudly
questions.explain: 第10句：哈里森的计时器"在海上守时到能把经度确定在几英里之内"——chronometer 即测时之器（chrono=时间，meter=测量）。

title: 《时间档案馆》· 多久才算久：耐用、忍受与一生的尺度

sentences.en: Once humans could measure time precisely, an entirely different question appeared: how long should a thing last? A bridge, a shoe, a promise, a marriage — every object and arrangement now carried an invisible warranty, and somebody, somewhere, would eventually be asked to honour it.
sentences.zh: 一旦人能精确计量时间，一个全然不同的问题浮现了：一样东西应该用多久？一座桥、一只鞋、一句承诺、一桩婚姻——每件东西、每种约定都带上一份看不见的保单，而迟早总有某处的某人，被要求兑现它。

sentences.en: Engineers separate durability, a material's resistance to wear, from endurance, a machine's or a runner's capacity to keep going; the words sound like sisters but describe different deaths — one crumbles at the surface while the other simply runs out of heart. A bridge can be both durable and out of endurance, and so, on a bad day, can a marathon runner.
sentences.zh: 工程师把耐用性（材料抗磨损的能力）与耐力（机器或跑者持续运转的能力）区分开来；这两个词听着像姐妹，描述的却是两种不同的死法——一种在表面碎裂，另一种只是把心跑完了。一座桥可以既耐用又没了耐力，而一个马拉松选手，在倒霉的日子里也一样。

sentences.en: Roman concrete has endured beneath Mediterranean harbours for two thousand years, actually growing harder as seawater reacts with volcanic ash, a recipe so forgiving that modern chemists spent decades reverse-engineering it and still confess that part of the answer remains a mystery.
sentences.zh: 罗马混凝土在地中海的港口水下已经历两千年，海水与火山灰反应反而让它愈发坚硬；这个配方宽厚到让现代化学家花了几十年做逆向工程，仍不得不承认一部分答案至今成谜。

sentences.en: Modern steel bridges, designed for roughly a century of service, demand constant inspection during their working lives; engineers walk them, X-ray their welds, listen to them in storms, and schedule their funerals — replacement dates — before the ribbon at the opening ceremony has been cut down.
sentences.zh: 现代钢桥按约百年的服役期设计，整个工作年限内都离不开持续检修；工程师走上桥身、给焊缝拍X光、在暴风里听它们的声音，而且早在剪彩的红绸还没摘下之前，就为它们排好了"葬礼"——更换日期。

sentences.en: To test durability in a reasonable human timescale, laboratories compress decades of simulated weather and load into a few brutal months; a bridge pier lives through a century of frost and traffic before its engineers have finished their coffee, and the machine never once apologises for the hurry.
sentences.zh: 为了在人类能接受的时间尺度里测试耐用性，实验室把几十年的模拟风雨与载荷，压缩进短短几个月的严酷考验；工程师的咖啡还没喝完，桥墩已经历了一个世纪的冰霜与车流——而机器从不对这份匆忙道歉。

sentences.en: Doctors make a similar distinction in the body, calling an illness chronic when it lasts beyond three months; the boundary is not magical, but it separates conditions that will pass from conditions that must be lived with, and the treatments differ accordingly.
sentences.zh: 医生在人体上也做类似的区分：病程超过三个月，便称为慢性病；这条界线并无魔力，但它把"会过去的病"与"必须与之共存的病"分开，治法也随之不同。

sentences.en: Chronic pain differs from acute pain not in its intensity but in its stubborn duration; a sharp ache can be survived like a storm, but a dull one that endures for a decade changes the person who carries it, in ways no single night's suffering ever could.
sentences.zh: 慢性疼痛与急性疼痛的差别不在强度，而在那纠缠不去的漫长持续；剧痛可以像一场风暴那样熬过去，可一种钝痛若持续十年，它对人的改变，是任何一夜的苦痛都做不到的。

sentences.en: Our sense of time also depends on scale: a summer feels endless to a child, who has owned only six of them, and brief to a grandparent, who measures it against the shrinking remainder; the same ninety days, counted against different supplies, occupies different amounts of inner room.
sentences.zh: 我们的时间感也取决于尺度：同一个夏天，在只拥有过六个夏天的孩子那里漫无边际，在拿所剩无几的岁月来丈量的祖辈那儿转瞬即逝；同样九十天，对照不同的存量，在心里的占位大不相同。

sentences.en: On geological scales, permanence dissolves entirely, and even the Himalayas rise and crumble on clocks of millions of years; the mountains we treat as the type of the eternal are, to a patient geologist, merely weather that happens to be made of stone — slow weather, but weather all the same.
sentences.zh: 放到地质尺度上，永固二字便彻底瓦解，连喜马拉雅也在以百万年计的钟上隆起又剥蚀；在我们眼里当作"永恒"代名词的那些山，在一位有耐心的地质学家看来，不过是恰好由石头构成的天气——很慢的天气，但终究是天气。

sentences.en: A mortgage belongs in this story too, because the word literally means a dead pledge — an arrangement that dies when the debt is repaid; the pledge's death, not the borrower's, is the clause that ancient lawyers found funny enough to name.
sentences.zh: 按揭这个词也属于这个故事，因为它的本义就是"死的抵押"——一笔还清债务便随之消亡的约定；古代律师觉得好笑、特意给它命名的，是抵押之死这一条款，而不是借款人之死。

sentences.en: Most mortgages run thirty years, a duration deliberately matched to a working life rather than to a full human one; the bank lends to the earning years and politely declines to depend on the pension, which is arithmetic dressed as sentiment.
sentences.zh: 多数按揭为三十年，这个年限是刻意对齐一段职业生涯，而非一整条人命；银行把钱借给能挣钱的年头，并客气地拒绝指望养老金——这是穿了感情外衣的算术。

sentences.en: In the end, every claim of durability is a quiet negotiation with time, and time never signs the contract; the material endures only as long as its chemistry, its maintenance and its luck concur, and two of those three can fail in a single afternoon.
sentences.zh: 说到底，每一句关于耐用的承诺，都是与时间的一场无声谈判，而时间从不肯签字；材料能撑多久，全看它的化学、它的维护与它的运气是否同时点头——而这三项里，两项可以在一个下午之内一起垮掉。

sentences.en: We build for permanence while knowing we are mortal builders, and only by arrangement does the material outlast the maker; every cathedral is a bet placed by people who will not see the payout, and the fact that the bet usually wins is one of the quiet wonders of civilization.
sentences.zh: 我们怀着凡人的自觉去追求恒久，材料之所以比匠人活得久，靠的全是人为的安排；每一座大教堂都是一场下注人自己看不到派彩的赌局，而这场赌局通常能赢——这算得上文明最安静的奇观之一。

questions.q: How do engineers distinguish endurance from durability?
options: Durability is a material's resistance to wear; endurance is a capacity to keep going
They are exact synonyms
Durability applies only to runners
Endurance means being cheap to repair
questions.explain: 第2句给出定义：耐用性是材料抗磨损的能力，耐力是机器或跑者持续运转的能力——"描述的却是两种不同的死法"。

questions.q: What has Roman concrete endured for two thousand years?
options: Beneath Mediterranean harbours, growing harder as seawater reacts with volcanic ash
On mountain railway bridges
In desert temples of Egypt
In modern city sewer systems
questions.explain: 第3句：罗马混凝土在地中海港口水下已历两千年，海水与火山灰反应，"反而让它愈发坚硬"。

questions.q: When do doctors call an illness chronic?
options: When it lasts less than a day
When it lasts beyond three months
When it strikes exactly once a year
When it follows surgery
questions.explain: 第6句："病程超过三个月，便称为慢性病"，这条界线把"会过去的病"与必须与之共存的病分开。

questions.q: What does the thirty-year term of most mortgages reveal about banks?
options: They lend against the earning years of a working life, not against a full human lifespan
They believe all borrowers live exactly thirty years
They are forbidden by law to lend longer
They prefer to be repaid in stone
questions.explain: 第11句：三十年"刻意对齐一段职业生涯，而非一整条人命"，银行"客气地拒绝指望养老金"——可推断其放贷逻辑锚定在挣钱年头（推断）。

questions.q: The Latin root mort ("death") appears in mortgage, mortal and immortal. In sentence 10, what does a mortgage literally mean?
options: A dead pledge that dies when the debt is repaid
A golden promise between friends
A payment repeated every year
A contract carved in stone
questions.explain: 第10句：mortgage 本义是"死的抵押"——一笔还清债务便随之消亡的约定；词根 mort=死，另见第13句 mortal builders（凡人匠人）。

title: 《时间档案馆》· 年与千年：历法的修订史

sentences.en: A year is a fact of astronomy before it is a fact of any calendar: the time Earth needs to circle the sun once, about 365.2422 days, a number with no respect whatsoever for the human fondness for round figures.
sentences.zh: 年首先是天文学的事实，其次才是历法的事实：地球绕太阳一周所需的时间，约365.2422天——一个对人类偏爱整数毫无敬意的数字。

sentences.en: No whole number of days fits that fraction, so every calendar ever invented must be corrected sooner or later, because the alternative is watching the seasons drift quietly out of their appointed boxes, midsummer snow and Christmas roses, until the calendar becomes a museum of good intentions.
sentences.zh: 没有任何整数天能装下这个零头，于是历来所有历法迟早都得修正；否则就只好眼看着四季悄悄漂出各自被指定的格子——仲夏落雪、圣诞玫瑰——直到整本历法沦为善意满满的老古董博物馆。

sentences.en: In 46 BC, Julius Caesar introduced a leap day every fourth year, and the Julian trick served for fifteen centuries, an administrative run that no modern institution has equalled; his calendar outlasted his republic, his empire, and the family that murdered him.
sentences.zh: 公元前46年，尤利乌斯·凯撒引入四年一闰，这套儒略历的办法用了十五个世纪——没有任何现代机构的行政方案能匹敌这个服役年限；他的历法比他的共和国、他的帝国，以及谋杀他的那个家族，都活得更久。

sentences.en: But the Julian year runs about eleven minutes too long, and those spare minutes accumulated like an uncollected debt, a few days per century, quiet as compound interest; nobody notices eleven minutes, which is precisely how eleven minutes conquers a civilization.
sentences.zh: 但儒略年比实际多出约十一分钟，这些零头像一笔无人催缴的债，一个世纪攒出几天，安静得如同复利；没人在意十一分钟——而这恰恰正是十一分钟征服一个文明的方式。

sentences.en: By the sixteenth century, the spring equinox had drifted ten days away from where the church calendar expected it, which endangered the intricate arithmetic of Easter; astronomers reported, councils debated, and finally the paperwork arrived on the desk of Pope Gregory XIII.
sentences.zh: 到了十六世纪，春分已悄悄漂离教会历法设定的位置整整十天，危及复活节那套精密的推算；天文学家上报，宗教会议争论，最后，文件终于摆上了格里高利十三世的案头。

sentences.en: In October 1582, Gregory simply deleted ten dates, so the fourth of October was followed by the fifteenth; peasants feared losing ten days of their wages, poets lost ten days of their lives on paper, and the equinox obediently returned to its assigned square.
sentences.zh: 1582年10月，格里高利索性删掉十个日期，10月4日的次日便是10月15日；农夫担心少拿十天的工钱，诗人在纸面上丢了十天的寿命，而春分则乖乖回到了它被指定的格子里。

sentences.en: The corrected Gregorian calendar is the one most of the world still follows for its annual business today, and its adoption travelled with trade and empire rather than with persuasion: Britain held out until 1752, Russia until 1918, and a few Orthodox calendars still keep their own candles burning.
sentences.zh: 修正后的格里高利历，就是今天世界上大多数人处理每年事务所用的历法；它的推行随贸易与帝国而行，而非靠劝服——英国硬撑到1752年，俄国撑到1918年，还有几部东正教历法至今点着自己的蜡烛。

sentences.en: Calendars matter because memory depends on them, for no chronicle can be assembled into history without agreed dates; two civilizations that count their years differently cannot even argue productively about when the arguing began, which is why diplomatic letters have carried two dates for most of recorded history.
sentences.zh: 历法之所以要紧，是因为记忆依赖它——没有公认的日期，任何编年记载都拼不成历史；连年方式不同的两个文明，连"争吵是何时开始的"都吵不出个结果，所以有文字记载以来，外交信函大多写着两个日期。

sentences.en: Nations celebrate their centennials and bicentennials with fireworks and speeches, and in the year 2000 the entire planet observed a millennium together; even countries that share almost nothing shared that particular party, and airlines sold out of seats flying people to the first sunrise.
sentences.zh: 各国以烟火与演说庆祝百年与两百年庆典，而2000年到来时，整个星球一起注视了一个千年的交替；连几乎毫无共同点的国家也共享了那一场庆典，航空公司载着人们飞往全球第一缕日出的航班座无虚席。

sentences.en: Historians consult the annals of earlier centuries, where each year's harvests, storms and wars were written down line by line by clerks who expected to be forgotten; the annals are often dull, which is precisely what makes them trustworthy — nobody embroiders a fact they plan to bore you with.
sentences.zh: 历史学家翻检早先各世纪的史册，那里逐年逐条记着收成、风暴与战事，落笔的书吏都料定自己会被遗忘；史册常常枯燥，而这恰恰是它们可信的原因——没有人会去渲染一个打算用来烦你的事实。

sentences.en: An annuity, a sum paid every year, takes its name directly from the Latin word annus, which simply means year; the insurance industry has built a considerable civilization on the difference between a year and a lifespan, which is the gap where all its arithmetic lives.
sentences.zh: 年金——每年支付的一笔钱——名字直接来自拉丁语的annus，意思就是年；保险业在"一年"与"一条命"的差额上建起了一座可观的文明，它全部的算术都住在那道缝隙里。

sentences.en: Retirement planning is really a problem of duration: how many years of income must one working lifetime support, and how long will the pension endure after the pay-cheques stop arriving; the answers depend on tables of mortality that each generation quietly rewrites in its own favour.
sentences.zh: 养老规划说到底是持续时间的算术题：一段工作人生，要支撑多少年的开销？工资停了以后，养老金又能撑多久？答案全依赖死亡率表——而每一代人都在悄悄把表往有利于自己的方向改写。

sentences.en: Some plants are annual, sprouting and dying within a single year, while others are perennial, returning each spring from the same roots; farmers who confuse the two can lose a harvest, and poets who confuse them can win a prize, which says something about the different tolerance of the two professions.
sentences.zh: 有些植物是一年生的，一年内萌发又死去；另一些是多年生的，每年春天都从同一条根上归来。把两者搞混的农夫会赔掉一季收成，把两者搞混的诗人却可能获奖——这多少说明了两种职业的容错率差异。

sentences.en: A calendar, in the end, is the filing system of civilization, deciding which events history keeps within easy reach; the years we agree to number are the years we agree to remember, and every reform of the calendar is, underneath the astronomy, an argument about whose memory deserves the shelf space.
sentences.zh: 说到底，历法是文明的档案系统，决定哪些事件被历史放在伸手可及的地方；我们同意编号的年份，就是我们同意记住的年份——而每一次历法改革，在天文学的下面，其实都是一场"谁的记忆配得上书架"的争论。

questions.q: Why must every calendar be corrected sooner or later?
options: The year is about 365.2422 days, not a whole number of days
The moon keeps interfering with the sun
Kings enjoyed announcing new calendars
Early printers made counting errors
questions.explain: 第1句给出年长365.2422天，第2句："没有任何整数天能装下这个零头"，否则四季会漂出格子。

questions.q: What was wrong with the Julian year?
options: It ran about eleven minutes too long each year
It forgot the leap day entirely
It counted only ten months
It started on the wrong solstice
questions.explain: 第4句：儒略年"比实际多出约十一分钟"，如无人催缴的债般逐年累积。

questions.q: What did Pope Gregory XIII do in October 1582?
options: He deleted ten dates from the calendar
He added a leap week to every year
He banned the Julian calendar forever
He moved the spring equinox by law
questions.explain: 第6句：格里高利"索性删掉十个日期，10月4日的次日便是10月15日"。

questions.q: What can we infer about the clerks who wrote the annals?
options: They recorded plainly, without motive to embellish, since they expected to be forgotten
They wrote to entertain their readers
They were ordered to exaggerate good harvests
They destroyed the dull entries
questions.explain: 第10句：落笔的书吏"都料定自己会被遗忘"，史册枯燥恰恰可信，"没有人会去渲染一个打算用来烦你的事实"（推断）。

questions.q: The Latin word annus ("year") lies behind annual, annals and annuity. In sentence 11, what is an annuity?
options: A sum paid every year
A debt that dies when repaid
A clock accurate to seconds
A plant that returns each spring
questions.explain: 第11句："年金——每年支付的一笔钱——名字直接来自拉丁语的annus"；annals（史册，第10句）与 annual（第7、13句）同根。

title: 《时间档案馆》· 时间的尽头：必死与不朽

sentences.en: Every system for measuring time eventually collides with the one deadline that no calendar can ever reschedule, the one appointment that declines every postponement and accepts no apology; clocks can be reset, calendars reformed, but this entry is written in ink that no chemist has solvents for.
sentences.zh: 每一套测量时间的系统，最终都会撞上那个任何历法都无法改期的最后期限——一个拒绝一切延期、不接受任何道歉的约定；钟可以重拨，历可以重修，但这一条目用的墨水，任何化学家都配不出溶剂。

sentences.en: Ancient Romans carved the words memento mori on their sundials — remember that you will die, even while you count the hours — a piece of engineering advice disguised as poetry: the shadow sweeping the dial is sweeping toward you as well.
sentences.zh: 古罗马人在日晷上刻下 memento mori——记住你终将死去，哪怕你正在数着时辰——一条伪装成诗歌的工程建议：扫过晷面的那道影子，同样也在扫向你。

sentences.en: Mortality is the statistical name for that deadline, and demographers track mortality rates the way astronomers track orbits, with tables, projections and a professional calm that would seem cold if it were not so quietly heroic; every row in their spreadsheets is a village of breathing people.
sentences.zh: 死亡率是那个期限的统计学名字；人口学家追踪它，就像天文学家追踪轨道——用表格、推算，和一种若非悄悄英勇便显得冷酷的职业平静。他们电子表格里的每一行，都是一村子活生生呼吸着的人。

sentences.en: In 1900, global life expectancy was about thirty-two years; today, after a single century of medicine, it is about seventy-three, a gain of forty years — not won by any single discovery but by clean water, vaccines, and the quiet annual bookkeeping of public health departments.
sentences.zh: 1900年，全球人均预期寿命约三十二岁；仅仅一个世纪的医学之后，如今约为七十三岁——四十年增幅，不是任何单一发现赢来的，而是净水、疫苗，以及公共卫生部门年复一年安静的记账赢来的。

sentences.en: Those gains against mortality were won slowly, town by town, and they can be lost again just as slowly; a public health system is a durable thing only while the public keeps agreeing to be healthy, which is one of the stranger contracts democracy ever wrote.
sentences.zh: 对必死性的这些胜利，是一镇一镇慢慢赢来的，也可能同样慢慢地再次输掉；公共卫生系统只有在公众持续同意"保持健康"时才是耐用的东西——这是民主制度写过的最奇怪的合同之一。

sentences.en: Awareness of being mortal has always shaped how people choose to spend their numbered hours; the knowledge is a wound and an instructor at once, and most of what we call culture is the long conversation a wounded species has held with its instructor.
sentences.zh: 对凡人必死的清醒，始终左右着人们如何花掉自己有数的时光；这份认知既是伤口又是教员，而我们所谓的文化，大半是这个带伤的物种与其教员之间一场漫长的对话。

sentences.en: Medieval monks kept clocks not for trains but for prayers, so that mortal work could pause at fixed hours for eternal concerns; the bell that called the field-worker to his knees and the abbot to his office was the same bell, and nobody pretended otherwise.
sentences.zh: 中世纪的修士造钟不为赶火车，而为按时祈祷，好让凡人的劳作在固定的钟点停下来，照看永恒的事；召唤田里的工人跪下、也召唤修道院长回到职责的那口钟，是同一口钟——谁也不假装不是。

sentences.en: The perennial question of philosophy — how a finite life should be spent — was written down, argued and annotated entirely by people now gone; we consult them the way farmers consult the annals, looking for weather patterns in the harvests of the dead.
sentences.zh: 哲学里那个千年常新的问题——有限的一生该如何度过——写下它、争论它、为它作注的人，全都已不在；我们求教于他们，就像农夫翻检历年史册，想从死者的收成里找出天气的规律。

sentences.en: Against mortality, humans have built three kinds of shelter: children, words and stone; the first is hope, the second is memory, and the third is memory with a warranty, and most civilizations have spent their surplus on all three at once.
sentences.zh: 为了对抗必死，人类盖起了三种庇护所：孩子、词语，和石头；第一种是希望，第二种是记忆，第三种是带保修的记忆——而大多数文明，是同时在三者身上花光盈余的。

sentences.en: Languages endure: the Rigveda, composed about three thousand years ago, is still recited today by living voices in unchanged metres; no marble and no museum were required, only breath passed from an old mouth to a young one, three thousand times in a row.
sentences.zh: 语言是能长久存续的东西：约三千年前写成的《梨俱吠陀》，今天仍由活着的人按原样的格律诵读；它不需要大理石，也不需要博物馆，需要的只是一口气，从一张苍老的嘴传到一张年轻的嘴——三千年来一口气没断。

sentences.en: Stone offers a slower shelter, and an Egyptian inscription can still speak its author's name aloud after forty centuries; the pharaohs built for a duration that embarrasses our thirty-year mortgages, and their granite has kept the appointment longer than their gods.
sentences.zh: 石头是更慢的庇护所：一段埃及铭文，在四十个世纪之后，仍能念出它作者的名字；法老们为一座建筑所设的年限，让我们三十年的按揭羞愧——而他们的花岗岩赴约的时间，比他们的神还久。

sentences.en: In an odd twist well known to historians, a speech written to mortify a rival may quietly preserve that rival's name forever; Cicero's enemies would be footnotes today if Cicero had not hated them so beautifully, sentence by immortal sentence.
sentences.zh: 有个史家们熟知的古怪转折：一篇为让对手蒙羞而写的文字，可能悄悄让那对手的名字永存；若非西塞罗恨得那么漂亮——一句接一句不朽的句子——他的政敌们今天早成了没人翻的脚注。

sentences.en: Immortality, if it exists anywhere, is distributed: nobody lives forever, but some sentences are still alive after two thousand years, still changing minds, still ending arguments in rooms their authors could not have imagined, which is as close to resurrection as grammar gets.
sentences.zh: 不朽，倘若真有，也是被分摊的：没有人能永远活着，但有些句子两千年后仍然活着，仍在改变想法，仍在它们作者想象不到的房间里终结一场争论——这已是语法所能达到的最接近复活的东西。

sentences.en: We measure time with shadows, pendulums and atoms, and now with chronometers that would not lose a second across the age of the ocean; in the end, time also measures us, and it uses a clock that keeps no numbers — we simply feel it running.
sentences.zh: 我们用影子、钟摆和原子测量时间，如今又用跨越一个大洋的年纪也慢不了一秒的精密计时器；到头来，时间也在测量我们——它用的那座钟不记数字，我们只是感到它在走。

questions.q: What did ancient Romans carve on their sundials?
options: Memento mori: remember that you will die
The names of their gods
The exact hours of prayer
The price of public water
questions.explain: 第2句：罗马人在日晷上刻 memento mori——"记住你终将死去"，连数时辰的人也不例外。

questions.q: How has global life expectancy changed since 1900?
options: From about thirty-two years to about seventy-three
From fifty years to sixty years
It has fallen sharply
It has stayed near seventy-three
questions.explain: 第4句：1900年约三十二岁，一个世纪的净水、疫苗与公共卫生记账之后，"如今约为七十三岁"。

questions.q: What three shelters against mortality does the author name?
options: Children, words, and stone
Clocks, calendars, and maps
Temples, coins, and roads
Water, vaccines, and medicine
questions.explain: 第9句："人类盖起了三种庇护所：孩子、词语，和石头"——分别是希望、记忆、带保修的记忆。

questions.q: Why would Cicero's enemies be footnotes today, if not for his hatred?
options: Because only his beautifully hateful sentences preserved their names for posterity
Because they never did anything important
Because their own books were burned
Because Romans could not read footnotes
questions.explain: 第12句：为让对手蒙羞而写的文字"可能悄悄让那对手的名字永存"——若非西塞罗恨得漂亮，政敌早被遗忘（推断）。

questions.q: The Latin root mort ("death") appears in mortal, mortality, immortal and mortify. In sentence 12, what does a speech written to mortify a rival do?
options: It shames and humiliates the rival
It pays the rival a pension
It measures the rival's years
It buries the rival in stone
questions.explain: 第12句："为让对手蒙羞而写的文字"——mortify 意为羞辱、使痛失体面；词根 mort=死，同根词见第3句 mortality、第13句 immortality。

title: 《会唱歌的市场》· 最亮的嗓音

sentences.en: My grandma is Grandma Lin, and she has sold tofu at the morning market for forty years, and every morning of my life begins with her voice.
sentences.zh: 我奶奶就是林奶奶，她在这个早市卖了四十年豆腐，我生命里的每个早晨都是从她的嗓音开始的。

sentences.en: Her call is the brightest vocal sound of the whole street, and even the sparrows on the wires stop and listen when she begins.
sentences.zh: 她的叫卖声是整条街上最亮的一副嗓音，连电线上的麻雀都会停下来听她开腔。

sentences.en: "Fresh tofu, warm tofu, taste it before you buy!" she sings in one long, happy line, and the words go up at the end like a small bird.
sentences.zh: "鲜豆腐，热豆腐，先尝后买嘞！"她用一句长长的、欢快的调子唱出来，尾音像只小鸟一样往上飞。

sentences.en: People often say that selling tofu is her true vocation, because she loves the work, and after forty years the work still loves her back.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，卖豆腐就是她真正的天职，因为她爱这门营生，四十年过去，这门营生也还爱着她。

sentences.en: She greets every old customer with a cordial smile and a warm word, and she remembers every name, every child, and every family's favorite breakfast.
sentences.zh: 她热情又客气地笑着，招呼每一位老主顾，记得住每一个名字、每一个孩子、每一家最爱吃什么早饭。

sentences.en: Old Mr. Pan, who buys two warm pieces every morning, says her voice can evoke the street's oldest memories, because forty years of mornings live inside it.
sentences.zh: 每天早上都买两块热豆腐的潘老先生说，她的嗓音能唤起这条街最老的回忆，因为四十年的清晨都装在里面。

sentences.en: "When I hear her call, I am thirty years old again," he tells me, "and my mother is calling me home for breakfast."
sentences.zh: "一听她吆喝，我就又回到三十岁了，"他跟我说，"就像我娘在喊我回家吃早饭。"

sentences.en: A warm piece of tofu is the core of many family breakfasts on our street, soft and white, like a little cloud on a cold plate.
sentences.zh: 一块热豆腐是这条街上许多人家早饭的核心，又软又白，像冷盘子里的一朵小云。

sentences.en: According to Grandpa Fu, her voice never gets tired, because a happy heart keeps a strong throat, and my grandma is happy every single day.
sentences.zh: 据福爷爷说，她的嗓子从来不累，因为心宽的人嗓子亮，而我奶奶天天都乐呵呵。

sentences.en: When the market is slow, she lets me stand on her little wooden stool, and we practice the call together, line by line, like a small choir of two.
sentences.zh: 市场没人的时候，她就让我踩上她的小木凳，我们一起一句一句地练叫卖，像个两个人的小合唱团。

sentences.en: "Loud and clear, my child," she tells me, "because honest work wants an honest voice, and tofu is the most honest work I know."
sentences.zh: "声音要响、要亮，孩子，"她跟我说，"本分生意要配一副本分的嗓子，卖豆腐是天底下最本分的生意。"

sentences.en: When my legs shake and my face turns red, she never laughs at me, and she always gives me courage with one small nod.
sentences.zh: 我腿发抖、脸通红的时候，她从来不笑话我，总是点一下头，就给了我勇气。

sentences.en: Grandma always encourages me to speak loudly and clearly, and she says a shy tongue can learn to sing, just like a shy bird can learn to fly.
sentences.zh: 奶奶总鼓励我说话要响亮、要清楚，她说害羞的舌头能学会唱歌，就像害羞的鸟能学会飞。

sentences.en: The market wakes up because her call comes first, and selling tofu is small work, she says, but it is honest work, and honest work is never small.
sentences.zh: 整个市场醒来，是因为她的叫卖声来得最早；她说卖豆腐是小生意，但是本分生意，本分生意从来都不小。

questions.q: What has Grandma Lin sold at the morning market for forty years?
options: Fresh fish
Warm bread
Tofu
Green vegetables
questions.explain: 第1句 "My grandma is Grandma Lin, and she has sold tofu at the morning market for forty years."，林奶奶卖了四十年豆腐。

questions.q: What do people often say about her work?
options: It is only a small hobby
It is her true vocation
It is too hard for her age
It will end this spring
questions.explain: 第4句 "People often say that selling tofu is her true vocation"，人们说卖豆腐是她真正的天职。

questions.q: What does Old Mr. Pan say her voice can do?
options: Make the sparrows sing along
Evoke the street's oldest memories
Sell tofu without any words
Wake up the whole town
questions.explain: 第6句 "her voice can evoke the street's oldest memories"，潘老先生说她的嗓音能唤起这条街最老的回忆。

questions.q: Why does Grandma never laugh when the narrator's face turns red?
options: Because she does not see it
Because she is too busy cutting tofu
Because she wants to give him courage, not shame
Because laughing is bad for her throat
questions.explain: 第12句 "she never laughs at me, and she always gives me courage with one small nod"，奶奶不笑话他，是想给他勇气而不是难堪。

questions.q: In sentence 6, the word "evoke" is closest in meaning to ______.
options: to call up old memories
to sell something fast
to sing too loudly
to taste warm food
questions.explain: 第6句 "her voice can evoke the street's oldest memories"。词根 vok- 表示"声音、喊"，evoke(e-向外+vok)意为"唤起"——她的嗓音把老街最旧的记忆叫了回来。

title: 《会唱歌的市场》· 星期五的争吵

sentences.en: On Friday morning, just after the first customers arrived, the fish stall and the vegetable stall began a loud quarrel, and half the market turned to watch them.
sentences.zh: 星期五早上，头一批客人刚到，鱼摊和菜摊就吵了起来，半条市场街的人都扭头看热闹。

sentences.en: A sharp provocation about water on the floor started it all, because the fish seller's bucket had made a small river under the green vegetables.
sentences.zh: 起因是一句关于地上积水的刺耳挑衅——鱼贩子的水桶在青菜底下冲出了一条小河。

sentences.en: "Your dirty water wetted my cabbage!" the vegetable seller shouted, and her angry voice was louder than the fish seller's hand bell.
sentences.zh: "你的脏水浇了我的白菜！"菜贩子喊道，她气冲冲的嗓门比鱼贩子的手铃还响。

sentences.en: The fish seller's cross answer provoked the vegetable seller even more, and soon the two of them were shouting at the same time, louder and louder.
sentences.zh: 鱼贩子没好气地回了一句，把菜贩子彻底激怒了，很快两个人就同时喊了起来，一声高过一声。

sentences.en: Their discordant voices flew over the street like cold wind, and nobody could hear the morning calls, the spoons, or the little songs anymore.
sentences.zh: 两边的声音互不相合，像冷风一样刮过整条街，谁也听不见叫卖声、勺子声和那些小曲了。

sentences.en: In one short minute, half of the market fell into discord, and even the bread seller stopped his warm song to listen to the angry words.
sentences.zh: 短短一分钟里，半个市场都失了和气，连面包师傅都停下了他暖暖的小曲，去听那些气话。

sentences.en: Grandma Lin did not shout, and she did not choose a side; she just kept cutting her white tofu into long, quiet strokes behind her little counter.
sentences.zh: 林奶奶没有喊，也没有站队，只在自家小摊后面安安静静地切着白豆腐，刀起刀落。

sentences.en: "When two voices fight, the street loses its music," she said softly to me, and her old hands never stopped their work.
sentences.zh: "两个嗓门打架，整条街就没歌听了。"她轻声对我说，那双老手上的活儿一点没停。

sentences.en: Old Zhou from the egg stall put down his two baskets and walked over to the angry sellers with a slow, warm smile.
sentences.zh: 蛋摊的老周放下两筐鸡蛋，挂着慢悠悠的暖笑，朝那两个动气的摊主走了过去。

sentences.en: With great courage, he invoked an old saying: "Fish and greens live in one pot, so why can't two stalls live on one street?"
sentences.zh: 他鼓足勇气，援引了一句老话："鱼和青菜能住一个锅里，两个摊子怎么就不能住一条街上？"

sentences.en: The fish seller laughed first, then the vegetable seller laughed too, and after that the whole market was laughing with them.
sentences.zh: 鱼贩子先笑了，接着菜贩子也笑了，随后整个市场都跟着笑成了一片。

sentences.en: Laughter brought concord back to the market street, and the two sellers shook hands over the wet and sorry cabbage.
sentences.zh: 笑声让和谐重新回到了这条市场街，两个摊主隔着那摊湿漉漉、委屈巴巴的白菜握了手。

sentences.en: By noon the fish stall and the vegetable stall stood in accord again, and the fish seller even carried a bucket of clean water to the greens with his own hands.
sentences.zh: 到了中午，鱼摊和菜摊又站在了一起、言归于好，鱼贩子还亲手提了一桶干净水给青菜送去。

sentences.en: According to Old Zhou, a market is like a choir: many different voices, one song, and a quarrel is only a wrong note in a long morning.
sentences.zh: 照老周的说法，市场就像一个合唱团：声部再多也是一首歌，吵架不过是一个漫长早晨里唱错的一个音。

questions.q: Which two stalls began the loud quarrel?
options: The tofu stall and the egg stall
The fish stall and the vegetable stall
The bread stall and the fish stall
The egg stall and the bread stall
questions.explain: 第1句 "the fish stall and the vegetable stall began a loud quarrel"，吵架的是鱼摊和菜摊。

questions.q: What started the quarrel?
options: A broken scale
A missing wallet
A sharp provocation about water on the floor
A bad price for cabbage
questions.explain: 第2句 "A sharp provocation about water on the floor started it all"，起因是一句关于地上积水的挑衅。

questions.q: What did Old Zhou invoke to stop the quarrel?
options: A call to the market office
An old saying about fish and greens living in one pot
A new rule about water
A song about cabbage
questions.explain: 第10句 "he invoked an old saying: 'Fish and greens live in one pot'"，老周援引了一句鱼和青菜同住一锅的老话。

questions.q: Why did Grandma Lin keep cutting her tofu while the others shouted?
options: Because she could not hear them
Because she was angry with both sellers
Because she believed a fight takes the music out of the street
Because she wanted to sell more tofu that day
questions.explain: 第8句 "When two voices fight, the street loses its music"——由这句可推知，她不掺和争吵，是因为她觉得吵架会把整条街的歌吵没。

questions.q: In sentence 4, "The fish seller's cross answer provoked the vegetable seller even more," the word "provoked" means ______.
options: made her calm
made her angry
made her laugh
made her leave
questions.explain: 第4句。词根 vok- 表示"喊"：pro-(向前)+voke(喊)→冲着人喊→激怒。下文两人"越喊越响"也是佐证。

title: 《会唱歌的市场》· 一盘磁带

sentences.en: One rainy afternoon, while I was looking for my lost pencil, I found an old tape recorder in Grandpa's drawer, under his old maps and a broken watch.
sentences.zh: 一个下雨的下午，我正找丢失的铅笔，却在爷爷的抽屉里翻出一台旧录音机，压在老地图和一块坏表底下。

sentences.en: Grandpa cleaned the grey dust off it, put in two new batteries, and the little machine woke up with a soft click, like a small animal.
sentences.zh: 爷爷擦掉灰，装上两节新电池，小机器"咔嗒"一声醒了过来，像只小动物。

sentences.en: I decided to record the sounds of the whole market, from the first call in the dark morning to the last spoon at noon.
sentences.zh: 我决定把整个市场的声音都录下来——从天没亮的第一声吆喝，到中午收摊的最后一记勺响。

sentences.en: According to my careful plan, I walked from stall to stall with the recorder held up high, like a boy carrying a small radio star.
sentences.zh: 按照我精心拟好的计划，我举着录音机挨个摊位走过去，像个捧着小电台明星的孩子。

sentences.en: I collected morning calls, spoons and ladles, water running on the stones, and the little talks between the sellers and their oldest friends.
sentences.zh: 我收进了叫卖声、勺子和漏勺、石板上的流水，还有摊主们和他们老哥们儿之间的零碎家常。

sentences.en: Grandma Lin was the brightest vocalist on my tape, and her long call opened the recording like the first note of a slow song.
sentences.zh: 林奶奶是这盘磁带上最亮的主唱，她那声长长的吆喝开了场，像慢歌的第一个音。

sentences.en: Every seller had a different vocal style of calling: the bread man sang high, the fish man sang fast, and Old Zhou almost spoke his, like a kind uncle.
sentences.zh: 每个摊主的吆喝都有自己的唱腔：面包师傅唱得高，鱼贩子唱得快，老周几乎是说出来的，像位和气的叔叔。

sentences.en: A young buyer from the city said the market taught him a whole new vocabulary of sounds, and he wrote some of them down in his little notebook.
sentences.zh: 一位城里来的年轻顾客说，这个市场教了他一整套全新的声音词汇，他还在小本子上记下了几条。

sentences.en: For many years, the office had a rule against loud morning music here, but last spring the sellers asked together, and the office revoked the old rule.
sentences.zh: 多年来管理处一直有条"早市禁乐"的规定，可去年春天摊主们一起去说情，管理处把这条老规定撤销了。

sentences.en: My teacher listened to my tape twice, encouraged me with both hands, and said that this street itself deserved a good record, its own small album.
sentences.zh: 老师把我的磁带听了两遍，双手捧着连声鼓励我，说这条街本身就该有一张像样的唱片，一张属于它自己的小专辑。

sentences.en: When the people of our street heard the tape, it evoked their own morning memories: wet stones, warm steam, and the first light on the roofs.
sentences.zh: 街坊们一听这盘磁带，各自的清晨记忆就被唤醒了：湿漉漉的石板、热腾腾的白汽，还有落在屋顶上的第一线天光。

sentences.en: One old woman cried a little and said, "I can hear my young husband's voice inside the fish man's call."
sentences.zh: 有位老太太掉了几滴眼泪，说："在鱼贩子的吆喝里，我能听见我年轻丈夫的嗓音。"

sentences.en: Grandma smiled and said our street had a singing soul, and every stall in the street kept one note of that soul.
sentences.zh: 奶奶笑了，说我们这条街有一条会唱歌的魂，街上每个摊子都存着那条魂里的一个音。

sentences.en: I wrote a label on the tape in my best letters — The First Record of Our Market — and Grandpa put it away in a warm, dry box.
sentences.zh: 我用自己最工整的字在磁带上写了标签——《我们市场的第一张唱片》——爷爷把它收进了一个又暖又干的盒子里。

questions.q: Where did the narrator find the old tape recorder?
options: Under the fish stall
In Grandpa's drawer
In the school music room
In Grandma's tofu box
questions.explain: 第1句 "I found an old tape recorder in Grandpa's drawer"，录音机是在爷爷抽屉里找到的。

questions.q: Who was the brightest vocalist on the tape?
options: Old Zhou
The bread man
Grandma Lin
The fish man
questions.explain: 第6句 "Grandma Lin was the brightest vocalist on my tape"，磁带上最亮的主唱是林奶奶。

questions.q: What did the office do about the old rule against loud morning music?
options: It made the rule stricter
It forgot the rule for a year
It revoked the rule last spring
It sold the rule to the sellers
questions.explain: 第9句 "the sellers asked together, and the office revoked the old rule"，去年春天管理处撤销了这条老规定。

questions.q: Why did the old woman cry a little when she heard the tape?
options: Because the tape was broken
Because it evoked the memory of her young husband
Because the fish man sang too fast
Because she could not buy tofu anymore
questions.explain: 第12句 "I can hear my young husband's voice inside the fish man's call"，磁带唤起了她对年轻丈夫的回忆，所以落泪。

questions.q: In sentence 8, "the market taught him a whole new vocabulary of sounds," the word "vocabulary" means ______.
options: a box of old tapes
a set of words or sounds of a place
a kind of morning song
a book of old maps
questions.explain: 第8句。词根 voc- 表示"声音、词语"，vocabulary 是一门语言或地方的"词语库"，这里是市场一整套声音。

title: 《会唱歌的市场》· 最后一个清晨

sentences.en: In spring, a white notice came up on the old wall of the market street, and it said that the whole street would be rebuilt into something new, something tall, and something without tofu stalls.
sentences.zh: 春天，市场街的老墙上贴出一张白告示，说整条街要改造，改成崭新的、高高的、没有豆腐摊的东西。

sentences.en: All the stalls had to move away by the end of May, and the sellers stood in front of the notice and read it again and again in long silence.
sentences.zh: 所有摊位得在五月末之前搬走，摊主们站在告示跟前，一遍又一遍地读，久久没人说话。

sentences.en: Grandma Lin felt sad for many days after that, but she never stopped her vocal call, not even on the coldest morning of that April.
sentences.zh: 那之后林奶奶难受了好些天，可她的叫卖声一天也没停过，连那个四月最冷的早晨也没停。

sentences.en: "The tofu is still warm, and the street is still ours until the very last day," she said to me, and her bright voice never went down.
sentences.zh: "豆腐还热着，到最后一天之前，这条街还是咱们的。"她对我说，那副亮嗓一直没有低下去。

sentences.en: On the last morning, every seller came earlier than ever before, and they greeted each other with cordial nods, like old friends meeting at a small, quiet festival.
sentences.zh: 最后一个清晨，每个摊主都来得比往常更早，彼此热络地点头致意，像老朋友在一个安静的小节日里相逢。

sentences.en: Old Zhou encouraged everyone to sing one last song together, and even the shy bread man, who had never sung in his life, said yes with a red face.
sentences.zh: 老周鼓励大家最后合唱一首歌，连一辈子没开过口的害羞的面包师傅都红着脸应了声好。

sentences.en: The fish seller and the vegetable seller, who once quarreled about water on the floor, now stood side by side in perfect accord, shoulder to shoulder.
sentences.zh: 曾经为地上积水吵过一架的鱼贩子和菜贩子，如今肩并肩站在一起，和和气气，一条心。

sentences.en: All the sellers sang the closing call together, and their many different voices found one warm concord in the fresh morning air.
sentences.zh: 所有摊主齐声唱起了收摊的调子，那么多各不相同的嗓音，在清晨的新鲜空气里汇成了一片暖和的和声。

sentences.en: The song was not perfect — somebody came in late, and somebody sang too high — but the empty street became their last quiet audience.
sentences.zh: 歌唱得并不完美——有人进晚了，有人唱高了——可空下来的街道，成了他们最后一位安静的听众。

sentences.en: That song needed more courage than any solo, because to sing together, you must open your heart to all your neighbors.
sentences.zh: 唱那首歌需要的勇气比任何独唱都多，因为要一起唱，就得把自己的心向所有街坊敞开。

sentences.en: I stood on Grandma's little wooden stool and held the tape recorder up high, and I recorded every note of the song, from the first to the very last.
sentences.zh: 我踩上奶奶的小木凳，把录音机高高举起来，从第一个音到最后一个音，一个不落地录了下来。

sentences.en: When the song ended, the sellers looked at each other for a long minute, and then they packed their stalls in a slow, gentle silence, folding the old cloths like flags.
sentences.zh: 歌声结束后，摊主们彼此对望了好一阵，然后在一阵缓慢而轻柔的安静里收拾摊位，把旧苫布像旗子一样叠好。

sentences.en: Grandma took my hand and said, "We will find a new street, and the street will find us, because singing people are never really lost."
sentences.zh: 奶奶牵起我的手说："我们会找到一条新街，新街也会找到我们，会唱歌的人是不会真正走散的。"

sentences.en: Now, when we play the old tape at home, it evokes the whole street again: the wet steam, the round stones, and every warm voice singing together.
sentences.zh: 如今在家里一放那盘旧磁带，整条街就又回来了：湿漉漉的白汽、圆圆的石板，还有所有暖和的嗓音在一起唱。

questions.q: What did the white notice in spring say?
options: The market street would be rebuilt into something new
The market would open every Sunday
The tofu price would double
A new singer would come to the street
questions.explain: 第1句 "the whole street would be rebuilt into something new"，告示说整条街要改造。

questions.q: Who encouraged everyone to sing one last song together?
options: Grandma Lin
The fish seller
Old Zhou
Grandpa Fu
questions.explain: 第6句 "Old Zhou encouraged everyone to sing one last song together"，是老周鼓励大家合唱的。

questions.q: How did the sellers sing the closing call that morning?
options: One by one, in turns
Only in pairs
In whispers
Together, in one warm concord
questions.explain: 第8句 "their many different voices found one warm concord in the fresh morning air"，大家的嗓音汇成了一片暖和的和声。

questions.q: Why did the song need more courage than any solo?
options: Because the song was very long
Because singing together means opening your heart to your neighbors
Because nobody knew the words
Because the street was too cold
questions.explain: 第10句 "to sing together, you must open your heart to all your neighbors"，合唱要把心向所有街坊敞开，所以比独唱更需要勇气。

questions.q: In sentence 8, "their many different voices found one warm concord," the word "concord" means ______.
options: a state of harmony and agreement
a kind of solo song
a sad goodbye
a loud quarrel
questions.explain: 第8句。词根 cord- 表示"心"：con-(共同)+cord(心)→多颗心走到一起→和声、和睦。

title: 《爱丽丝掉进的洞》· 兔子洞

sentences.en: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the river bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures and no formal conversations in it, and she wondered, with a yawn, what in the world was the use of a book that neither showed pictures nor talked sense.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝坐在河岸上，靠着姐姐，开始觉得无聊透顶：她偷看过一两回姐姐读的那本书，里面既没有插图，也没有像样的对话；她打着哈欠想，一本既不画给人看、又不跟人说正经话的书，到底有什么用处。

sentences.en: The sun was hot, the shade under the hedge was thin, and a soft weight of sleepiness pressed upon her eyelids; her sister was reading a book without pictures or conversations, about statistics or history — something equally patient — and Alice, who liked her lessons short and her stories illustrated, decided the afternoon was a great deal too long for either.
sentences.zh: 太阳很晒，树篱下的荫凉又很薄，一阵困意像温水一样压上她的眼皮；姐姐读的那本书没有插图、没有对话，讲的是统计学或历史——反正一样需要耐心——而爱丽丝这个人，功课喜欢短的，故事喜欢带画的，于是断定这个下午对哪一样来说都实在太长了。

sentences.en: Suddenly a white rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her, saying to itself, "Oh dear, I shall be too late," and Alice thought nothing of this, for a talking rabbit is only one degree stranger than a hurried one; but when the rabbit drew a formal watch from its waistcoat pocket, looked at it, frowned, and hurried on, Alice rose to her feet, burning with curiosity.
sentences.zh: 忽然，一只粉眼睛的白兔子从她身边跑过，嘴里念着"哎呀，我要迟到了"；爱丽丝并没觉得这有什么奇怪——会说话的兔子，不过是比匆匆忙忙的兔子再怪上一分罢了；可当那兔子从背心口袋里掏出一块规规矩矩的怀表，看了一眼，皱了皱眉，又匆匆赶路时，爱丽丝站了起来，好奇心烧得她坐不住。

sentences.en: She ran across the field after it, just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge, and in another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering, in the hurry of the moment, how in the world she was to get out again — which is the sort of thought that arrives only after its owner is already falling.
sentences.zh: 她跑过田野去追，正赶上看见它钻进树篱下一个大大的兔子洞；转眼之间，爱丽丝也跟着跳了进去——在那阵慌忙里，她压根没想过，出去了该怎么再出来；这一类念头，向来只在主人已经落下去之后，才姗姗来迟。

sentences.en: The hole went down like a deep vertical well, yet she fell not quickly but gently, slowly enough to look about her and to take an inventory of the walls, which were lined with cupboards and bookshelves in tidy formation, and with jars of jam hanging on pegs beside maps and pictures, all in the most finished order, as if somebody were expected.
sentences.zh: 那洞像一口深井一样笔直向下，可她下坠得并不快，慢得足够她边落边打量四周：洞壁上排着碗柜和书架，整整齐齐，煞有队形，挂钉上还吊着一罐罐果酱，旁边是地图和画片——一切都收拾得妥妥帖帖，仿佛随时有客人要来。

sentences.en: She took down a jar marked ORANGE MARMALADE, was disappointed to find it empty, and, fearing to drop it upon anybody below, she managed to put it into one of the cupboards as she passed — which was, she thought afterwards, very proper conduct for a falling girl.
sentences.zh: 她取下一只标着"橘子酱"的罐子，却失望地发现里面是空的；她怕随手一扔砸到下面的人，落过碗柜时便设法把它放了进去——她后来想，对一个边下落边办正事的小姑娘来说，这算是很有分寸的举止了。

sentences.en: Down, down she went, trying to predict how far she had fallen, and guessing it must be near the centre of the earth, half believing that the whole universe had turned upside down with her, and that she would never arrive anywhere at all.
sentences.zh: 她落啊落，落啊落，一面猜自己已经落到多深——准是快到地心了吧——一面又半信半疑，觉得整个宇宙都跟着她翻了个个儿，而她永远到不了任何地方。

sentences.en: "After a fall like this," she said aloud to nobody, "I shall think nothing of tumbling down the stairs at home; I could not feel vertigo now if I wished for it; why, I might fall right through the earth and come out among the antipodes, and fancy asking a native the way back."
sentences.zh: "经过这样一摔，"她对着空处大声说，"在家从楼梯上滚下来根本不算什么；现在就算我想晕，也晕不起来了；没准我能一直穿过地球，从地球背面那头掉出去——你想想，还得开口找当地人问回程的路。"

sentences.en: She tried to remember her multiplication tables as she fell, which gave the darkness the pleasing form of a lesson, and she found she could still say them, if a little slurred, which suggested to her that falling, on the whole, agreed with her memory — and this comforted her, as multiplication has comforted falling girls from time immemorial.
sentences.zh: 下落时她试着背乘法口诀，这就给黑暗安上了一种功课的好形式；她发现自己居然还背得出——尽管有点含混——由此她认定，下落这件事，总体来说，不碍她的记性；这个发现让她安心，须知自古以来，乘法口诀安慰过多少往下掉的小姑娘。

sentences.en: Presently the shelves ran out, and she dropped past the last of them into an amorphous darkness that had no top, no bottom, and no shape her eyes could honestly name; the fall, which had seemed gentle, now felt long enough to be a residence.
sentences.zh: 不久搁板到头了；她落过最后一块，坠进一团无定形的黑暗里——没有顶，没有底，也没有眼睛叫得出名字的形状；这场原本温柔的下落，如今长得都快够资格称为定居了。

sentences.en: The darkness did not frighten her so much as it informed her — for it was perfectly quiet, perfectly empty, and perfectly unlike anything in her lessons — that the world she knew had been quietly folded up and put away, and that some other version of it had been unfolded in its place.
sentences.zh: 这黑暗与其说吓着她，不如说是通知了她：它安安静静、空空荡荡，和她功课里的任何东西都不像——她所熟悉的那个世界，已经被悄悄叠好收起来了，另一个版本，正在原地被展开。

sentences.en: At last the fall ended all at once: a thump, a heap of dry sticks and leaves, and Alice found herself sitting on a bank, unhurt, in another world, looking about her with wide eyes and not one bone out of order.
sentences.zh: 下坠终于戛然而止：噗的一声，一堆干树枝和树叶；爱丽丝发现自己坐在一层落叶上，毫发无伤地置身另一个世界，睁大眼睛四下张望，一根骨头也没错位。

sentences.en: Before her ran a passage a little larger than a rat-hole, and along it came the white rabbit, trotting back and talking to itself still; "Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!" said the rabbit, and it popped down its own hole and vanished.
sentences.zh: 面前是一条比耗子洞大不了多少的走廊，那只白兔子正沿着它往回小跑，嘴里还在自言自语；"我的耳朵和胡须啊，越来越晚了！"兔子说完，一头钻进自己的洞，不见了。

sentences.en: Alice followed it at once, at a run, burning with the same curiosity, and the little passage turned a corner, and the light at the end of it opened into a long, low hall, lit by a row of lamps hanging from the roof.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝立刻拔腿追了上去，还是那股烧人的好奇心；走廊拐了个弯，尽头那点亮光豁然敞开，变成一间又长又矮的大厅，屋顶下挂着一排灯，把厅里照得亮堂堂。

questions.q: Why did Alice doubt the use of her sister's book?
options: It was far too long for one afternoon.
It had no pictures and no formal conversations in it.
It was written in a foreign language.
It belonged to a grown-up library.
questions.explain: 第1句 "it had no pictures and no formal conversations in it, and she wondered... what in the world was the use of a book that neither showed pictures nor talked sense"。

questions.q: What finally made Alice stand up and chase the rabbit?
options: The rabbit spoke aloud to itself.
The rabbit drew a formal watch from its waistcoat pocket.
The rabbit had remarkable pink eyes.
The rabbit wore a smart waistcoat.
questions.explain: 第3句写她起初不以为然，"but when the rabbit drew a formal watch from its waistcoat pocket, looked at it, frowned, and hurried on, Alice rose to her feet, burning with curiosity"——掏出怀表才是转折点。

questions.q: What did Alice find inside the jar marked ORANGE MARMALADE?
options: Sweet orange marmalade.
A little golden key.
A paper label saying DRINK ME.
Nothing — the jar was empty.
questions.explain: 第6句 "She took down a jar marked ORANGE MARMALADE, was disappointed to find it empty"，罐子是空的，她还很有分寸地把它放回了碗柜。

questions.q: The quiet darkness is said to "inform" Alice of something. What has happened, in her own understanding?
options: She is about to land on the moon.
The world she knew has been folded away, and another version of it unfolded in its place.
She has been asleep on the river bank all along.
She has fallen all the way through the earth.
questions.explain: 第11句 "the world she knew had been quietly folded up and put away, and that some other version of it had been unfolded in its place"——由此可推知，她已认定自己换到另一个世界的版本里了。

questions.q: With vert meaning to turn, what is "vertigo" in "I could not feel vertigo now if I wished for it"?
options: A great thirst.
A fear of rabbits.
The dizzy, head-turning feeling of falling from a height.
A pain in the feet after running.
questions.explain: 第8句 "I shall think nothing of tumbling down the stairs at home; I could not feel vertigo now if I wished for it"——vertigo（词根 vert，转）指从高处跌落时那种天旋地转的眩晕感。

title: 《爱丽丝掉进的洞》· “喝我”

sentences.en: At the end of the long low hall stood a tiny door, only about fifteen inches high, and through the keyhole Alice saw the loveliest garden she had ever dreamed of — bright flowers, cool fountains, and beds of flowers she could not name — and she longed to get into it with all her heart, and, being ten times too large, she could not.
sentences.zh: 又长又矮的大厅尽头有一扇小门，只有大约十五英寸高；透过锁孔，爱丽丝看见了她梦寐以求的最美的花园——鲜艳的花、清凉的喷泉，还有许多叫不上名字的花圃；她一心想进去，可她比门大了十倍，进不去。

sentences.en: She sat down and wept, then scolded herself for weeping, quite like a nurse scolding a child, and quoted her own lessons back at herself like a disagreeable governess: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a great girl like you, crying in this way — stop this minute, I tell you!"
sentences.zh: 她坐下来哭了一场，接着又为哭鼻子训斥自己，活像保姆训孩子，还像个讨厌的家庭教师，把自己的功课背给自己听："真不害臊，这么大个姑娘了，这样哭鼻子——立刻给我停下，听见没有！"

sentences.en: Presently her eye fell upon a very small bottle standing on the glass table, tied to it with a paper label bearing, in neat formal letters, the words DRINK ME; and she found a little golden key on the same table, which she guessed, correctly, belonged to the little door.
sentences.zh: 不久，她看见玻璃桌上立着一只很小的瓶子，系着纸标签，用端正的正式字体写着"喝我"两个字；同一张桌上还躺着一把小金钥匙，她猜——猜得没错——正是那扇小门的。

sentences.en: Her lessons had informed her that if you drink much from a bottle marked poison, it will almost certainly contradict you sooner or later — that is, disagree with you, "disagree" being the polite word for it — so she checked the label carefully for that dangerous word, and was glad to find it absent.
sentences.zh: 功课教过她：标着"毒药"的瓶子，喝下去早晚会"反驳"你——也就是跟你过不去，"过不去"是客气些的说法——于是她把标签仔仔细细检查了一遍，看有没有那个危险的字眼，很高兴没有找到。

sentences.en: "It seems to have no poison in it, and it is only polite to drink what one is formally invited to drink," she reasoned; the strange formula inside tasted of cherry tart, custard, pine-apple, roast turkey and hot buttered toast, all in a single sip, and she finished it to the last drop, for a child at her stage of life is a scientist.
sentences.zh: "看来里面没有毒，况且人家正式请我喝，喝了才礼貌，"她这样推理；瓶里那古怪的配方，一口下去，樱桃馅饼、蛋奶糊、菠萝、烤火鸡和热黄油吐司全都在了；她把它喝到了最后一滴——她这个年纪的孩子，个个都是科学家。

sentences.en: A warm transformation swept through her, and in a moment she was barely ten inches high; she was delighted at first, for now she could creep under the door — but she had forgotten the little golden key, and her new size had dictated a fresh problem instead of a solution, for the key lay on the table, far above her head.
sentences.zh: 一阵暖烘烘的变化涌遍全身，转眼间她只有十英寸高了；起先她高兴坏了——这下能从门底下爬进去了——可她忘了那把小金钥匙；新身材没有解决旧难题，反倒指定了一道新的：钥匙还躺在桌上，远远高过她的头顶。

sentences.en: Nothing remained but to try her old verses, and to see whether her head had shrunk along with her body; she began to recite, but the words came out all wrong, her diction stumbling over lines she had once known perfectly, and she concluded that she must have been transformed into some other little girl, who did not know her lessons properly.
sentences.zh: 她只剩一个法子：背背旧诗，看看脑袋是不是跟着身子一起缩小了；她开口一背，词全跑偏了，措辞在从前烂熟的诗行上一跤接一跤地绊倒；于是她断定，自己准是变成了另一个小姑娘，一个功课学得不怎么样的。

sentences.en: "I am sure I am not Ada, and I am sure I cannot be Mabel, for she knows such a very little; I must have been changed for one of them" — and as she said it a tear rolled down one cheek, and then a whole procession of tears, and nothing in the world could be done to stop them.
sentences.zh: "我肯定不是艾达，也肯定当不了梅布尔，她懂得那么少；我一定是被换成了她们中的一个"——话音未落，一颗泪珠从一边脸颊滚下来，随后是整整一队眼泪，天底下没有任何办法能拦住它们。

sentences.en: Soon she found a little glass box lying under the table, and inside it a very small cake, on which currants had spelled, in letters even more formal than the label's, the words EAT ME; she put the box in her lap and set herself to think, as well as a girl in her position could.
sentences.zh: 很快她在桌子底下找到一只小玻璃盒，里面有一块很小的蛋糕，上面的葡萄干拼出"吃我"两个字，那字体比标签上的还要正式；她把盒子搁在膝上，让自己尽力思考——一个处在这种境地的小姑娘，能想到多远就想多远。

sentences.en: "If this makes me larger, I can reach the key; if it makes me smaller, I can creep under the door; either way I shall get into the garden, and it is only the size of the middle that puzzles me" — which is the kind of reasoning that looks admirable until it is tested, and hers was about to be.
sentences.zh: "要是吃了变大，我够得着钥匙；要是变小，我能从门底下爬过去——不管哪样都能进花园；麻烦只出在中间那个不大不小的尺寸上。"——这一类推理，在没受检验之前总显得头头是道，而她这套，马上就要受检验了。

sentences.en: She ate a piece, and the metamorphosis was not gentle: she grew, and grew, and grew, until her head pressed against the ceiling — nine feet high at the least — and one arm went out the window, and one foot up the chimney, whichever came handiest.
sentences.zh: 她吃了一块，这次的变形毫不温柔：她长啊，长啊，长个不停，直到头顶顶住天花板——至少也有九英尺高——一条胳膊伸出了窗外，一只脚翘上了烟囱，哪儿顺手往哪儿去。

sentences.en: Looking down at her own vast shoes, she felt that something deformed and monstrous had replaced the little girl she had been, and she began to cry again; and the tears were enormous, being the tears of a giantess, and the hall began to be a wet place.
sentences.zh: 低头看着自己巨大的鞋，她觉得有什么畸形而吓人的庞然大物，顶替了原来那个小姑娘；她又哭了起来——这回的眼泪也是巨人的眼泪，一颗颗大得吓人，大厅渐渐成了个湿乎乎的地方。

sentences.en: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself," she told the giant, meaning herself, "crying over nothing in a great hall like this; you should have a bonnet to drop your tears into, or a proper handkerchief, either of which would be formal and useful" — and the great tears rolled down all the same.
sentences.zh: "真不害臊，"她对那巨人训道——也就是训她自己——"守着这么大的厅堂，没事就哭鼻子；你该有顶帽子接眼泪，或者有块正正经经的手帕，哪一样都体面又管用"——可那些大大的泪珠，还是照样一颗颗滚下来。

sentences.en: She sat, enormous and weeping, in the middle of the hall, and wondered whether she would ever be the right size again, or whether she was now a version of herself that would never fit through any door in the world.
sentences.zh: 她坐在大厅正中，巨大，淌着泪，心里嘀咕：自己还能不能变回合适的尺寸，还是从此成了又一个版本的自己——一个再也钻不进世上任何一扇门的版本。

questions.q: Why did Alice decide the bottle was probably safe to drink?
options: The label was written in formal letters.
She had checked it carefully and found no mark of poison on it.
It smelled like hot buttered toast.
The glass table looked clean and honest.
questions.explain: 第4句她想起毒药瓶的教训，"she checked the label carefully for that dangerous word, and was glad to find it absent"——查过标签，没有"毒药"字样，她才敢喝。

questions.q: When a poison bottle is said to "contradict" you, what is meant?
options: The bottle will start an argument with you.
The poison will disagree with you — make you seriously ill.
The label will contradict the taste.
You will forget all your lessons.
questions.explain: 第4句她自己给出了注解——"that is, disagree with you, 'disagree' being the polite word for it"——contradict（contra 反 + dict 说）在这里是双关：字面像"出言反驳"，实指毒药跟你"过不去"，让你中毒。

questions.q: After shrinking to ten inches, what new problem did Alice face?
options: She could no longer see the little door.
The golden key lay on the table, far above her head.
The door had grown even smaller.
She had lost her old verses entirely.
questions.explain: 第6句 "her new size had dictated a fresh problem instead of a solution, for the key lay on the table, far above her head"——人变小了，钥匙却够不着了。

questions.q: After eating the cake, why does Alice feel "something deformed and monstrous" has replaced the little girl she was?
options: Her body has become ugly and too large for the room, and she no longer recognizes herself in it.
A real monster has taken her place in the mirror.
Her shoes have been stolen by the rabbit.
She has grown so small that she cannot see herself.
questions.explain: 第12句她低头看着自己的巨鞋、头抵天花板、臂出窗外——身体大得装不下这个房间，与第11句的 metamorphosis 对照可知：她觉得这具失控变形的身体顶替了原来的小姑娘，自我都要认不出了。

questions.q: With morph meaning form, shape, what does "metamorphosis" describe in sentence 11?
options: A polite conversation about weather.
A change from one form into another — here, Alice's sudden enormous growth.
A very slow walk across a hall.
A kind of cake baked with currants.
questions.explain: 第11句 "She ate a piece, and the metamorphosis was not gentle: she grew, and grew, and grew"——metamorphosis（meta 变 + morph 形）指形态的根本改变，即她吃下蛋糕后身体的急剧变形。

title: 《爱丽丝掉进的洞》· 眼泪池

sentences.en: Alice was still enormous, and her tears were enormous too, and before long the long low hall held a pool of salt water four inches deep and half a mile wide, if you counted it the way she counted it, which was emotionally rather than mathematically, though her arithmetic masters would have called it four inches and no more.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝哭的时候还是那么巨大，泪水也跟着巨大；不一会儿，又长又矮的大厅里就积起了一池咸水，四英寸深，足有半英里宽——如果是照她的算法算的话：她的算法从来是感情用事，不是数学用事；虽然她的算术老师们，只会管它叫四英寸，一寸不多。

sentences.en: "I wish I had not cried so much," she said, swimming about the hall in a rising despair; but it was already too late to avert a flood of her own making, and the flood, in the manner of floods, did not care whose it was; the water stood, in fact, at her chin, and rising.
sentences.zh: "早知道就不哭那么久了，"她在厅里划着水说，越划越绝望；可要躲开这场自己亲手哭出来的洪水，已经太迟了；而洪水向来是洪水的做派：它是谁的，根本不在乎——那水，事实上已经齐到她的下巴，还在涨。

sentences.en: Presently she heard a splash in the middle of the pool, and a mouse swam towards her; and in this strange version of the world it seemed to Alice quite natural that the mouse should talk, though what it would say was anybody's guess.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，池子中央传来扑通一声，一只老鼠朝她游了过来；在这个奇怪版本的世界里，老鼠会说话，爱丽丝觉得再自然不过——只是它要说什么，谁也猜不着。

sentences.en: "O Mouse," she began, borrowing the diction of her brother's Latin grammar, "do you know the way out of this pool? I am very tired of swimming about here, O Mouse" — for she had read that this was the correct form of address, and had never once been contradicted on the point by anybody who mattered.
sentences.zh: "老鼠啊，"她开口了，措辞 borrowed 自哥哥的拉丁语法书，"你知道怎么游出这个池子吗？在这儿划来划去我实在累了，老鼠啊。"——因为她读到过，这才是标准的称呼格式，而这一点，从来没有哪个要紧的人反驳过她。

sentences.en: The Mouse said nothing, but looked at her uneasily, and only later, in cool retrospect, did Alice understand how rude that opening must have sounded; and the Mouse, whose history was indeed long and sad, gave her one more chance before going away — which was, of mice, a very generous decision.
sentences.zh: 老鼠没作声，只是不安地看了她一眼；很久之后冷静回想，爱丽丝才明白那个开场白听上去有多失礼；而这只老鼠——它的经历确实又长又惨——决定再给她一次机会，之后再走不迟；以老鼠的规矩，这算得上宽宏大量了。

sentences.en: "Mine is a long and a sad tale," said the Mouse with a sigh, "and it is the driest thing I know, which is exactly what you want, being so wet."
sentences.zh: "我的故事（tale）又长又惨，"老鼠叹了口气说，"也是我知道的最干巴巴的东西——你们湿成这样，正需要它。"

sentences.en: "A sad tail?" said Alice, looking at the Mouse's tail with great wonder; "it is certainly a long one, but I should call it wet rather than sad, and curly rather than either" — and the Mouse, whose patience was already a thin coat in the rain, explained rather coldly that it had meant its history, not its tail.
sentences.zh: "惨的尾巴（tail）？"爱丽丝好奇地盯着老鼠的尾巴说，"它确实挺长，可我觉得它湿乎乎的，不算惨——要说卷，倒还沾点边。"——老鼠的耐心本就薄得像雨里的一层外套，它冷冷地解释：自己说的是经历，不是尾巴。

sentences.en: Alice hurried to divert the conversation to safer ground, and the safest ground she could find in her whole stock of knowledge was her cat Dinah, a wonderful mouse-catching creature; and at the name of Dinah the whole pool seemed to stiffen, as if the water itself had heard of cats, and Dinah had never in her life been so influential.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝赶紧把话题引到更安全的地方去，而她全部学问里最保险的话题，就是她的猫黛娜——一只抓老鼠的好手；"黛娜"两个字一出口，整池水仿佛都僵住了，好像连水都听说过猫的厉害；黛娜这辈子，还从没这么有过影响力。

sentences.en: "Let us get to the shore," said the Mouse, rising in the water with a shiver that converted its fur into a wet flag, "and there I will tell you my story, and you will understand things" — and Alice, apologizing in every direction at once, swam after it as fast as she could.
sentences.zh: "咱们上岸吧，"老鼠从水里立起身，抖得皮毛成了一面湿旗，"到岸上我把故事讲给你听，你就明白一些事了"——爱丽丝朝着四面八方同时道歉，拼尽全力跟在它后面游。

sentences.en: When she stood up in the pool, Alice saw her own doing clearly for the first time: she had converted a private sorrow into a public sea, and the hall had undergone a complete transformation, from a place where she had sat alone into a place where everybody else was obliged to swim.
sentences.zh: 站在池子里，爱丽丝头一回看清了自己的所作所为：她把一场私人的伤心，转换成了一片公共的海；这间大厅也经历了彻底的变形——从她一个人坐着的地方，变成了所有人都不得不游泳的地方。

sentences.en: On the bank stood a crowd of unhappy creatures, dripping — a duck, a dodo, an eaglet, a lory, and several others whose names Alice did not catch — and they were uniform only in being wet through, and uniform, which is a kind of politeness among strangers, in saying nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 岸上站着一大群湿淋淋的可怜动物——鸭子、渡渡鸟、小鹰、小鹦鹉，还有些名字爱丽丝没听清的——它们唯一一致的地方，就是个个浑身湿透；它们对这一点也一律只字不提——在陌生动物中间，这算是一种礼貌。

sentences.en: They looked at one another and shivered, and the dodo, who seemed to be the wisest and was, at least, the roundest, remarked at last that the best thing to get them dry would be a Caucus-race, and the Mouse, in the formal way of mice, suggested first its history, the dodo's idea being the only one put forward with the advantage of motion.
sentences.zh: 它们面面相觑，抖个不停；看起来最智慧、至少最圆的渡渡鸟最后发话：要把大家弄干，最好的办法是来一场会议式赛跑；老鼠则按老鼠们一本正经的规矩，先提议讲讲自己的经历——结果被全体谢绝了；渡渡鸟的主意，是全场唯一自带运动量的一条。

sentences.en: Alice promised, in her politest manner, to listen to the Mouse's history once they were dry, though privately she was more interested in the strange animals, who stood about like a wet audience that has not been told whether it is a congregation or a jury, and she could not settle which either.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝以她最礼貌的方式许诺：等大家干了，一定专心听老鼠的经历；尽管私底下，她更感兴趣的是这群奇怪的动物——它们站在那儿，像一群没弄清自己是来听道的还是来当陪审的湿淋淋的听众；而这两样究竟哪一样，她也定不下来。

sentences.en: And so they stood on the bank, wet and solemn, the tears of one little girl, grown enormous and then shed, now lapping at all their feet — a fact which nobody chose to mention, because the girl who had done the crying was the only one offering to organize the drying, and had already begun, in her head, to do it.
sentences.zh: 于是它们站在岸上，湿着，庄重着；一个小姑娘的眼泪——先长得巨大、再一涌而出——此刻正轻轻拍打着所有人的脚背；这件事谁也不肯提，因为那个哭出这场水的姑娘，偏偏是唯一一个站出来张罗烘干的——而且她已经在心里张罗起来了。

questions.q: What caused the pool that Alice swam in?
options: The white rabbit's spilled tea.
The tears of the giant Alice herself.
Rain falling through the ceiling.
The river rising into the hole.
questions.explain: 第1句写她还巨大时"her tears were enormous too"，四英寸深的水很快积满大厅，第2句更点明"too late to avert a flood of her own making"——是她自己哭出来的洪水。

questions.q: What mistake does Alice make about the Mouse's "sad tale"?
options: She thinks the Mouse is lying about it.
She hears "tail" and looks at the Mouse's tail instead.
She believes the tale is far too short.
She thinks it belongs to the dodo.
questions.explain: 第6句老鼠说的是 tale（故事），第7句爱丽丝却去端详它的 tail（尾巴）说"it is certainly a long one, but I should call it wet rather than sad"——tale 与 tail 同音，她听岔了。

questions.q: What happened when Alice mentioned the name Dinah?
options: The animals cheered for the cat.
The whole pool seemed to stiffen, as if the water had heard of cats.
The dodo proposed the race at once.
The Mouse swam away without a word.
questions.explain: 第8句 "at the name of Dinah the whole pool seemed to stiffen, as if the water itself had heard of cats"——在老鼠面前夸猫，全场都僵住了。

questions.q: Standing up in the pool, Alice "saw her own doing clearly for the first time". What did she realize?
options: That her private sorrow had become a public sea that others were forced to swim in.
That the pool was secretly fed by the river.
That the animals had brought the water in buckets.
That she was still growing larger.
questions.explain: 第10句 "she had converted a private sorrow into a public sea"——她把一己的伤心变成了所有人的麻烦，由第14句"眼泪正拍打所有动物的脚背"可印证。

questions.q: With vert meaning to turn, what does "avert" mean in "too late to avert a flood"?
options: To turn aside or prevent something from happening.
To swim quickly through deep water.
To cry louder than before.
To measure a pool mathematically.
questions.explain: 第2句 "it was already too late to avert a flood of her own making"——avert（a 离开 + vert 转）指把事情转开、防止它发生；她已来不及阻止这场自己哭出来的洪水。

title: 《爱丽丝掉进的洞》· 没有终点的赛跑

sentences.en: "What is a Caucus-race?" asked Alice, and the dodo answered that the best way to explain it was to do it, for talking, in its long experience, never informed anybody of anything that could be learned by running; and as the party was wet, and the afternoon long, nobody contradicted this proposition.
sentences.zh: "什么是会议式赛跑？"爱丽丝问。渡渡鸟回答：最好的解释办法就是跑一遍——依它多年的经验，凡是跑步能学会的事，光靠说是从来教不会任何人的；大家又湿着，午后又长，于是没有人反驳这个提议。

sentences.en: The dodo marked out a course in a rough circle — the exact shape, it said, not mattering — and there was no starting and no finishing post, and the party was placed here and there, and ran when it liked and stopped when it liked, all of which was understood by everybody except the one runner who won, there being no such runner.
sentences.zh: 渡渡鸟圈出一条大致圆形的跑道——它说，形状准不准无所谓；没有起点，也没有终点；大家东一个西一个站好，想跑就跑，想停就停——这一切人人都懂，唯独那个跑赢了的例外；因为压根没有这么一位。

sentences.en: They ran for half an hour or so, by the end of which everybody was quite dry, and the dodo called out, "The race is over!" — and every bird and beast sat down at once, panting, and asked who had won, a question the dodo had been preparing itself to receive for the full half hour, the whole half hour having been one long rehearsal.
sentences.zh: 他们跑了半个小时左右，跑到最后人人都干了；渡渡鸟喊道："赛跑结束！"——于是飞禽走兽一齐坐下来喘气，齐声问：谁赢了？这个问题，渡渡鸟整半小时都在备着答案，专等人来问——那整整半小时，本来就是一场漫长的排练。

sentences.en: "But who has won?" asked Alice, who had a plain mind and expected a plain answer; the dodo thought long, with its eyes closed, and then said that everybody had won, and all must have prizes — a verdict which nobody contradicted, chiefly because nobody could tell what it would mean.
sentences.zh: "可到底谁赢了呢？"爱丽丝问——她是个直心眼，盼着一句直话；渡渡鸟闭上眼睛想了很久很久，然后宣布：人人都赢了，人人都要有奖品。这个裁决没有人反驳，主要是因为谁也说不清它究竟是什么意思。
