sentences.en: "Who is to give the prizes?" was the next question, and it was decided at once that Alice must, and she had a box of sweets in her pocket, just enough to go round, though by what formula each flavour found its runner, not even the dodo could say.
sentences.zh: 下一个问题是："奖品由谁来发？"大家当场议定：非爱丽丝莫属。她口袋里正好有一盒糖果，分一圈不多不少；至于按什么章法让每种口味找到自己的主人，连渡渡鸟也说不清。

sentences.en: The sweets were handed round and eaten, some before the ceremony was over, and then, finding herself the only one without a prize, Alice received her own thimble back from the dodo with great formality, and as solemnly as she could manage, while the animals cheered — the thimble being, by weight, the least prize and, by ceremony, the greatest.
sentences.zh: 糖果挨个分下去，有些没等仪式结束就进了肚；随后大家发现只剩爱丽丝一人没有奖品，渡渡鸟便郑重其事地把她自己先前交出去的顶针颁还给她；她竭尽全力庄严地收下，动物们一片欢呼——这枚顶针，论分量是全场最轻的奖品，论仪式，却是分量最重的一枚。

sentences.en: The Mouse then offered to tell its long history — the history that had once been a tale and once a tail — but one by one the animals drifted away, like notes leaving a page of music, and no story was begun, and no story, in that company, ever would be.
sentences.zh: 老鼠接着提议讲它长长的经历——就是那桩一会儿是"故事"、一会儿是"尾巴"的经历——可动物们一个个散了，像音符从乐谱上飘走；故事终究没有开场，而且在这群听众中间，永远也开不了场。

sentences.en: Alice stayed to listen, first out of politeness and then out of a real sadness; but the Mouse's voice came from farther and farther off, as if told from the bottom of the pool, which by now was only a memory of water, warm and salt and going nowhere.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝留下来想听，先是出于礼貌，后来是当真难过；可老鼠的声音越来越远，像是从池底讲出来的——而那池子，到这时也只剩一段关于水的回忆了：温的，咸的，哪儿也去不了。

sentences.en: The hall grew dim, and the crowd of creatures faded like wet paper held up to the light, their colours running together, until only their voices remained, and then not even those; and Alice, alone in the dimness, understood that something enormous and gentle was closing over the whole afternoon.
sentences.zh: 大厅暗了下来，那群动物像对着光举起的湿纸一样褪去，颜色一层层洇开，先是只剩下声音，最后连声音也没有了；爱丽丝独自站在昏暗里，明白有什么巨大而温柔的东西，正轻轻合拢，罩住这一整个下午。

sentences.en: "You are only a dream," she told them, or perhaps told herself, "and maybe I am somebody's dream too; who can predict where a dream begins, or whose sleeping head it is walking about in?" — and this thought, which should have frightened her, struck her instead as a great and curious mercy.
sentences.zh: "你们只是一场梦，"她对它们说，也许是对自己说，"说不定我也是别人梦里的东西；谁能预言一场梦从哪儿开头，又走在谁的睡着的脑袋里呢？"——这个念头本该吓着她，落在她心上，反倒成了一种巨大而奇妙的慈悲。

sentences.en: In one last transformation, the water became grass, the grass became a river bank, the bank held her sister, reading on exactly as before, and the warm afternoon, with all its creatures folded inside it, was handed back to Alice as a single sentence: "I have had such a curious dream."
sentences.zh: 在最后一次变化里，池水变成了草地，草地变成了河岸，河岸上坐着她的姐姐，正同从前一样读着书；那个暖洋洋的下午，连同叠在里面的所有动物，被一并交还给爱丽丝，收成一句话："我做了一个好奇怪的梦。"

sentences.en: She described the metamorphosis, the tears, and the race that everybody won, and her sister, who could see none of it, listened kindly, and smoothed her hair, and said that she would wake tomorrow and remember it — which was true — and that it would all be gone — which was not entirely so.
sentences.zh: 她讲了自己的变形、那些眼泪，还有那场人人都赢的赛跑；姐姐什么也看不见，却和气地听着，抚着她的头发，说：明天一早醒来，你还会记得它——这半句是真的；又说：到时候这一切就都不见了——这半句，倒不见得。

sentences.en: But her sister, sitting on in the warm dusk, kept her eyes on the river, and half believed, for a minute, that she heard the tiny clatter of the Caucus-race far off, and the faint treble of a rabbit asking the time — that other universe, with its formalities and its verdicts, lying very near to this one, and only one sleep away.
sentences.zh: 可她的姐姐在暖融融的暮色里坐下去，眼睛望着河面，有一分钟竟半信半疑：她听见远处传来会议式赛跑细细的哒哒声，还有一只兔子尖细的嗓音在报时——那个另外的宇宙，连同它的一套礼数和裁决，就躺在这一个的近旁，中间只隔一场睡眠。

sentences.en: For a sister who has been told the whole of a dream will dream the edges of it herself; and the grass rustled, and the pool — that there was no pool — and the bank was quiet, and the book, patient to the last, waited without pictures and without conversations for somebody to begin it again.
sentences.zh: 因为一个听完了整个梦的姐姐，自己也会梦到梦的边角；草在沙沙响，池水——本没有池水——岸上安安静静；那本书耐心到了极点，依旧没有插图、没有对话，等着有谁再来翻开第一页。

questions.q: How did the dodo explain what a Caucus-race was?
options: By drawing the course on paper.
By making everybody simply run it, since talking never informed anybody.
By reciting a long list of rules.
By dictating a formal speech about running.
questions.explain: 第1句渡渡鸟说 "the best way to explain it was to do it, for talking... never informed anybody of anything that could be learned by running"——最好的解释就是跑一遍。

questions.q: What was the verdict of the Caucus-race?
options: The dodo alone had won.
Nobody had really won at all.
Everybody had won, and all must have prizes.
The race would have to be run again.
questions.explain: 第4句 "everybody had won, and all must have prizes — a verdict which nobody contradicted"，人人有奖的裁决无人反驳——因为谁也说不清它什么意思。

questions.q: What prize did Alice herself receive?
options: A sweet from her own pocket.
A medal made by the dodo.
Nothing at all, like the Mouse.
Her own thimble, handed back with great formality.
questions.explain: 第6句 "finding herself the only one without a prize, Alice received her own thimble back from the dodo with great formality"——她把自己交出去的顶针，被郑重其事地颁还给了她。

questions.q: At the end, the sister keeps her eyes on the river and half believes she hears the race. What does this suggest?
options: That she is planning to follow the rabbit herself tomorrow.
That the dream world lies very close to the ordinary one, separated only by a sleep.
That Alice has not really woken up yet.
That the sister will write the story down for a book.
questions.explain: 第13句她"半信半疑"地听见了赛跑声和兔子报时，说那个另外的宇宙"lying very near to this one, and only one sleep away"——可知在卡罗尔笔下，那个奇幻世界离平常的世界只隔一场睡眠。

questions.q: With dict meaning to say, what is a "verdict" in sentence 4?
options: A kind of race run in a circle.
A formal statement or decision that something is so — here, the dodo's ruling that all had won.
A box of sweets shared among runners.
A prize given to the fastest animal.
questions.explain: 第4句 "a verdict which nobody contradicted, chiefly because nobody could tell what it would mean"——verdict（ver 真实 + dict 说）指郑重宣布的决定、裁决，即渡渡鸟"人人皆赢、人人有奖"的裁定。

title: 《贝克街的暗号》· 委托人的来信

sentences.en: In the second week of November, as the fog settled thick upon Baker Street and turned the lamps into moons, a letter slid beneath our door and changed the shape of the whole winter; Holmes passed it over to me without a word, and I saw a thick envelope, a small and careful hand, an exact description of the sender's address, and, at the very end, a postscript crossed through twice, as if the writer had fought with it and won only on points.
sentences.zh: 十一月的第二个星期，浓雾沉甸甸压在贝克街上，把一盏盏路灯泡成了一个个月亮；一封信从我们的门底下滑了进来，改变了整个冬天的形状；福尔摩斯一言不发把信推给我：厚厚的信封，工整小心的小字，寄信人地址写得一丝不苟，末尾还有一条附言，被划掉又重写过两回，像写信人跟它搏斗了一场，只勉强赢了点数。

sentences.en: "Miss Violet Marsh of Hartfield," Holmes read aloud, "writes to submit a problem which the police, she has been told, would dismiss as a daughter's fancy" — and he looked up, with the letter balanced on one finger, and remarked that in his experience the cases which open with an apology rarely deserve one.
sentences.zh: "哈特菲尔德的维奥莱特·马什小姐，"福尔摩斯念道，"提交一个问题；别人告诉她，警察会把这种事当作女儿的胡思乱想而不予理会。"——他把信在一根手指上掂了掂，抬起头说，依他的经验，开头先道歉的案子，反倒很少真配得上一句道歉。

sentences.en: Her father, she wrote, had sailed for Buenos Aires fourteen months before, leaving her to the care of her uncle, Mr. Silas Crane; since that day his letters had arrived on the first Monday of every month without fail, punctual as a bill, and no daughter could have wished for a more regular correspondent.
sentences.zh: 她写道，父亲十四个月前驶往布宜诺斯艾利斯，把她托给叔叔西拉斯·克莱恩照管；从那天起，父亲的信每月第一个星期一准时到，从无例外，准得像一张账单——天下再没有哪个女儿，能指望一位比这更守时的写信人了。

sentences.en: "Every one is in my father's hand, and yet the diction is not his; he never called me 'child' in his life, and he never wrote a letter in his life that said less than a page."
sentences.zh: "每一封信都是我父亲的笔迹，可措辞不像他；他这辈子从没叫过我'孩子'，也从没写過一张不足一整页的信。"

sentences.en: She enclosed an old note of his, written three years before, "so that you may compare the script for yourself" — My dear Violet, the roses against the south wall want pruning; I shall do it on Friday, and we shall have honey for tea — and she enclosed, too, the newest letter from Buenos Aires, dated the first of this month: My dear child, I am well. The roses against the south wall want pruning; I shall do it on Friday, and we shall have honey for tea.
sentences.zh: 她随信附上父亲三年前的一张便条，"好让您亲自比对笔迹"——亲爱的维奥莱特，南墙下的玫瑰该修剪了；我周五来弄，咱们喝茶时配蜂蜜——她还附上了本月一日寄自布宜诺斯艾利斯的新信：亲爱的孩子，我很好。南墙下的玫瑰该修剪了；我周五来弄，咱们喝茶时配蜂蜜。

sentences.en: "There is your whole case in two pieces of paper," said Holmes, laying them side by side; "a gardener who has not changed his roses, his Fridays or his honey for three years, and a father who has, in fourteen months, stopped saying anything that a man says to a daughter."
sentences.zh: "两页纸，你整个案子就都在里头了，"福尔摩斯说着，把两页并排摆开；"一个三年没换过玫瑰、没换过周五、没换过蜂蜜的园丁，加上一位十四个月里不再说任何一句父亲会对女儿说的话的父亲。"

sentences.en: The postscript, added in a suddenly smaller hand, read: P.S. — Do not send your reply to Hartfield; I am never alone. Address it to the post office at Blackheath — and Holmes read that line four times, which, for him, was applause.
sentences.zh: 附言的字忽然小了下来，写的是：又及——回信请勿寄到哈特菲尔德；我身边从没有一个人的时候。请寄到布莱克希斯邮局——这一行福尔摩斯来来回回读了四遍；对他来说，这就算是鼓掌了。

sentences.en: "Look at the envelope," he said at last, holding it to the lamp; "the letter claims to have crossed the world, and the postmark tells us it was transmitted no farther than the London SE district; a lie in the writing is bad, Watson, but a lie in the postmark is a confession written by somebody else."
sentences.zh: "看信封，"他终于开口，把信封举到灯前；"信里自称跨越了半个地球，邮戳却说它传递的距离没有超出伦敦东南区；写在信里的是谎，固然糟糕，华生，可邮戳上的谎，是别人替你招认的。"

sentences.en: He laid the two manuscripts side by side and studied them for a long while, tracing the same sentence as it appeared in both, word for word, three years apart; his fingers moved along the lines like a blind man reading a face, and I knew better than to interrupt an inspection that was going well.
sentences.zh: 他把两份手稿并排摆开，端详了许久，用指尖沿着那个在两页纸上、相隔三年、一字不差反复出现的句子慢慢移动；他的手指顺着字行走，像盲人读一张脸；我也懂事了，绝不打断一场进行顺利的检查。

sentences.en: "It is a capital mistake to theorize before one has all the evidence," said he; "I begin by suspecting everything and dismissing nothing, and the first thing I suspect, in this case, is that a man who copies himself is either very careful or not free — and the careful ones, as a rule, do not need an apology in the postscript."
sentences.zh: "证据没有齐就推理，是致命的错误，"他说；"我的做法是先怀疑一切，不轻易排除任何可能；而本案里我头一个怀疑的就是：一个照抄自己旧句的人，要么格外仔细，要么身不由己——照规矩说，格外仔细的人，是用不着在附言里道歉的。"

sentences.en: I asked him what he made of the suddenly smaller hand; "a smaller hand," said he, "is a hand trying to be quiet in its own house; lean over a man while he writes, Watson, and you may watch his letters shrink — our correspondent, I begin to suspect, dictates to nobody, and is dictated to."
sentences.zh: 我问他怎么看那笔忽然变小的字；"变小的字，"他说，"是一只想在自家房子里放轻动静的手；华生，你俯身看一个人写字试试，你能亲眼看着他的字母缩下去——我开始怀疑，我们的这位来信人从不向别人口授什么，倒是被人天天口授着。"

sentences.en: "Write to Blackheath, then," he said, taking up his pen, "and ask Miss Marsh to bring every letter she has, and to come up tomorrow, if she can leave the house without being followed; ask her, too, to describe the road from her gate to the station, and not to spare the details."
sentences.zh: "那就写信到布莱克希斯，"他拿起笔来，"请马什小姐带上她所有的信，明天来一趟伦敦——前提是，她能在不被跟踪的情况下离开那座房子；另外，请她把从家门前到车站的那段路描述一遍，细节千万不要省。"

sentences.en: "And why the road, Holmes?" I asked; "because," he answered, "a man who watches a house soon forgets that a road remembers him; I have committed very few errors by trusting the ground against the people who walk on it."
sentences.zh: "为什么要问那条路，福尔摩斯？"我问；"因为，"他答道，"盯梢一座房子的人，很快就会忘记：路是记得他的；把宝押在路这边、跟走在路上的人作对，我这一辈子，几乎没栽过跟头。"

sentences.en: That night I wrote the letter at his dictation, sealed it, and carried it myself through the fog to the pillar-box at the corner; the fog took my breath and the letter took my ease, and I walked home with the plain feeling that a frightened girl had submitted to us a case that would cost somebody dear.
sentences.zh: 当夜，我按他的口授写好信，封上，亲自揣着它穿过浓雾，投进街角的邮筒；雾收走了我的呼吸，那封信收走了我的安宁；我往回走的路上，心里只有一个明明白白的预感：一个吓坏了的姑娘提交到我们手里的这桩案子，是要有人付出高昂代价的。

questions.q: What two documents did Violet Marsh enclose with her letter?
options: A photograph and a train timetable.
An old note of her father's and his newest letter from Buenos Aires.
A map of Hartfield and an unpaid bill.
Two letters written by her uncle Crane.
questions.explain: 第5句她附上父亲三年前的便条"so that you may compare the script for yourself"，又附上本月一日的新信——玫瑰那句一字不差地出现在两页纸上。

questions.q: What did the postmark on the envelope reveal to Holmes?
options: The letter had truly come from Buenos Aires.
It had been posted no farther away than the London SE district.
It had been sent by the uncle himself.
It was older than Violet had claimed.
questions.explain: 第8句 "the postmark tells us it was transmitted no farther than the London SE district"——信自称跨越世界，邮戳却招认它只走过了伦敦东南区。

questions.q: What did Holmes suspect about a man who copies his own old sentences?
options: That he is very careful and nothing more.
That he is either very careful or not free to write his own mind.
That he is lazy rather than watched.
That he has forgotten how to read.
questions.explain: 第10句 "a man who copies himself is either very careful or not free — and the careful ones, as a rule, do not need an apology in the postscript"——照抄自己的人，要么格外仔细，要么身不由己，而附言里的恐惧指向后者。

questions.q: What did Holmes mean by "a lie in the postmark is a confession written by somebody else"?
options: The sender had written the wrong address on purpose.
The claim of Buenos Aires was undone by an official mark the writer could not control.
The post office had opened and resealed the letter.
Postmarks are always printed upside down in November.
questions.explain: 第8句：写信人可以在信里撒谎，但邮戳不由他掌控——它诚实地记录了"no farther than the London SE district"，等于邮局替真相作了证；由此可推断信根本没出过伦敦。

questions.q: With dict meaning to say or speak, what does "diction" refer to in Violet's phrase "the diction is not his"?
options: Her father's handwriting and signature.
The choice and style of the words used — the way the letters sound on paper.
The date at the top of each letter.
The colour of the ink and paper.
questions.explain: 第4句 "Every one is in my father's hand, and yet the diction is not his; he never called me 'child'"——diction（dict 说 + ion）指措辞、用词风格：笔迹是父亲的，话却不像他说的。

title: 《贝克街的暗号》· 观察的艺术

sentences.en: Violet Marsh arrived on the morning train: a pale girl of nineteen, with a canvas bag of letters and the steady voice of somebody who has rehearsed being calm in front of a mirror; she submitted the letters at once, arranged in order by month, and her gloves were thinner than the day, and her knuckles white about the bag, which was the day's honest colour.
sentences.zh: 维奥莱特·马什乘早班火车到了：十九岁的姑娘，脸色苍白，拎着一帆布袋信，说话声音平稳，像对着镜子把"镇定"排练过许多遍的人；她当场把信交了上来，按月份排得整整齐齐；她的手套，比这个天气该穿的还单薄，攥着帆布袋的指节发白——这才是这个日子诚实的颜色。

sentences.en: Holmes asked her first, not about the letters, but about her walk from the station; she replied, a little surprised, that she had come by the road, as the morning was fine, and that she had seen nothing out of the common on the way.
sentences.zh: 福尔摩斯开口头一个问题不问信，倒问她从车站怎么走过来的；她有点意外，答说今早天气好，是顺着大路来的，一路上没见任何反常的事。

sentences.en: "You omitted the river path," said Holmes quietly, "and your boots have permitted no argument about it: there is green glass dust on each heel, and none of the road's yellow clay; glass dust, Miss Marsh, is not a common crop on a public highway."
sentences.zh: "你省略了河边那条纤道，"福尔摩斯轻声说，"可你的靴子不留任何争辩的余地：两只鞋跟上都沾着绿玻璃粉，却没有大路的黄泥；玻璃粉这种东西，马什小姐，可不是大路上寻常的收成。"

sentences.en: She held his gaze for a moment, and then admitted it, in a low voice, like a confession committed under a doctor's lamp: twice, by night, she had followed her uncle's cart along the towpath, and both times it had stopped at the gate of the old Marsh bottle-works.
sentences.zh: 她盯着他看了一瞬，随即低声承认了，像在医生灯下招认的一桩事：她夜里两次沿着纤道跟踪叔叔的马车，两次都眼看着它停在旧马什玻璃厂的大门口。

sentences.en: The works had been shut and locked since her father sailed, she said; yet she had seen lamplight moving in the upper story — not steady, but intermittent, as of somebody pacing the floor with a lamp in hand, in a building where nobody was supposed to be living at all, and to which no neighbour would ever have let her admit a doubt.
sentences.zh: 她说，玻璃厂自父亲出海那天起就上锁封闭了；可她看见顶楼里有灯光移动——不是长明的，而是一阵一阵的，像有人提着灯在屋里踱步——在一座本不该住人的厂房里，一座她连向邻居吐半个字的怀疑、都没人肯让她吐的厂房里。

sentences.en: Holmes examined the fourteen letters next, one by one, with circumspect patience, laying each specimen in a row across the table like a biologist with pinned moths; and I confess that, to me, the letters continued to look exactly like letters, which I did not say aloud.
sentences.zh: 接着福尔摩斯逐封检查那十四封信，耐心而谨慎，像生物学家钉蝴蝶标本似的，把每件样品在桌上排成一行；我承认，在我看来，这些信依旧活脱脱就是信——这话我没敢说出口。

sentences.en: "Every line is your father's hand," he said at last, "and that is the most terrible aspect of the case; no forger wrote these, Miss Marsh — your father wrote them himself, every one, and the question is no longer who held the pen, but under what conditions a man copies his own roses."
sentences.zh: "每一行都是你父亲的笔迹，"他最后说，"而这正是本案最可怕的一个方面：没有伪造者写过这些信，马什小姐——每一封都是你父亲亲手写的；现在的问题已不再是"谁执的笔"，而是"一个人在什么境况下，才会照抄自己的玫瑰"。"

sentences.en: "Fourteen letters from a sea voyage," he went on, turning to me, "and in none of them does he mention the sea; what a writer omits, Watson, is often louder than what he says, and your omission, in a letter, is a sentence written in invisible ink."
sentences.zh: "横渡大洋写来的十四封信，"他转向我接着说，"竟没有一封提到过海；作者省略掉的东西，华生，常常比他说出来的更响；一封信里的省略，是用隐形墨水写下的一句话。"

sentences.en: "Each letter is a patchwork of sentences lifted from his older ones — the same roses, the same Friday, the same honey — stitched together for a man who can copy but is no longer permitted to compose; you cannot dictate a man's mind, Watson, but you can dictate his paper, and somebody has been dictating this paper for fourteen months, in a hand that never once shakes, which is its own horror."
sentences.zh: "每封信都是从旧信里摘句子缝出来的活计——同样的玫瑰、同样的周五、同样的蜂蜜——缝给一个还会照抄、却已不被允许创作的人；一个人的心思你口授不了，华生，可他的纸你口授得了；十四个月来，这张纸一直有人在一句一句地口授——而且笔下没有一次发抖，这本身就是一种恐怖。"

sentences.en: I confessed that I had been only a spectator to his reasoning: to me the letters had looked like letters, the boots like boots, and the whole case like a family disagreeing by post; and I said so, with the freedom of an old friendship.
sentences.zh: 我承认，在他的推理面前我一直只是个旁观者：在我看来，信就是信，靴子就是靴子，整桩案子不过是一家人隔着邮政在闹别扭；凭着老交情的分上，我照实说了。

sentences.en: "Any spectator can read what is written, Watson," said he; "the silent half of a thing is what repays inspection — the green dust on a heel, the word a frightened man is not permitted to write, the letter that claims to cross the world and never leaves the county."
sentences.zh: "任何旁观者都读得出写下来的东西，华生，"他说；"值得下功夫检查的，是每样东西沉默的那一半——鞋跟上一点绿粉，一个吓坏了的人不被允许写出的那个词，一封自称跨越了世界、却从没出过郡界的信。"

sentences.en: He sent Violet back by the afternoon train with a promise and one instruction — to say nothing at Hartfield, and to permit no change in her habits — and she submitted to both with the docility of somebody who has carried fear so long that it has become a posture, like a soldier's shoulders at the end of a long war.
sentences.zh: 他让维奥莱特乘午后的火车回去，给了她一个承诺，外加一条嘱咐——在哈特菲尔德什么都不要说，日常习惯也不要有半点改动；她两样都顺从地应下了，那副温顺，是一个把恐惧背得太久、背成了姿势的人的温顺——像一个久经沙场的老兵那副卸不下来的肩膀。

sentences.en: Then he scribbled a note to the chemist of the district asking one question only: who had lately bought laudanum in quantity; the description of the buyer, he said, would tell us more than any interview, for a man who drugs another man buys his medicine from somebody who remembers faces.
sentences.zh: 随后他潦草写下一张便条，寄给本区的药剂师，只问一个问题：近来谁大批买过鸦片酊；他说，买药人的相貌描述，比任何约谈都顶用——因为给人下药的人，总是从记得住脸的人手里买药。

sentences.en: "Tonight," he said, pulling on his coat while the fog pressed at the window like a subscriber to our misfortunes, "Inspector Lestrade and two constables will meet us at the bottle-works; the story of the intermittent lamp must be settled before anybody is warned, and the mission is simple: we go in quiet, and we let the building describe itself."
sentences.zh: "今晚，"他一边穿外套一边说，窗上的浓雾正像个专订我们倒霉消息的订户似的往里挤，"雷斯垂德督察和两名警员会在玻璃厂跟我们碰头；那盏一阵一阵的灯的故事，必须在有人得到风声之前弄清楚；任务很简单：悄悄进去，让那座厂房自己开口描述自己。"

questions.q: What did Violet's boots reveal to Holmes?
options: She had walked the river towpath, not the road.
She had been climbing over the works' fence.
She had recently travelled by sea to London.
She was hiding letters in the heels.
questions.explain: 第3句 "green glass dust on each heel, and none of the road's yellow clay"，她随即承认曾沿纤道夜行至玻璃厂——靴子拆穿了"走大路"的说法。

questions.q: Why did Holmes call the genuine handwriting "the most terrible aspect of the case"?
options: It meant a forger had perfectly copied Marsh's hand.
It meant the letters were not forgeries at all — the father wrote them under someone's control.
It proved that the father was already dead.
It showed that Violet had written them herself.
questions.explain: 第7句 "no forger wrote these... your father wrote them himself"——字迹为真反而最可怕：问题变成"一个人在什么境况下才会照抄自己的玫瑰"，即写信人身不由己。

questions.q: What does Holmes say about a writer's omissions?
options: They are usually simple forgetfulness.
They are often louder than what the writer actually says.
They prove the writer never learned grammar.
They matter only in letters about the weather.
questions.explain: 第8句 "what a writer omits, Watson, is often louder than what he says"——十四封横渡大洋的信竟无一字提到海，这处省略响过一切。

questions.q: What can be inferred about Violet's life at Hartfield from her behaviour in this chapter?
options: She is free to come and go as she pleases.
She lives under constant watching, and has rehearsed calmness to survive it.
She quarrels openly with her uncle every day.
She has already told the police everything.
questions.explain: 第1句她"把镇定排练过许多遍"，第3句她起初瞒下纤道夜行，第12句福尔摩斯叮嘱她"什么都不说、习惯不改动"而她"温顺地应下"——处处可见她活在监视之下，早已学会把恐惧背成姿势。

questions.q: In sentence 3, Holmes says Violet "omitted the river path". With mit meaning to send, what does "omitted" mean here?
options: She sent a letter about the path to the police.
She left it out — failed to mention it in her account of the walk.
She walked along it in the dark without a lamp.
She cleaned the path of glass dust before coming.
questions.explain: 第3句 "You omitted the river path"——omit（o- 向前 + mit 送）即"送出去、漏掉不说"：她的陈述里漏掉了纤道，鞋跟上的绿玻璃粉却替她说了实话。

title: 《贝克街的暗号》· 玻璃厂的灯

sentences.en: By eleven that night we stood in the black shadow of the bottle-works, the Thames breathing cold beside us and Inspector Lestrade's men around the fence; the mission had been laid out by Holmes with three rules only: no lantern, no loud word, and no man to enter the upper room before him.
sentences.zh: 当晚十一点，我们站在玻璃厂的黑色阴影里，泰晤士河在身旁吐着寒气，雷斯垂德督察的人手已围住栅栏；福尔摩斯把这次任务只立了三条规矩：不许点灯，不许高声，任何人不得抢在他前面进顶楼。

sentences.en: Lestrade, who respected Holmes the way a practical man respects a professor, submitted to the rules with visible pain; and for an hour nothing moved at all, except the river, which has never once in its life followed instructions, or apologised for it.
sentences.zh: 雷斯垂德对福尔摩斯的敬重，是实干家对教授的那种敬重；这三条规矩他忍痛服从了；一个钟头里毫无动静，只有河在动——这条河这辈子，还从来没有照过谁的吩咐行事，也从没为这事道过歉。

sentences.en: Then, high in the sealed story, a lamp emitted its pale glow, travelled slowly across the window, went out, and a minute later returned and crossed again; "there is your intermittent signal," whispered Holmes; "somebody carries that lamp on a nightly round, like a keeper who cannot sleep, in a house that locks no treasure and keeps no animal."
sentences.zh: 随后，封闭的顶楼上，一盏灯放出微光，缓缓横过窗口，熄了，一分钟后又回来再横一遍；"这就是你那一阵一阵的信号，"福尔摩斯低声说；"有人每夜提着那盏灯巡一圈，像个睡不着的看守——守着一座既没锁着财宝、也没养着牲口的房子。"

sentences.en: Lestrade wanted to force the door at once, with the honest instincts of a man whose business is arrests; Holmes permitted nothing of the kind — we waited, he said, for the second crossing, since a building, like a witness, contradicts itself most freely when it believes itself unobserved.
sentences.zh: 雷斯垂德想立刻破门，这是以抓人为业的人的老实本能；福尔摩斯却一步不让——他说，我们等它走第二回：一座厂房和一名证人一样，都只在自己以为没人看的时候，才畅所欲言地自相矛盾。

sentences.en: On the second crossing we climbed the stair in silence, boots in one hand, and from behind the upper door came a small dry sound, the scratch of a pen nib, in a building where no one was supposed to be living; it is the most solitary sound I know, and it stopped me in the dark, that night, like a hand laid flat on my chest.
sentences.zh: 等灯走第二回时，我们悄无声息上了楼梯，靴子拎在一只手里；顶楼的门后传来一种细小干涩的声音——笔尖划纸的声音——在一座本不该住人的厂房里；那是我所知道的最孤独的一种声音，那晚在黑暗里，它像一只摊平的手掌，稳稳按住了我的胸口。

sentences.en: Holmes pushed the door, and the light of our dark lanterns fell upon the room: on the desk his own old letters lay spread like school copies, and John Marsh sat writing — a transcript of himself, fingers ink-dark, eyes turned wholly inward, with no window in them for us at all.
sentences.zh: 福尔摩斯推开门，几盏手提灯的光圈落进屋里：书桌上摊着他自己那些旧信，像供人临摹的范本；约翰·马什坐在那里写个不停——成了自己的一份抄本，指头全是墨，目光整个儿转向内里，里面没有一扇留给我们的窗。

sentences.en: He looked up without fear and without interest, as a clerk looks up, and asked: "Is it Friday? I have written about the roses; may I go home now, for honey and tea?" — and the sentence, word for word, was the sentence that had crossed the world from Buenos Aires every month.
sentences.zh: 他抬起头，没有惧色，也没有兴致，像小职员抬头那样，问道："到周五了吗？玫瑰的事我已经写完了；现在可以回家了吗，喝茶配蜂蜜的那种？"——这句话，一字不差，正是每月"跨越半个世界"从布宜诺斯艾利斯寄来的那一句。

sentences.en: On a shelf by the cot stood a bottle of laudanum with a label freshly written out in a physician's hand — a prescription in the name of Dr. Grimesby, Mr. Crane's business partner — and on the desk, beside the ink, a little pile of envelopes already addressed and stamped for the first Monday of next month, the month's work already done.
sentences.zh: 小床边的架子上立着一瓶鸦片酊，标签是新写的医生笔迹——处方署名格里姆斯比医生，克莱恩先生的生意伙伴；书桌上墨水旁，还压着一小摞已经写好地址、贴好邮票、只等下月第一个星期一寄出的信封——那个月的活儿，其实已经干完了。

sentences.en: Then a key turned below, and Mr. Silas Crane came up the stair with a supper tray, stopped dead at the ring of our dark lanterns, and set the tray down very slowly, with the care of a man who has committed his face to the wrong memory.
sentences.zh: 这时楼下钥匙一转，西拉斯·克莱恩先生端着晚餐托盘上了楼梯，在手电灯围成的一圈光里僵住，又极慢极慢地把托盘放下——那份小心，是一个人发现自己这张脸，已经留进了不该留的记忆时的那份小心。

sentences.en: "I have committed no crime," he said at last, and the sentence came out of him like a speech prepared against this exact interruption; "my brother-in-law is gravely ill, everything done for him was prescribed by a physician, and the letters — the letters were his own idea, his own comfort, his own handwriting."
sentences.zh: "我没有犯罪，"他终于开口，这句话从他嘴里出来，像一段专为眼前这场打断背熟了的说辞；"我内弟病得很重，为他做的一切都遵医嘱而行；至于那些信——那些信是他自己的主意，是他自己的安慰，也是他自己的笔迹。"

sentences.en: "Your physician," said Holmes, taking up the bottle and reading the label to the room, "prescribes; your brother-in-law copies; and on the first Monday of every month, somebody posts his copies to Buenos Aires and back — a busy practice, sir, for a sick man."
sentences.zh: "你的医生，"福尔摩斯拿起那只瓶子，对着满屋的人念标签，"负责开方；你的内弟负责照抄；然后每月第一个星期一，有人把这些抄件寄去布宜诺斯艾利斯、再寄回来——先生，对一位病人来说，这可是份够忙的诊所工作。"

sentences.en: Before he finished, a step that had been waiting in the dark of the stair bolted for the water door, and Dr. Grimesby, physician and partner, was taken by the two constables whom Holmes had posted at the river an hour before, ankle-deep in the Thames and subscribing loudly to his own innocence.
sentences.zh: 话音未落，一道在楼梯暗处等候多时的脚步夺路奔向临河的水门；格里姆斯比医生——开方的医生，也是合伙人——被一小时前就被福尔摩斯安插在河边的两名警员按住了，站在没踝的泰晤士河水里，高声认领着自己的清白。

sentences.en: Holmes wrapped John Marsh in his own coat and said, very gently, "Your daughter sent us" — and at the words, for the first time in fourteen months, something surfaced in the man's eyes and sank again, like a fish showing its back; he asked no more about Friday, and put out his hand, and let himself be led.
sentences.zh: 福尔摩斯把自己的大衣裹在约翰·马什身上，极轻地说："是你女儿叫我们来的。"——话音落下，十四个月来头一回，有什么东西在那人的眼睛里浮上来，又沉下去，像一条鱼亮了一下脊背；他没有再问周五的事，伸出手，任人领着走了。

sentences.en: And the lamp in the upper window, which had been permitted to burn its rounds for fourteen months, was permitted at last to go out for good; the works stood dark above the river, and the Thames, which had watched the whole transaction without comment, went on to the sea, carrying, as far as I know, nothing but fog.
sentences.zh: 顶楼窗口那盏被允许烧了十四个月夜巡的灯，终于被允许永远地熄灭了；厂房立在河上，一片漆黑；泰晤士河从头到尾看着这桩交易，一言不发，继续往海里去——据我所知，它带走的，只有雾。

questions.q: What three rules did Holmes set for the night's mission?
options: No lantern, no loud word, and none to enter the upper room before him.
Break in at once, seize the lamp, and wake the neighbours.
Wait for daylight, bring a dog, and ring the bell.
Follow the cart, guard the gate, and question the chemist.
questions.explain: 第1句 "three rules only: no lantern, no loud word, and no man to enter the upper room before him"。

questions.q: What did the pattern of the lamplight suggest about the person upstairs?
options: A whole family was living and working there.
Someone walked a nightly round with a lamp in hand, like a sleepless keeper.
The building was lit by gas from the street.
A signal was being flashed to the far shore.
questions.explain: 第3句灯光缓缓横过窗口、熄灭、又回来，福尔摩斯说"somebody carries that lamp on a nightly round, like a keeper who cannot sleep"。

questions.q: What did the desk and the shelf beside the cot reveal?
options: Forged letters in a stranger's hand, and a bottle of wine.
Old letters spread as copying models, and a laudanum prescription signed by Dr. Grimesby.
Maps of Buenos Aires, and a pistol wrapped in cloth.
Money hidden in an ink pot, and a false key.
questions.explain: 第6句旧信"lay spread like school copies"供临摹；第8句架子上的鸦片酊标签是医生笔迹，处方署名"Dr. Grimesby, Mr. Crane's business partner"。

questions.q: Why does John Marsh ask whether it is Friday and mention the roses?
options: He is mocking his visitors with old jokes.
He has copied his old sentences for so long that he has lost track of time and truth.
He is leaving a coded message for his daughter.
He truly keeps a garden in Buenos Aires.
questions.explain: 第6句他面前摊着自己的旧信当范本，日复一日照抄；第7句他问"Is it Friday? I have written about the roses"——抄得久了，已分不清今夕何夕、真话和抄本。

questions.q: With mit meaning to send and e- meaning out, what does "emitted" describe in sentence 3?
options: The lamp was sent away to another building.
The lamp sent out — gave off — its pale glow.
The lamp was swallowed up by the darkness.
The lamp received light from the street.
questions.explain: 第3句 "a lamp emitted its pale glow, travelled slowly across the window"——emit（e 向外 + mit 送）即向外发出：那盏灯放出微光，缓缓横过窗口。

title: 《贝克街的暗号》· 贝克街的裁决

sentences.en: Three days later, with Mr. Marsh asleep upstairs and a good fire going, Holmes set the whole case out before Lestrade and me, from the first letter to the last lamp, in the order in which he had perceived it — which, he reminded us, is not the order in which he had proved it, and the difference between the two orders is the whole method.
sentences.zh: 三天后，马什先生在楼上睡着，壁炉烧得正旺，福尔摩斯把整桩案子——从第一封信到最后一盏灯——按他察觉的顺序摊给我和雷斯垂德看；他提醒我们，这个顺序跟证明它的顺序并不一样，而两个顺序之间的差别，就是整套方法。

sentences.en: "First the letters: the script was genuine, the diction belonged to nobody, and one sentence about roses appeared in a note three years old and a letter three weeks old, word for word; a sound memory never repeats itself to that degree — a man copies so only when the words are dictated to him, sentence by sentence, from his own past."
sentences.zh: "先说信：笔迹是真的，措辞却不属于任何人；一句关于玫瑰的话，三年前的便条里有，三周前的信里也有，一字不差；健全的记忆不会重复到这个地步——只有当句子被人逐句从他自己的过去里指定下来、叫他照抄时，才会这样。"

sentences.en: "The chemist described the buyer, the envelopes described the journey, and the patient himself described, in fourteen letters, the exact size of his cage; every document in this case was honest, Lestrade — which is precisely why it deceived nobody who read it with respect, and everybody who read it in a hurry."
sentences.zh: "药剂师描述了买药人，信封描述了行程，而那位病人自己，用十四封信描述了他那口笼子的准确尺寸；本案里每一份文件都是诚实的，雷斯垂德——正因如此，凡是怀着敬意细读的人，它一个也骗不了；凡是匆匆一翻的人，它一个也漏不掉。"

sentences.en: "Second, the envelope: every letter claimed Buenos Aires and confessed London — a contradiction posted openly, because nobody thought to look at it; and no forger was ever engaged, which permitted the one piece of evidence a forged hand could never have supplied: a genuine signature written by a genuine prisoner."
sentences.zh: "其次，信封：每封信都自称来自布宜诺斯艾利斯，邮戳却招认了伦敦——一个就贴在外面、却因为没人想到去看而被无视的矛盾；而且从头到尾没请过任何伪造者，这才许可了一件伪造笔迹永远给不出的证据：一个真正的囚徒，签下的真正的笔迹。"

sentences.en: "My prediction was a humble one," he went on: "only that the letters were written in England, by a man not free to write his own mind; the bottle-works followed from Miss Marsh's boots, not from my genius, and the rest — the laudanum, the partnership, the monthly posting — was transmitted to us by the case itself, which always talks, Lestrade, to anybody who permits it."
sentences.zh: "我的预测很谦虚，"他接着说，"不过是"这些信写于英国，写信的人不自由"这么一句；玻璃厂是从马什小姐的靴子上跟下来的，不是我的天才；至于其余的——鸦片酊、合伙人关系、每月一寄——都是案子自己传递给我们的：案子永远在说话，雷斯垂德，只看谁容许它说。"

sentences.en: "Third, the motive: while her father lived abroad, the income of the Marsh estate was Crane's to spend; a living prisoner was safer than a forged signature, for the hand was genuine and the man was not — the design, I confess, is the most economical piece of wickedness I have indicted in twenty years."
sentences.zh: "第三，动机：只要父亲'身在海外'，马什家产业的进项就归克莱恩支配；一个活着的囚徒比伪造的签名安全——字迹是真的，人却不自由；这个设计，恕我直言，是我二十年来起诉过的最省钱的一桩恶行。"

sentences.en: Crane admitted it all before the magistrate next morning: fourteen months of laudanum, of dictated letters, of the monthly walk to a London posting-house with the envelopes; and Dr. Grimesby admitted the prescriptions, which was the only piece of medicine he ever wrote honestly.
sentences.zh: 克莱恩次日在裁判官面前全部供认：十四个月的鸦片酊、照口授抄写的信，以及每月揣着信封走去伦敦代寄点的那么一程路；格里姆斯比医生也供认了那些处方——那是他这辈子唯一诚实写下的一味药。

sentences.en: Mr. Marsh, waking clean of the drug, asked first for his daughter and then for the roses against the south wall; before spring the bed was replanted, and the first Friday pruning was a family ceremony, half of Hartfield attending — the sentence that had been written in captivity becoming, at last, a sentence that was simply true.
sentences.zh: 马什先生药劲褪尽醒来，先要女儿，再要南墙下的那丛玫瑰；开春前花床重新栽好，第一个周五的修剪成了一家人的仪式，半个哈特菲尔德都来了——那句在囚禁中抄了十四个月的话，终于变成了一句单纯为真的话。

sentences.en: Violet Marsh, who had watched the door of the works from a distance on that night, wrote us a letter afterwards which I have kept: she described the fog, the arrest, and the walk home, and in the last line, in the same small careful hand that had first slid beneath our door, she permitted herself one whole page.
sentences.zh: 那晚曾在远处守着玻璃厂大门的维奥莱特·马什，事后给我们写来一封信，我一直留着：她描述了那场雾、那次抓捕和回家的路；最后一行里，用最初从我们门底下滑进来的那笔同样细小工整的字，她许可自己，写了整整一页。

sentences.en: "And yet," said I, "I saw everything you saw — the letters, the boots, the lamp — and I was nowhere near you; you describe a case as a painter describes a landscape, and I can only describe what is standing in front of me."
sentences.zh: "可是，"我说，"你看到的我都看到了——那些信、那双靴子、那盏灯——我却连你的边都没摸着；你描述一桩案子，像画家描述一片风景，而我只会描述站在我眼前的东西。"

sentences.en: "You describe what anybody may see, Watson," he answered; "the rare art is to see what nobody has described, until the silent parts of a thing begin to speak — the word a man is not permitted to write, the dust a road keeps on a heel, the letter that confesses where it was posted."
sentences.zh: "你描述的是人人都看得见的东西，华生，"他答道；"稀罕的本事，是看见没人描述过的东西，直到一件事沉默的部分也开口说话——一个不被允许写下的词，一条路留在鞋跟上的粉，一封自己招认投寄地点的信。"

sentences.en: In retrospect it is that sentence I remember, not the handcuffs; the case is filed in Lestrade's notebooks under a name nobody recognizes, and his manuscript of that winter runs to three pages, of which the second contradicts the first and the third omits the second, as official prose will.
sentences.zh: 如今回想，我记得的是这句话，不是那副手铐；案子在雷斯垂德的笔记本里归在一个没人认得出的名目下，他那个冬天的手稿统共写了三页——第二页跟第一页自相矛盾，第三页又把第二页省略掉了，公文向来如此。

sentences.en: The rest of the story belongs to the newspapers and to the courts, and it is not the part I have kept; what I have kept is the fog, the lamp crossing the window, the scratch of the nib, and the faces of two men who had committed a large crime out of small greed.
sentences.zh: 故事的其余部分归报纸和法庭，不是我心存的那一份；我心存的，是那场雾、那盏横过窗口的灯、那阵笔尖的沙沙声，还有两张脸——两张为了一点小小的贪心，犯下一桩大大的罪的脸。

sentences.en: But in my own pages I transmit it whole, for whoever comes after us — the letter, the postscript, the green glass dust, the fourteen patient copies — so that something of that winter at least was sent on undiminished; and if any young inspector reads this, let him subscribe to the one rule that solved it: read the letter, and then read everything the letter did not say.
sentences.zh: 而在我自己的这些纸页里，我把它完完整整地传下去，给后来看的人——那封信、那条附言、那点绿玻璃粉、那十四个月耐心的抄件——那个冬天，至少有一件事是原封不动送出去的；倘若哪位年轻督察读到这里，就请他认下解决了此案的那条唯一的规矩：把信读一遍，再把信里没说的一切，读一遍。

questions.q: Which clue did Holmes call "a contradiction posted openly"?
options: The copied sentence about roses and honey.
The genuine handwriting of the prisoner.
The envelopes claiming Buenos Aires but postmarked London.
The monthly first-Monday punctuality.
questions.explain: 第4句 "every letter claimed Buenos Aires and confessed London — a contradiction posted openly"，指信封上自称的寄出地与邮戳之间的矛盾。

questions.q: Why did Crane keep John Marsh alive rather than forge his signature?
options: Forging was beyond Crane's ability.
A living prisoner writing in a genuine hand was safer for spending the estate.
Marsh had hidden his will and Crane needed its location.
Murder would have left a body at the works.
questions.explain: 第6句 "a living prisoner was safer than a forged signature, for the hand was genuine and the man was not"——活囚的真笔迹比伪造签名更保险，产业的进项便可放心挥霍。

questions.q: What had Holmes's original "prediction" actually been?
options: That Marsh was dead and all the letters were forgeries.
That the letters were written in England, by a man not free to write his own mind.
That Crane would try to flee by the river.
That Grimesby had once treated the Marsh family.
questions.explain: 第5句 "My prediction was a humble one... only that the letters were written in England, by a man not free to write his own mind"，他还自谦说玻璃厂是从靴子上跟下来的。

questions.q: What can be inferred about Violet from her letter after the rescue?
options: She has left Hartfield for London in anger.
She still writes carefully out of habit, but the full last page shows her fear finally lifting.
She has forgotten the whole affair within a week.
She suspects her father was a willing partner in the plot.
questions.explain: 第9句她写来的信仍是"同样细小工整的字"——长期受监视养成的习惯仍在；但"最后一行，她许可自己写了整整一页"——对照第2章第12句她被叮嘱"什么都不说"的温顺，可推知恐惧正在松开她。

questions.q: With mit meaning to send and trans- meaning across, what does "transmitted" mean in sentence 5?
options: Hidden away where nobody could find it.
Sent across — handed on — from the case to the detectives.
Written down in Latin for the courts.
Stopped before it reached Baker Street.
questions.explain: 第5句 "the rest... was transmitted to us by the case itself, which always talks... to anybody who permits it"——transmit（trans 越过 + mit 传递）即把信息传递过来：线索由案子自己送到侦探手上。

title: 《星星邮递员》· 山路上的包裹

sentences.en: Tomas was a young postman in a small town between two dark mountains, and he loved his morning work more than anything else in the world.
sentences.zh: 托马斯是夹在两座黑山之间的小镇上的年轻邮差，他爱自己的晨间工作胜过世上一切。

sentences.en: Every day he put his letters in a heavy brown bag, closed the door of the little post office, and walked up the long stone road.
sentences.zh: 每天他把信装进沉重的棕色邮包，关上小邮局的门，走上长长的石头山路。

sentences.en: The road was old and narrow and the morning stones were cold, but Tomas knew every turn of it like the lines on his own hand.
sentences.zh: 这条路又老又窄，清晨的石头冰凉，可托马斯熟悉每一个转弯，就像熟悉自己手上的纹路。

sentences.en: Today his bag was light, because it held only one small package with a letter for the astronomy tower at the top.
sentences.zh: 今天他的邮包很轻，因为里面只有一个小包裹，还有一封寄往山顶天文塔的信。

sentences.en: On the label there was a small asterisk next to the name, a little star made of careful black ink.
sentences.zh: 标签上的名字旁边画着一个小星号，是用细心的黑墨水画成的一颗小星星。

sentences.en: An asterisk means the letter is important, his boss told him once, so you must carry it with clean hands and a quiet heart.
sentences.zh: 老板有一次告诉他：星号意味着这封信很重要，所以你要用干净的手和平静的心去送它。

sentences.en: Some people in the town liked astrology, and every week they read their star signs in the thin grey paper by the window.
sentences.zh: 镇上有些人喜欢占星术，每周都坐在窗边，在薄薄的灰报纸上读自己的星座运势。

sentences.en: Tomas did not believe in astrology, because he could not see how the stars could know anything about his own small life.
sentences.zh: 托马斯不信占星术，因为他想不出星星怎么可能知道他那小小的生活。

sentences.en: But he did like the real stars, the quiet stellar lights that came out one by one after the sun went down.
sentences.zh: 但他确实喜欢真正的星星——太阳落山后一颗一颗亮起来的、安静的星光。

sentences.en: There was only one small problem: he could not name one constellation in the night sky, not even the most famous one.
sentences.zh: 只有一个小小的遗憾：夜空里的星座，他一个也叫不出名字，连最有名的那个也不行。

sentences.en: He looked up on many cold nights, but for him the sky was a book with astronomical words and no easy answers in it.
sentences.zh: 许多个寒夜里他都抬头看天，可对他来说，天空是一本满是天文数字、却没有答案的书。

sentences.en: The tower at the top of the road was the town's small observatory, a round white building with a silver door and a quiet bell.
sentences.zh: 山路尽头的那座塔，是小镇自己的小天文台：一座圆的白色建筑，有一扇银色的门和一只安静的铃。

sentences.en: An astronomer named Dr. Vega worked there all year, alone with her hot tea, her thin notebooks and her long black telescope.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫维加博士的天文学家整年都待在那里，陪伴她的只有热茶、薄薄的笔记本和长长的黑色望远镜。

sentences.en: Tomas thought about her as he climbed: did she study asteroids, those big silent rocks that sail far away in the dark?
sentences.zh: 爬山的时候他想起了她：她研究的是不是小行星——那些在黑暗远处默默航行的巨大岩石？

questions.q: What does the small asterisk on the label mean?
options: The letter is important
The road is dangerous
The tower is closed
The star is bright
questions.explain: 第6句 "An asterisk means the letter is important"，老板说过星号代表重要的信。

questions.q: Where does Dr. Vega work?
options: In the post office
In the town school
In the small observatory at the top of the road
In a big city by the sea
questions.explain: 第12句说山顶的塔是小镇的小天文台，第13句 "An astronomer named Dr. Vega worked there all year"，她在那里工作。

questions.q: What does Tomas wonder about Dr. Vega's work?
options: Whether she sells star maps
Whether she studies asteroids far away
Whether she likes the town
Whether she reads the grey paper
questions.explain: 第14句 "did she study asteroids, those big silent rocks that sail far away in the dark?"，他猜测她研究的是遥远的小行星。

questions.q: Why does Tomas not believe in astrology?
options: He cannot read the paper
His boss forbids it
He cannot see how the stars could know about his small life
He only believes in the moon
questions.explain: 第8句 "he could not see how the stars could know anything about his own small life"，这是他自己想通的道理。

questions.q: Asterisk and constellation both come from the old word for star. In the chapter, what does the asterisk on the label look like?
options: A long black line
A little star made of ink
A round silver moon
A small white bird
questions.explain: 第5句 "a little star made of careful black ink"，词根 ast/stell 意为"星"，所以 asterisk（星号）与 constellation（星座）同源。

title: 《星星邮递员》· 天文台的一天

sentences.en: Tomas stood in front of the silver door with the package under his arm, and he raised his free hand, but Dr. Vega opened the door before he could knock.
sentences.zh: 托马斯夹着包裹站在银色的门前，刚抬起空着的那只手，维加博士却在他敲门之前就把门打开了。

sentences.en: She was a quiet astronomer with warm grey eyes, and her old grey cardigan had small holes from many long winter nights on the mountain.
sentences.zh: 她是位安静的天文学家，有一双温和的灰眼睛；她那件旧灰开衫上留着山上许多漫长寒夜磨出的小洞。

sentences.en: Thank you for walking so far up the old road, she said softly, and please come inside, because the wind is sharp on the mountain today.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你沿老路走了这么远，她轻声说，请进来吧，今天山上的风很硬。

sentences.en: The round room held a big black telescope under the great white dome, and the walls were covered with star maps and long tables of numbers.
sentences.zh: 圆形的房间里，巨大的白色穹顶下架着一台黑色大望远镜，墙上贴满了星图和一列列长长的数字表。

sentences.en: As a small child, Dr. Vega wanted to be an astronaut, and she drew white ships on every page of her school books.
sentences.zh: 小时候，维加博士想当一名宇航员，还在课本的每一页上都画过白色的飞船。

sentences.en: Later she chose astronomy instead, because the stars asked better questions than any white ship, and she never once felt sorry about it.
sentences.zh: 后来她转而选择了天文学，因为星星提出的问题比任何白色飞船都更有意思，而且她从未后悔过。

sentences.en: She studied astrophysics, the science of stars and light, and she explained it to Tomas with two cups of hot sweet tea.
sentences.zh: 她研究天体物理学——一门关于恒星与光的学问——并就着两杯热甜茶把它讲给托马斯听。

sentences.en: One day ships may travel on interstellar roads between the stars, she said, and perhaps your grandchildren will buy the first tickets.
sentences.zh: 她说，也许有一天，飞船会行驶在星星之间的星际航道上，说不定你的孙辈会买下第一批船票。

sentences.en: Tomas asked a slow, careful question: could an asteroid ever fall out of the dark sky and hit the earth, like a stone into a cup of water?
sentences.zh: 托马斯慢慢问出一个郑重的问题：会不会有一天，一颗小行星从黑暗的天空坠落，像石子掉进水杯一样撞上地球？

sentences.en: Most asteroids stay far away on their own quiet roads around the sun, she answered with a small smile, so you can sleep well tonight.
sentences.zh: 她微微一笑，回答道：大多数小行星都待在绕太阳的安静轨道上，离得很远，所以你今晚可以安心睡觉。

sentences.en: But the sky keeps astronomical surprises, she added, and that is exactly why somebody must watch it every single night.
sentences.zh: 但她又补充说，天空藏着多得数不清的意外，这正是必须有人每个夜晚都守望它的原因。

sentences.en: Her desk notes were full of small asterisks, like tiny stars lying on thin white paper between the black lines.
sentences.zh: 她桌上的便签里满是小小的星号，像躺在白纸黑行之间的细碎星星。

sentences.en: Each little asterisk marked something important, she said, the way a white stone marks a safe place on a mountain path.
sentences.zh: 她说，每个小星号都标记着要紧的事，就像山路上一块白石子标记着安全落脚的地方。

sentences.en: Tomas forgot the time completely, the tea grew cold in the two cups, and outside the dome the first stellar lights came quietly out, one by one.
sentences.zh: 托马斯全然忘了时间，两杯茶都凉了；穹顶之外，最初的星光一颗接一颗，静静地亮了起来。

questions.q: What did Dr. Vega want to be as a child?
options: A postman
An astronaut
A doctor
A painter
questions.explain: 第5句 "As a small child, Dr. Vega wanted to be an astronaut"，她小时候想当宇航员。

questions.q: What does Dr. Vega say about most asteroids?
options: They stay far away, so we can sleep well
They visit the earth every year
They follow fishing boats
They are made of sweet tea
questions.explain: 第10句 "Most asteroids stay far away on their own quiet roads"，她安慰托马斯说小行星离得很远。

questions.q: What are Dr. Vega's desk notes full of?
options: Long sea stories
Old photos
Small asterisks, like tiny stars
Grey clouds
questions.explain: 第12句 "Her desk notes were full of small asterisks, like tiny stars"，便签上满是像小星星一样的星号。

questions.q: What can we tell about Dr. Vega's feelings toward her work?
options: She regrets her choice every winter
She loves it and never once felt sorry about it
She wants to sell her telescope
She finds the stars boring
questions.explain: 第6句 "she never once felt sorry about it"——结合她讲得入迷、茶都凉了（第14句），可推断她由衷热爱这份工作。

questions.q: What is astrophysics, as Dr. Vega explains it?
options: The science of stars and light
The study of old letters
The art of star signs
The work of a postman
questions.explain: 第7句 "She studied astrophysics, the science of stars and light"，天体物理学是关于恒星和光的学问。

title: 《星星邮递员》· 暴雨与修补

sentences.en: In late autumn a great storm came up from the grey sea, and it fell on the little mountain town like a wet black blanket.
sentences.zh: 深秋，一场大暴雨从灰色的海面上扑来，像一条湿漉漉的黑毯子罩住了这座小小的山镇。

sentences.en: Rain hit the windows of the little post office, and the cold glass shook in its old wooden frame all through the night.
sentences.zh: 雨点砸在小邮局的窗玻璃上，冰凉的玻璃在旧木框里整整响了一夜。

sentences.en: The wind pulled at the roof and tried to take the grey tiles away one by one, like a thief with cold fingers.
sentences.zh: 风撕扯着屋顶，想一片一片揭走灰瓦片，像个手指冰凉的贼。

sentences.en: In the middle of that grey morning, one thin letter fell out of Tomas's open bag into a deep pool of black rainwater.
sentences.zh: 就在那个灰蒙蒙的上午，一封薄薄的信从托马斯敞开的邮包里滑落，掉进了深深的黑色雨水中。

sentences.en: It came from the observatory at the top of the road, and for the small post office it was now a real disaster, the worst day of the year.
sentences.zh: 这封信来自山顶的天文台，对小邮局来说，这是一场真正的灾难，是全年最糟的一天。

sentences.en: Some people in town called it an astronomical storm, the worst in twenty years, but Tomas, who knew nothing of astronomy, only looked at his wet bag.
sentences.zh: 镇上有人把它叫作二十年不遇的天文级暴雨，可对天文学一无所知的托马斯，只是盯着自己湿透的邮包。

sentences.en: The wet ink ran across the paper, and the address turned into a grey cloud that told him nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 受潮的墨水在纸上洇开，地址化成一团灰雾，什么也告诉不了他。

sentences.en: Only a small asterisk in the corner stayed clear and dry, a little star that the water could not wash away.
sentences.zh: 只有角落里那个小星号还清晰干爽，一颗水也冲不掉的小星星。

sentences.en: Tomas knew that mark at once, because it was Dr. Vega's quiet sign, the same little star from her desk notes.
sentences.zh: 托马斯一眼就认出了那个记号：那是维加博士安静的签名，和她便签上的小星星一模一样。

sentences.en: The star-sign readers said the storm was written in the sky by the planets, but their astrology gave Tomas no help at all.
sentences.zh: 看星象的人说这场暴雨是行星写在天上的，可他们的占星术对托马斯一点忙也帮不上。

sentences.en: So he wrapped the wet letter in a dry cloth and climbed the long road while the storm still shouted above him.
sentences.zh: 于是他用干布裹好湿信，在头顶暴雨的咆哮声中爬上了长长的山路。

sentences.en: That night the dark clouds hid every constellation, and no stellar light could be seen through the grey wall of the rain.
sentences.zh: 那天夜里，乌云遮住了每一个星座，隔着雨幕织成的灰墙，看不见一丝星光。

sentences.en: Dr. Vega took the letter with two careful hands and dried the paper slowly, like a careful astronomer at work on a very old and very precious star map.
sentences.zh: 维加博士用两只小心翼翼的手接过信，慢慢烘干那张纸，像一位天文学家在修复一张非常古老、非常珍贵的星图。

sentences.en: A wet letter is a small disaster, not the end, she said, because paper is patient, and astronomers are patient too, and both can wait for the sun.
sentences.zh: 她说，一封淋湿的信只是小小的灾难，不是结束，因为纸有耐心，天文学家也有耐心，两者都等得起太阳。

questions.q: What happens to the letter during the storm?
options: It flies away with the wind
It falls into a pool of rainwater and the ink runs
It becomes a star map
It is burned by lightning
questions.explain: 第4句 "fell out of Tomas's open bag into a deep pool of black rainwater"，第7句 "The wet ink ran across the paper"。

questions.q: Which part of the wet letter stays clear?
options: The address
The stamp
The name of the town
A small asterisk in the corner
questions.explain: 第8句 "Only a small asterisk in the corner stayed clear and dry"，只有角落里的小星号还看得清。

questions.q: Why does Tomas know the asterisk on the wet letter?
options: Because he wrote it himself
Because it is Dr. Vega's quiet sign
Because his boss draws it on every letter
Because it appears in the grey paper
questions.explain: 第9句 "it was Dr. Vega's quiet sign, the same little star from her desk notes"，那是维加博士的记号。

questions.q: What can we tell about Tomas from this chapter?
options: He waits at home until the storm ends
He blames the star-sign readers
He climbs the mountain through the storm to fix his mistake
He throws the wet letter away
questions.explain: 第11句 "So he wrapped the wet letter in a dry cloth and climbed the long road while the storm still shouted above him"——冒雨上山补救，可推断他尽忠职守。

questions.q: In this chapter, the star-sign readers' astrology gives no help. What does the word astrology mean here?
options: The science of stars and light
The art of reading star signs to tell the future
The work of a mountain postman
The study of black rainwater
questions.explain: 第10句 "The star-sign readers said the storm was written in the sky by the planets, but their astrology gave Tomas no help"——astrology 是用星座断事的占星术，与真正的 astronomy（天文学）不同。

title: 《星星邮递员》· 夜空开放日

sentences.en: In the first cold week of winter, the observatory had an open night, a big quiet party for the whole town below.
sentences.zh: 在冬天最冷的第一个星期，天文台办了一场开放夜——为山下全镇人准备的一场安静的大型聚会。

sentences.en: Dr. Vega wrote the invitations herself, and each letter carried one small asterisk in the corner, her quiet sign for something important.
sentences.zh: 邀请信是维加博士亲手写的，每一封的角落里都画着一个小星号——她标记要紧之事的安静记号。

sentences.en: That evening almost the whole village walked up the mountain road together, with oil lamps and warm coats and small red noses.
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚，几乎全村人一起爬上山路，提着油灯，穿着厚外套，鼻子冻得通红。

sentences.en: The children ran ahead over the wet stones, and the old people walked slowly behind, holding each other's cold arms.
sentences.zh: 孩子们踩着湿漉漉的石头跑在前头，老人们挽着彼此冰凉的手臂，慢慢走在后面。

sentences.en: One small child with white ice on his wool hat asked if they could see an astronaut from up there, walking in his white suit between the stars.
sentences.zh: 一个毛线帽上结着白霜的小孩问：从这儿能不能看见宇航员，穿着白色宇航服在星星之间行走。

sentences.en: Dr. Vega laughed softly, turned the big black telescope, and said, tonight, my friends, we will all fly far away without ever leaving the ground.
sentences.zh: 维加博士轻轻笑了，转过大望远镜说：朋友们，今晚我们全都要飞去远方，而且一步也不用离开地面。

sentences.en: She showed the people a bright stellar cluster in the dark, a little city of stars holding hands in the cold.
sentences.zh: 她让大家看黑暗中一团明亮的星团——一座在寒夜里手挽着手的星星小镇。

sentences.en: Then she named every winter constellation, one by one, and the people repeated the strange old names after her like the words of a song.
sentences.zh: 接着她把冬季的星座一个一个报出名字，人们跟着念那些古老而陌生的名字，像唱一支歌的歌词。

sentences.en: This soft light travelled across interstellar space for hundreds and thousands of long, silent years, she said, and it arrived tonight, just for you.
sentences.zh: 她说，这柔和的光在星际空间里走了成百上千个漫长而寂静的年头，今晚才抵达——专程为你而来。

sentences.en: Late that night the last grey clouds moved away like a slow curtain, and the Milky Way appeared above the dark mountain.
sentences.zh: 夜深了，最后一片灰云像缓缓拉开的幕布一样退去，银河在黑山上空显现出来。

sentences.en: Tomas saw the great wide sea of stars above him, and he opened his mouth, but not one word came out.
sentences.zh: 托马斯望见头顶那片辽阔的星的海洋，他张开嘴，却一个字也说不出来。

sentences.en: The sky felt astronomical, too big for any words in any language that he had ever learned at school.
sentences.zh: 他觉得天空大得像天文数字，学校里学过的任何语言、任何词语都装不下它。

sentences.en: For the first time he understood why the quiet old astronomer had given her whole life to astronomy, and why she had never wanted a different one.
sentences.zh: 他第一次明白了，这位安静的天文学家为什么把一生都交给天文学，为什么从未想要别的人生。

sentences.en: That night the mountain stood very close to the sky, and every person on it walked home a little quieter and a little larger.
sentences.zh: 那一夜，山离天空特别近；山上每一个人回家时，都变得更安静了一点，也更辽阔了一点。

questions.q: Why does almost the whole village walk up the mountain that evening?
options: To see the stars at the observatory's open night
To fix the roof of the tower
To buy medicine
To watch a boat race
questions.explain: 第1句 "the observatory had an open night, a big quiet party for the whole town"，第3句 "almost the whole village walked up the mountain road together"。

questions.q: What does the child with ice on his hat ask?
options: If they can see an astronaut walking between the stars
If the telescope can see the sea
If the tower has warm tea
If the stars are made of ice
questions.explain: 第5句 "asked if they could see an astronaut from up there, walking in his white suit between the stars"。

questions.q: What does Dr. Vega show the people in the dark?
options: A burning rocket
A bright stellar cluster
A sea monster
A new letter
questions.explain: 第7句 "She showed the people a bright stellar cluster in the dark"，她让大家看一团明亮的星团。

questions.q: What changes in Tomas on this night?
options: He decides to leave the town
He understands for the first time why Dr. Vega gave her life to astronomy
He stops liking his job
He learns to fly a ship
questions.explain: 第11句他看见星海说不出话，第13句 "For the first time he understood why the quiet old astronomer had given her whole life to astronomy"。

questions.q: The sky felt astronomical, too big for any words. Here astronomical means:
options: Warm and soft
Too big to measure or describe
Quiet and small
Full of grey clouds
questions.explain: 第12句 "too big for any words in any language"，astronomical 在此意为大得无法估量，词根 astro 意为"星"。

title: 《星星邮递员》· 最后一封信

sentences.en: Spring came up the mountain quietly, with soft rain and small green flowers, and with the first warm wind Dr. Vega had to say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 春天伴着细雨和小小的绿花悄悄上山，而随着第一阵暖风，维加博士不得不道别了。

sentences.en: Her astronomy work was moving to a bigger city near the sea, where the observatories were new and the money was better.
sentences.zh: 她的天文学工作要搬去海边一座更大的城市，那里的天文台是新的，薪水也更好。

sentences.en: On her last morning she gave Tomas a sealed letter, and her grey eyes were bright but not quite dry.
sentences.zh: 最后一个早晨，她递给托马斯一封封好的信；她的灰眼睛亮亮的，却并不算干。

sentences.en: On the front of the envelope there was one small asterisk, the same quiet star from three seasons of letters.
sentences.zh: 信封正面只有一个小星号——三个季节通信以来，那颗同样安静的星。

sentences.en: The words inside read: To a future astronomer, who also walks up long mountain roads with a heavy brown bag.
sentences.zh: 信里写着：致一位未来的天文学家——那个同样背着沉重棕色邮包、走过漫长山路的人。

sentences.en: Keep the small telescope I leave in the tower, the letter went on, because good tools should never sleep in the dark.
sentences.zh: 信接着说：我把留在塔里的那台小望远镜送给你，因为好工具不该在黑暗里沉睡。

sentences.en: The sky belongs to careful eyes, she wrote, and careful eyes can live in a postman just as well as in a professor.
sentences.zh: 她写道：天空属于认真的眼睛，而认真的眼睛，长在邮差身上和长在教授身上一样好。

sentences.en: Tomas read that letter many times that spring, once in the quiet post office and once under every new star that came out over the mountains.
sentences.zh: 那个春天，托马斯把那封信读了许多遍：在安静的邮局里读一遍，在山间新亮起的每颗星星下再读一遍。

sentences.en: He began to learn the true name of every constellation, first from an old paper map and then from the real sky itself.
sentences.zh: 他开始学习每一个星座真正的名字，先是照着一张旧纸星图，后来干脆对着夜空本身。

sentences.en: Some nights he dreamed about asteroids, interstellar roads and stellar light travelling astronomical distances, and in the dreams the sky knew his name.
sentences.zh: 有些夜里，他梦见小行星、星际航道和跨越天文距离的星光；在梦里，天空认得他的名字。

sentences.en: The round tower was quiet now, but his heart was full, like a small room with warm tea and good news inside.
sentences.zh: 圆塔如今安静了，可他的心是满的，像一间有热茶和好消息的小屋。

sentences.en: He wrote one short letter to the big city by the sea, with one small asterisk in the corner, and he did not explain it to anyone.
sentences.zh: 他给海边那座大城市写了一封短信，角落里画上一个小星号，而且没有向任何人解释它。

sentences.en: The answer came back in one short week: a star map drawn by hand, and under it one small word written in careful ink: begin.
sentences.zh: 短短一周后回信来了：一张手绘的星图，星图下面用细心的墨水写着一个小小的词：开始。

sentences.en: Above the dark mountain the stars kept their old slow light, and the long white road between the little town and the sky stayed open.
sentences.zh: 黑山的上方，星星们保持着古老而缓慢的光；小镇与天空之间那条长长的白色道路，一直敞开着。

questions.q: Why does Dr. Vega have to leave the mountain?
options: She is tired of the stars
Her astronomy work is moving to a bigger city near the sea
The town asks her to go
The tower is too cold in winter
questions.explain: 第2句 "Her astronomy work was moving to a bigger city near the sea"，她的工作要搬去更大的城市。

questions.q: What does the letter tell Tomas to keep?
options: Her thin notebooks
The small telescope in the tower
Her grey cardigan
The star map from the city
questions.explain: 第6句 "Keep the small telescope I leave in the tower"，她把塔里的小望远镜留给托马斯。

questions.q: What does Dr. Vega write about careful eyes?
options: They can live in a postman as well as in a professor
They belong only to scientists
They must move to the big city
They need a big telescope
questions.explain: 第7句 "careful eyes can live in a postman just as well as in a professor"，认真的眼睛人人可以有。

questions.q: Why does Tomas not explain the asterisk on his own letter to anyone?
options: He forgot its meaning
It is a private sign between him and Dr. Vega
The boss forbids asterisks
The letter has no asterisk
questions.explain: 第4句的星号是维加博士安静的签名，第12句 "he did not explain it to anyone"——这是只属于两人的暗号，可见他珍视这份情谊（推断）。

questions.q: What does Tomas begin to learn that spring?
options: How to fix roofs
How to sail a boat
The name of every constellation
The price of stamps
questions.explain: 第9句 "He began to learn the true name of every constellation"，他开始学习每个星座的名字。

title: 《小船长的航行》· 老船长的帽子

sentences.en: Ada lived in a small fishing village by a cold grey sea, in a street of thin houses that all looked at the water.
sentences.zh: 艾达住在一片灰冷大海边的渔村里，那条街上一排瘦瘦的房子，全都朝着海水。

sentences.en: The old captain of the village boat was sick in bed; his tired chest could not sustain a deep breath, and his cough was louder than the winter wind.
sentences.zh: 村里那条船的老船长病倒在床上，他疲弱的胸腔连一口深呼吸都撑不住了，咳嗽声比冬天的风还响。

sentences.en: One island across the water needed a box of medicine that very day, and no shop in the small village could obtain it in time.
sentences.zh: 海对面的一座岛当天就急需一箱药，而小村里没有一家铺子能及时弄到它。

sentences.en: Who can captain the boat in this weather, the people asked in the port office, and the room went quiet.
sentences.zh: 这种天气谁来当船长开船？港务所里众人发问，屋里一下子安静了。

sentences.en: Ada put up her hand at the back, and some people laughed, because she was young and small and only a girl.
sentences.zh: 艾达在后排举起了手，有人笑出了声，因为她年纪小、个子小，还只是个女孩。

sentences.en: But she was capable: she had sailed with the old captain for five summers, and she knew every rope and every stone in the bay.
sentences.zh: 可她是有本事的：她跟老船长跑了五个夏天的船，湾里每一根缆绳、每一块礁石她都认得。

sentences.en: The sea contains many dangers, she said, but I know this water like the floor of my mother's kitchen.
sentences.zh: 她说，大海里藏着许多危险，可这片水我熟悉得就像我妈厨房的地板。

sentences.en: The old man heard everything from his bed, and he sent for Ada and gave her his hat from the dark shelf.
sentences.zh: 老人在床上听见了这一切，便派人叫来艾达，从暗暗的架子上取下自己的帽子交给她。

sentences.en: A captain keeps the crew calm, he told her in his dry old voice, and a calm crew comes home alive.
sentences.zh: 他用沙哑苍老的声音告诉她：船长要让船员镇定，镇定的船员才能活着回家。

sentences.en: Stay tenacious, hold your course, and maintain your courage, he said, and the medicine box will arrive, and the children will sleep.
sentences.zh: 他说：顽强一点，把住航向，守住你的勇气，药箱会送到，孩子们会安然入睡。

sentences.en: The hat was too big for her head, but Ada wore it with care, like a crown that had chosen her first.
sentences.zh: 帽子对她来说太大了，可艾达戴得郑重，像一顶先选中了她的王冠。

sentences.en: The little seaport woke slowly around them, grey and cold, and the morning tide called her name against the wet stones.
sentences.zh: 小小的海港在两人身边慢慢醒来，灰蒙蒙、冷清清，清晨的潮水拍着湿石头，唤着她的名字。

sentences.en: The box contained the medicine, wrapped in white paper against the sea wet, and she tied it under the seat with her own two hands.
sentences.zh: 箱子里装着用白纸包好、防着海潮的药，她亲自动手把它捆在座位下面。

sentences.en: She stepped onto the boat, and the whole village watched from the cape until her sail went small and white in the grey.
sentences.zh: 她踏上船，全村人站在海角上望着，直到她的帆在灰色海面上缩成小小的一点白。

questions.q: Why does the village need someone to captain the boat?
options: The old captain is sick in bed and the island needs medicine
The boat is brand new
The island asked for a bigger crew
Ada wants to travel
questions.explain: 第2句老船长病倒，第3句 "One island across the water needed a box of medicine that very day"，所以必须有人替他掌舵。

questions.q: Why does Ada say she is capable of the trip?
options: She has a lot of money
She sailed with the old captain for five summers and knows every rope and stone
The sea contains no dangers
Her mother told her to go
questions.explain: 第6句 "she had sailed with the old captain for five summers, and she knew every rope and every stone in the bay"。

questions.q: What does the old captain tell Ada about leading the crew?
options: A captain keeps the crew calm
A captain must shout all the time
A captain lets the crew decide
A captain sails alone
questions.explain: 第9句 "A captain keeps the crew calm"，他叮嘱船长要让船员镇定。

questions.q: What can we tell about the old captain's feelings when he gives the hat?
options: He does not trust Ada at all
He is angry about the medicine
He believes in her and passes his place to her
He wants his hat back the same day
questions.explain: 第8句他主动把帽子给她，第10句叮嘱 "Stay tenacious, hold your course"——交出船长之帽加上临别赠言，可推断他是把信任和位置一起托付给了她。

questions.q: Where do the villagers watch Ada leave?
options: From the school
From the port office
From the mountains
From the cape
questions.explain: 第14句 "the whole village watched from the cape"，全村人从海角上目送她出发。

title: 《小船长的航行》· 风浪之间

sentences.en: At first the sea was kind, and the little boat ran well with the wind behind it, like a bird with warm hands on its back.
sentences.zh: 起初大海很和气，顺风推着小船走得顺顺当当，像一只被人用暖手托着背的鸟。

sentences.en: Ada checked the ropes twice, ate a little bread, and began to dream of the white houses on the far island.
sentences.zh: 艾达把缆绳查了两遍，啃了点面包，开始想远处岛上那些白色的房子。

sentences.en: Then grey clouds walked in from the west, and the waves stood up tall like walls of dark green glass.
sentences.zh: 随后灰云从西边压了过来，浪像一堵堵墨绿色玻璃墙，立了起来。

sentences.en: The other sailors looked at the grey sky with white faces, and one old fisherman began to talk about turning back to the home port.
sentences.zh: 其他船员脸色发白地望着灰色的天，一个老渔民开始念叨着要不要掉头回港。

sentences.en: Ada spoke like a captain: sit down, hold on, and no one goes into the sea today, she said, and they sat.
sentences.zh: 艾达像船长一样开口：坐稳，抓牢，今天谁也不许下海——她说完，大家就都坐下了。

sentences.en: The wooden box contained the medicine, so she tied it down with three knots and put her own coat over the top.
sentences.zh: 木箱里装着药，她打了三个结把它牢牢捆住，又把自己外套盖在上面。

sentences.en: Water came in through a small hole in the floor, cold and quick, like a silver snake looking for a warm place.
sentences.zh: 水从船底一个小洞里渗进来，又冷又急，像一条银蛇在找暖和地方。

sentences.en: A captain must maintain her boat in bad weather, Ada remembered, so she pushed a cloth into the hole and held it with her knee.
sentences.zh: 艾达记起来：坏天气里，船长必须保养好自己的船。于是她把一块布塞进洞里，用膝盖死死抵住。

sentences.en: The old words sustained her through every wave: stay tenacious, hold your course, and the sea is only water after all.
sentences.zh: 老人的话支撑她扛过每一个浪头：顽强一点，把住航向——说到底，海不过就是水。

sentences.en: The boat has the capacity for these waves, she told herself, because the old captain built her bones for weather like this.
sentences.zh: 她对自己说：这条船的承量扛得住这些浪，因为老船长造它的时候，就是照着这种天色造的骨头。

sentences.en: A capable sailor works with the sea, not against it, so Ada turned the sail a little and let the storm pass by like a train.
sentences.zh: 能干的船员是顺着海走的，不是顶着海走的，于是艾达稍稍转了转帆，任风暴像一列火车那样从旁边驶过。

sentences.en: She retained the old man's voice in her ears all through the worst hour, and she did not once look back at the cape.
sentences.zh: 最难熬的那个钟头里，老人的声音一直留在她耳边；她一次也没有回头望海角。

sentences.en: Slowly the grey clouds opened, the water turned soft and blue again, and the whole crew breathed out at the same time.
sentences.zh: 灰云慢慢散开，海水重新变得柔和湛蓝，全船的人同一刻长出了一口气。

sentences.en: Ada dried her hands on her wet coat and looked for the far island, a small dark tooth on the edge of the sea.
sentences.zh: 艾达在湿外套上擦干手，望向远处的岛——海平线上一颗小小的深色牙齿。

questions.q: How does Ada keep the medicine box safe?
options: She ties it down with three knots and covers it with her coat
She throws it in the sea
She holds it in one hand
She puts it under the floor
questions.explain: 第6句 "she tied it down with three knots and put her own coat over the top"。

questions.q: What does Ada do about the hole in the floor?
options: She ignores it
She pushes a cloth into it and holds it with her knee
She cries for help
She turns the boat back
questions.explain: 第8句 "she pushed a cloth into the hole and held it with her knee"。

questions.q: What does Ada say to the crew when the storm stands up?
options: Sit down, hold on, no one goes into the sea
Turn back to the port
Throw the box away
Jump and swim to the island
questions.explain: 第5句 "sit down, hold on, and no one goes into the sea today"。

questions.q: Why does Ada turn the sail instead of fighting the storm head-on?
options: Because she is afraid of the dark
Because a capable sailor works with the sea, not against it
Because the boat is broken
Because the old fisherman tells her to
questions.explain: 第11句 "A capable sailor works with the sea, not against it"——她顺着海走，所以转帆让风暴过去（推断其动机）。

questions.q: "The boat has the capacity for these waves" — here capacity means:
options: The money the boat costs
The boat is strong and big enough to take these waves
The number of people on board
The speed of the wind
questions.explain: 第10句接着说老船长"照着这种天色造的骨头"，capacity 在此意为承受能力、容量。

title: 《小船长的航行》· 银色的徽章

sentences.en: The island people saw the small boat come into the port, with its sail torn and its captain still standing at the wheel.
sentences.zh: 岛上的人看见小船驶进港来，帆撕破了，船长却还站在舵前。

sentences.en: Ada stepped onto the wet stones with the box in her arms, and her legs shook a little, but only a little.
sentences.zh: 艾达抱着箱子踏上湿漉漉的石阶，双腿有点发抖——但只是一点点。

sentences.en: The doctor took the medicine at once, and that night the two sick children obtained a long, cool, quiet sleep.
sentences.zh: 医生立刻接过了药，当天夜里，两个生病的孩子得到了一场漫长、清凉而安稳的睡眠。

sentences.en: By morning the fever was gone, and the whole island felt content, like a house after a storm when every window still holds.
sentences.zh: 到早晨烧退了，整座岛都安心下来，像暴雨之后一扇窗都没碎的房子。

sentences.en: You did not just bring medicine, the doctor said to her, you brought the village a kind of good news that no money can obtain.
sentences.zh: 医生对她说：你送来的不只是药，你还给全村带来了一种多少钱都买不到的好消息。

sentences.en: You also obtained our trust, he added with a smile, and trust, once given to a sailor, sails with her for life.
sentences.zh: 他又笑着说：你还赢得了我们的信任；信任一旦给了水手，就随她航行一辈子。

sentences.en: An old woman with white hair and sea-blue eyes came up and gave Ada a small silver badge on a blue ribbon.
sentences.zh: 一位白发蓝眼、眼睛像海一样的老婆婆走上前，把一枚系着蓝丝带的小银徽章交给艾达。

sentences.en: The badge had the shape of a wave and a star, and the silver was old and soft from many years of fingers.
sentences.zh: 徽章是一朵浪和一颗星的形状，银子经了多年指尖摩挲，旧得温润。

sentences.en: Retain this and remember this day, the woman said, because the sea remembers every good captain, even the small ones.
sentences.zh: 老婆婆说：收好它，记住这一天；因为大海记得每一位好船长，连最小的那位也记得。

sentences.en: In the evening the children asked Ada to entertain them with sea stories, and she gave them the storm, the hole, and the words that had sustained her.
sentences.zh: 傍晚，孩子们请艾达讲海上的故事逗他们开心，她把风暴、船洞，还有支撑过她的那些话，都讲给了他们。

sentences.en: She felt like a real captain now, capable and calm, and the hat sat on her head like it had grown there.
sentences.zh: 她现在觉得自己是一位真正的船长了，能干又镇定；那顶帽子扣在头上，好像是在那里长出来的。

sentences.en: The little port was full of warm yellow light, and the smell of fish soup moved from door to door like a friend.
sentences.zh: 小港口满是暖黄的灯火，鱼汤的香气像个朋友似的挨家挨户串门。

sentences.en: Some island men asked her how she had maintained the boat through the grey waves, and she showed them her cloth, her knot, and her knee.
sentences.zh: 几个岛上人问她是怎么把船保养着闯过灰浪的，她给他们看了那块布、那个结，还有自己的膝盖。

sentences.en: Ada slept well that night, with the badge under her pillow and the old hat on the chair, like a queen in a small cold palace.
sentences.zh: 那一夜艾达睡得很沉，徽章压在枕头下，旧帽子搁在椅子上，像一座小而寒冷的宫殿里的女王。

questions.q: What does the doctor say Ada obtained besides the thanks of the village?
options: A new boat
A bag of gold
Their trust
A big house
questions.explain: 第6句 "You also obtained our trust"，医生说她还赢得了岛上人的信任。

questions.q: What does the old woman give Ada?
options: A warm coat
A small silver badge
A sea map
A box of tea
questions.explain: 第7句 "gave Ada a small silver badge on a blue ribbon"，第8句说徽章是浪和星的形状。

questions.q: What does the old woman tell Ada about the badge?
options: To retain it and remember this day
To sell it in the port
To give it to the doctor
To hide it under the boat
questions.explain: 第9句 "Retain this and remember this day"。

questions.q: How does Ada change during her evening on the island?
options: She becomes afraid of the sea
She feels like a real captain, capable and calm
She decides to leave the village
She gives the hat away
questions.explain: 第11句 "She felt like a real captain now, capable and calm"——对照第1章里被嘲笑的小女孩，可推断这次渡海让她真正长大了。

questions.q: "Retain this and remember this day" — here retain means:
options: To sell
To keep and hold
To throw away
To borrow
questions.explain: 第9句老婆婆把徽章郑重交给她，retain 意为收好、留存。

title: 《小船长的航行》· 把帽子留着

sentences.en: The next morning Ada sailed home across the quiet water, and the island stood behind her like a green friend waving goodbye.
sentences.zh: 第二天清晨，艾达驶过安静的海面回家；岛立在她身后，像一个挥手道别的绿色朋友。

sentences.en: The wind was small and kind, and she maintained the boat with easy hands, singing an old island song about fish and stars.
sentences.zh: 风又小又和气，她闲闲地操着船，唱一支岛上的老歌，唱鱼，也唱星星。

sentences.en: When the little boat came into the home port, the whole village was waiting on the wet stones, and nobody said one word.
sentences.zh: 小船驶进家乡的港口时，全村人都在湿漉漉的石滩上等着，却没有一个人出声。

sentences.en: The sick old captain stood at his window in a grey coat, and Ada walked to his house with the hat in her two hands.
sentences.zh: 生病的老船长披着灰外套站在窗前，艾达双手捧着那顶帽子，朝他家走去。

sentences.en: I retained your hat with care, she said, and it did not fall into the sea, not even once, I promise.
sentences.zh: 她说：我把您的帽子好好收着呢，它一次也没有掉进海里，我保证。

sentences.en: The old man held the hat for a long time in his two old hands, and he looked at her the way fathers look at daughters.
sentences.zh: 老人用两只苍老的手捧着帽子看了很久，看她的眼神，就像父亲看女儿那样。

sentences.en: Retain it, he said at last, because a captain keeps her own hat, and this one has made its choice.
sentences.zh: 他终于开口：留着吧，船长该有自己的帽子——这一顶已经做出了它的选择。

sentences.en: Then Ada gave him a short recap of the trip: the grey walls of water, the small hole, the wet cloth, and the three knots.
sentences.zh: 接着，艾达把这次航行简要地讲给他听：灰墙一样的浪、那个小洞、那块湿布，还有三个结。

sentences.en: She told him about the tenacious little boat that would not lie down, even when the sea stood up like a mountain.
sentences.zh: 她给他讲那条顽强的小船——哪怕海像山一样立起来，它也不肯倒下。

sentences.en: He listened with deep content, like a man drinking warm tea after a long cold walk, and he asked for the story twice.
sentences.zh: 他听得心满意足，像走了很长一段冷路的人喝着热茶，还把故事要求讲了两遍。

sentences.en: You have the courage of a true captain, he said, and the village contains no braver heart than yours this year.
sentences.zh: 他说：你有真正船长的勇气，今年全村再找不出比你更勇敢的心了。

sentences.en: Encourage the young ones, he added, because the sea needs them, and the sea will obtain from them more than it takes.
sentences.zh: 他又说：多鼓励那些年轻人吧，大海需要他们，而大海从他们身上得到的，会比它拿走的多。

sentences.en: Then he put the hat on her head with his own two careful hands, and it sat there like it was always hers.
sentences.zh: 然后他用自己的双手、小心翼翼地把帽子戴到她头上，帽子稳稳地扣着，好像从来就是她的。

sentences.en: Outside, the evening came down on the grey port, and the water held the last of the light like a cup that retains its wine.
sentences.zh: 屋外，暮色落在灰色的港口上；水面兜着最后一点光，像一只存得住酒的杯子。

questions.q: What does Ada try to do with the hat at first?
options: Return it to the old captain
Sell it in the port
Give it to a child
Throw it into the sea
questions.explain: 第4、5句：她捧着帽子走到老船长家，说 "I retained your hat with care"——她是去还帽子的。

questions.q: What does the old captain tell Ada about the hat?
options: Give it back tomorrow
Put it on a shelf
Lend it to the doctor
Retain it, because a captain keeps her own hat
questions.explain: 第7句 "Retain it, he said at last, because a captain keeps her own hat"。

questions.q: What does Ada give the old captain on her return?
options: A silver badge
A short recap of the trip
A box of medicine
A new hat
questions.explain: 第8句 "Ada gave him a short recap of the trip"。

questions.q: How does the old captain feel while listening to Ada's story?
options: Bored and sleepy
Worried about the boat
Proud and deeply content
Angry about the hole
questions.explain: 第10句 "He listened with deep content, like a man drinking warm tea after a long cold walk"，还要求再讲一遍——可推断他为她骄傲满足。

questions.q: The little boat "would not lie down, even when the sea stood up like a mountain" — the word tenacious means:
options: Heavy and slow
Holding on and never giving up
New and shiny
Small and afraid
questions.explain: 第9句用浪立成山也不倒下来解释 tenacious，即顽强、咬住不放。

title: 《心跳合唱团》· 试音

sentences.en: In September, when the classrooms still smelled of new books and fresh paint, our school choir opened its doors to new singers, and Miss Carter, our conductor, pinned a white sign on the door that said: Every voice is welcome here.
sentences.zh: 九月里，教室里还留着新课本和新鲜油漆的味道，学校合唱团向新团员敞开了大门；我们的指挥卡特老师在门上钉了一张白纸，写着：每一个声音都受欢迎。

sentences.en: More than sixty students signed up in the first week, and, in accordance with the choir's oldest tradition, every single one of us had to sing alone on audition day, behind a small white curtain.
sentences.zh: 第一周就有六十多个学生报了名，而按照合唱团最老的传统，试音那天每个人都得独自站到一道小白幕后唱歌。

sentences.en: The auditorium felt full, warm, and a little frightening that afternoon, like an airport before a long journey, and even the ceiling seemed to hold its breath.
sentences.zh: 那天下午的礼堂满满当当、暖烘烘，又有点吓人，像长途旅行前夜的机场，连天花板仿佛都屏住了呼吸。

sentences.en: Miss Carter listened to every voice behind the curtain, because she wanted her ears, and not her eyes, to do the choosing.
sentences.zh: 卡特老师在幕布后面听每一个声音，因为她要让耳朵、而不是眼睛来做选择。

sentences.en: "The ears should decide, not the eyes," she told the long line of nervous students with a cordial, easy smile, and that one sentence calmed the whole room like a warm hand.
sentences.zh: "该由耳朵来定，不该由眼睛来定。"她带着亲切从容的笑，对排成一长排的紧张学生说，这一句话像一只温暖的手，让整间屋子安静了下来。

sentences.en: Some voices were soft as paper, some were strong as brass, and one boy sang like a small steam engine, but Miss Carter wrote something kind about every single one of them.
sentences.zh: 有的声音薄得像纸，有的亮得像铜号，还有个男生唱得像一台小蒸汽机，但卡特老师在每一个人的名字旁边都写下了一句好话。

sentences.en: When Ken's turn came, her high notes went badly off key, the wrong sounds jumped around the hall like a handful of dropped plates, and her face turned the color of the curtain.
sentences.zh: 轮到 Ken 的时候，她的高音跑调跑得厉害，错音像一把摔在地上的盘子，在礼堂里四处乱蹦，她的脸也涨成了幕布一样的白。

sentences.en: A few students in the back rows laughed quietly, because her song sounded strange to them, and quiet laughter, we all learned that day, can be crueler than the loud kind.
sentences.zh: 后排几个学生偷偷笑了，因为她的调子听着实在古怪；而我们那天都学到了，轻轻的笑声有时比放声大笑更伤人。

sentences.en: Some listeners showed pity, but Miss Carter showed real sympathy instead, and she asked Ken to sing the second line once more, slowly, in her own time, and without any fear.
sentences.zh: 几个人露出可怜她的神情，而卡特老师给出的是真切的同情，她请 Ken 再唱一遍第二句，慢一点，按自己的节奏来，不用害怕。

sentences.en: Ken lowered her head and held her music book like a shield, because she thought her chance was over and her year of secret hope had ended on that small stage.
sentences.zh: Ken 低下了头，把乐谱抱在胸前像一面盾牌，她以为自己的机会没了，一整年偷偷攒下的希望就断在了那个小台上。

sentences.en: It cost her all her courage to look up again, but Miss Carter kept a written record of every audition that day, and next to Ken's name she wrote one short word in red ink.
sentences.zh: 她用尽全部的勇气才重新抬起头；而那天卡特老师把每场试音都记了档，在 Ken 的名字旁边，她用红笔写了一个短短的词。

sentences.en: At the first rehearsal she told us the word was "stay", because the choir did not need perfect voices; it needed people who truly loved to sing, even when the singing was far from perfect.
sentences.zh: 第一次排练时她告诉我们，那个词是"留下"，因为合唱团不需要完美的嗓音，它需要真心热爱唱歌的人——哪怕唱得远谈不上完美。

sentences.en: "Sympathy is easy," she explained to the new members, "because it only stands outside a heart; empathy means standing inside another heart and hearing its music, even the shaky notes."
sentences.zh: "同情很容易，"她向新团员解释，"因为它只是站在一颗心外面；共情是要站进另一颗心里，听见它的音乐——连那些发抖的音也听。"

sentences.en: "We need empathy more than perfect pitch," she said with a small smile, and while we encouraged Ken with quiet applause, she told us once more that the core of our choir was never sound but hearts.
sentences.zh: "比起完美的音准，我们更需要共感。"她微微一笑说；我们用轻轻的掌声鼓励 Ken 时，她再一次告诉我们：合唱团的核心从来不是声音，是人心。

questions.q: How many students signed up in the first week?
options: About twenty
More than sixty
Only five
More than two hundred
questions.explain: 第2句 "More than sixty students signed up in the first week"，第一周报名的超过六十人。

questions.q: What happened when Ken's turn came?
options: She sang a perfect high note
Her high notes went badly off key
She refused to sing
