She left the room in tears
questions.explain: 第7句 "her high notes went badly off key, the wrong sounds jumped around the hall"，Ken 的高音严重跑调。

questions.q: What short word did Miss Carter write next to Ken's name?
options: Stay
Go
Home
Sing
questions.explain: 第11句 she wrote one short word in red ink；第12句 "she told us the word was 'stay'"，那个红笔写的词是"留下"。

questions.q: Why did Miss Carter listen to every voice behind a small curtain?
options: Because she was afraid of the students
Because she wanted her ears, and not her eyes, to do the choosing
Because the curtain was a school rule
Because the light was too strong
questions.explain: 第4句 "she wanted her ears, and not her eyes, to do the choosing"，第5句又解释"该由耳朵来定，不该由眼睛来定"，所以她隔着幕布听。

questions.q: In sentence 13, "empathy means standing inside another heart and hearing its music," the word "empathy" means ______.
options: feeling with another person from the inside
copying another person's singing
a kind of music lesson
a fear of the stage
questions.explain: 第13句。词根 path- 表示"感受"：em-(进入)+path(感受)→站进别人的心里去感受→共情。与只站在心外的 sympathy（同情）相对。

title: 《心跳合唱团》· 一首老歌

sentences.en: For the winter concert, Miss Carter chose a very old song, and when she placed the thin, yellow pages on the piano stand, nobody in the practice room had ever heard its strange, soft name.
sentences.zh: 为了冬季音乐会，卡特老师选了一首很老的歌；她把那几页发黄变薄的乐谱放上琴架时，排练室里没有一个人听说过这个又陌生又温柔的名字。

sentences.en: According to the record in the school office, a music teacher wrote it in 1968, in a small town school much like ours, with the same long windows and the same cold radiators.
sentences.zh: 根据学校办公室的记载，一位音乐教师在 1968 年写下它，就在一所和我们差不多的小镇学校里，有同样的长窗和同样冰凉的暖气片。

sentences.en: The old teacher had written it long ago for her lost students, for the ones who never came back after that hard, gray year, and the song had waited in a drawer for half a century before Miss Carter found it.
sentences.zh: 很久以前，那位老师为那些再也回不来的学生写下它——那一年又冷又灰暗；这首歌在抽屉里等了半个世纪，才被卡特老师翻了出来。

sentences.en: Miss Carter read the first line out loud in a plain, calm voice, and the practice room went very quiet, as if the walls themselves had started listening to the old paper.
sentences.zh: 卡特老师用平实、安静的声音念出第一句歌词，排练室一下子静了，仿佛连墙壁都开始听那张老纸说话。

sentences.en: When we sang it for the first time, the slow melody had a deep resonance in that small room, a low, warm ring that lived under every note and stayed after the notes were gone.
sentences.zh: 我们头一回唱它时，舒缓的旋律在小屋里激起很深的共鸣——一记低沉温热的回响，藏在每个音底下，音散了它还没散。

sentences.en: Ken closed her eyes while she sang, and later she told me that it took real courage to close them, because the melody moved like an old story she had known all her life without ever reading.
sentences.zh: Ken 唱的时候闭上了眼睛；后来她告诉我，闭上眼其实需要真勇气，因为那旋律像一段她生来就熟、却从没读过的旧故事。

sentences.en: Everyone in the room, without any plan or signal, quietly remembered a special person: a grandmother, a lost brother, a friend who had moved away to a far, bright city.
sentences.zh: 屋里每个人，没有任何约定或暗号，都默默想起了一个特别的人：一位外婆、一个失散的兄弟、一个搬去远方亮堂城市的朋友。

sentences.en: I thought about my own grandfather, who taught me three folk songs before he died, and my eyes grew warm while my mouth kept singing his favorite line.
sentences.zh: 我想起了我自己的外公，他在世时教过我三首民歌；嘴上还唱着他最爱的那句，眼眶却先热了。

sentences.en: Miss Carter let the silence stay for a whole minute after the last note faded, because real singing, she said, begins at the exact moment when memory opens the heart.
sentences.zh: 最后一个音散去之后，卡特老师让那份安静足足留了一分钟，因为她说，真正的歌唱，正是从记忆推开人心那一刻才开始的。

sentences.en: That afternoon our two voice parts, which had argued for three long weeks about everything, moved in perfect unison for the first time, like two rivers joining into one quiet water.
sentences.zh: 那天下午，吵了整整三个星期的两个声部第一次做到了完全的齐声，像两条河汇成了一片安静的水。

sentences.en: "It was not telepathy," she said with a soft laugh when she saw our surprised faces, "it was shared feeling — empathy, if you like the long word — and it took a sad, beautiful song to teach it to us."
sentences.zh: "这不是心灵感应，"看到我们惊讶的脸，她轻轻笑了，"这是共同的感受——愿意用长词的话，叫共情——是一首又忧伤又好听的歌教会了我们。"

sentences.en: The old song became the core of our winter programme, and we printed its little story on the back page of the concert programme, so every family could read about the teacher from 1968.
sentences.zh: 这首老歌成了我们冬季演出的核心曲目；我们把它的故事印在节目单的封底，好让每个家庭都读一读 1968 年那位老师的故事。

sentences.en: From that evening on, we kept a careful, honest record of every rehearsal, with dates, tempos, and short notes about our mistakes, and Miss Carter encouraged us to write down even our worst moments.
sentences.zh: 从那个晚上起，每次排练我们都认真诚实地留下记录：日期、速度，还有关于失误的短注；卡特老师鼓励我们连最糟的时刻也要写下来。

sentences.en: Ken wrote the very first note in the new book, and her cordial, round letters said: "Today the song felt less like paper and more like weather."
sentences.zh: Ken 在新本子里写下了第一条记录，她那亲切的圆滚滚的字说："今天这首歌不像纸了，倒像天气。"

questions.q: When was the old song written, according to the record?
options: Last winter
questions.explain: 第2句 "a music teacher wrote it in 1968"，据记载写于 1968 年。

questions.q: Who had the old teacher written the song for?
options: Her own children
The school's principals
Her lost students
A winter concert
questions.explain: 第3句 "The old teacher had written it long ago for her lost students"，是为那些再也回不来的学生写的。

questions.q: What did the slow melody have in the small room?
options: A deep resonance
A loud echo
A strange noise
A broken rhythm
questions.explain: 第5句 "the slow melody had a deep resonance in that small room"，旋律在屋里激起深深的共鸣。

questions.q: Why did Ken close her eyes while she sang?
options: Because she was too tired
Because the light was too strong
Because Miss Carter told her to
Because it took courage, and the melody felt like a story she had always known
questions.explain: 第6句 "it took real courage to close them, because the melody moved like an old story she had known all her life"，闭眼需要勇气，而那旋律像她生来就熟的故事。

questions.q: In sentence 11, Miss Carter said it was not telepathy. The word "telepathy" means ______.
options: hearing with your ears
knowing another's feelings without words
a kind of piano playing
a long journey
questions.explain: 第11句。词根 path- 表示"感受"：tele-(远)+path(感受)→隔着距离感知对方的心→心灵感应。她说那其实是共同的感受（共情），不是心灵感应。

title: 《心跳合唱团》· 心里的鼓点

sentences.en: By November, a quiet discord had grown between the two voice sections of our choir, and it grew the way winter does: slowly, slowly, and then all at once, like a field of snow overnight.
sentences.zh: 到了十一月，两个声部之间悄悄生出了不和，它长得很像冬天：慢一点、慢一点，然后一夜之间铺满整个原野。

sentences.en: The sopranos wanted the main melody of the old song for themselves, and the altos wanted the very same melody, and each section believed that the other one was being unfair.
sentences.zh: 女高音想把老歌的主旋律据为己有，女低音想要同一条旋律，两边都认定是对方不讲理。

sentences.en: One gray Wednesday, the two sections even sang against each other on purpose, the sopranos loud and bright, the altos low and stubborn, like two trains pushing through one small tunnel, and the song fell to pieces around their feet.
sentences.zh: 一个灰蒙蒙的周三，两个声部干脆故意对着唱：女高音又响又亮，女低音又低又倔，像两列火车挤同一条小隧道，那首歌在他们脚边摔了个粉碎。

sentences.en: Their discordant voices filled the practice room like cold weather, and Miss Carter stopped the piano with both hands and looked at us for a long, silent minute, her arms folded.
sentences.zh: 两边的声音互不相合，像冷空气一样灌满了排练室；卡特老师双手按停了钢琴，抱着胳膊，沉默地看了我们整整一分钟。

sentences.en: After that Wednesday, some members of the choir showed real apathy; they stopped coming to Tuesday rehearsals, and their empty chairs stood in the back row like missing teeth in a friendly smile.
sentences.zh: 那个周三之后，有些团员表现出真正的冷漠：周二的排练干脆不来了，后排那些空椅子像一张笑脸里缺掉的几颗牙。

sentences.en: Miss Carter, however, refused to choose a winner between the two sections, because a winner, she said, would only mean that half of the choir had lost, and a choir is one body or nothing.
sentences.zh: 然而卡特老师拒绝在两个声部之间评出赢家，因为她说，有赢家就等于合唱团输了一半，而合唱团要么是一条心，要么什么都不是。

sentences.en: "A melody is not a prize," she told us quietly, "it is a road, and a road is only useful when two people agree to share it, and sharing is the whole secret of music."
sentences.zh: "旋律不是奖品，"她平静地告诉我们，"它是路；一条路只有两个人肯分享时才有用，而分享就是音乐全部的秘密。"

sentences.en: She asked both sections to stand up, to place one hand on their hearts, and to close their eyes in the middle of that noisy, unhappy afternoon.
sentences.zh: 她让两个声部都站起来，把一只手放在心口上，在那个吵吵嚷嚷、谁也不痛快的下午，闭上了眼睛。

sentences.en: "Feel the drumbeat inside," she said, "and follow that quiet tempo; your hearts have been keeping time together since September, in every song, whether you knew it or not."
sentences.zh: "去摸里头那个鼓点，"她说，"跟着那个安静的节奏走；从九月起，在每一首歌里，你们的心就一直在合着同一个拍子——不管你们知不知道。"

sentences.en: When the sopranos finally stopped shouting and started listening, they heard the altos' hidden line moving below them, warm and patient, like a river moving under the winter ice, and they were a little ashamed.
sentences.zh: 女高音终于不再较劲、开始倾听了，这才听见女低音藏在下面的那条线：温和、有耐心，像冬天冰层下走的一条河——她们有点不好意思了。

sentences.en: The two parts reached an accord without one single angry word, and they divided the melody between them, half and half, like neighbors sharing one long, difficult road.
sentences.zh: 两个声部没说一句气话就达成了一致，把旋律一分为二、你一半我一半，像两个邻居合走一条又长又难走的路。

sentences.en: Miss Carter said empathy was not the same as agreeing with everyone; it was the harder art of hearing each other, even the quiet lines, even the lines you do not like.
sentences.zh: 卡特老师说，共情不等于人人都附和；它是更难的一门功夫——听见彼此，连最轻的那条线也要听，连你不喜欢的那条线也要听。

sentences.en: Before the lesson ended, the two sections sang the old song in soft concord, and Ken, once so badly off key, held her low note with quiet, steady courage, and nobody laughed, not even in the back rows.
sentences.zh: 那节课结束前，两个声部已经和谐地唱起了那首老歌；曾经严重跑调的 Ken 安安静静、稳稳当当地托住了她的低音——没有一个人笑，后排也没有。

sentences.en: Our conductor encouraged us to remember that day for the rest of the year, because it was the day discord became our best teacher and taught us the one skill a choir needs most: listening.
sentences.zh: 指挥鼓励我们把那一天记一整年，因为正是"不和"在那一天成了我们最好的老师，教会了合唱团最需要的一门功夫：倾听。

questions.q: What had grown between the two sections by November?
options: A quiet discord
A strong friendship
A new song
A shared solo
questions.explain: 第1句 "a quiet discord had grown between the two voice sections"，两个声部之间生出了不和。

questions.q: What did some members show when they stopped coming to rehearsals?
options: Courage
Apathy
Sympathy
Enthusiasm
questions.explain: 第5句 "some members of the choir showed real apathy; they stopped coming to Tuesday rehearsals"，不来的团员表现出的是冷漠。

questions.q: What did Miss Carter ask both sections to do?
options: Sing louder
Go home early
Place one hand on their hearts and close their eyes
Choose a winner
questions.explain: 第8句 "She asked both sections to stand up, to place one hand on their hearts, and to close their eyes"，她让大家手放心口、闭上眼睛。

questions.q: Why did Miss Carter refuse to choose a winner between the sections?
options: Because she liked both melodies equally
Because a winner would mean half of the choir had lost
Because the school did not allow prizes
Because nobody wanted to sing anymore
questions.explain: 第6句 "a winner, she said, would only mean that half of the choir had lost, and a choir is one body or nothing"，评出赢家等于合唱团输了一半。

questions.q: In sentence 5, "some members showed real apathy," the word "apathy" means ______.
options: great interest
a lack of feeling or interest
loud anger
perfect singing
questions.explain: 第5句。词根 path- 表示"感受"：a-(无)+path(感受)→没有感受→冷漠、无所谓。连排练都懒得来，正是这种状态。

title: 《心跳合唱团》· 演出夜

sentences.en: On concert night, the auditorium filled slowly with families, old teachers, and small children in their best winter sweaters, and the warm air smelled of dry coats, oranges, and pencil erasers.
sentences.zh: 演出那晚，礼堂里渐渐坐满了家人、退休的老教师，还有穿着过年才穿的好毛衣的小孩子；暖烘烘的空气里是干大衣、橘子和橡皮的气味。

sentences.en: The audience went silent when the lights above the stage dimmed, and two hundred faces turned together toward the curtain like a field of sunflowers turning toward the last evening sun.
sentences.zh: 舞台顶灯暗下来的时候，观众席安静了，两百张脸一齐转向幕布，像一园子向日葵一起转向傍晚最后一缕太阳。

sentences.en: Somewhere in the third row sat a small grandmother with a hearing aid, who had bought her ticket a full month before anyone else in town, and who smiled a cordial thank-you at every stranger who helped her to her seat.
sentences.zh: 第三排的某个位子上，坐着一位戴助听器的小个子老奶奶；她的票比全城任何人买得都早一个月，每个帮她入座的陌生人都收到她一声亲切的道谢。

sentences.en: Miss Carter had recorded our final rehearsal that very afternoon, and before the doors opened she played one short minute of it to us in the big, empty hall.
sentences.zh: 就在当天下午，卡特老师录下了我们最后一场排练；开门迎客之前，她在这座空荡荡的大礼堂里给我们放了一小段。

sentences.en: "Sing it like this," she said, "not perfect, but together," and she encouraged us one last time to sing the old song exactly according to that last, honest recording.
sentences.zh: "就照这个唱，"她说，"不求完美，但求在一起。"她最后一次鼓励我们，完全照着那次诚实录音的感觉，唱那首老歌。

sentences.en: Our two sections, which had once been enemies of the same melody, now sang in perfect unison, and the hall slowly filled with a warm, low resonance, like a room remembering a fire.
sentences.zh: 曾经为同一条旋律反目的两个声部，此刻齐声合唱，整个礼堂慢慢泛起一片温热的低共鸣，像一间屋子回想起一炉火。

sentences.en: With quiet courage, Ken sang her low line far below the bright sopranos, and many hands in the dark audience moved, without thinking, toward other hands.
sentences.zh: Ken 鼓着安安静静的勇气，在亮堂的女高音底下远远地唱着她那条低声部；黑暗的观众席里，许多手不由自主地伸向了旁边的另一只手。

sentences.en: The old song rose through its words about lost students and long waits, and the final chord rose slowly, held like a held breath, and then fell into a silence so deep that even the radiators seemed to listen.
sentences.zh: 老歌穿过那些关于离散的学生和漫长等待的歌词升起来；最后一个和弦缓缓升起，像一口屏住的气，然后落进一片深得连暖气片都仿佛在倾听的安静。

sentences.en: For one long second, nobody in the audience made a sound, and I felt that every heart in the room was keeping one quiet concord, the same slow tempo, the same warm beat.
sentences.zh: 有那么长长的一秒，观众席上没有任何人出声；我感到屋里每一颗心都合着同一片安静的和声，同一个缓缓的速度，同一记温热的鼓点。

sentences.en: Then the applause came, loud and long, from every seat and every corner, and the grandmother in the third row clapped with both small hands until they must have hurt.
sentences.zh: 然后掌声起来了，每一排每一座，又响又久；第三排那位老奶奶用两只小小的手一个劲儿地鼓，鼓到后来一定是拍疼了。

sentences.en: After the show, she found Miss Carter near the piano, and because her voice was barely audible, she pulled the conductor's hand close to her mouth, like a person sharing a secret.
sentences.zh: 散场后，她在钢琴边找到了卡特老师；因为她的声音小得几乎听不见，她把指挥的手拉到自己嘴边，像要分享一个秘密。

sentences.en: "I heard it with my bones," she said, "every single word of the old song; my ears gave up years ago, but my heart never learned how to stop listening."
sentences.zh: "我是用骨头听见的，"她说，"老歌里的每个字都听见了；我的耳朵多年前就认输了，可我的心一直没学会怎么停下倾听。"

sentences.en: Miss Carter cried a little then, partly from sympathy and partly from joy, because the old teacher from 1968 had been her own music teacher, and those words meant more to her than any prize.
sentences.zh: 卡特老师当场掉了几滴眼泪，一半出于心疼，一半出于欢喜——因为 1968 年那位老教师，正是她自己的音乐老师，这句话在她心里的分量胜过任何奖项。

sentences.en: That night our choir finally understood the core of Miss Carter's whole year of lessons: hearts can hear what ears cannot, and empathy, in the end, is a kind of listening.
sentences.zh: 那一夜，合唱团终于懂了卡特老师一整年功课的核心：耳朵听不见的，心能听见；而共情，说到底就是倾听的一种。

questions.q: Who sat in the third row on concert night?
options: A music critic
A small grandmother with a hearing aid
The school principal
Ken's grandfather
questions.explain: 第3句 "in the third row sat a small grandmother with a hearing aid"，第三排是一位戴助听器的老奶奶。

questions.q: How did the choir sing the old song that night?
options: From a new paper score
Exactly according to the last, honest recording
Without a conductor
In complete silence
questions.explain: 第5句 "sing the old song exactly according to that last, honest recording"，他们照着最后一次排练的录音唱。

questions.q: Why did Miss Carter cry a little after the show?
options: Because the choir sang off key
Because the hall was too hot
Because the old teacher from 1968 had been her own music teacher
Because the grandmother could not hear
questions.explain: 第13句 "the old teacher from 1968 had been her own music teacher, and those words meant more to her than any prize"，那句话分量太重，因为老教师正是她的老师。

questions.q: Why did the grandmother pull the conductor's hand close to her mouth?
options: Because she was angry with the conductor
Because her voice was barely audible and she wanted her words to reach
Because she wanted to hold the piano
Because she could not stand up
questions.explain: 第11句 "because her voice was barely audible, she pulled the conductor's hand close to her mouth"，她声音太小，怕话送不到，才把手拉到嘴边。

questions.q: In sentence 13, "partly from sympathy and partly from joy," the word "sympathy" means ______.
options: sharing another person's sorrow from the outside
winning a music prize
a kind of piano chord
a fear of crowds
questions.explain: 第13句。词根 path- 表示"感受"：sym-(共同)+path(感受)→和他人的感受一起→同情（站在心外的体恤，与站进心里的 empathy 相对）。

title: 《心跳合唱团》· 团史记录本

sentences.en: At the end of the school year, in the last quiet week of June, we wrote the choir's little history book, all fourteen pages of it, in one long, happy afternoon, with a plate of biscuits between us and the windows open.
sentences.zh: 学年末，六月最后一个安安静静的星期里，我们用一个漫长又快活的下午写完了合唱团那本小小的团史——整整十四页，中间摆着一盘饼干，窗户全开着。

sentences.en: The old notebook kept a record of every rehearsal and every concert of the year, and Miss Carter had started it, in soft pencil, back on the first day of September.
sentences.zh: 这本旧笔记记下了这一年的每一次排练、每一场演出；九月的头一天，卡特老师就用一支软铅笔开了头。

sentences.en: The first page was full of hope, plans, and careful lists, and the last page had waited empty for June, like a train seat waiting for its last passenger.
sentences.zh: 第一页写满了期待、计划和细细的名单；最后一页一直空着等六月来，像列车上留给最后一位乘客的座位。

sentences.en: Ken wrote a page about her grandmother, who had sung in a village choir long ago, and about her own off-key beginning on that small, frightening stage, and about the red word that changed it.
sentences.zh: Ken 写了一页：写她那位年轻时在村里唱过合唱的外婆，写她自己在那个又小又吓人的台子上跑调的开头，也写那个改变了这一切的红笔字。

sentences.en: "Sympathy brought me through the door," she wrote in her small, round letters, "but empathy kept me singing all year, and courage grew in the warm room between the two."
sentences.zh: "是同情把我领进了门，"她用圆圆的小字写道，"可让我唱满一整年的，是共情；勇气就在这两者之间那间暖和的屋子里长了出来。"

sentences.en: A soprano wrote about the November discord, and an alto wrote about the Wednesday when the two sections finally reached their accord, and their two pages sat side by side in the notebook.
sentences.zh: 一位女高音写了十一月的不和，一位女低音写了两个声部终于言归于好的那个周三，两页纸在笔记本里挨着放在了一起。

sentences.en: The two pages read like two halves of one story, like the two voices that now walked side by side inside the old song from 1968, and neither writer wanted to give the story an ending.
sentences.zh: 那两页读起来像一个故事的两半，像 1968 年那首老歌里如今并肩走着的两条声线——而且谁都舍不得给这个故事写上结尾。

sentences.en: I wrote my own page about the small grandmother in the third row, and about her strange, beautiful sentence about hearing the whole winter concert with her bones.
sentences.zh: 我自己写的一页，是关于第三排那位小个子老奶奶的，关于她那句又古怪又动人的话——整场冬季音乐会，她都是用骨头听见的。

sentences.en: Another member wrote about the final chord and the long second of silence, when two hundred people kept one quiet concord without knowing it, and the writer called that second "our loudest music."
sentences.zh: 还有一位团员写了最后的和弦和那长长的静默一秒——两百个人不知不觉合着同一片安静的和声；这一页的作者把那一秒称作"我们最响的音乐"。

sentences.en: Our paths had crossed for one short school term, but a term, as the little book quietly showed, is long enough to change a voice forever, in both directions.
sentences.zh: 我们的路，不过在一个短短的学期里交汇了一次；可这本小本子悄悄证明，一个学期足够永远地改变一个声音——往哪个方向改都够。

sentences.en: Miss Carter wrote the very last page on a quiet June afternoon, while the windows stood open and the far, happy sound of football games floated in from the green field.
sentences.zh: 六月一个安静的下午，卡特老师写下了最后一页；窗户开着，远处绿茵场上足球赛那欢欢喜喜的声音一阵一阵飘进来。

sentences.en: Her words were short, but their core was deep, so every member of the choir copied them, by hand, into their hearts before the summer began.
sentences.zh: 她的话很短，核心却极深；暑假来临之前，团里每一个人都把它亲手抄进了心里。

sentences.en: "We did not learn singing," she wrote, "we learned to hear each other; the notes were only the road that carried us there, and hear first, sing second, and the singing will take care of itself."
sentences.zh: "我们学会的不是唱歌，"她写道，"是听见彼此；音符只是载我们到那儿的路——先会听，再会唱，唱这件事自己会好起来。"

sentences.en: When new students ask about the choir next September, we will show them the old record, encourage them to sing even when they are afraid, and tell them that every voice matters, because every heart matters.
sentences.zh: 明年九月，新学生再问起合唱团，我们就把那本旧记录翻给他们看，鼓励他们哪怕害怕也开口唱，并告诉他们：每一个声音都重要，因为每一颗心都重要。

questions.q: What did the old notebook keep a record of?
options: Ticket sales and prizes
Every rehearsal and every concert of the year
Names of visitors
Song lyrics only
questions.explain: 第2句 "The old notebook kept a record of every rehearsal and every concert of the year"，笔记记下了全年每次排练和每场演出。

questions.q: What did Ken say kept her singing all year?
options: Sympathy
Good training
Empathy
Perfect pitch
questions.explain: 第5句 "Sympathy brought me through the door... but empathy kept me singing all year"，让她唱满一年的是共情。

questions.q: When did Miss Carter write the last page?
options: On concert night
On a quiet June afternoon
On the first day of September
On a cold Wednesday
questions.explain: 第11句 "Miss Carter wrote the last page on a quiet June afternoon"，最后一页写于六月一个安静的下午。

questions.q: Why did the soprano's page and the alto's page sit side by side in the notebook?
options: Because there was no more space
Because they were written on the same day
Because they were two halves of one story, like the two voices now walking side by side
Because Miss Carter put them together
questions.explain: 第7句 "The two pages read like two halves of one story, like the two voices that now walked side by side"——两页纸像一个故事的两半，正如如今并肩同行的两条声线。

questions.q: In sentence 12, "Her words were short, but their core was deep," the word "core" means ______.
options: the outside cover
the most important, central part
the longest page
the paper quality
questions.explain: 第12句。词根 cord- 表示"心"：core 由"心"引申为"核心、最重要的中心部分"。

title: 《城市地下十米》· 井盖之下

sentences.en: Every morning for three whole years, Lin walked over the same round manhole cover near her bus stop, and every morning it was exactly the same: grey, quiet, and full of small secrets.
sentences.zh: 整整三年，每天早上，琳都会走过公交站旁那块圆圆的井盖；每个早晨它都一模一样：灰扑扑、不声不响，装满了小小的秘密。

sentences.en: One Tuesday, in a light autumn rain, she stopped in the middle of the pavement, looked down at the wet iron circle, and asked herself one simple question that changed her whole year: what lies below it?
sentences.zh: 一个下着小雨的周二，她在人行道中间停下脚步，低头看着那块湿漉漉的铁圆盖，问了自己一个改变了她一整年的简单问题：它下面是什么？

sentences.en: The next morning, a city engineer in a yellow coat met her at the bus stop, and he used a long metal instrument to lift the heavy cover, carefully, like a nurse waking a sleeping patient.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，一位穿黄外套的市政工程师在公交站等她；他用一根长长的金属器械小心翼翼地掀开沉重的井盖，像护士唤醒一位睡着的病人。

sentences.en: Below the street, in a darkness that smelled of cold stone and old iron, water pipes and power lines formed a hidden structure, layered like the floors of an upside-down house.
sentences.zh: 街道之下，在那片散发着冷石头和旧铁味道的黑暗里，水管与电线组成了一套看不见的结构，像一栋倒过来的房子，一层压着一层。

sentences.en: Clean water arrived through one fat pipe and waste water left through another, and the two of them never mixed, never touched, and never once argued about their very different duties.
sentences.zh: 清水从一根粗管子进来，废水从另一根管子离开，两条管线从不掺和、从不碰面，也从不为彼此天差地别的职责拌一句嘴。

sentences.en: Thick copper cables carried the electricity for the whole street, while thin glass fibers, no thicker than a single hair, carried the Internet, the photographs, the films, and the late-night messages of a thousand strangers.
sentences.zh: 粗粗的铜缆为整条街输送电力；而细得像头发丝的玻璃光纤，传输着互联网、照片、电影，和一千个陌生人的深夜留言。

sentences.en: "People call this the real infrastructure of the city," the engineer said quietly, "but almost nobody looks at it until something breaks, and that, I think, is the city's oldest joke."
sentences.zh: "人们管这个叫这座城市真正的基础设施，"工程师轻声说，"可直到哪儿坏了，几乎没有一个人肯看它一眼——我觉得，这是这座城市最老的一个笑话。"

sentences.en: The pipes ran below the pavement in a neat geometry of right angles and straight lines, turning at every corner like a patient train following invisible rails under the shops.
sentences.zh: 管道在路面下沿着直角和直线构成的一套利落几何排布，每个街角都规规矩矩地转弯，像一列有耐心的火车，追着店铺底下看不见的铁轨走。

sentences.en: Workers constructed this pipe network more than eighty years ago, layer by layer, winter by winter, with shovels, bricks, and far more patience than any modern machine could ever understand.
sentences.zh: 八十多年前，工人们一层一层、一个冬天接一个冬天地建造了这套管网，靠的是铁锹、砖头，和一台任何现代机器都理解不了的耐心。

sentences.en: The engineer explained that the geology under the street — soft river clay, then wet sand, then hard old rock — quietly decided where every pipe was allowed to sleep, and for how long.
sentences.zh: 工程师解释说，真正悄悄说了算的，是街道底下的地质——先是松软的河泥，再是湿沙，然后是坚硬的老岩层：哪根管子能睡在哪儿、能睡多久，全由它定。

sentences.en: "If one pipe breaks, we follow the printed instructions, close the nearest valve, and repair everything at night, while the street above is sleeping and the buses are parked," he said.
sentences.zh: "哪根水管坏了，我们就照着印好的操作说明，关掉最近的阀门，趁夜里抢修——那时上面的街睡了，公交也进场了。"他说。

sentences.en: A broken-down truck can obstruct the street above for a whole morning, and everybody complains loudly about it, but the quiet pipes below can work for decades without one single word of thanks.
sentences.zh: 一辆抛锚的卡车能堵住上面的街道一整个上午，人人都会大声抱怨；可下面那些不出声的管子，干上几十年也听不到一句谢。

sentences.en: Lin looked down into the dark square hole and felt the cool, damp air rising against her face, soft and slow, like the breath of the city itself.
sentences.zh: 琳朝那个黑漆漆的方洞里望下去，一股清凉潮湿的空气软软地、慢慢地扑上她的脸，像这座城市自己的呼吸。

sentences.en: The first ten meters held water, power, and messages, all moving in silence under her shoes, and she walked home that evening without ever stepping on a manhole cover again.
sentences.zh: 最初的十米装着水、电和讯息，一切都在她的鞋底下无声地流动；那天傍晚她走回家去，从此再没有像从前那样踩过任何一块井盖。

questions.q: What question did Lin ask herself near her bus stop?
options: Who built the bus stop?
When does the bus arrive?
What lies below the manhole cover?
Why is the street so noisy?
questions.explain: 第2句 "she asked herself one simple question... what lies below it?"，it 指井盖，她问的是井盖下面有什么。

questions.q: According to the passage, what carried the Internet under the street?
options: Thick copper cables.
Thin glass fibers.
Old water pipes.
Metal instruments.
questions.explain: 第6句 "thin glass fibers... carried the Internet, the photographs, the films"，网络信号由细玻璃光纤传输。

questions.q: What did the engineer call the real infrastructure of the city?
options: The tall towers.
The busy bus stop.
The pipes and lines under the street.
The manhole covers.
questions.explain: 第7句，工程师掀开井盖、指着下方的水管电线说 "People call this the real infrastructure of the city"，指的是街道下的管线。

questions.q: Why did Lin never step on a manhole cover the same way again?
options: Because the covers were all replaced that year.
Because she now knew the silent water, power and messages moving under her feet.
Because the engineer told her the covers were dangerous.
Because she stopped taking the bus.
questions.explain: 由第14句 "The first ten meters held water, power, and messages, all moving in silence under her shoes, and she walked home... without ever stepping on a manhole cover again" 可推知，她看见了井盖下的世界，从此走路的心情不同了。

questions.q: In sentence 8, "a neat geometry of right angles and straight lines," the word "geometry" means ______.
options: the study of shapes, lines and measurement
a kind of water pipe
a street map for buses
a book of old photographs
questions.explain: 第8句。词根 geo- 表示"大地"，-metry 表示"测量"：geometry 本义是"丈量土地"的学问，即几何学；这里指管道按直线和直角排成的利落布局。

title: 《城市地下十米》· 隧道里的钢铁巨兽

sentences.en: Under the east side of the city, where the old maps showed only grey clay and vegetable fields, a new metro line was under construction, and the whole city argued happily all year about the color of its future trains.
sentences.zh: 在城市东侧的地下——旧地图上那里只有灰泥和菜地——一条新地铁线正在施工，全城人整年都在兴高采烈地争论未来列车该是什么颜色。

sentences.en: The machine that dug the tunnel was called "Little Dragon", and it was not an animal but a tunnel boring machine, forty meters long, like a hungry steel train slowly eating its own railway in the dark.
sentences.zh: 负责掘进的机器叫"小龙"，它不是动物，而是一台隧道掘进机，足足四十米长，像一列饥饿的钢铁火车，在黑暗里一口一口吃掉属于自己的铁路。

sentences.en: At the front, a spinning wheel with rows of metal teeth cut the earth in front of it, and the teeth were changed every single week, because rock is patient and steel, in the end, is not.
sentences.zh: 机身前端是一只旋转的刀盘，一排排金属齿切开面前的泥土；刀齿每周都得换，因为岩石有耐心，而钢铁终究没有。

sentences.en: Engineers watched the pressure gauges every minute, because soft mud under the city could destroy the cutter's face in one unlucky hour, and destruction down here cost months, not days.
sentences.zh: 工程师每一分钟都盯着压力表，因为城下的软泥要是不走运，一个钟头就能毁掉整个刀盘——在这里，一次毁灭赔进去的是几个月，不是几天。

sentences.en: When the cutter met a wall of hard rock, the whole machine slowed down and sang, a deep, tired note that traveled up through the ground and into people's tea cups on the surface.
sentences.zh: 刀盘碰上硬岩壁时，整台机器就慢下来唱歌，那声低沉疲惫的轰鸣顺着地层一路往上，钻进地面上人们的茶杯里。

sentences.en: Behind the cutter, workers constructed the tunnel wall ring by careful ring, and each concrete ring locked into the next one until the whole tube became one strong, patient structure.
sentences.zh: 刀盘身后，工人们一环一环、仔仔细细地建造隧道壁，每一环混凝土管片咬住下一环，直到整条隧道成为一条结实而有耐性的结构。

sentences.en: Every morning, the team's geologist studied the soil that the machine had eaten the day before, and she told the crew what the next hundred meters were probably dreaming about.
sentences.zh: 每天清晨，队里的地质学家研究机器头一天"吃"进去的土样，然后告诉大伙儿，前面那一百米大概正做着什么梦。

sentences.en: "If we find an old riverbed, the mud is soft and wet, and the machine must slow down and hold the walls with all of its strength," she warned them more than once.
sentences.zh: "要是碰上古河道，泥就会又软又湿，机器必须减速，拿出全部力气撑住两壁。"她不止一次提醒大家。

sentences.en: Her instruments measured the ground every hour, and one rainy Thursday they found hidden water sleeping inside a pocket of wet sand, exactly where the old maps had promised nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 她的仪器每小时测量一次地层；一个下着雨的周四，仪器在一兜湿沙子里找到了藏着的水——偏偏就在旧地图信誓旦旦说"什么都没有"的地方。

sentences.en: The line of the tunnel had been drawn on paper with the purest geometry, but the geology below the city had its own older ideas about straight lines.
sentences.zh: 隧道的线路是用最纯粹的几何画在纸上的，可城市底下的地质，对"直线"自有一套更老的主意。

sentences.en: The engineers instructed the machine drivers hour by hour, and the great steel animal turned, patiently, around every surprise that the old ground pushed into its path.
sentences.zh: 工程师们一小时一小时地给司机下达指令，而这头钢铁巨兽呢，不慌不忙地绕开老地层塞到它路上的每一个意外。

sentences.en: When the work finally finished, Little Dragon had constructed two kilometers of tunnel in exactly one year, and it was taken apart with almost the same ceremony as a retiring teacher.
sentences.zh: 工程收尾时，小龙用整整一年建成了两公里隧道；拆解它时的仪式感，几乎不输给一位荣休的老教师。

sentences.en: Today, bright trains run through the dark tube, and the passengers look at their phones and never once think about Little Dragon, its metal teeth, or its long, patient, unfed hunger.
sentences.zh: 如今，明亮的车厢在那条黑暗的管道里穿行，乘客们低头看手机，没有一个人想起过小龙、它的金属齿，和它那份漫长的、没喂饱过的耐心胃口。

sentences.en: The machine destroyed only rock and left a smooth, straight road through the dark earth, and the city, which never learned its digger's name, sleeps a little better above it.
sentences.zh: 这台机器只毁坏过岩石，却在黑暗的地层里留下了一条平整笔直的路；而这座从没记住挖掘者名字的城市，在它上方睡得踏实了一点。

questions.q: What was "Little Dragon"?
options: A dangerous animal in the tunnel.
A tunnel boring machine.
The first metro train.
A famous engineer.
questions.explain: 第2句 "it was not an animal but a tunnel boring machine, forty meters long"，小龙是四十米长的隧道掘进机。

questions.q: Why did engineers watch the pressure gauges every minute?
options: To check the weather.
To count the passengers.
Because soft mud could destroy the cutter's face.
Because the machine needed electricity.
questions.explain: 第4句 "soft mud under the city could destroy the cutter's face in one unlucky hour"，盯压力表是为了防软泥毁掉刀盘。

questions.q: What did the geologist do every morning?
options: She drove the boring machine.
She sold tickets to passengers.
She studied the soil and told the crew what lay ahead.
She cleaned the tunnel.
questions.explain: 第7句 "the team's geologist studied the soil that the machine had eaten the day before, and she told the crew what the next hundred meters were probably dreaming about"，她研究土样、预报前方地层。

questions.q: What can we learn about the old maps from sentence 9?
options: They were drawn by the geologist herself.
They did not show everything under the city.
They showed too much underground water.
They were maps of the new metro line.
questions.explain: 第9句 "they found hidden water... exactly where the old maps had promised nothing at all"——旧地图上什么都没标，地下却藏着水，可见旧图并没有画全城下的一切。

questions.q: In sentence 4, "destruction down here cost months, not days," the word "destruction" means ______.
options: the act of building faster
the act of destroying or ruining something
a kind of underground train
a pressure gauge
questions.explain: 第4句。词根 struct- 表示"建造"：de-(毁坏)+struct(建造)→把建造好的东西拆毁→毁灭。刀盘被毁，工期就要多赔几个月。

title: 《城市地下十米》· 老城的地下层

sentences.en: In the old part of the city, where the streets are narrow and the bricks remember everything, the underground had a much longer and more human story than any metro line.
sentences.zh: 在老城区，街道窄，砖头什么都记得；这里地下的故事，比任何一条地铁线都长得多，也更有人味儿。

sentences.en: During the war, people dug deep shelters under their houses with shovels, buckets, and borrowed courage, and they stored water, rice, and warm blankets in the cold halls below.
sentences.zh: 战争年代，人们靠铁锹、木桶和跟人借来的胆量，在自家房子底下挖出深深的防空洞，在那些寒冷的大厅里存上水、米和厚毯子。

sentences.en: After the war, the empty shelters were reconstructed into shops and small warehouses, and the city, which needed almost everything in those years, used the dark rooms for almost everything.
sentences.zh: 战争结束后，空置的防空洞被改建成了商铺和小仓库；那些年这座城几乎什么都缺，于是这些黑屋子几乎被派上了各种用场。

sentences.en: Grandma Chen was a small girl when the shelters first opened as an underground market, and she still walks down there every week after week, slowly, in her good coat, like a person rereading a favorite page.
sentences.zh: 防空洞第一次开放成地下商场那年，陈奶奶还是个小姑娘；如今她一个星期接一个星期地下到那儿去，穿着出客的好大衣慢慢走，像一个人重读最爱的一页书。

sentences.en: "The walls were cold, and the lamps were few," she remembers, "but the market was warm and full of voices, and in those years, warm voices were everything a person needed to go on."
sentences.zh: "墙是凉的，灯也没几盏，"她记得，"可市场里暖烘烘、满是人声；在那些年，一屋子热乎的人声，就是一个人撑下去需要的全部。"

sentences.en: Workers constructed new stairs, bright lights, and clean white signs, but they kept the old brick arches, because the arches were part of the original structure, and the structure, not the signs, was the memory.
sentences.zh: 工人们建了新楼梯、亮灯和干净的白招牌，却留下了那些老砖拱——因为拱顶是最初结构的一部分，而是这结构、而不是招牌，才是记忆本身。

sentences.en: The arches had been built with simple, honest geometry, half-circles of brick holding hands above every shop door, strong enough to carry the whole street without any concrete at all.
sentences.zh: 那些拱顶用的是简单、老实的几何：半圆的砖在每家店铺门顶上手拉着手，一滴混凝土都不用，就足以扛起整条街。

sentences.en: Some doors at the ends of the long halls have stayed closed for forty long years, because the old tunnels behind them are not safe, and the geology behind them has shifted, over the years, like a tired sleeper.
sentences.zh: 长廊尽头有几扇门，一关就关了整整四十年，因为门后的老隧道已经不安全——门后的地层，这些年里像一个睡累了的人，翻过身了。

sentences.en: In one corner of the market, a small museum shows photographs of the construction from 1969: young workers, muddy boots, and faces proud enough to light up the dark.
sentences.zh: 市场的一个角落里，有座小博物馆，陈列着 1969 年施工时的照片：年轻的工人、糊满泥的靴子，还有一张张骄傲得能照亮黑暗的脸。

sentences.en: A guide instructed the visiting children to walk quietly through the narrow hall, and the children, for once in their short lives, obeyed, because the silence down there felt older than their grandparents.
sentences.zh: 讲解员叮嘱来参观的孩子们安静地走过狭窄的展厅；这一回，孩子们居然照办了——因为那底下的安静，闻起来比他们的爷爷奶奶还要老。

sentences.en: History was layered under the city like pages in a heavy book: war under peace, fear under bread, and destruction under daily life, page after page after page.
sentences.zh: 历史在这座城市下面层层叠叠，像一本厚书里的书页：战争压在和平下面，恐惧压在面包下面，毁灭压在日常生活下面，一页，又一页，又一页。

sentences.en: The instruments in the museum measure nothing at all, but they still teach: an old lamp, a cracked rice bowl, and a wartime clock that stopped forever, one black evening, at a quarter to nine.
sentences.zh: 博物馆里那些"仪器"什么也不测量，却照样教人：一盏旧灯、一只裂了口的饭碗，还有一只战时钟，在某个漆黑的夜晚永远停在了八点四十五分。

sentences.en: Grandma Chen buys her warm bread in a hall that was built to hide from bombs, walks slowly up the new stairs, and returns to the bright, noisy street above.
sentences.zh: 陈奶奶在一座当年为躲避炸弹而建的大厅里买了热乎乎的面包，慢慢走上新楼梯，回到上面那条又亮堂又喧闹的街上。

sentences.en: "The same city," she says to nobody in particular, "just one floor apart," and the street above carries her home without ever knowing what it stands on, or what it owes.
sentences.zh: "还是这座城，"她像是随口地说，"不过隔了一层楼。"上面的街道载着她回家，却从不知道自己脚下踩着什么，欠着什么。

questions.q: What did people store in the deep shelters during the war?
options: Warm bread for the market.
Water, rice, and warm blankets.
Construction tools.
Old photographs.
questions.explain: 第2句 "they stored water, rice, and warm blankets in the cold halls below"，战时防空洞里存的是水、米和毯子。

questions.q: What happened to the empty shelters after the war?
options: They were filled with rocks.
They were forgotten by everyone.
They were reconstructed into shops and small warehouses.
They became train stations.
questions.explain: 第3句 "the empty shelters were reconstructed into shops and small warehouses"，防空洞战后改建成了商铺和小仓库。

questions.q: What does the small museum in the corner show?
options: Old maps of the metro.
Photographs of the construction from 1969.
Modern computers.
Bread from the market.
questions.explain: 第9句 "a small museum shows photographs of the construction from 1969"，小博物馆陈列的是 1969 年施工的照片。

questions.q: Why did the workers keep the old brick arches when they built the new market?
options: Because concrete was too expensive.
Because the arches were part of the original structure, and the structure was the memory.
Because the law required it.
Because the arches were fashionable.
questions.explain: 第6句 "they kept the old brick arches, because the arches were part of the original structure, and the structure was the memory"——拱顶是原始结构的一部分，留住它就是留住记忆。

questions.q: In sentence 3, "the empty shelters were reconstructed into shops," the word "reconstructed" means ______.
options: to build again in a new form
to destroy completely
to sell to strangers
to close forever
questions.explain: 第3句。词根 struct- 表示"建造"：re-(重新)+construct(建造)→重新建造、改建——防空洞保留主体，改成了商铺和仓库。

title: 《城市地下十米》· 城市坐在什么上面

sentences.en: A geologist named Dr. Wu has loved this city for thirty years, for one simple, strange reason: "It sits on a young river plain," she says, "and the ground remembers everything that ever happened here."
sentences.zh: 一位姓吴的地质学家爱了这座城市三十年，理由既简单又奇怪："它坐在一片年轻的河流平原上，"她说，"而地面记得在这里发生过的一切。"

sentences.en: In the small park behind the central library, her team drilled a deep, narrow hole and pulled up thin soil samples, one after another, like a careful nurse drawing the city's slow, grey blood.
sentences.zh: 在中央图书馆后面的小公园里，她的团队钻了一个又深又细的孔，把一管管细细的土样取上来，像一位细心的护士，抽取这座城市缓慢的灰血。

sentences.en: The top layer held black, rich mud, because the great river had flooded this ground a thousand times, spring after spring, before anyone in the whole region thought of drawing the very first map.
sentences.zh: 最上面一层是肥沃的黑泥，因为在大河春复一春地泛滥过千百次之后，整个地区才有人想起来画第一张地图。

sentences.en: Below the mud lay an old riverbed, a structure of smooth, round stones, rolled soft by water that stopped flowing here long before the first stone house was built.
sentences.zh: 泥层之下是一条古河道，一片由光滑圆石构成的结构——那些石头被流水磨圆，而流水停下的年代，比第一间石头房子还早。

sentences.en: Deeper still, the drill touched hard, grey rock formed by ancient volcanoes, and the drill bit came up hot, dusty, tired, and quietly satisfied, like a woodpecker after a very long, very honest tree.
sentences.zh: 再往下，钻头碰到了远古火山形成的坚硬灰岩；钻头上来时又烫、又是泥、又累，却带着一种安安静静的满足，像啄木鸟啃完一棵很长、很实诚的树。

sentences.en: Each layer, Dr. Wu explains to her students, is a page, and geology is simply the art of reading them in order, from the youngest grass down to the oldest, deepest fire.
sentences.zh: 吴博士向学生们解释：每一层都是一页，地质学不过是一门按顺序读它们的技艺——从最年轻的草，一路读到最古老、最深处的火。

sentences.en: "Once you can read the pages," she instructed her students at the edge of the drill hole, "you will never see a flat, boring city in the same way again."
sentences.zh: "等你们会读这些书页了，"她站在钻孔边上教学生们，"你们再看任何一座平平无奇的城市，眼光就再也不一样了。"

sentences.en: The old river channel, buried but never quite dead, still carries groundwater slowly beneath the busy city streets, a hidden artery that nobody has ever drawn on the bus maps.
sentences.zh: 那条被掩埋却没死透的古河道，至今仍在繁忙的城市街道下缓缓输送着地下水——一条隐秘的动脉，只是从没有人把它画上公交地图。

sentences.en: Engineers used geometry to map the layers before constructing anything new and heavy above them, because a building that argues with the ground below always loses that long argument in the end.
sentences.zh: 工程师先用几何绘出地层图，然后才在上面建造任何新的、有分量的东西——因为一栋和脚下地层讲道理的楼，在这场漫长的争论里到头来总是输的那一方。

sentences.en: One of Dr. Wu's maps showed a buried channel running exactly under the planned site of the new hospital, soft as wet soap and just as friendly to any heavy wall above it.
sentences.zh: 吴博士的一张图纸上，一条被掩埋的河道不偏不倚，正好从新医院的规划选址底下穿过——那里的地面软得像湿肥皂，对上面任何一堵重墙也同样"友好"。

sentences.en: Because the ground there was soft, the city moved the new hospital two kilometers to the north, where older, harder rock had been waiting patiently under the deep, quiet grass for millions of quiet years.
sentences.zh: 由于那里的地面松软，城市把新医院向北挪了两公里——那底下更老、更硬的岩层，已经在深深、安静的草皮下面，安安静静等了几百万年。

sentences.en: Her instruments listen to the layers all winter long, and geothermal heat sleeps in the deepest rock, patient and enormous, waiting quietly under every single pair of feet in the whole city.
sentences.zh: 她的仪器听了一整个冬天地层的声音；而地热能沉睡在最深的岩层里，耐心又庞大，在全城每一双脚底下静静等候。

sentences.en: "If you understand the layers," Dr. Wu says, rolling up her maps as the sun goes down behind the tall towers, "the city stops being a picture and becomes a living thing."
sentences.zh: "如果你读懂了这些层，"吴博士说，在高高的塔楼后面、落日里卷起图纸，"这座城市就不再是一张画，而成了一件活物。"

sentences.en: She walks home above the quiet layers that evening, and the street lamps come on above a million unread pages, readable, patient, and full of warm, slow fire.
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚，她从安睡的地层上方走回家去；路灯次第亮起，照着底下百万页无人读过的书——可读、有耐心，而且藏着温热的、缓慢的火。

questions.q: Why was the top layer of soil black mud?
options: Because workers spilled paint there.
Because the great river flooded there many times.
Because the volcanoes burned the city.
Because the market dropped bread there.
questions.explain: 第3句 "the great river had flooded this ground a thousand times, spring after spring"，黑泥来自大河年复一年的泛滥。

questions.q: What did the drill touch below the old riverbed?
options: More black mud.
Cold groundwater.
Hard rock formed by ancient volcanoes.
An old shelter.
questions.explain: 第5句 "Deeper still, the drill touched hard, grey rock formed by ancient volcanoes"，古河道之下是火山形成的硬岩。

questions.q: Why did the city move the new hospital to the north?
options: Because the north was closer to the river.
Because the ground at the planned site was soft.
Because the north was cheaper.
Because the doctors asked for it.
questions.explain: 第10-11句：选址下面埋着软如湿肥皂的古河道，"Because the ground there was soft, the city moved the new hospital two kilometers to the north"。

questions.q: What did Dr. Wu mean when she said "the ground remembers everything"?
options: The ground can think like a person.
Every layer of soil keeps a record of what happened to the land long ago.
The ground is angry with the city.
Rivers have good memories.
questions.explain: 第1句的这句话与第6句呼应："Each layer... is a page, and geology is simply the art of reading them"——泥土、河石、火山岩层层层叠叠，等于把过去全都记了下来。

questions.q: In sentence 12, "geothermal heat sleeps in the deepest rock," the word "geothermal" means ______.
options: heat from burning coal
heat that comes from inside the earth
cold wind from the north
a kind of thermometer
questions.explain: 第12句。词根 geo- 表示"大地"，therm- 表示"热"：geothermal＝大地内部的热，即地热。

title: 《城市地下十米》· 第二座城市

sentences.en: Engineers now dream of a second city hidden below the first one, and, unlike most dreams, this one comes with drawings, budgets, and very long, very serious meetings about fire escapes.
sentences.zh: 如今，工程师们梦想在第一座城市之下再藏一座城；与众梦不同的是，这一个梦是带图纸、带预算，还带着一场场关于消防通道的漫长会议的。

sentences.en: In one pilot project, a data center moved underground last spring, into a wide, dry, quiet hall where the thick old walls contained the noise of a thousand busy machines.
sentences.zh: 在一个试点项目里，一座数据中心去年春天搬进了地下，住进一座又宽又干又安静的大厅；厚厚的老墙，把一千台忙个不停的机器的噪音关在了里面。

sentences.en: The machines produce heat all day and all night, but the earth around them swallows the sound completely, and the street above hears nothing louder than ordinary rain on the wet pavement.
sentences.zh: 机器白天黑夜地发热，可四周的土层把声音吞了个干干净净；上面的街道听到的，无非比落在湿路面上的寻常雨声更响一点的东西。

sentences.en: The ground stays cool all year, like a cellar that remembers winter even in the middle of July, so the servers need far less electricity for cooling than their cousins in the glass towers above.
sentences.zh: 地下全年凉爽，像一间七月中旬还记得冬天的地窖，于是服务器需要的散热电费，远比它们玻璃塔楼里的堂兄弟们少得多。

sentences.en: In another hall, farmers grow vegetables under purple lamps without one single drop of real sunlight, and the long green rows look like a whole library of quiet, glowing green books.
sentences.zh: 在另一个大厅里，农人在紫光灯下种菜，一滴真正的阳光也不用；一垄一垄的绿，看上去像整整一图书馆安安静静、微微发光的绿书。

sentences.en: The farm uses the servers' wasted heat to warm the plants in winter, so the two halls, one loud and one green, quietly keep each other alive and warm through the cold months.
sentences.zh: 农场用服务器排出的废热，在冬天为植物供暖；于是一间喧闹、一间碧绿的两个大厅，就这样在寒月里悄悄地互相养活、互相取暖。

sentences.en: An architect showed her finished plan to the whole city last month: shops, farms, and libraries stacked in a deep, careful structure, floor under floor, light under light, stair under stair.
sentences.zh: 上个月，一位建筑师向全城展示了她画完的图纸：商铺、农场和图书馆叠放进一个纵深、精密的结构里——楼层压着楼层，光压着光，楼梯压着楼梯。

sentences.en: "We construct down, not up," she said, "because the surface belongs to trees, children, and dogs, and the surface is the only sky that an underground city will ever have."
sentences.zh: "我们向下建造，而不是向上，"她说，"因为地表属于树木、孩子和狗；对一座地下城来说，地表是它此生唯一的天空。"

sentences.en: In a way, the first city becomes the superstructure of the second, and the hidden infrastructure of stairs, pipes, and halls quietly holds them both together.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，第一座城成了第二座城的上层建筑；而楼梯、管道与大厅这套隐形的基础设施，把两座城一起稳稳托在手里。

sentences.en: The engineers drew the deep halls with clean, careful geometry, wide stairs and honest corners, because underground, a wrong angle is not a question of style but a very serious question of safety.
sentences.zh: 工程师用干净、讲究的几何来画这些深厅：宽楼梯、实打实的转角——因为在地下，一个错误的角度不是审美问题，是性命攸关的安全问题。

sentences.en: But the underground needs strict rules, because water and darkness never forgive mistakes, and one small flood down below can close a busy supermarket for a whole month.
sentences.zh: 但地下世界需要严苛的规矩，因为水和黑暗从不原谅错误；地下一场小小的淹水，就能让一家热闹的超市关上一整月。

sentences.en: Firefighters instruct the crews every month, and every door in the deep halls opens onto a bright, wide escape stair that points straight up, like an arrow, to the open sky.
sentences.zh: 消防员每个月都对地下团队培训一次；深厅里的每一扇门都通向一道又亮又宽的逃生梯，像一支箭，笔直指向开阔的天空。

sentences.en: A good underground city must sustain its air, light, and water for a hundred quiet years; geothermal heat warms the deepest floors from far below, and engineers test the walls with sensitive instruments, repairing every hairline crack early.
sentences.zh: 一座好的地下城市，必须让它的空气、光线和水安安稳稳维持一百年：地热从极深处为最底的楼层供暖，工程师用精密仪器检测墙体，每一道发丝般的裂缝都趁早修补。

sentences.en: Lin, now a student of engineering, visited the new center last month; she stood ten meters under the busy street with one hand on a warm pipe, and finally, after all those years, understood the old manhole cover near her bus stop.
sentences.zh: 如今已学工程的琳，上个月参观了这座新中心；她站在喧闹街道下方十米处，一只手贴着温热的管道，隔了这么多年，终于读懂了公交站旁那块老井盖。

questions.q: Why do the underground servers need less electricity for cooling?
options: Because the machines are very small.
Because the ground stays cool all year.
Because the farmers help them.
Because the city pays the bill.
questions.explain: 第4句 "The ground stays cool all year... so the servers need far less electricity for cooling"，地下常年凉爽，散热耗电更少。

questions.q: What did the underground farm use to warm the plants in winter?
options: Sunlight from mirrors.
Coal from the old boiler.
The servers' wasted heat.
Warm underground rivers.
questions.explain: 第6句 "The farm uses the servers' wasted heat to warm the plants in winter"，农场用的是服务器废热。

questions.q: Why do the new architects construct down instead of up?
options: Because underground buildings are cheaper.
Because the surface belongs to trees, children, and dogs.
Because the ground is softer.
Because tall towers are dangerous.
questions.explain: 第8句 "We construct down, not up, because the surface belongs to trees, children, and dogs"，把地表留给树木、孩子和狗，所以向下建。

questions.q: Why does the author say that water and darkness "never forgive mistakes"?
options: Because the underground city is very rich.
Because small underground mistakes, like floods, can have serious and lasting results.
Because the engineers are always wrong.
Because fire happens every month.
questions.explain: 第11句 "water and darkness never forgive mistakes, and one small flood below can close a supermarket for a whole month"——地下一场小淹水就能带来整月的停业，可见地下容不得差错。

questions.q: In sentence 9, "the first city becomes the superstructure of the second," the word "superstructure" means ______.
options: the part built on top of a base
the deepest floor
a kind of underground train
an escape stair
questions.explain: 第9句。词根 struct- 表示"建造"：super-(在上方)+structure(结构)→建在基底之上的结构，即"上层建筑"。

title: 《暖屋计划》· 零下二十度的清晨

sentences.en: In the northern town of Qinghe, January mornings arrive at minus twenty degrees, and the bare trees along the street stand in the cold like long lines of patient grey statues.
sentences.zh: 在北方小城清河，一月的清晨总是以零下二十度报到；街边光秃秃的树在严寒里站着，像一列列耐心的灰色雕像。

sentences.en: Grandma Bai wakes at six, before the radio, and looks first at the thermometer on her wall, an old glass tube with a thin red line inside, like a small, honest, well-behaved snake.
sentences.zh: 白奶奶六点就醒，比广播还早；她先看墙上的温度计——一支旧玻璃管，里头一根细细的红线，像一条小小的、诚实的、守规矩的蛇。

sentences.en: The red line has fallen again during the long night, and she writes the new number in her notebook, page after page, winter after winter, in handwriting that has not changed since 1980.
sentences.zh: 那根红线在漫漫长夜里又落了下去；她把新的数字记进本子，一页又一页，一个冬天接一个冬天，字迹从 1980 年起就没变过。

sentences.en: Her old building is famous in town, but not for good reasons: people call it "the icebox", and the local children joke that the thin walls are made of cold air held together with hope.
sentences.zh: 她住的这栋老楼在小城很有名，可惜不是因为什么好事：人们叫它"冰窖"，镇上的孩子们开玩笑说，那几堵薄墙是用希望粘起来的冷空气。

sentences.en: The concrete walls are thin and cannot contain the heat inside, and the north wind finds every small crack and seam and sings through it at night, in long, confident whistles.
sentences.zh: 混凝土墙很薄，留不住屋里的热气；北风总能找到每一道细缝和接缝，在夜里像吹口哨一样，长长地、笃定地穿堂而过。

sentences.en: No thermostat controls the old iron radiators, so the first-floor rooms cook like steamed bread in a basket, while the fifth-floor rooms freeze like the inside of a fish truck.
sentences.zh: 老式铁暖气片上没有任何恒温器，于是底楼的屋子热得像笼屉里蒸着的馒头，顶楼的屋子却冷得像运鱼卡车内部。

sentences.en: When the heating pipes knock in the walls, the whole sleeping floor can hear them, and some neighbors knock back sometimes, out of loneliness or solidarity, or both, nobody knows which.
sentences.zh: 暖气管在墙里一敲，整层睡梦中的楼都听得见；有时候有邻居也回敲两下——是孤单呢，还是同病相怜，还是都有呢，谁也说不清。

sentences.en: A young, serious engineer named Xiao Yu lives on the fourth floor, and she measures the walls with a thermal camera, a black instrument that shows heat as colors.
sentences.zh: 四楼住着一位年轻、较真的工程师，名叫小余；她用一台热成像仪测量墙体——一台能把热量显示成颜色的黑色仪器。

sentences.en: On the little screen, cold air leaks in around the old windows like blue rivers, and the warm air inside flows out through the same gaps, meeting in the middle of the glass like two tired, polite armies.
sentences.zh: 小屏幕上，冷空气绕着旧窗渗进来，像一条条蓝色的河；屋里的暖空气又从同一批缝隙流出去，两支又累又客气的军队在玻璃中间相遇。

sentences.en: "Heat always flows from warm to cold, and it never once asks your permission," Xiao Yu says, "and that single stubborn fact is the very beginning of all thermodynamics."
sentences.zh: "热永远从暖处流向冷处，而且一次也不会征求你的同意，"小余说，"这唯一一条倔强的规律，就是全部热学的开头。"

sentences.en: The old drawings of the building follow a simple, square geometry, and nobody in 1979 drew any insulation at all, because fuel was cheap and winters were expected to be brave.
sentences.zh: 这栋楼的老图纸用的是横平竖直的简单几何，1979 年没有一个人画保温层——那会儿燃料便宜，冬天嘛，大家默认要硬扛。

sentences.en: Xiao Yu has a friend, a geologist, who once told her, over a slow cup of tea, that the geology under Qinghe holds warm rock and geothermal heat, though the whole town above it burns coal like there is no tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 小余有位地质学家朋友，曾经就着一杯慢慢喝的茶告诉她：清河地下的地质里藏着温热的岩层和地热，可它上面这整座小镇，烧起煤来却像没有明天。

sentences.en: Grandpa Bai, who studied a little geology in his young years, likes to say that the warm ground below is the town's best-kept warm secret, sleeping all winter under the frost.
sentences.zh: 白爷爷年轻时学过一点地质，他爱说：脚底下那片暖地，是这座小镇守得最好的暖秘密，一冬天一冬天地在冻土下面睡着。

sentences.en: Something has to change before the next winter, because no one in the building, young or old, can sustain another long January of blue rivers, cold floors, and long, confident, singing wind.
sentences.zh: 下个冬天来临之前，总得改变些什么了；因为这栋楼里无论老小，谁也撑不过又一个满是蓝河、冷地板和笃定风哨的漫长一月。

questions.q: What does Grandma Bai look at first when she wakes at six?
options: Her notebook.
The thermometer on her wall.
The street outside.
The thermal camera.
questions.explain: 第2句 "she looks first at the thermometer on her wall, an old glass tube with a thin red line inside"，她醒来先看墙上的温度计。

questions.q: Why did the first-floor rooms cook while the fifth-floor rooms froze?
options: Because the windows were broken.
Because no thermostat controlled the old iron radiators.
Because the north wind was too strong.
Because the sun never reached the fifth floor.
questions.explain: 第6句 "No thermostat controls the old iron radiators, so the first-floor rooms cook... while the fifth-floor rooms freeze"，暖气片上没有恒温器，各屋冷暖不均。

questions.q: What did Xiao Yu's thermal camera show around the old windows?
options: Warm air leaving the roof.
Cold air leaking in like blue rivers.
Broken furniture in the rooms.
Old pictures inside the walls.
questions.explain: 第9句 "cold air leaks in around the old windows like blue rivers"，热成像仪显示冷空气像蓝河一样绕窗渗入。

questions.q: Why do the children joke that the walls are made of "cold air held together with hope"?
options: Because the children are afraid of the wind.
Because the thin walls keep in so little heat that the building hardly feels warmer than outside.
Because the building is very new.
Because the children love physics class.
questions.explain: 由第4句的玩笑和第5句 "The concrete walls are thin and cannot contain the heat inside" 可推知：墙太薄、存不住热，屋里几乎和外面一样冷。

questions.q: In sentence 10, "that single stubborn fact is the beginning of all thermodynamics," the word "thermodynamics" means ______.
options: the science of how heat moves and works
a kind of camera
the study of old buildings
a winter sport
questions.explain: 第10句。词根 therm- 表示"热"：thermodynamics 是研究热量如何流动、如何做功的科学，即热力学。

title: 《暖屋计划》· 老锅炉的心跳

sentences.en: The heart of the old building is a coal boiler in the cold basement, a black, round-shouldered machine that has burned coal for forty years, winter after winter, night after night, without one long rest.
sentences.zh: 这栋老楼的心脏，是冷飕飕地下室里的一台燃煤锅炉——一台黑黢黢、溜肩膀的机器，四十年了，一个冬天接一个冬天、一夜接一夜地烧着，没歇过一个长假。

sentences.en: Mr. Han, the boiler man, maintains the machine with wrenches, patience, and a small pocket radio that only plays old opera, and he knows the machine's moods better than his own.
sentences.zh: 锅炉工韩师傅，靠扳手、耐心和一台只放老歌剧的袖珍收音机维持着这台机器；它的脾气，他比自己心里的还清楚。

sentences.en: "This steel tank is durable," he likes to say, patting it like an old horse, "but the pipes are tired now, and tired pipes always lie about their age."
sentences.zh: "这口钢罐子是耐用，"他爱这么说着，像拍一匹老马那样拍拍它，"可管子已经累了，累了的管子，报起年龄来从来不说实话。"

sentences.en: A thermometer hangs beside the boiler, because the water temperature matters every single hour of the night, and Mr. Han reads it the way farmers read the morning sky.
sentences.zh: 锅炉边挂着一支温度计，因为每个钟头的水温都马虎不得；韩师傅读它，就像庄稼人读清晨的天。

sentences.en: Hot water rises through the pipes, and a warm thermal current climbs slowly from floor to floor, warming the first rooms quickly and the last rooms, in a kind democracy, almost never.
sentences.zh: 热水顺着管道上行，一股温热流一层一层慢慢往上爬：底楼的屋子很快暖了，顶楼的屋子嘛——按某种"民主"，几乎轮不上。

sentences.en: Because hot water is lighter than cold water, it always travels upward first; that quiet rule of thermodynamics is written into every pipe in the building, whether Grandma Bai likes it or not.
sentences.zh: 因为热水比冷水轻，它总是先往高处走；这条不出声的热力学规律，写在楼里每一根管子上——白奶奶乐意也好，不乐意也罢。

sentences.en: Grandma Bai lives on the fifth floor, the last stop of the rising heat, and by the time the warmth reaches her door, it has already given most of itself away to the lower floors.
sentences.zh: 白奶奶住五楼，是上升暖流的最后一站；等那点暖意爬到她门口，它早就把大半个自己发给了下面的楼层。

sentences.en: Without a thermostat, nobody can balance the rooms above and below, so the first floor happily opens its windows in January, while the fifth floor sleeps in two sweaters and thick socks.
sentences.zh: 没有恒温器，谁也没法让楼上楼下一样暖：一月里底楼乐呵呵地开着窗散气，五楼的人却穿着两件毛衣、两双厚袜子睡觉。

sentences.en: When one pipe leaks, the whole system stops in the night, the rooms cannot sustain their warmth, and Mr. Han comes down the stairs at midnight with his wrenches, his coat over his pajamas, and his endless patience.
sentences.zh: 只要有一根管子漏水，整个系统半夜就得停摆，屋里的暖意撑不住；韩师傅睡衣外面套上大衣，拎着扳手和那份没完没了的耐心，深一脚浅一脚下楼来。

sentences.en: The pipes run through the basement in a tired, grey geometry of right angles, and Mr. Han has walked around them so often that he could find any valve in the dark with his eyes closed.
sentences.zh: 管道在地下室里走出一套疲惫的灰色几何，全是直角；韩师傅绕着它们走了千百遍，闭着眼也能摸到任何一个阀门。

sentences.en: The boiler also makes smoke, and gray snow covers the parked cars by early morning, while the town's doctor writes angry, polite letters to the local newspaper about tired lungs.
sentences.zh: 锅炉还吐烟；清晨，灰色的雪落满停着的车。镇上的医生则给本地报纸写一封封客气而愤怒的信，主题是"疲惫的肺"。

sentences.en: One cold day, a young geologist from the big city visits the basement, puts one hand on the warm steel, and shakes her head slowly, twice, like a doctor at a sick bed.
sentences.zh: 一个冷天，一位从大城市来的年轻地质学家走进地下室，一只手贴在温热的钢板上，像病床边的医生那样，缓缓地摇了两回头。

sentences.en: "The geology under this town holds real, patient geothermal heat," she says, "warm rock, two whole kilometers down; you are burning coal on top of a sleeping fire."
sentences.zh: "这座镇子底下的地质里，存着货真价实、有耐心的地热，"她说，"温岩层，整整两千米深；你们是在一堆沉睡的火上烧煤。"

sentences.en: One warm April evening, the old fire cools for the last time, and Qinghe begins looking, for the first time, for a new answer somewhere below its frozen feet.
sentences.zh: 四月一个暖和的傍晚，老炉火最后一次熄了；清河第一次开始往自己冻僵的脚底下，寻一个新的答案。

questions.q: Where is the heart of the old building?
options: On the fifth floor.
In the community room.
In the basement: a coal boiler.
Outside in the yard.
questions.explain: 第1句 "The heart of the old building is a coal boiler in the cold basement"，老楼的心脏是地下室的燃煤锅炉。

questions.q: Why does hot water always travel upward first?
options: Because the pumps are broken.
Because hot water is lighter than cold water.
Because the roof is warmer.
Because the boiler man pushes it.
questions.explain: 第6句 "Because hot water is lighter than cold water, it always travels upward first"，热水密度小、先往高处走。

questions.q: What did the young geologist say was under the town?
options: A coal mine.
Warm rock and geothermal heat, two kilometers down.
An old riverbed.
Cold groundwater only.
questions.explain: 第13句 "warm rock, two whole kilometers down"，地质学家说地下两千米处是温岩层，藏着地热。

questions.q: Why does the author say the top rooms are warmed "in a kind democracy, almost never"?
options: Because the building held a vote about heating.
Because rising heat gives itself to the lower floors first, so the system is naturally unfair to the top.
Because the boiler liked the first floor best.
Because the fifth-floor pipes were broken.
questions.explain: 第5句与第7句 "by the time the warmth reaches her door, it has already given most of itself away to the lower floors"——热量物理上先暖下层，顶楼分到的最少，所以说是"不公平的民主"。

questions.q: In sentence 5, "a warm thermal current climbs slowly from floor to floor," the word "thermal" means ______.
options: related to heat
related to water
related to sound
related to light
questions.explain: 第5句。词根 therm- 表示"热"：thermal＝与热有关的；thermal current 即"热流、暖气流"。

title: 《暖屋计划》· 图纸上的新方案

sentences.en: In May, a team from the city arrives with drawings, instruments, folding tables, and heavy boxes of paper, and they hold their first meeting in the cold community room, with tea, biscuits, and old complaints.
sentences.zh: 五月，一支市里来的队伍到了，带着图纸、仪器、折叠桌和一箱箱沉甸甸的文件；他们头一场会就开在冷清的活动室里，配着茶、饼干，和大家积攒多年的老抱怨。

sentences.en: Their leader is Dr. Song, a geologist who has studied the geology under Qinghe for ten patient years, and she speaks quietly, in the tone of somebody who has already won the long argument with the ground.
sentences.zh: 带头人宋博士是位地质学家，耐着性子研究了十年清河地下的地质；她说话轻声细语，用的却是一种早已赢了和地层那场漫长官司的人才有的口气。

sentences.en: She has found warm rock two kilometers below the town, hot as a sleeping animal in a warm cave, and it has been sleeping there, patient and enormous, for very much longer than the town has existed.
sentences.zh: 她在小镇地下两千米处找到了温热的岩层，热得像暖洞里一头睡着的动物；它在那儿睡了很久很久——久到远比这座小镇的岁数还长。

sentences.en: "Geothermal heat can warm every single room in this old building," she tells the meeting, "and the town can stop burning coal on top of its own best-kept secret."
sentences.zh: "地热足够把这栋老楼里每一个房间都焐热，"她在会上说，"这座镇子，可以不再压着自己的头号秘密烧煤了。"

sentences.en: Her plan has two parts, one under the ground and one on the outside walls, and she draws them both on the board with the clean geometry of somebody who loves straight lines.
sentences.zh: 她的方案分两部分：一部分在地下，一部分在外墙上；她用一种热爱直线的人才有的干净几何，把两部分都画上了白板。

sentences.en: First, workers drill two deep, narrow wells, and water goes down cold and comes back up warm, again and again and again, in a slow, patient circle that never once asks for coal — the friendliest kind of thermodynamics, Dr. Song calls it.
sentences.zh: 第一步，工人们钻了两口又深又细的井：水下去时是凉的，上来时是暖的，一遍、一遍、又一遍，沿着一个从不讨煤吃的、慢性子的圆圈走——宋博士管这叫"最和气的热力学"。

sentences.en: Second, the crew wraps the whole building in a thermal coat of white insulation panels, light, durable, cheap, and thick as a winter quilt for a concrete giant.
sentences.zh: 第二步，施工队给整栋楼穿上保温的热外衣——白色的保温板，又轻、又耐用、又便宜，厚得像给一位混凝土巨人备的冬被。

sentences.en: The panels are fixed onto the old walls with care, because the drawings from 1979 are not always honest about what still lives inside those old walls.
sentences.zh: 保温板往老墙上固定时格外小心，因为 1979 年的图纸，并不总肯老实交代那些老墙肚子里究竟还住着什么。

sentences.en: In the old boiler room, the workers construct a small heat station, all new pipes, quiet pumps, bright valves, a fresh thermometer on the wall, and one green light that means "everything is well".
sentences.zh: 在原来的锅炉房里，工人们建起一座小小的换热站：全是新管道、安静的泵、亮闪闪的阀门、墙上新挂的一支温度计，还有一盏绿灯，意思是"一切安好"。

sentences.en: New pipes contain the warm water and carry it to every floor, and a small smart thermostat balances the rooms one by one, floor by floor, ending forty years of the first-floor sauna.
sentences.zh: 新管道装着暖水，把热送到每一层；一台小巧的智能恒温器逐层逐屋地调配冷暖，给底楼四十年的"桑拿"划上了句号。

sentences.en: Mr. Han is instructed to watch the new station for one quiet hour every day, and he learns the green screens slowly, word by word, with his wrenches still in his back pocket, just in case.
sentences.zh: 韩师傅受命每天照看新换热站一个钟头；他一个词一个词地慢慢学着认那些绿屏，扳手照旧插在后裤兜里——以防万一。

sentences.en: The construction lasts all summer, dust sits on every single windowsill, and the neighbors, who have complained together for years, now quarrel cheerfully about the right color for the new coat.
sentences.zh: 施工持续了一整个夏天，每一扇窗台上都落了灰；抱怨了多年抱怨到一起的邻居们，如今改为兴致勃勃地拌嘴：新外衣到底该刷什么颜色才对。

sentences.en: Dr. Song's instruments measure the deep wells every single week, and the geothermal circle below runs quietly and well, day and night, like a second, invisible season.
sentences.zh: 宋博士的仪器每个星期都测那两口深井；地下的地热循环昼夜安安静静地运转，像藏着的第二个季节。

sentences.en: In October, before the first hard frost, the team tests the whole system from top to bottom, the green light comes on, and Dr. Song, for the first time in ten years, smiles like spring.
sentences.zh: 十月，头一场重霜之前，团队把整个系统从上到下试了一遍：绿灯亮了；宋博士十年来头一回，笑得像春天。

questions.q: What did Dr. Song find two kilometers below Qinghe?
options: An old riverbed.
Warm rock with geothermal heat.
A coal mine.
Cold groundwater.
questions.explain: 第3句 "She has found warm rock two kilometers below the town"，并说 "Geothermal heat can warm every single room"（第4句），地下两千米是含地热的温岩层。

questions.q: What are the two parts of Dr. Song's plan?
options: New windows and new doors.
Deep wells under the ground and insulation panels on the walls.
More coal and bigger pipes.
Solar panels and wind machines.
questions.explain: 第5句 "Her plan has two parts, one under the ground and one on the outside walls"，一是地下的深井，二是外墙的保温板。

questions.q: What was the building's new thermal coat made of?
options: Old bricks from the shelter.
Light, durable white insulation panels.
Heavy steel plates.
Warm blankets.
questions.explain: 第7句 "a thermal coat of white insulation panels, light, durable, cheap, and thick"，热外衣是又轻又耐用的白色保温板。

questions.q: Why does the story mention that Mr. Han keeps his wrenches in his back pocket "just in case"?
options: Because the new station needed old tools.
Because he was asked to repair the old pipes.
Because old habits are hard to leave behind, and he still trusts his wrenches more than green screens.
Because the new station was already broken.
questions.explain: 第11句 "he learns the green screens slowly, word by word, with his wrenches still in his back pocket, just in case"——他还在慢慢学新屏幕，扳手舍不得撒手，可推知他对旧手艺的信赖和改不掉的老习惯。

questions.q: In sentence 10, "a small smart thermostat balances the rooms," the word "thermostat" means ______.
options: a device that holds a steady temperature
a kind of boiler
a window frame
a thermometer for walls
questions.explain: 第10句。词根 therm- 表示"热"：therm+stat(稳定)＝让温度稳定在设定值的装置，即恒温器。

title: 《暖屋计划》· 极寒之夜

sentences.en: In late December, the coldest night in thirty long years arrives at a proud minus thirty-two, and the sharp stars over Qinghe look close enough to touch and cold enough to know better.
sentences.zh: 十二月底，三十年来最冷的一夜降临，零下三十二度，冷得趾高气扬；清河上空的寒星看着近得能摸，又冷得让人识趣地缩回了手。

sentences.en: At midnight, a heavy valve in the new heat station freezes and cracks open, and the warm water stops like a good sentence interrupted by a slammed door.
sentences.zh: 半夜，新换热站里一只沉重的阀门冻裂了；暖水一下子停住，像一句好好的话，被一记摔门声拦腰打断。

sentences.en: When the warm water stops, the pipes begin to cool in the long dark, and every lost degree is a small, quiet theft that nobody downstairs can hear.
sentences.zh: 暖水一停，管道便在漫漫黑暗里开始变凉；每丢掉的一度，都是一场楼下没人听得见的小小的、无声的偷窃。

sentences.en: Dr. Song's phone rings at half past midnight, and she runs through the deep snow to the old building, with her coat half on and her geologist's instinct fully awake.
sentences.zh: 半夜十二点半，宋博士的电话响了；她大衣只穿了一半就冲进大雪，往老楼跑——外套半披着，地质学家的直觉却全醒着。

sentences.en: The repair needs three whole hours, because the frozen valve sits deep in the yard, at the far end of a pipe that follows, in her angry words, "the geometry of somebody who never once visited a winter."
sentences.zh: 抢修要整整三个小时，因为冻裂的阀门在院子深处、管道的最远端；用她气头上的话说，那段管子的几何，是"哪个从没过过冬天的人"画的。

sentences.en: The community room contains a small backup heater, so the neighbors gather there with blankets, dogs, thermoses, board games, sleepy children, and one guitar that nobody feels like playing.
sentences.zh: 活动室里有一台小小的备用暖风机，于是邻居们裹着毯子，带着狗、热水壶、桌游和困倦的孩子，聚到了那儿——还有一把谁也没心思弹的吉他。

sentences.en: Grandma Bai makes hot tea in her big old pot, the children sleep on folded chairs like kittens, and the room thermometer reads sixteen degrees and holds it until the grey morning, out of pure stubbornness.
sentences.zh: 白奶奶用她那口大旧壶烧了热茶；孩子们像小猫似的蜷在折椅上睡着了；屋里的温度计停在十六度，全凭一股倔劲儿撑到灰蒙蒙的天亮。

sentences.en: Mr. Han teaches everyone a small, useful lesson about hypothermia that cold night, standing by the tea pot like an old professor by his blackboard.
sentences.zh: 那天夜里，韩师傅就站在茶壶边，像老教授站在黑板前，给大家上了一堂关于失温的短课，短而有用。

sentences.en: "If the body loses heat for too long, hypothermia quietly begins," he says, "and the first sign is not shivering; the first sign is feeling sleepy and far, far too polite about it."
sentences.zh: "身体失热太久，失温就悄悄开始了，"他说，"第一个信号不是打哆嗦；第一个信号是犯困，而且困得过分客气、一声不吭。"

sentences.en: The human body, he explains, follows the same old thermodynamics as a warm, well-built house: if you lose heat faster than you make it, the lights go out room by room.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，人的身体和一座暖和、盖得结实的房子遵循同一套老热学：只要散热快过产热，灯就会一个房间一个房间地熄。

sentences.en: Warm drinks, dry clothes, and close company sustain the body through a cold night, and by two in the cold morning, the community room is a living textbook example of all three.
sentences.zh: 热饮、干衣服，还有挨得近近的人，能撑着身体熬过寒夜；到凌晨两点，这间活动室俨然是这三条的活教科书。

sentences.en: One old man grows cold and sleepy by the door, so they wrap him at once, without one word of argument, in two thermal blankets, and he wakes up an hour later, asking, very politely, for one more cup of tea.
sentences.zh: 有位老爷爷在门口犯了冷、发了困，大家二话没说，立刻给他裹上两条保温毯；一小时后他醒过来，客客气气地讨了一杯茶。

sentences.en: Dr. Song, kneeling in the frozen yard, mutters to herself that the geology of this town has never promised easy nights, and that the geothermal wells below are working fine; only one small valve disagreed.
sentences.zh: 宋博士跪在冻硬的院子里，自己嘀咕：这座镇子的地质，从来没担保过什么轻松的夜晚；底下的地热井运转得好好的——不过是只小阀门闹了脾气。

sentences.en: At three in the morning, the water returns, the thermometer in the community room slowly stands up straight again, like a small soldier, and the whole building exhales like one warm, tired animal.
sentences.zh: 凌晨三点，暖水回来了；活动室里的温度计像一个小士兵，慢慢重新站直了；整栋楼像一只又暖又乏的动物，长长吐出一口气。

questions.q: What happened at midnight on the coldest night?
options: The boiler ran out of coal.
A heavy valve in the new heat station froze and cracked open.
All the lights went out.
The neighbors moved away.
questions.explain: 第2句 "a heavy valve in the new heat station freezes and cracks open"，半夜换热站阀门冻裂导致停暖。

questions.q: Why did the repair need three whole hours?
options: Because the tools were missing.
Because the frozen valve sat deep in the yard, at the far end of a pipe.
Because nobody knew the building.
Because the snow blocked the doors.
questions.explain: 第5句 "the frozen valve sits deep in the yard, at the far end of a pipe"，冻裂的阀门在院子深处、管道尽头，抢修耗时三小时。

questions.q: According to Mr. Han, what is the first sign of hypothermia?
options: Loud shivering.
Feeling sleepy and too polite about it.
A red face.
A dry cough.
questions.explain: 第9句 "the first sign is not shivering; the first sign is feeling sleepy and far, far too polite about it"，第一个信号是犯困而且过分安静。

questions.q: Why did everyone worry about the old man who grew cold and sleepy by the door?
options: Because he was being rude to the neighbors.
Because sleepiness and quiet politeness are exactly the dangerous early signs of hypothermia.
Because he had drunk too much tea.
Because he wanted to go home alone.
questions.explain: 第9句说失温的第一个信号是"犯困而且过分客气"，第12句里老爷爷正是"grows cold and sleepy"，所以他们立刻裹上两条保温毯——对上号了。

questions.q: In sentence 12, "they wrap him... in two thermal blankets," the word "thermal" means ______.
options: designed to keep body heat in
made of paper
used only in summer
a kind of medicine
questions.explain: 第12句。词根 therm- 表示"热"：thermal blankets 即保温毯——专门用来锁住人体热量的毯子。

title: 《暖屋计划》· 春天与账单

sentences.en: When spring finally comes, Qinghe melts all at once, and the old building stands proud and clean in its new white coat, like a retired ship waiting for good weather.
sentences.zh: 春天总算来了，清河一下子化了个干净；老楼穿着崭新的白外衣，又体面又干净地站着，像一艘等好天气的退役航船。

sentences.en: Grandma Bai opens her notebook and writes one round number at the top of a fresh, clean page: twenty-three degrees, the temperature of her front room on the first warm morning.
sentences.zh: 白奶奶翻开本子，在一页崭新的纸头上写下了一个圆滚滚的数字：二十三度——第一个暖和的早晨，她前屋的温度。

sentences.en: Her wall thermometer has stayed high all winter long, even through the coldest, darkest week, and the red line inside the glass tube has never once visited the bottom of its little world.
sentences.zh: 整个冬天，连最冷最黑的那一周，她墙上的温度计也没低下去过；玻璃管里那根红线，一次也没到过它那个小小世界的底部。

sentences.en: The geothermal wells run quietly below the yard, twenty-four hours a day, warming the water that warms the rooms that warm the people, all in one long, invisible, reliable chain.
sentences.zh: 地热井在院子底下一天二十四小时安静运转：井焐热水，水焐热屋子，屋子焐热人——一条长长的、看不见的、可靠的链。

sentences.en: The town's air clears week by week, because no gray coal smoke rises from the rooftops anymore, and blue sky returns to Qinghe like a shy, long-lost relative who finally agrees to come to dinner.
sentences.zh: 小镇的天一周一周地变清亮，因为屋顶上再没有灰煤烟升起来；蓝天回到了清河，像一位久未登门、生性腼腆的亲戚，总算肯来吃顿饭了。

sentences.en: The children draw the sky with real blue crayons, and their young teacher pins the best drawings in the corridor, a small, proud gallery of a color nobody had trusted for years.
sentences.zh: 孩子们用真正的蓝蜡笔画天；年轻的老师把画得最好的几张钉在走廊里，办了一个小小的、得意洋洋的画廊——展的是那个多年没人敢信的颜色。

sentences.en: The winter bill arrives in April, and it is almost exactly half of last year's; "a thin bill means thick walls," Grandma Bai says, laughing at her own joke for the rest of the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 四月份账单寄来，几乎不多不少，正好是去年的一半；"账单薄了，墙就厚了"——白奶奶被自己这句笑话逗乐了一下午。

sentences.en: Mr. Han finds a new job maintaining the quiet heat station; his wrenches still work, but now he also watches the smart little thermostat and its green screen full of patient, honest numbers.
sentences.zh: 韩师傅找了份新工作，照看那座安静的换热站；他的扳手依然用得上，只是如今还要盯着那台小巧的智能恒温器，和满屏耐心的、诚实的绿字数字。

sentences.en: "The coal is gone, but the work is not," he says, patting the new pump the way he used to pat the old boiler, "and machines, like choirs and old boilers, need somebody who listens."
sentences.zh: "煤走了，活儿还在，"他说着，像从前拍老锅炉那样拍了拍新水泵，"机器这东西，跟合唱团、跟老锅炉一样，得有个肯听它说话的人。"

sentences.en: The durable thermal panels on the outside walls need no repair after the hard winter, not one crack, not one loose corner anywhere, and the white coat came through the winter like a good soldier.
sentences.zh: 一整个严冬过后，外墙那些耐用的保温板一处也不用修：没有一条裂，没有一处翘角；那件白外衣像个好士兵，从头扛到了尾。

sentences.en: Dr. Song's team plans two more stations in the nearby towns, drawn with the same clean geometry, and the geologist gives cheerful, patient talks about geology in the primary school every Friday morning.
sentences.zh: 宋博士的团队计划在邻近几个镇子再建两座换热站，用的还是那套干净的几何画法；这位地质学家每周五上午还会去小学，乐呵呵、有耐心地讲地质课。

sentences.en: On television, experts in far, warm cities argue about coal, energy, and geopolitics, but in little Qinghe the answer lies quietly two kilometers under the primary school.
sentences.zh: 电视里，远方温暖大城市里的专家们还在为煤炭、能源和地缘政治争论不休；而在小小的清河，答案就安安静静躺在小学底下两千米处。

sentences.en: The project even sustains itself, because the saved energy slowly, steadily pays back its own high cost, with interest, like a good seed returning the farmer's patience.
sentences.zh: 这个项目甚至养活了自己：省下来的能源正一点一点、稳稳当当地把当初的高成本连本带息地还回来，像一粒好种子，报答庄稼人的耐心。

sentences.en: The building is old, older than most of its neighbors, but it now holds its warmth like a new young heart, and old thermodynamics, for once in its life, has agreed to be kind.
sentences.zh: 楼还是那栋老楼，比左邻右舍都老；可它如今揣着温暖，像一颗崭新的年轻的心；而老热学呢，这辈子头一回，肯发一发善心了。

questions.q: What number does Grandma Bai write in her notebook in spring?
options: Sixteen degrees.
Twenty-three degrees.
Minus thirty-two.
Half of last year.
questions.explain: 第2句 "writes one round number... twenty-three degrees, the temperature of her front room"，开春她记下的室温是二十三度。

questions.q: Why did the town's air become cleaner?
options: Because everyone moved away.
Because it rained all winter.
Because no gray coal smoke rose from the rooftops anymore.
Because the wind was stronger.
questions.explain: 第5句 "because no gray coal smoke rises from the rooftops anymore"，不再烧煤，天就清亮了。

questions.q: How much was the new winter bill compared to last year's?
options: Almost double.
Almost the same.
Almost exactly half.
Ten times higher.
questions.explain: 第7句 "it is almost exactly half of last year's"，新账单几乎是去年的一半。

questions.q: What does Grandma Bai's joke "a thin bill means thick walls" really mean?
options: The bill paper was too thin.
Better insulation kept the heat in and cut the cost.
The bills were printed by mistake.
The walls were painted white.
questions.explain: 由第7句的账单一半、第10句的保温板"not one crack"可推知：账单变"薄"，是因为保温的"厚"墙留住了热量，采暖费随之大降。

questions.q: In sentence 12, "experts argue about coal, energy, and geopolitics," the word "geopolitics" means ______.
options: the study of stars
politics shaped by land, resources and place
the art of drawing maps
a kind of thermometer
questions.explain: 第12句。词根 geo- 表示"大地"：geo+politics＝围绕土地、能源、地理位置展开的政治，即地缘政治。

title: 《词语的化石》· 地层与活化石

sentences.en: Every language carries its own past the way a cliff above the sea carries its strata: layer upon layer of words, pressed down and hardened by the speech of countless generations, each one waiting quietly for a reader patient enough to climb down and read the whole story.
sentences.zh: 每一种语言都背负着自己的过去，就像海边峭壁背负着地层：一层又一层的词语，被无数代人的言语压实变硬，每一层都静静等着某个足够耐心的读者爬下来，读完整部故事。

sentences.en: Geologists read the history of the earth in strata of rock, and linguists, who are geologists of speech in everything but name, read the history of words in layers that are just as real, though far softer to the touch and far harder to date.
sentences.zh: 地质学家从岩层中读出地球的历史；而语言学家——不过是没有名分的言语地质学家——从同样真实的地层中读出词语的历史，只是这些地层摸上去软得多，断代却难得多。

sentences.en: Icelandic is the famous living fossil of this book: cut off on a remote northern island in the cold Atlantic, it has changed so little in nine hundred years that linguists sometimes joke that it refuses to age like the rest of us, or even to admit that time exists.
sentences.zh: 冰岛语正是本书著名的活化石：在与世隔绝的寒冷大西洋孤岛上，它九百年来变化之小，以至于语言学家开玩笑说，它拒绝像我们其余人那样老去，甚至不肯承认时间的存在。

sentences.en: A modern Icelandic farmer can still open the medieval sagas on a winter evening and follow the old dialogue without a special dictionary; imagine a Londoner today picking up Beowulf, in the original, purely for pleasure after a hard day's work, and you will feel the distance.
sentences.zh: 今天的一位冰岛农民仍能在冬夜翻开中世纪的萨迦，不需要特殊词典就能读懂那些古老的对话；设想一位伦敦人今天在劳累一天之后，纯粹为了消遣而捧读古英语原文的《贝奥武甫》，你就能体会到这中间的距离。

sentences.en: "But is that not strange?" an imagined reader once asked me; the continuity can indeed seem almost illogical in a world where fashion reinvents itself every decade, where slang is born and buried within a single season, and where yesterday's joke is today's embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 这不是很奇怪吗？一位想象中的读者曾这样问我；在时尚十年一换、俚语一季生一季死、昨天的笑话今天就成了尴尬话的世界里，这种延续性确实显得近乎不合逻辑。

sentences.en: "Strange, yes, but not random," I answered, for the logic of change is simple enough to state in one sentence: the more a language is spoken with outsiders, on ships and in markets and across borders, the faster it drifts away from its old shape.
sentences.zh: 奇怪，是的，但并非无规律可循。我答道，因为演变的逻辑一句话就能说清：一种语言与外人——在船上、市场上、边境之间——说得越多，它就漂离旧形态越快。

sentences.en: Isolation acts like cold storage, sealing an island speech in ice, while heavy contact acts like a busy port where every ship that docks leaves some cargo behind: a word here, a habit of pronunciation there, and sometimes a whole grammar shaken loose from its moorings.
sentences.zh: 隔离像冷库，把一座岛屿的语言封进冰里；而频繁的接触像繁忙的港口，每艘靠岸的船都会卸下些货物：这儿留一个词，那儿留一种发音习惯，有时整部语法都被晃得脱了锚。
