sentences.en: A remote community that talks mostly to itself keeps up a very long monologue, decade after decade, and that monologue grows ever more consistent, more peculiar, and more perfectly tuned to its own small world of sheep and fish, snow, and long dark winters.
sentences.zh: 一个多半只跟自己说话的偏远社群，等于在进行一场漫长的独白，十年复十年；这场独白变得越来越自洽，越来越奇特，也越来越完美地适配它那个由羊、鱼、冰雪与漫长黑冬组成的小世界。

sentences.en: Borrowing, it must be said plainly, is never a sign of weakness but always a record of contact, trade, conquest, and honest curiosity between peoples, so a language rich in loans deserves an apology from anyone who has ever called it careless, poor, or impure.
sentences.zh: 必须直说：借词从来不是软弱的标志，而始终是一份记录——记录人群之间的接触、贸易、征服与真切的好奇；因此，一门富于借词的语言，值得任何一个曾骂它潦草、贫瘠或不纯的人道歉。

sentences.en: Some purists object to borrowed words in the loudest possible tones, writing angry letters to newspapers; yet no major language on earth, however proud, has ever managed to avoid them, which should tell us something about the strength of the objection and the weakness of the case behind it.
sentences.zh: 有些纯化论者以最高亢的声调反对借词，向报纸写愤怒的信；然而地球上没有任何一种主要语言——无论多么骄傲——真正躲开过它们；这足以说明这种反对有多有力，以及它背后的论据有多无力。

sentences.en: The deepest layers of English were laid down by Germanic tribes who crossed the sea with swords, farms, and songs, and those ancient settlers remain the subject of the oldest English poetry, brooding over mead-halls, monsters, and the sea, the cold gray northern sea.
sentences.zh: 英语最深的地层，是由带着剑、农田与歌谣渡海而来的日耳曼部族铺下的；这些古老的移民至今仍是英语最古老诗歌的主角，在蜂蜜酒厅、怪兽与大海——寒冷灰暗的北方之海——上空沉思。

sentences.en: Beneath every sentence you speak there lies a buried landscape of this kind, and this little book is meant to serve as a rough catalogue of the excavation, mapping trench after trench of buried speech, from the Germanic basement to the Norman roof and the Latin steeple.
sentences.zh: 你说出的每个句子底下都埋着这样一片旧地貌，而这本小书想充当一份粗略的发掘目录，给一段接一段的埋藏言语绘制地图：从日耳曼的地下室，到诺曼的屋顶，再到拉丁的尖塔。

sentences.en: The analogy that guides every page is borrowed from the geologists themselves: just as they date a hill by its bands of ash and clay, we date a vocabulary by its bands of loan-words, and both sciences read ruins with respect, and with a certain thrill.
sentences.zh: 指引本书每一页的类比，正是从地质学家那里借来的：正如他们凭火山灰与黏土的条带给山丘断代，我们也凭借词的条带给一种词汇断代；而且这两门科学读废墟时都心怀敬意——还带着一点激动。

sentences.en: To ask where words come from is, in the end, to ask where we ourselves came from, and if that double question sounds grand, remember that it is the most logical opening move a curious reader could possibly make before the digging begins in earnest.
sentences.zh: 追问词语从哪里来，终究是在追问我们自己从哪里来；倘若这个双重问题听上去宏大，请记住：在正式动土发掘之前，这是一个好奇的读者所能走出的最合逻辑的第一步。

questions.q: Why has Icelandic changed so little over nine hundred years, according to the chapter?
options: It has been cut off on a remote island with little outside contact.
Its speakers are forbidden to read foreign books.
It was frozen by a royal decree in the Middle Ages.
Its grammar was completely reinvented by modern scholars.
questions.explain: 第3句 “cut off on a remote northern island in the cold Atlantic”——冰岛语因地处隔绝的孤岛、缺少与外界的接触，所以九百年来几乎不变，被语言学家戏称为拒绝变老的活化石。

questions.q: According to the author, what does heavy contact with outsiders do to a language?
options: It freezes the language like cold storage.
It protects the oldest words from dying.
It makes the language drift away from its old shape faster.
It has no effect at all.
questions.explain: 第6句 “the more a language is spoken with outsiders”——演变的逻辑是：与外人交流越多，语言漂离旧形态越快；隔离则像冷库，把语言封存起来。

questions.q: In the author's comparison, what does a busy port stand for?
options: A library full of medieval sagas.
A community that borrows words through constant contact.
A cold storage room for grammar.
A university where linguists give lectures.
questions.explain: 第7句 “every ship that docks leaves some cargo behind”——繁忙的港口比喻频繁的语言接触：每艘靠岸的船（每个外来的群体）都会留下一点货物（借词、发音习惯，甚至语法）。

questions.q: What does the author imply about the purists' objection to borrowed words?
options: That it is loud but hopeless, since no major language avoids loans.
That it is wise and should be followed by every country.
That it has already stopped borrowing in several languages.
That purists secretly write the best dictionaries.
questions.explain: 第10句 “no major language on earth, however proud, has ever managed to avoid them”——无论多么骄傲的语言都躲不开借词，可见纯化论者的反对声势虽大，实际上注定徒劳。

questions.q: In sentence 8, what does the word 'monologue' literally mean?
options: A long speech by one person alone.
A conversation between two speakers.
A printed list of goods for sale.
A formal expression of sorrow for the dead.
questions.explain: 第8句 “keeps up a very long monologue”——mono 表示单一，log 源自希腊语 logos（言语），monologue 即一个人的长篇言语（独白）；这里比喻与世隔绝的社群只对自己说话。

title: 《词语的化石》· 借来的大教堂

sentences.en: English is often described as a cathedral built from borrowed stone, its arches raised by craftsmen who never met, never wrote to one another, and never even shared a common tongue; if that sounds like chaos, look how long the roof has held.
sentences.zh: 英语常被形容为一座用借来的石头砌成的大教堂，拱顶出自一群从未谋面、从不通信、甚至没有共同语言的工匠之手；如果这听上去像一场混乱，那就看看这屋顶撑了多久。

sentences.en: After the Norman conquest of 1066, French became the language of power in England for nearly three hundred years, and an English shepherd who wanted his complaint heard in a courtroom had to borrow French words or else hire a patient translator of his own.
sentences.zh: 1066年诺曼征服之后，法语成为英格兰的权力语言，统治了近三百年；一个想让法庭听取自己申冤的英格兰牧羊人，只能借用法语词，否则就得自己雇一位耐心的翻译。

sentences.en: The peasant raised the animal and called it a cow, while the Norman lord dined on the same animal and called it beef, and in that little pair of words you can read the whole social history of the country: who labored, and who ate.
sentences.zh: 农民养这头牲口，叫它 cow；诺曼老爷吃同一头牲口，叫它 beef——在这对小小的词里，你能读出这个国家完整的社会史：谁在劳作，谁在吃肉。

sentences.en: Latin arrived later with the scholars, who needed abstract subjects for their abstract work, law, medicine, and theology, and those learned loans still lend English a certain formality, a suit of clothes for serious occasions, while the older Germanic layer keeps the warm, everyday heartbeat of the language.
sentences.zh: 拉丁语随后随学者而来，他们需要抽象的科目来做抽象的工作——法学、医学与神学；这些学术借词至今给英语带来一种正式感，像出席郑重场合的一套正装，而更古老的日耳曼层则维持着这门语言温暖日常的心跳。

sentences.en: A catalogue of English synonyms therefore reads like a social history of the island: ask beside inquire, freedom beside liberty, hearty beside cordial, and the humble word in each pair almost always came first, from the fields, while its elegant twin came from the castle.
sentences.zh: 因此，一本英语同义词目录读起来就像这座岛屿的社会史：ask 旁边站着 inquire，freedom 旁边站着 liberty，hearty 旁边站着 cordial；每一对里朴素的那个几乎总是先来，来自田野；优雅的那位则来自城堡。

sentences.en: Old Norse, the tongue of the Viking settlers, left its marks not in official documents but in daily dialogue, in the kitchen and the fishing boat, which is precisely why those words feel so native that we mistake them for the bedrock of the language.
sentences.zh: 古诺斯语——维京移民的舌头——没有把痕迹留在官方文书里，而是留在了厨房与渔船上的日常对话中；正因如此，那些词才显得如此地道，以至于我们误把它们当成了这门语言的基岩。

sentences.en: Words like sky, egg, and they were injected into English so long ago, and so deeply, that no living speaker now notices them as foreign; they ride along inside every sentence we build, quiet as rivets, holding the structure together through every storm.
sentences.zh: sky、egg、they 这些词被注入英语的年代太久、扎得太深，如今没有一个活着的说话者还觉得它们是外来户；它们藏在我们搭建的每个句子里，像铆钉一样安静，替结构扛住每一场风暴。

sentences.en: A borrowed word is not a foreign object forever; after a century or two of daily use it starts to feel native, and I have watched visitors argue, with perfect confidence, that ketchup and pajamas could not possibly be loans, because they sound so English.
sentences.zh: 借来的词不会永远是外来物；经过一两百年的日常使用，它就开始有母语的感觉——我亲眼见过有人言之凿凿地争辩说，ketchup 和 pajamas 绝不可能是借词，因为它们听起来太英语了。

sentences.en: Linguists can date these layers the way archaeologists date pottery, comparing spellings, sounds, and shifting meanings, and a well-trained eye can often tell, within a century or so, when a given word crossed the water, settled down in English soil, married, and raised a family.
sentences.zh: 语言学家能像考古学家给陶器断代那样给这些词层断代：比较拼写、语音与流变的意义；一双训练有素的眼睛往往能在一个世纪上下的误差内，说出某个词何时渡海而来、在英语土壤里落脚、成家、又繁衍出一整族词。

sentences.en: Even the word adjective is itself a loan, a Latin grammar term borrowed to describe other borrowed words, and if you find that funny, you have begun to understand what this layering of English really means: the tools are part of the collection.
sentences.zh: 连 adjective（形容词）这个词本身也是借来的——一个拉丁语法术语，借来描述其他被借来的词；如果你觉得这好笑，你便开始明白英语这种层积意味着什么：连工具也是藏品的一部分。

sentences.en: Some Norman words were later rejected by fashion, dropped in the street and never picked up again, but the great majority stayed, multiplied, and had children, and the few rejections only prove how much the speakers of English loved to choose their words freely.
sentences.zh: 有些诺曼词后来被时尚抛弃，掉在街上再没人捡起；但绝大多数留了下来，成倍增长，生儿育女——而那寥寥几次被拒，恰恰证明了说英语的人何等喜欢自由地挑选自己的词。

sentences.en: "So which layer should I trust?" a student once asked me after a lecture; the logical answer is all of them, because every layer, humble or grand, Norse or Norman, tells its part of the story, and a language that hides a layer is lying to you somewhere.
sentences.zh: 那我该信哪一层呢？一次讲座后，一个学生这样问我；合乎逻辑的回答是：每一层都信——因为每一层，无论卑微还是显赫，是诺斯还是诺曼，都讲述着故事中属于它的那一部分；而一种掩饰某一层的语言，必定在某处对你撒谎。

sentences.en: People have written whole sad essays mourning English as a mongrel tongue, as if delivering a premature eulogy at a funeral where nobody has died, but a mongrel, as any dog owner will tell you, is often the healthiest animal in the yard, vigorous and full of tricks.
sentences.zh: 有人写过整篇伤感的文章，哀叹英语是杂种语言，仿佛在一场没人去世的葬礼上提前念悼词；但任何养过狗的人都会告诉你，杂种狗往往是院子里最健康的动物——精力充沛，浑身是戏。

sentences.en: To speak English, then, is to speak a compressed history of Europe, one borrowed object at a time: a Germanic frame, a Norse roof-beam, a Norman banquet hall, and a Latin library, all still standing, all still in daily use, and all still open to the next ship that docks.
sentences.zh: 所以说英语，就是以一次借来一件东西的方式，说出一部压缩的欧洲史：日耳曼的骨架、诺斯的房梁、诺曼的宴会厅、拉丁的书房——全都立着，全都在日常使用，而且全都向下一艘靠岸的船敞开大门。

questions.q: What happened to English after the Norman conquest of 1066?
options: English disappeared entirely for a century.
French became the language of power for nearly three hundred years.
Latin replaced both English and French.
All word-borrowing stopped for three hundred years.
questions.explain: 第2句 “French became the language of power in England for nearly three hundred years”——诺曼征服后法语掌权近三百年，连牧羊人上法庭都得借法语词或请翻译。

questions.q: Why do 'cow' and 'beef' come from different language layers?
options: Because French speakers preferred farming words.
Because the peasant raised the animal while the Norman lord dined on it.
Because dictionaries picked the two words at random.
Because 'beef' was invented in the fourteenth century.
questions.explain: 第3句 “who labored, and who ate”——农民养牛用日耳曼词 cow，诺曼老爷吃肉用法语词 beef，阶级分工直接写进了词汇。

questions.q: Where did Old Norse leave its marks on English?
options: In official documents and royal charters.
In legal and medical terminology.
In the vocabulary of the Norman court.
In daily dialogue, in kitchens and fishing boats.
questions.explain: 第6句 “not in official documents but in daily dialogue”——古诺斯语的痕迹不在文书里，而在厨房与渔船的日常口语中，因此 sky、egg、they 才显得如此地道。

questions.q: When the author compares English to a mongrel dog, what is he suggesting?
options: That English is a weak and sick language.
That its mixed vocabulary made it healthier and richer.
That English should be purified as soon as possible.
That only pure languages survive for long.
questions.explain: 第13句 “is often the healthiest animal in the yard”——杂种狗往往最健康，暗示英语因混血（多来源的词汇）反而更强大、更丰富，悼词念得为时过早。

questions.q: What is ironic about the word 'adjective'?
options: It has no connection to French at all.
It was invented by Shakespeare.
It was rejected by dictionary editors for centuries.
It is a borrowed word used to describe other borrowed words.
questions.explain: 第10句 “Even the word adjective is itself a loan”——连用来描述语言的工具词 adjective 本身都是拉丁借词，借来的工具被用来整理借来的藏品。

title: 《词语的化石》· 词义的漂移

sentences.en: Words do not only travel across borders, carried by ships and armies and traders; they also drift across meanings, slowly and without asking anyone's permission, so that a word you trust today may have been an insult, a prayer, or a legal term five hundred years ago.
sentences.zh: 词语不只是被船队、军队与商队带着跨越国界地旅行，还会在词义上漂移——缓慢地，且不经任何人允许；因此你今天信赖的一个词，五百年前可能是一句骂人话、一段祷文，或一条法律术语。

sentences.en: In the fourteenth century, calling a person nice was no compliment at all, for the word then meant foolish or ignorant, and a knight so described might well have drawn his sword; the compliment of the Middle Ages was a serious business indeed.
sentences.zh: 在十四世纪，说一个人 nice 绝不是恭维，这个词当时意味着愚蠢或无知；一位被如此形容的骑士很可能当场拔剑——中世纪的恭维，可是件要命的正经事。

sentences.en: The sense drifted from foolish to shy, from shy to precise, and from precise to the warm and friendly word we use now, each step small enough that no speaker involved ever felt the ground moving beneath their feet, or thought of objecting.
sentences.zh: 它的词义从愚蠢漂向羞怯，从羞怯漂向精细，再漂到我们如今使用的这个温暖友好的词；每一步都小到让身处其中的说话者谁也没有察觉脚下的地面在移动，谁也没想过要抗议。

sentences.en: Silly traveled the opposite road entirely: it once meant blessed, then innocent, then pitiable, and finally plain foolish, and somewhere along that downward path the saints lost a word and the fools gained one, which seems a very unfair trade, unless you keep the receipts.
sentences.zh: silly 走的完全是反向的路：它曾意为有福的，后来是天真，再到可怜，最后成了彻头彻尾的愚蠢；在这条下坡路上，圣徒丢了一个词，傻瓜捡了一个——这笔交易看起来很不公平，除非你留着收据。

sentences.en: Semantic change works like a projector in a dark hall, throwing an image of society onto the small screen of a single word; whatever a community loves, fears, or refuses to look at, that image lands on the nearest word and stays there.
sentences.zh: 词义变化的工作方式像黑暗大厅里的一台投影仪，把社会的影像投到一个小词这块小小的幕布上；一个社群爱什么、怕什么、拒绝看什么，那幅影像就落在最近的词上，并留在那里。

sentences.en: When a society fears ignorance, as most societies quietly do, the word for foolish gathers moral weight, and it can start to sting; the true subject of every such shift is society itself, painting its own anxieties onto whatever words happen to be nearby.
sentences.zh: 当一个社会恐惧无知——大多数社会都暗暗如此——表示愚蠢的词就会积起道德分量，开始带刺；每一次这种转变真正的主角都是社会本身，把自己的焦虑涂到恰好就在近旁的词上。

sentences.en: These shifts can seem illogical from a distance, yet each one made perfect sense to the speakers who were living through it, because they never saw the whole road, only the next bend, and a bend never announces the valley beyond, or the sea after it.
sentences.zh: 这些转变远看仿佛不合逻辑，但对身历其境的说话者而言，每一个都完全说得通：因为他们从来看不见整条路，只看得见下一个弯道——而弯道从不预告山那边的谷地，更不预告谷地之后的海。

sentences.en: Meaning moves forward through dialogue between speakers and the changing world, never by decree from a dictionary or an academy, and no royal order has ever stopped a word from sliding, though several kings have tried and one lost his head over less.
sentences.zh: 词义的前进经由说话者与变动世界之间的对话完成，从不依靠词典或学术院的敕令；从来没有一道王命能拦住一个词下滑的脚步——尽管好几位国王试过，还有一位为更小的事丢了脑袋。

sentences.en: Euphemism is deliberate drift with a purpose: we reject a word because we cannot reject the fear or the sorrow underneath it, so we throw a fresh layer of paint over the old word and tell ourselves the wall has changed, which it has not.
sentences.zh: 委婉语是带有目的的蓄意漂移：我们拒绝一个词，是因为拒绝不了它底下那份恐惧或哀伤；于是我们在旧词上刷一层新漆，并告诉自己墙已经变了——其实墙没有变。

sentences.en: Linguists name the upward climb amelioration and the downward slide pejoration, and both paths are everywhere in the record, from the lordly words that fell into the gutter to the gutter words that rose to the parlor; every language keeps a full catalogue of both.
sentences.zh: 语言学家把向上的爬升命名为褒化（amelioration），把向下的滑落命名为贬化（pejoration）；两条路在文献里随处可见——有贵族词跌进阴沟的，也有阴沟词爬进客厅的；每种语言都完整收藏着两份清单。

sentences.en: The trajectory of any word can be traced through dated texts, citation by citation, century by century, and the resulting curve on the scholar's page looks exactly like a flight path: a slow climb, a long cruise, and sometimes a very sudden fall.
sentences.zh: 任何一个词的轨迹都能凭借标了年代的文献，一条引文接一条引文、一个世纪接一个世纪地追溯出来；它在学者纸页上画出的曲线，活脱脱是一条飞行轨迹：缓慢爬升，漫长巡航，有时则骤然坠落。

sentences.en: A conjecture about meaning is worthless without evidence, however clever it sounds, so scholars collect dated examples the way detectives collect fingerprints, and only when the pattern holds across a hundred documents does the conjecture earn the right to be called a finding.
sentences.zh: 缺乏证据的词义推测再聪明也一文不值；所以学者像侦探采集指纹那样搜集标了年代的例证——只有当这个模式在一百份文献中都站得住，推测才挣得被称为结论的资格。

sentences.en: An old dictionary therefore reads like a secret diary that a whole society kept without knowing it, and you can open it anywhere: in one column a word rejoicing, in the next a word standing dejected, and between them the entire quiet machinery of change.
sentences.zh: 一本旧词典因此读起来像全社会在不知不觉中共同记下的一本秘密日记，随手翻开哪一页都行：这一栏里一个词在欢庆，下一栏里一个词垂头丧气，而在两者之间，是整套悄然运转的演变机器。

sentences.en: So the next time you call a stranger nice, pause for half a second and remember that you are handling a fossil that once called people fools; "Words do change," a wise reader once interjected, "and we change inside them without noticing, century by century."
sentences.zh: 所以，下次你夸一位陌生人 nice 时，不妨停上半秒钟，记住你手里这块化石曾把人叫作傻瓜；一位聪明的读者曾插话说：词语确实在变，而我们就在词语里面，一个世纪接一个世纪地、不知不觉地跟着变。

questions.q: What did the word 'nice' mean in the fourteenth century?
options: Friendly and agreeable.
Precise and careful.
Foolish or ignorant.
Blessed and innocent.
questions.explain: 第2句 “the word then meant foolish or ignorant”——十四世纪说人 nice 是侮辱，被形容的骑士可能因此拔剑，与今天的友好之意相去甚远。

questions.q: Which road did the word 'silly' travel?
options: From foolish to blessed.
From precise to shy.
From shy to foolish only.
From blessed to foolish.
questions.explain: 第4句 “it once meant blessed, then innocent, then pitiable, and finally plain foolish”——silly 从有福的滑向愚蠢，与 nice 的上行路线正好相反。

questions.q: According to the chapter, why is a euphemism described as 'deliberate drift'?
options: Because we cannot reject the fear underneath the old word.
Because dictionaries order the change by decree.
Because kings force the population to use new words.
Because speakers mishear the old word accidentally.
questions.explain: 第9句 “we reject a word because we cannot reject the fear or the sorrow underneath it”——委婉语的动机是：换掉旧词容易，换不掉旧词底下的恐惧与哀伤。

questions.q: What does the author mean by calling an old dictionary 'a secret diary'?
options: That lexicographers hide their drafts from the public.
That dictionaries record a society's unspoken changes without its awareness.
That old dictionaries were written in secret code.
That only professional scholars may open them.
questions.explain: 第13句 “a secret diary that a whole society kept without knowing it”——旧词典的词义起落（一个词欢庆、一个词垂头丧气）无意间记下了整个社会的观念变迁，社会自己却毫无察觉。

questions.q: In sentence 11, what does the word 'trajectory' describe?
options: A scholar's guess without any evidence.
The flight-path-like curve of a word's meaning across centuries.
A polite way to apologize in writing.
A speech delivered by a single speaker.
questions.explain: 第11句 “The trajectory of any word can be traced through dated texts”——ject 意为投掷，trajectory 指被掷出之物划出的轨道；这里指词义经引文追溯画出的飞行曲线般的变化路径。

title: 《词语的化石》· 新词的生与死

sentences.en: New words are born every day, in playgrounds and laboratories and late-night kitchens, and most of them die before their first birthday, unmourned and unrecorded, the way most small businesses fail and most seedlings never reach the light, and nobody holds a funeral.
sentences.zh: 新词每天都在诞生——在操场上、实验室里、深夜的厨房里；而其中大多数活不过一岁，无人哀悼，无人记录，就像大多数小生意会倒闭、大多数幼苗见不到阳光——也没有谁为它们办一场葬礼。

sentences.en: William Shakespeare alone injected English with hundreds of words, from lonely to assassination, that his audience had never heard before, and when a groundling asked his neighbor what a new word meant, the neighbor could only shrug, guess, and applaud anyway.
sentences.zh: 仅莎士比亚一人就往英语里注入了数百个词——从 lonely 到 assassination——观众此前闻所未闻；当站票观众问邻座某个新词是什么意思时，邻座也只能耸耸肩、猜一猜，然后照旧鼓掌。

sentences.en: A word survives not by cleverness but by usefulness: it must fill a gap that ordinary speakers actually feel in their ordinary days, because language, for all its beauty, is a workshop before it is a gallery, and workshops keep only working tools.
sentences.zh: 一个词能否存活，靠的不是巧妙，而是有用：它必须填补普通说话者在普通日子里真正感到的空缺——因为语言再美，也先是车间后是画廊，而车间里只留得下能干活的工具。

sentences.en: Some coinages are logical, assembled from familiar parts like bricks in a wall, while others are accidents, jokes, or mishearings that somehow stuck, and the surviving examples of both kinds sit side by side in the dictionary, equally legitimate, equally alive, and equally English.
sentences.zh: 有些新造词是合逻辑的，像砌墙的砖一样由熟悉的部件组装而成；另一些则是偶然、玩笑或听岔了的话，却莫名地粘住了；两类中活下来的例证在词典里并肩而坐，同样正统，同样鲜活，也同样英语。

sentences.en: Dictionary editors therefore reject far more words than they record, watching each candidate for years like a doctor watching a patient, and an editor who fell in love with every new word would produce a volume that melted into fashion by spring.
sentences.zh: 词典编辑因此拒绝的词远多于收录的词；他们像医生观察病人那样，一盯就是好几年——而一个对新词来者不拒、见一个爱一个的编辑，编出的书到开春就会随时尚一同融化。

sentences.en: The usual standard is sustained, independent use: a word must appear in print, from different sources, over several years, and only then does it enter the catalogue; a modern dictionary is a record of observed usage, not a set of commands issued from an office above the clouds.
sentences.zh: 通常的标准是持续且独立的使用：一个词必须在数年间、出现在不同来源的印刷品中，才有资格进入那份目录；一部现代词典是对观察到的用法的记录，而不是从云端上的办公室里下发的一套命令。

sentences.en: Speakers sometimes object that editors are lowering the bar, letting slang in the front door, but lexicographers answer every such objection the same way: they describe the parade, they do not lead it, and a dictionary that commanded the language would be ignored within a decade.
sentences.zh: 有人反对说编辑在放低门槛，把俚语从正门放了进来；但词典编纂者对每一次这类反对的回答都一样：他们只是描述游行队伍，并不领队——一部想要指挥语言的词典，不出十年就会无人理会。

sentences.en: "But someone must keep standards!" a reader interjected during a talk I once gave; perhaps, I replied, but the standards that last are the ones that describe what people already say, because the public outvotes every academy, every year, without ever filling in a ballot.
sentences.zh: 总得有人守住标准吧！我在一次演讲上有位听众这样插话；也许吧，我答道，但真正能存活的，是那些描述人们已在说什么的标准——因为公众每年都会投出胜过一切学术院的票，却从不填写选票。

sentences.en: Whole vocabularies die as well, quietly and in batches: new technologies eject the words of old ones, and the gramophone, the quill pen, and the telegram have each faded away with their equipment, taking their rich technical vocabulary along like luggage on a one-way trip.
sentences.zh: 整块整块的词汇也会死去，悄悄地、成批地：新技术把旧技术的词一一弹出；留声机、鹅毛笔和电报都随着各自的设备一同淡出，把它们丰厚的技术词汇像行李一样带上一趟单程旅行。

sentences.en: A language with no power to reject new words would drown in a flood of noise, while one that rejected them all would starve in a locked room; between those two deaths lies the living road, and every healthy language walks it with the doors and windows open.
sentences.zh: 一种无权拒绝新词的语言，会在噪音的洪水里淹死；一种把新词全拒之门外的语言，会在上锁的房间里饿死；在这两种死法之间横着一条活路，而每一种健康的语言都敞着门窗走在这条路上。

sentences.en: Every generation leaves a fresh layer behind it, a geological deposit of slang and jargon and small projects of the imagination, and future scholars will dig through our memes and abbreviations the way we dig through the slang of the 1890s, with the same mixture of wonder and doubt.
sentences.zh: 每一代人都会在自己身后留下一层新沉积：俚语、行话，以及想象力的小小工程；未来的学者会像我们挖掘十九世纪九十年代的俚语那样，带着同样的惊奇与疑虑，去挖掘我们的梗与缩写。

sentences.en: The poet's office is to inject the language with new life, to take risks that would terrify a committee, while the dictionary's office, slower and colder, is to keep count of what actually survived; between those two offices, coinage and record, English has quietly renewed itself for over a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 诗人的职责是为语言注入新生命，去冒那些能把委员会吓坏的险；词典的职责则更慢、更冷——为真正存活下来的词记账。在铸造与记录这两个职位之间，英语已经悄悄地自我更新了一千多年。

sentences.en: Some people deliver funeral speeches for dying words, and I have eulogized a few myself, usually in an essay nobody read; but the honest apology owed to a dead word is simply to remember where it worked, what room it lit, and whose voice it carried.
sentences.zh: 有人会为垂死的词念悼词，我自己也为几个词写过颂文，通常登在没人读的文章里；但对一个死去的词，真正诚实的道歉其实很简单：记得它在哪里派过用场，照亮过哪个房间，又承载过谁的声音。

sentences.en: So do not feel dejected the next time your favorite new coinage vanishes by autumn; most words miss the dictionary, a few make it, and the language itself, which has buried millions and kept tens of thousands, has never once stopped writing, not even for a season.
sentences.zh: 所以，下次你心爱的新造词到秋天就消失时，不必垂头丧气；大多数词进不了词典，少数进了，而语言本身——埋葬过百万、留存了数万——从未停止过书写，连一季也没有停过。

questions.q: According to the chapter, what usually decides whether a new word survives?
options: The cleverness of its coinage.
Its usefulness in filling a gap speakers actually feel.
The approval of a royal academy.
Its length and elegant spelling.
questions.explain: 第3句 “it must fill a gap that ordinary speakers actually feel”——词语存活靠有用而非巧妙：语言先是车间后是画廊，车间只留下能干活的工具。

questions.q: What is the usual standard for a word to enter the dictionary?
options: One famous author using it a single time.
A public vote held every decade.
Sustained, independent use in print across sources and years.
The personal taste of the chief editor.
questions.explain: 第6句 “appear in print, from different sources, over several years”——标准是持续、独立的使用；现代词典记录观察到的用法，而非发号施令。

questions.q: What does the author say happens to the vocabulary of an old technology?
options: It is preserved forever in daily speech.
It always turns into playground slang.
New technologies eject it, and it fades away with its equipment.
It is translated into French and stored there.
questions.explain: 第9句 “new technologies eject the words of old ones”——留声机、鹅毛笔、电报都随设备一起淡出，技术词汇像行李一样被带上单程旅行。

questions.q: When lexicographers say they 'describe the parade but do not lead it', what do they mean?
options: That dictionaries should march in street festivals.
That dictionaries record usage rather than command the language.
That editors secretly control public opinion.
That the public must follow whatever editors print.
questions.explain: 第7句 “they describe the parade, they do not lead it”——编纂者只记录语言的实际用法，不指挥它；公众每年都用嘴投票，胜过一切学术院。

questions.q: In sentence 12, what does the root ject- in 'inject' suggest the poet does?
options: Throws new life into the language.
Throws the old words away.
Throws words onto a screen for study.
Throws an objection at the committee.
questions.explain: 第12句 “to inject the language with new life”——ject 意为投掷，in- 表示向内，inject 即向内投入：诗人把新生命投入到语言之中，冒委员会不敢冒的险。

title: 《词语的化石》· 序言与尾声

sentences.en: Behind all this history of borrowing and drift lies one deep habit of mind, and it is worth naming before we part: we understand new things by comparing them with old ones, and we have done so since the first fire was compared with the sun.
sentences.zh: 在这部借贷与漂移的历史背后，藏着一种深层的思维习惯，在告别之前值得为它命名：我们靠把新事物比作旧事物来理解它们——自从有人把第一堆火比作太阳起，我们便一直如此。

sentences.en: Analogy is the quiet engine of language and of thought itself, and nearly every idea in this little book has been its product: the language as a body, as a building, as a garden, as a harbor, as a layer of rock pressed into stone.
sentences.zh: 类比是语言也是思想本身的安静引擎，而这本小书里几乎每一个想法都是它的产物：语言像身体、像建筑、像花园、像港口、像一层被压成岩石的沉积物。

sentences.en: When we call a word living or dead, we are thinking by analogy, comparing language to a body, and the comparison is not just decoration; it guides what we look for, where we dig, and which fossils we bother to dust off and display in the light.
sentences.zh: 当我们说一个词是活的还是死的，我们就在用类比思考，把语言比作身体；这比喻不只是装饰——它指引我们找什么、往哪里挖，以及值得为哪些化石掸去灰尘、摆到光亮处展出。

sentences.en: The word logic itself descends from the Greek logos, which meant word, reason, and account all at once, a threefold meaning that the Greeks saw no need to separate; to speak, they felt, was already to reason, and to reason was already to give an account.
sentences.zh: logic（逻辑）一词本身源自希腊语 logos，它同时意味着词、理性和账目——希腊人认为这三层意思无须分开；在他们看来，说话即是推理，推理即是交代理由。

sentences.en: Every argument in logic is a dialogue carried out under strict rules, a conversation with consequences, and even the loneliest scholar writing at midnight is holding an imaginary debate: the objections of an unseen opponent are answered, one by one, on the page.
sentences.zh: 逻辑中的每一次论证，都是一场在严格规则下进行的对话——一场有后果的交谈；就连午夜独自写作的最孤独的学者，也在进行一场想象中的辩论：把那位看不见的对手的异议，一条接一条地在纸面上作答。

sentences.en: A logician can tell you whether a sentence follows from the sentences before it; only history can tell you where the sentence came from, which invaders carried it, and which poet first bent it into a shape worth keeping through the centuries, dark and bright alike.
sentences.zh: 逻辑学家能告诉你一个句子是否能由前面的句子推出；只有历史能告诉你这个句子从哪里来、是哪些入侵者带来的、又是哪位诗人最先把它弯折成一个值得穿越世纪——无论暗淡还是明亮——而留存下来的形状。

sentences.en: The illogical charm of etymology is that it rarely behaves like proof; it behaves like a story, full of sidetracks and missing chapters, and the reader who demands strict logic from it will be disappointed, while the reader who wants a story will not be able to stop.
sentences.zh: 词源学那不合逻辑的魅力在于：它很少表现得像证明，而更像一个故事，满是岔道和缺失的章节；向它索要严密逻辑的读者会失望，而想要听故事的读者则会欲罢不能。

sentences.en: Word families grow by analogy as well: project, reject, inject, and eject are four gestures made by the same hand, four ways of throwing, forward, away, inward, and out, and once your eye has grouped them, they will never scatter again, not even on the final page.
sentences.zh: 词族也靠类比生长：project、reject、inject、eject 是同一只手做出的四个手势，是投掷的四个方向——向前、推开、掷入、掷出；一旦你的眼睛把它们归了组，它们就再也不会散开，哪怕读到最后一页。

sentences.en: Once you notice one root, you begin to see it everywhere, in the monologue of a stage actor, in the catalogue of a museum, in the apology of a politician, and vocabulary stops being a list to be suffered and becomes a map to be traveled.
sentences.zh: 一旦你注意到一个词根，你便开始到处看见它——在舞台演员的独白里，在博物馆的目录里，在政客的道歉里；词汇于是不再是一张拿来受罪的清单，而成了一张可以游历的地图。

sentences.en: The prologue of English was written long ago, and by many hands at once: by tribes crossing the cold water, by invaders with their dictionaries of power, by poets taking unreasonable risks, by printers spreading pages, and by patient editors keeping count of it all.
sentences.zh: 英语的序言早已写就，而且是许多只手同时写下的：渡过冷海的部族、带着权力词典的入侵者、冒不合理之险的诗人、传播书页的印刷工，还有为这一切记账的耐心的词典编辑。

sentences.en: The epilogue is unwritten, and every speaker of English holds the pen for a sentence or two before passing it on; a child asking for a bedtime story tonight is quietly drafting a page that scholars will cite, with footnotes, a century from now.
sentences.zh: 但尾声尚未写就，每一位说英语的人都握笔写上一两句，然后把它传下去；今晚一个讨睡前故事的孩子，正在悄悄起草一页文字——一个世纪后，学者们会带着脚注引用它。

sentences.en: "Could English ever die?" a reader may reasonably interject here, and my honest answer is a conjecture, not a guarantee: languages die when their speakers stop passing the pen, but this one is being passed, at this moment, on every continent on earth, and shows no sign of putting it down.
sentences.zh: 英语难道不会死吗？读到此处，读者插这么一句也合情合理；我诚实的回答是一份推测，而非保证：语言死于说话者不再传笔的那一刻——而这一支笔，此刻正在地球上的每一片大陆之间传递，且毫无搁下的迹象。

sentences.en: This book opened with fossils and now closes in a nursery, for a language is less a museum than a garden: it is planted, weeded, watered, and constantly rearranged, and some of what is planted in it this spring will still be blooming when nobody remembers the gardener's name.
sentences.zh: 这本书以化石开篇，而如今在一间育婴室里收尾——因为语言与其说是博物馆，不如说是花园：它被栽种、除草、浇灌，并被不断重新布置；今年春天种下的某些东西，将来仍会开花，即便那时已无人记得园丁的名字。

sentences.en: The words that were borrowed yesterday will feel native tomorrow, the words you are using today are fossils in training, and if you someday write a eulogy for a word you loved, take comfort: the root will survive it, ready to be thrown once more into new speech.
sentences.zh: 昨天借来的词，明天就会像母语；你今天使用的词，正是训练中的化石；倘若有一天你为一个深爱的词写下悼词，也请稍感安慰：词根会活过它，随时准备再一次被掷进新的言语。

questions.q: What does the author call 'the quiet engine of language and of thought itself'?
options: Grammar.
Memory.
Analogy.
Etymology.
questions.explain: 第2句 “Analogy is the quiet engine of language”——类比是安静的引擎，本书里几乎每个想法（语言像身体、像花园、像岩层）都是它的产物。

questions.q: What did the Greek word 'logos' mean, according to the chapter?
options: Only reason and argument.
Word, reason, and account all at once.
Only speech and sound.
Light and truth together.
questions.explain: 第4句 “meant word, reason, and account all at once”——logos 一词身兼词、理性、账目三义，希腊人认为说话即是推理，推理即是交代理由。

questions.q: Who, according to the author, wrote the prologue of English?
options: A royal academy founded in the eighteenth century.
Tribes, invaders, poets, printers, and patient editors together.
Shakespeare working entirely alone.
The Norman kings and their official scribes.
questions.explain: 第10句 “The prologue of English was written long ago”——序言由渡海的部族、入侵者、冒险的诗人、印刷工和耐心的编辑许多只手共同写成。

questions.q: When the author says every speaker 'holds the pen for a sentence or two', what is he suggesting?
options: That only professional writers can change English.
That ordinary speakers, even a child at bedtime, are each writing part of the language's unfinished story.
That English is finished and needs no more writers.
That scholars will soon write the final dictionary.
questions.explain: 第11句 “every speaker of English holds the pen for a sentence or two”——尾声尚未写就，每个说话者（连讨睡前故事的孩子）都在续写一页，可见语言的未来在所有普通使用者手中。

questions.q: Why do 'project, reject, inject, and eject' feel like one family, according to the chapter?
options: They all rhyme in modern English.
They were all coined by one poet.
They are four directions of throwing, made by the same root ject through analogy.
They all entered English through Norman French.
questions.explain: 第8句 “four gestures made by the same hand”——ject 意为投掷，四个词分别表示向前掷、掷回、掷入、掷出，是同一词根借类比做出的四个手势。

title: 《鲁滨逊的岛》· 风暴

sentences.en: Robinson Crusoe was born in the English seaport of York, the youngest son of a merchant who intended him for the law; his father, a wise and careful man, loved to explain that the middle station of life carried the fewest sorrows, and he offered to support his son comfortably in any honest office of the town.
sentences.zh: 鲁滨逊·克鲁索出生在英格兰的海港城市约克，是商人家最小的儿子，父亲本打算让他去学法律；他父亲是个谨慎明白人，总爱说人生的中间阶层烦恼最少，并答应出钱供儿子在城里任何体面的职位上安稳度日。

sentences.en: But Robinson's heart followed the ships, and no report of drowned sailors, however true, could detain his imagination for a single day; at nineteen, without asking anyone's permission, he went aboard a vessel bound for London, and that one act of wilfulness transferred him out of his father's quiet world for ever.
sentences.zh: 可鲁滨逊的心一直跟着船走，再真实的溺亡传闻也拴不住他的想象，连一天都拴不住；十九岁那年，他没跟任何人打招呼，就上了一艘开往伦敦的船，这一次任性，把他从父亲那个安静的世界里永远地转了出去。

sentences.en: On later voyages he watched the great trade at work, and his education, such as it was, came from the sea itself: English cloth went out as export, sugar from the Indies came home as import, and at every port he saw a porter staggering under bales and barrels, while the merchant's whole fortune depended on safe transport.
sentences.zh: 在后来的几次航行里，他见识了这门大生意的运转，他受的那点教育，全是海给的：英国的布匹作为出口运出去，西印度群岛的蔗糖作为进口运回来，每个港口都有搬运工扛着成捆成桶的货摇摇晃晃，而商人全部身家，都押在运输是否平安上。

sentences.en: He learned by watching that an importer in London could gain a fortune or lose one to a single storm, that opportunity and ruin often sailed on the same deck, and that the sea, which offered young men adventure, offered nobody any mercy — a lesson he was very slow to believe.
sentences.zh: 他边看边明白：伦敦的进口商人可以发一笔财，也可以一场风暴赔个精光；机会和厄运常常同乘一块甲板；海给了年轻人冒险，却谁也不给怜悯——这一课他很久都不肯相信。

sentences.en: Then, on a voyage toward the Indies, the sky turned the colour of wet slate, and the wind came down from the north like a hammer swung by an invisible arm; the captain shouted for the topsails to be lowered, but the gale struck the mast before the men could contain the sails, and the ropes sang like instruments of pain.
sentences.zh: 后来，在一次驶向西印度群岛的航程中，天空变成了湿石板的颜色，北风像一只看不见的胳膊抡着锤子砸下来；船长吼着命人收顶帆，可人还没拢住帆，狂风已经打上桅杆，缆绳绷得像痛苦的乐器一样尖啸。

sentences.en: Water poured through the decks until the hold could not contain it, and the ship sat lower and lower in the dark, like a tired animal lying down; the sailors worked with tenacious, silent fury, passing buckets from hand to hand, but their prayers obtained nothing from the sea, which took no notice of them at all.
sentences.zh: 海水从甲板上灌进来，船舱里盛不下，船在黑暗里越坐越低，像一头乏了躺倒的牲口；水手们憋着一股顽强劲，沉默地一桶一桶传递，可他们的祷告从海那里什么也换不来——海根本不理会他们。

sentences.en: "We are lost," the boatswain cried at last; "the windows of heaven are opened, and no vessel built by men can sustain such blows" — and every man on that deck suffered the same thought at the same moment, though nobody dared to say it twice.
sentences.zh: "完了，"水手长终于喊出声，"天上的窗户全开了，人造的船经不起这样的捶打"——甲板上每个人在同一刻都熬着同一个念头，只是谁也不敢再说第二遍。

sentences.en: They lowered a boat in the hope of escape, and it overturned at once; Robinson suffered the sea twice in one night, first in the ship and then in the water, until a third wave, stronger than all the others, tore him from the rope he held and threw him into the black sea alone.
sentences.zh: 他们放下小艇指望逃生，小艇当场就翻了；一夜之间鲁滨逊遭了两回海的罪，先在船上，后在水里，直到第三道浪——比先前所有的都猛——把他从攥着的绳子上扯下来，独自抛进了黑沉沉的大海。

sentences.en: One wave carried him towards the shore and another drew him back, as if the elements themselves differed about his fate to the very last; he swam until his strength was gone, and then he stopped fighting and let the sea decide, which is the last deference a drowning man can offer to anything.
sentences.zh: 一道浪把他往岸上送，另一道又把他往回拽，仿佛天地四方对他的命运各执一词，直到最后一刻还在争执；他游到力气用尽，索性不再挣扎，把决定交给大海——这是一个溺水的人能向任何东西献上的最后的恭顺。

sentences.en: A great billow, kinder than all the rest, lifted him up and set him upon the dry sand of an unknown coast, where he lay breathing like a man newly born; the land, which he had never once valued in his life before, now supported his whole weight like a promise kept.
sentences.zh: 一个格外好心的大浪把他托了起来，放上一片不知名海岸的干沙；他躺在那里喘气，像个新出生的人；这块他此生从未看重过的陆地，此刻像一句践了约的诺言，稳稳托住了他的全部重量。

sentences.en: When daylight came he saw the wreck sitting half a mile off upon a sandbank, masts down and hull broken, and the water between still ran too high for any swimmer; he was alive, and that was all — no tool, no food, no companion, and no report of where in the world this island stood.
sentences.zh: 天亮后他看见沉船搁浅在半英里外的沙洲上，桅杆倒了，船身裂了，中间那片海仍旧浪头太高，谁也游不过去；他活着，仅此而已——没有工具，没有食物，没有同伴，也说不清这座岛在世界上的哪个角落。

sentences.en: He wept for a while like a child, and then, because his father's practical blood spoke in him, he remembered that tears sustain no man, stood up, wiped his face with his sleeve, and said aloud — to nobody, for nobody was there — "I have suffered for my own choice, and now I must maintain myself with my own hands."
sentences.zh: 他像孩子一样哭了一阵，随后父亲传给他的务实血性开了口：他想起眼泪养不活任何人，便站起身，用袖子抹了脸，对着空处大声说——没有人，因为根本没有人在——"这是我自找的苦，往后我得靠这双手养活自己了。"

sentences.en: Along the sand he collected what the storm had transferred to him as a kind of bitter pension: a barrel stave, a rotten plank, a torn piece of sailcloth; he drank from a stream, ate sour berries, and retained enough hope to climb the nearest hill twice and search the horizon for smoke or a sail.
sentences.zh: 沿着沙滩，他把风暴转手给他的那点苦涩抚恤一样捡起来：一块桶板、一片烂木板、一角撕破的帆布；他喝了溪水，吃了酸浆果，还留着足够的希望，把最近的山头爬了两遍，在海平线上搜寻炊烟或船帆。

sentences.en: The horizon was empty in every direction, and that emptiness informed him plainly that his case was his alone; but he was a merchant's son and understood ledgers, and the entry he made that night was simple: on the debit side, a whole ship and its cargo; on the credit side, one line — alive.
sentences.zh: 四面八方的海平线都空空荡荡，这片空旷明白地告诉他：这桩案子只属于他一个人；但他到底是商人的儿子，懂账本，那晚他记下的账再简单不过：借方一栏，一整条船和满船的货；贷方一栏，只有一行——活着。

questions.q: What future did Robinson's father plan for him, and what did he offer?
options: To be a sailor like his elder brothers.
To study law; he offered to support him in any honest office of the town.
To take over the family's shop at the port.
To become a captain in the navy.
questions.explain: 第1句写父亲 "intended him for the law"，并 "offered to support his son comfortably in any honest office of the town"——学法律、在城里体面任职。

questions.q: What did Robinson learn about the sea trade on his later voyages?
options: English cloth went out as export while sugar from the Indies came home as import.
The ships carried only passengers between ports.
The trade moved gold secretly between England and France.
He learned nothing, because he never sailed twice.
questions.explain: 第3句 "English cloth went out as export, sugar from the Indies came home as import"，他还看见每个港口的 porter，明白商人的身家全押在 transport 上。

questions.q: Why did the ship sit lower and lower in the dark water?
options: The crew had thrown the cargo overboard.
Water poured through the decks until the hold could not contain it.
The mast had fallen and dragged the bow down.
The tide was rushing out from under the hull.
questions.explain: 第6句 "Water poured through the decks until the hold could not contain it, and the ship sat lower and lower"——海水灌进船舱盛不下，船身便一点点下沉。

questions.q: What does the "ledger" entry in the last sentence suggest about Robinson's state of mind?
options: He has gone half-mad from fear of the sea.
He is beginning to face his ruin in a cool, merchant-like way.
He plans to swim out to the wreck that very night.
He believes his father will send a rescue ship soon.
questions.explain: 第14句他把整场海难记成一笔账：损失一整船货，收益只有"活着"一行。用商人的记账方式清点绝境，说明他已冷静下来正视处境，这正是后文"两栏日记"的先声。

questions.q: The word "sustain" (from a root meaning to hold, to keep) appears in "tears sustain no man". What does the sentence mean?
options: Crying can hold a broken ship together.
Crying cannot keep a person alive or fed.
Tears are worth money to merchants.
Sailors should be allowed to cry in private.
questions.explain: 第12句 "he remembered that tears sustain no man... 'I have suffered for my own choice, and now I must maintain myself with my own hands'"——眼泪养不活人，只能靠自己双手维持生计。

title: 《鲁滨逊的岛》· 两栏日记

sentences.en: On the second day the tide left the wreck high upon a sandbank, and Robinson saw that the sea, having robbed him of everything, now offered him a strange gift; he swam out through the surf, climbed the broken side, and obtained from the cabin a carpenter's tools, two guns, a cask of powder, ship's biscuit, a little ink, and three Bibles; for this small salvage, at least, he thanked heaven, with a warmth he had never once felt for his father's whole warehouse in York.
sentences.zh: 第二天，潮水把沉船高高搁上沙洲；鲁滨逊明白了，大海抢光了他的一切，如今却送来一件古怪的礼物；他穿过拍岸的浪游过去，从裂开的船帮爬上去，从船舱里弄到了木工工具、两支枪、一桶火药、船用饼干、一点墨水，还有三本《圣经》；单为这一小批抢救出来的东西，他就热热乎乎地谢了天——这份热乎劲儿，他从前对着父亲在约克的整座货栈，可是一次也不曾有过。

sentences.en: Raft after raft he transferred the treasure to the shore — planks, nails, sails, a portable chest of clothes — but his first attempt nearly killed him: he loaded the raft too greedily, it tilted in the current, and he learned, gasping on the sand, that a castaway must transport his fortune slowly, or lose it all at once.
sentences.zh: 他扎了一趟又一趟木筏，把这份家当搬上岸——木板、钉子、帆布、一只便携的小衣箱——可头一回差点要了他的命：他贪心装得太满，木筏在急流里一歪；他瘫在沙滩上喘着气，明白了落难的人转移家财必须慢慢来，否则一次就赔个精光。

sentences.en: He chose a hollow in the ground beside a spring of fresh water, where a horseshoe of rising rock already contained the space on three sides, and there he planted a double fence of stakes, a wall to sustain him while he slept and to detain any wild thing that came hunting in the dark.
sentences.zh: 他在一眼淡水泉边的洼地里选了落脚处，一道马蹄形的天然岩壁三面把这块地方兜住；他在那里打下两圈木桩围栏，一面在他睡着时撑着他，一面拦住夜里来觅食的任何野物。

sentences.en: Behind the fence he maintained a strict order: tools in one corner, food in another, powder wrapped in cloth high and dry, and a tent of sailcloth for the night; every evening he inspected his little kingdom and counted everything twice, like a shopkeeper closing his books; and every morning he took them out again, to check that the world had not subtracted anything overnight.
sentences.zh: 栅栏之内，他维持着一套严格的秩序：工具归一角，食物归一角，火药用布裹好高高放在干燥处，夜里睡一顶帆布小帐篷；每天傍晚他都要巡视一遍自己小小的王国，把家什清点两遍，像掌柜打烊前对账；每天清早再搬出来核一遍，看看这个世界夜里有没有悄悄从他账上划走什么。

sentences.en: The days contained no speech at all, and silence pressed upon him more heavily than hunger; he began, therefore, to keep a journal, and the writing of it was like keeping a friend, for a pen, unlike the sea, answers when you speak to it.
sentences.zh: 白天里没有一句话可说，寂静比饥饿更沉地压在他身上；于是他开始写日记，写日记这件事就像养着一个朋友——因为笔和海不一样，你对它说话，它会应你。

sentences.en: Ink was a treasure beyond every other, and he used it sparingly, so that his reports of the weather grew shorter as the months grew longer: "Rain, and the birds restless" — that was a whole day, set down in five words and a dash.
sentences.zh: 墨水是压倒一切的宝贝，他省着用，天气报告便越写越短，月份却越拖越长："雨，鸟不安"——一整天，就用五个词加一道破折号记完了。

sentences.en: To weigh his case honestly, he divided a page into two columns, one for evil and one for good, exactly like a merchant balancing an account at the year's end, and though the invention was his own, the need for it was as old as shipwreck itself.
sentences.zh: 为了老老实实掂一掂自己的处境，他把一页纸分成两栏，一栏记坏，一栏记好，跟商人在年终结账时对账一模一样；这法子虽是他自己想出来的，人对它的需要，却和海难本身一样古老。

sentences.en: Under evil he wrote that he was cast away upon a hopeless island, with no prospect of deliverance; under good, on the opposite side, he set down that he was alive, that his shipmates were drowned and he was spared, and that the island, so far as he could tell, contained nothing that meant to kill him.
sentences.zh: 坏栏底下他写：流落在一座无望的岛上，没有获救的前景；好栏那边他写：人还活着；同伴都淹死了，唯独他得免；还有，就他所知，这座岛上没有任何存心要他命的东西。

sentences.en: Thus he found that the worst condition still retains something to be thankful for, and that the ledger never quite closes on the dark side; a man who computes his blessings, he wrote, will always find the good column longer than he expected at the start, and the bad, when he counted it honestly, always shorter.
sentences.zh: 这样他发现，最坏的处境里也还留着值得感谢的东西，这本账永远不会彻底倒在暗的那一边；他写道，肯数算自己福分的人，数到最后，总会发现好那一栏比起头料想的要长，而坏那一栏，老老实实点下来，反倒更短。

sentences.en: While the powder stayed dry the guns obtained him fresh meat; with the tools he built himself a table and a chair, the first things he referred to in the journal as comforts, and he observed that even a plank, cut to the shape of a table, transfers some of the dignity of a house to a hole in the ground.
sentences.zh: 火药还干着的时候，那两支枪替他弄来鲜肉；靠那套工具，他给自己做了桌子和椅子——这是他头一回在日记里称之为"舒适"的东西；他还留意到，哪怕一块木板，锯成桌子的形状，也能把一点房子的体面，转移到地上的一个坑里来。

sentences.en: He entertained himself with schemes of future years — a goat enclosure, a grain field, a boat — each plan drawn in the sand and erased by the next rain, though some of them, though he could not know it yet, the island would one day hand him whole, and exactly when he had stopped asking for them.
sentences.zh: 他用往后岁月的种种盘算来给自己解闷——围一圈羊、种一片谷、造一条船——每个计划都在沙地上画出来，又被下一场雨抹掉；其中有一些，他还无从知道，这座岛日后会完完整整地送到他手上，而且偏偏送到他不再开口去讨的时候。

sentences.en: Later he would tame a parrot that entertained him with his own words, but that small comfort still lay years ahead; for the present his only music was the sea, which performed the same long piece every night and never once took a different tempo.
sentences.zh: 再往后他会驯养一只鹦鹉，用他自己说过的话逗他开心——不过那点小小的安慰还在几年之后；眼下他唯一的音乐是大海，它每夜演奏同一支冗长的曲子，节拍从来不肯换一换。

sentences.en: Months passed, and the island obtained a strange hold upon him: he no longer watched the horizon every hour, but once a day, at noon, and if that single look found nothing, he went back to his fence and his ledger with something almost like peace.
sentences.zh: 几个月过去，这座岛对他生出一种古怪的掌控：他不再是每个钟头都望一眼海平线，而是每天正午望一次；若是那一眼里什么也没有，他便回到自己的栅栏和账本跟前，心里竟近乎安宁。

sentences.en: Tent, fence and journal he maintained like a tenant keeping up the property of some invisible landlord, and in the two columns of his account the balance moved, sentence by sentence, from the dark side towards the light; "I am a tenant paying rent in labour," he wrote, "and the landlord has never yet sent the bill."
sentences.zh: 帐篷、栅栏和日记本，他像租客打理一位看不见的房东的产业那样一一维护着；在账本的两栏之间，天平一句一句地从暗侧移向亮处；"我是个用劳动交租的租客，"他写道，"只是房东至今还没寄来账单。"

questions.q: What lesson did Robinson's first raft trip teach him?
options: Never swim out to the wreck again.
A castaway must transport his goods slowly, or lose everything at once.
Rafts are stronger than boats in a current.
The tide is more dangerous than the wind.
questions.explain: 第2句 "he loaded the raft too greedily, it tilted in the current"，他学到的道理是 "a castaway must transport his fortune slowly, or lose it all at once"——搬家必须慢慢来。

questions.q: Why did Robinson divide a journal page into two columns?
options: To record the weather of each season.
To count his remaining stores of food and powder.
To weigh his case like a merchant balancing an account, evil against good.
To practise the handwriting he had lost.
questions.explain: 第7句 "To weigh his case honestly, he divided a page into two columns, one for evil and one for good, exactly like a merchant balancing an account"。

questions.q: Which entries went under the good column?
options: Fresh meat, a table and a chair.
That he was alive, spared while his shipmates drowned, and safe on an island without killers.
The three Bibles he had obtained from the cabin.
His plans for a goat enclosure and a boat.
questions.explain: 第8句好栏底下写的是 "he was alive, that his shipmates were drowned and he was spared, and that the island... contained nothing that meant to kill him"。

questions.q: Watching the horizon only once a day instead of every hour suggests what change in Robinson?
options: He has decided the island is his true home.
He is slowly growing used to island life, though his hope is not dead.
He has forgotten how to keep time.
He no longer believes any ship exists at all.
questions.explain: 第13句 "the island obtained a strange hold upon him: he no longer watched the horizon every hour, but once a day"——望海平线从每小时一次降到一天一次，说明他正渐渐习惯岛上的日子，但每天正午仍要看一眼，希望并未死绝。

questions.q: In the last sentence, Robinson calls himself a "tenant". What does the word mean here?
options: A prisoner kept by force in one place.
Someone who holds and keeps up property that belongs to another.
A sailor who has signed a ship's articles.
A merchant who rents goods to other merchants.
questions.explain: 第14句 "like a tenant keeping up the property of some invisible landlord"——tenant（词根 tain，持有）指持有并照看他人产业的人，他像替看不见的房东打理产业的租客，还幽默地说"用劳动交租"。

title: 《鲁滨逊的岛》· 麦田

sentences.en: Among the rescued goods lay a small bag that had once held chicken feed, worthless by every measure of a cargo manifest, and Robinson, shaking its dust and husks out upon the ground beside his fence, thought no more of it than a man thinks of an empty pocket.
sentences.zh: 抢救回来的物件里有一只小口袋，从前装鸡饲料，照货物清单的任何标准都一文不值；鲁滨逊把里头的碎渣壳子抖在栅栏边的地上，就没再多想——人对一只空口袋，能多想什么呢。

sentences.en: Some weeks later thin green blades stood up in the shaken dust — barley, and a few stalks of rice, the most fertile surprise he had ever owned — and he stood over them in silence for a long time, hardly able to refer what he saw to any cause except providence, which seemed to prefer working through empty pockets.
sentences.zh: 几个星期后，抖过碎渣的地方立起了细绿的芽——是大麦，还夹着几茎稻子，这是他拥有过的最肥沃的惊喜；他在它们旁边默默站了很久，实在想不出该把这桩事归因于什么，除了天意——天意似乎偏爱借着空口袋做工。

sentences.en: He guarded the first seeds like a miser's gold, sowed them by the handful in guarded beds, and only in the fourth year dared to plant a field large enough to sustain him in bread, for a single impatient harvest, he had learned the hard way, can transfer a whole future to the dinner table of one hungry week.
sentences.zh: 他把头一批种子当守财奴的金子一样看着，一把一把地撒进严加看护的苗床；直到第四年，他才敢种一块大到足以供他吃粮的田——因为他吃过苦头，懂得一季等不及的收成，会把整个未来转移到某一个饥荒礼拜的饭桌上去。

sentences.en: The island's seasons differed from the English year in every particular: the wet months and the dry came by their own laws, the rains, not the calendar, chose the time of sowing, and twice he lost a whole planting by referring to York weather instead of to the sky above his own head.
sentences.zh: 岛上的季节和英国的年份处处不同：湿季旱季各按各的规矩来，播种的日子由雨水说了算，不由日历说了算；他有两回照着约克的天气想事，没看自己头顶这片天，结果赔掉了整整一茬庄稼。

sentences.en: He caught young goats, tamed them with bread and patience, and preferred a slow, safe herd to the doubtful luck of powder and shot; a goat enclosure, once built and maintained, offers meat, milk and butter every day of the year, whereas a gun offers only whatever it happens to meet, and that never twice the same; besides, meat and milk come every day, like wages.
sentences.zh: 他捉来小羊，用面包和耐性把它们驯熟；比起火药枪弹那点靠不住的运气，他更喜欢一群慢慢长大、稳稳当当的羊——圈栏一旦建起、好好维护，一年三百六十五天都有肉、有奶、有黄油；而枪给的只有它碰巧撞见的那个，回回还不一样；再说肉和奶天天都来，像发工钱。

sentences.en: From the clay of the stream side he made pots, and the work taught him more humility than the storm had: the first cracked, the second cracked, the tenth held water, and patience retained him at the wheel long after his fingers were cut and his hopes had cracked as often as the clay; no schoolmaster in York, he wrote afterwards, had ever taught him so much for so little pay.
sentences.zh: 他用溪边的黏土做陶罐，这门活计教给他的谦卑，比那场风暴教的还多：第一只裂了，第二只裂了，第十只终于盛得住水；手指割破了，希望也和黏土一样裂了一回又一回，可耐心把他留在轮盘前，一直留到最后；他后来写道，约克城里没有一个教书先生，肯这么少收学费教他这么多的东西。

sentences.en: In time he possessed two goat enclosures, a barley field, a small vineyard and a pottery shed, and the castaway had quietly become a farmer, holding his territory not by any title written on paper but by the older title of daily labour, which no court on earth can cancel.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，他有了两圈山羊、一块大麦田、一座小葡萄园和一间陶棚；落难的人不声不响变成了农夫——他对这片领地的持有，靠的不是纸上写着的什么名契，而是比那更古老的、日复一日的劳动，这地契世上哪个法庭也撤消不了。

sentences.en: He counted his possessions in the journal as a merchant maintains his books, each item dated and weighed, for order was the rope he held in the dark, and a man who cannot report what he owns will very soon be unable to report what he is.
sentences.zh: 他像商人记账一样，在日记里清点家当，每一件都标上日期和分量；因为秩序就是他在黑暗里攥着的那根绳——一个说不上自己有什么的人，要不了多久，也就说不上自己是什么了。

sentences.en: Bread baked in a clay oven, goat butter, raisins dried in the sun, and eggs from tame birds gathered near the fence: his table now offered more than any dinner he had eaten in Brazil, though every dish on it had cost him a season to obtain, and the finest of his tools had been fire, patience and mud.
sentences.zh: 黏土炉里烤出的面包、羊奶黄油、太阳晒的葡萄干，还有栅栏边驯养的鸟下的蛋：他这张桌子，如今比他在巴西吃过的任何一餐都丰盛——只是桌上每一样，都费了他一季才弄到手；他最好使的工具，是火、耐心和泥。

sentences.en: Yet he confessed in the same entry that contentment differed from happiness: he had everything a body needed, and still his heart kept an ear turned towards home, like a sentry who cannot be relieved of his post and stops expecting to be.
sentences.zh: 可就在同一篇日记里，他坦白道：满足与幸福不是一回事——身体要的他全有了，心却仍竖着一只耳朵听着家的方向，像个永远换不了岗、也不再指望换岗的哨兵。

sentences.en: Sometimes he referred in his diary to England, to his father's advice, to his mother's face, and to the plain comfort of a street with people in it; on those evenings the ledger gained an entry that he could not honestly put into either column, for it belonged, he wrote, to both of them at once.
sentences.zh: 有时他在日记里提起英国，提起父亲的劝告、母亲的脸，还有一条街上人来人往的那种最普通的安逸；那样的夜晚，账本上便多出一笔他没法老老实实归进任何一栏的账——他写道，这笔账，同时属于两栏。

sentences.en: Four full years the bread had cost him; when the first loaf of his own raising came out of the clay oven he held it in both hands like an inheritance, and wrote that in his private treasury it stood above a chest of gold, being the only coin he had ever minted himself; he ate it standing up, slowly, with his cap off, as one does at a funeral and a birth at once.
sentences.zh: 这条面包前后整整花了他四年；当第一炉自己种出来的面包从黏土炉里端出来，他双手捧着，像捧一笔遗产，并写道：在他私人的金库里，它压过一整箱金子——因为这是他此生唯一亲手铸造的钱币；他站着，摘下帽子，慢慢把它吃了，像人同时出席一场葬礼和一场新生。

sentences.en: "I am king here," he wrote, "and parliament too; I make the laws, maintain the police, and hear every case myself — but I am also the tenant who pays the whole rent in labour, and the landlord, whoever he is, is very slow about repairs."
sentences.zh: "我在这里是国王，"他写道，"也是议会；立法的是我，维持治安的是我，每桩案子都亲耳听审——可我同时也是那个用劳动交清全部房租的租客，而那位房东，不管他是谁，修房顶修得可真够慢的。"

sentences.en: And yet, when a strange sail crossed the horizon one afternoon and vanished, he stood watching the empty sea for a full hour, and understood, with a calm that surprised him, that no field, however fertile, and no kingdom, however peaceable, could ever contain the whole of a man.
sentences.zh: 然而，某个午后一张陌生的船帆掠过海平线又消失了，他站在那里，望着空掉的海整整一个钟头；他带着一种连自己都吃惊的平静明白了：任何一块田，再肥沃也是它；任何一片江山，再太平也是它——都装不下一个完整的人。

questions.q: How did the first barley plants come to the island?
options: Robinson bought seed from a passing ship.
Seeds shaken out of an old chicken-feed bag sprouted in the dust.
The wind carried them over from the mainland.
Friday brought them as a gift years later.
questions.explain: 第1句他抖掉鸡饲料袋的碎渣便不再理会，第2句 "thin green blades stood up in the shaken dust — barley"，正是碎渣里的种子自己发了芽。

questions.q: Why did Robinson wait until the fourth year to sow a full field?
options: He had to study the island's rains for four seasons first.
He was waiting for better tools from the wreck.
He guarded the first seeds like treasure until there were enough to live on.
The goats kept eating the young green plants.
questions.explain: 第3句 "He guarded the first seeds like a miser's gold... only in the fourth year dared to plant a field large enough to sustain him in bread"，先攒够能养活自己的种子。

questions.q: What did the island's climate teach him about the time of sowing?
options: To follow the English calendar strictly.
To sow only on the first Monday of each month.
To let the rains, not the calendar, choose the time.
To sow twice every year, spring and autumn.
questions.explain: 第4句 "the rains, not the calendar, chose the time of sowing"，他还因照搬约克天气赔过两茬庄稼。

questions.q: Robinson wrote that one evening's entry "belonged to both columns at once". What does he mean?
options: His homesickness was both a loss and a kind of gratitude.
The weather that day was both wet and dry.
The goats and the barley were both counted twice.
The ink and the paper came from the same wreck.
questions.explain: 第11句他写起英国、父母和街上的人来，却发现这笔账进不得坏栏也进不得好栏，"it belonged... to both of them at once"——想家既是他账上的亏欠，也证明他心里还有值得记挂的东西，需要同时记在两栏。

questions.q: The root of "fertile" carries the sense of bearing, bringing forth. In sentence 2, what does "the most fertile surprise" mean?
options: A surprise that frightened him most.
A surprise capable of producing growth — seeds that could feed him.
A surprise worth a great deal of money.
A surprise that was almost too heavy to carry.
questions.explain: 第2句大麦和稻芽从鸡饲料碎渣里长出，"the most fertile surprise he had ever owned"——fertile（词根 fer，结出、带来）指能带来生长和收成的东西，这几粒种子日后养活了他。

title: 《鲁滨逊的岛》· 沙上的脚印

sentences.en: One midday, walking along the shore, Robinson saw printed deep in the sand a single footprint that was not his own; he stood like a man struck, looked behind him, looked at the sea, and found no living thing anywhere, so that the print, quite innocent of any owner, became in his mind more terrible than a whole army in sight.
sentences.zh: 一天正午，鲁滨逊沿着海滩走，看见沙子上深深印着一只脚印——不是他自己的；他像挨了一记闷棍似的僵住，回头看看，又望望海，四下里没有任何活物；正因为这脚印找不着主人，它在他心里，竟比一支看得见的大军还吓人。

sentences.en: From that one mark he inferred a whole world of fear — cannibals, prisoners, fleets of canoes, wars on some unseen coast — and every inference grew out of the same small seed: where one man has walked, more men can; and every inference, as he later admitted, was built upon nothing but a hollow in the sand, and yet he believed every one of them completely.
sentences.zh: 从那一枚印子，他推断出一整个恐惧的世界——食人生番、俘虏、成队的独木舟、某处看不见海岸上的战争；而每一个推断，都是从同一粒小小的种子里长出来的：一个人走过的地方，更多的人也能走到；可他也后来承认，所有这些推断，全建立在沙子上一道凹坑之上——而他竟一个不落地全信了。

sentences.en: He ran home, fortified the fence, doubled his wall of stakes, and for two years the footprint detained his mind more completely than the island had ever done: he rebuilt, he hid, he slept in new places, and slowly turned a free kingdom back into the fortress of a frightened tenant.
sentences.zh: 他奔回住处，加固栅栏，把木桩墙加成两层；之后的两年里，那只脚印把他扣在心里，比整座岛从前做到的更彻底：他修了又修，躲了又躲，换地方睡，硬是把一片自由的王国有条不紊地，变回了胆战心惊的租客的堡垒。

sentences.en: Fear, he later wrote in the journal, is the worst tenant a man can offer lodging to: it pays no rent, it damages the house it lives in, and it obtains a lease that no honest lawyer would admit exists.
sentences.zh: 他后来在日记里写道：恐惧是一个人能给住房的最糟糕的租客——不交房租，还糟蹋它住的那所房子，而且它弄到手的那份租约，任何正经律师都不会承认它存在。

sentences.en: Then one morning the sand told a longer story: canoes had come in the night, fires had burned on the beach, and bones lay about the ashes, and Robinson, watching from a rock, suffered the plain truth that his neighbours across the water were man-eaters, and that his island lay in their sea-lane, near enough to be visited and far enough to have been spared until now.
sentences.zh: 后来某个清晨，沙滩讲出一个更长的故事：夜里来过独木舟，沙滩上烧过火，灰烬周围散着骨头；鲁滨逊从岩石上望着，被迫咽下一个明白的真相——水那边的邻居是吃人的，而他的岛正处在他们的航线上，近得随时会被光顾，远得侥幸撑到今天。

sentences.en: Some time later the story came again with flesh on it: two prisoners broke from the treeline, running for their lives along the sand, two pursuers behind them and, beyond all of them, the indifferent sea, which never refers any question to the shore.
sentences.zh: 过了一阵，这故事又一次有了血肉：两个俘虏从树林边窜出来，沿着沙滩没命地逃，身后追着两个杀手，再远处是一切都不放在心上的大海——大海从不把任何问题转呈给岸上。

sentences.en: Robinson felled the first pursuer with the butt of his gun, shot the second where he stood, and the rescued stranger — spared, breathless, and unable to transfer his gratitude into any words they shared — knelt and set Robinson's foot upon his head, which needed no translation at all: submission and thanks, in every language, kneel the same way.
sentences.zh: 鲁滨逊用枪托撂倒头一个追兵，把第二个原地击毙；获救的陌生人捡回了命，喘着气，感激得没法用两人共通的任何言语传递，便跪下来，把鲁滨逊的脚搁在自己头顶——这一下完全不需要翻译：臣服和感激，在哪一种语言里，跪的姿势都一样。

sentences.en: Because the rescue fell upon a Friday, Robinson gave the man that word for a name; his true name belonged to a country across the water, and it was never referred to again without a shadow crossing the new one.
sentences.zh: 因为获救那天正逢星期五，鲁滨逊便拿这个词给那人当了名字；他真正的名字，属于海那边的一个国度，而往后再提起它，总会有一道阴影掠过这个新名字。

sentences.en: Friday was tenacious in learning, retaining every lesson his master taught with a memory that suffered nothing to fall out of it: within a year he could talk of tools, goats, bread and God, and his English, though strange in its music, was never stupid in its meaning; indeed, he learned his master's tongue faster than his master ever learned patience.
sentences.zh: 星期五学得极顽强，主人教的每一样都留得住，那记性好到什么都不肯漏掉：不出一年，工具、山羊、面包和上帝，他都能谈；他的英语虽说起来腔调古怪，意思却从来不糊涂；说真的，他学主人的语言，比主人学耐心还快得多。

sentences.en: Robinson taught him to say Master, Yes and No, and sometimes, watching Friday kneel and smile, he wondered privately to whom that word Master, as between the two of them, really referred — for it was Friday who could milk, cook, fish and sing, and Robinson who needed teaching how to smile again.
sentences.zh: 鲁滨逊教他说"主人""是"和"不是"；可有时看着星期五跪下、微笑，他心里犯嘀咕：主人这个词，在他们两人中间，究竟指的哪一个——挤奶、做饭、打鱼、唱歌样样会的是星期五，需要人教"怎么重新笑"的反倒是鲁滨逊。

sentences.en: They talked by the fire of the sea, of Friday's nation beyond the water, and of the God who had made both shores; and Robinson, whose religion had lain for years like a dry bone in a drawer, found it regained some juice the moment he had to explain it aloud to a friend; explanations, he discovered, are a form of belief.
sentences.zh: 火堆边，他们聊大海，聊水那边星期五的族人，聊同时造出这两片海岸的上帝；鲁滨逊的信仰多年来像抽屉里一根干骨头，如今为了对朋友开口解释，倒渗出了一点汁水，活了回来；他发现，解释本身，就是一种相信的方式。

sentences.en: For the first time in many years Robinson could say "we", and the word sustained him like a second fence built around the heart; the difference it made was out of all proportion to its size, as the single footprint once had been — only in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 多少年来，鲁滨逊头一回能说出"我们"；这个词撑住了他，像在心外头又围了一道栅栏。它起的作用，和它小小的个头全不成比例——正如当年那一只脚印，只不过方向恰好相反。

sentences.en: "I am no longer the only tenant of this island," he wrote in the journal, and the dark column of the old ledger showed one entry fewer, while the good column, for the first time, began to run on past the foot of the page; the account of his case, kept so long in two careful columns, had at last produced a balance he could live on.
sentences.zh: "我不再是这座岛上唯一的住客了，"他在日记里写道；旧账本那栏坏底下少了一笔，好那一栏则头一回密密写下去，写到了页脚还收不住——这本用两栏精心记了多年的账，总算结出了一个他靠得住活得下去的余额。

sentences.en: Years later an English ship would offer them passage home; but that night, by the fire, with the tide breathing on the sand and Friday's voice asking a hundred questions about heaven, the island held two men, and that, Robinson wrote, was enough; fear had been a fence, and so was the friendship, but only one of the two had a gate in it.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，自会有一艘英国船载他们回家；但那天夜里，火堆旁，潮水在沙滩上呼吸，星期五的声音问出一百个关于天堂的问题——这座岛上有两个人，鲁滨逊写道，这就够了；恐惧曾是一道栅栏，友谊也是一道栅栏，只是两道栅栏里，只有一道装了门。

questions.q: What did Robinson infer from the single footprint in the sand?
options: That a European ship had wrecked on the far side of the island.
A whole world of fear — cannibals, prisoners and wars on an unseen coast.
That Friday had been living on the island all along.
That the tide had carried a shoe ashore from the wreck.
questions.explain: 第2句 "From that one mark he inferred a whole world of fear — cannibals, prisoners, fleets of canoes, wars on some unseen coast"，虽然他后来承认这一切推断只建立在沙子上一道凹坑上。

questions.q: Why was the rescued stranger given the name Friday?
options: He was captured on a Friday two years earlier.
Because the rescue fell upon a Friday.
It was the first English word he learned to say.
Robinson could not pronounce his true name.
questions.explain: 第8句 "Because the rescue fell upon a Friday, Robinson gave the man that word for a name"，获救之日是星期五，便以这一天为名。

questions.q: According to Robinson's journal, what kind of tenant is fear?
options: A faithful one, guarding the house through the night.
The worst one: it pays no rent, damages the house, and holds a lease no lawyer would admit exists.
A generous one, bringing food to the door.
A quiet one, hardly ever noticed by its landlord.
questions.explain: 第4句 "Fear... is the worst tenant a man can offer lodging to: it pays no rent, it damages the house it lives in"——恐惧是个不交房租、糟蹋房子的租客。

questions.q: Robinson's private wondering about the word "Master" reveals what about him?
options: He is proud of his power over another man.
He feels uneasy about owning a person, and suspects Friday may be the better man of the two.
He plans to teach Friday to be a master too.
He has forgotten the word for friend in English.
questions.explain: 第10句他暗自琢磨 "to whom that word Master, as between the two of them, really referred"，又说会挤奶做饭打鱼唱歌的是星期五，需要人教怎么重新笑的是自己——说明他心里不安，隐约觉得两人中更配称"主人"的反倒是星期五。

questions.q: In sentence 3, what does "the footprint detained his mind" mean?
options: It kept his thoughts held captive, occupying him for two whole years.
It delayed his walk along the beach by an hour.
It forced him to report the print to the police.
It made him dream of the port of York again.
questions.explain: 第3句 "for two years the footprint detained his mind more completely than the island had ever done"——detain（词根 tain，扣住、留住）指把他的心思牢牢扣住，整整两年不得脱身。

title: 《地壳下的引擎》· 热的来历

sentences.en: Deep beneath our feet, the Earth is not a cold stone but a working engine driven by heat, an idea that surprises people who imagine the planet as finished and still; in truth, the ground beneath our cities is alive, restless, and quietly enormous, a machine still burning beneath the pavements and gardens of ordinary life.
sentences.zh: 脚下深处，地球并不是一块冷石头，而是一台靠热驱动的引擎；在那些把行星想成完工静物的人听来，这个念头令人吃惊——事实上，我们城市脚下的地面是活的、不安分的，安静得惊人，是一台仍在寻常街巷与花园之下燃烧的机器。

sentences.en: Anyone who has climbed down into a deep mine knows this by instinct, for the temperature rises by roughly one degree Celsius for every forty meters of depth, and the deeper the shaft, the hotter the rock that waits at the bottom of it.
sentences.zh: 凡是下过深井的人凭本能就知道这一点：每往下约四十米，温度大约升高一摄氏度，井越深，等在井底的岩石就越烫。

sentences.en: This pattern, which geologists call the geothermal gradient, proves that something below is still producing energy; the sweating miners who carve tunnels through hot rock are, without quite knowing it, resting their hands on the skin of an ancient furnace.
sentences.zh: 地质学家把这种规律叫作地热梯度，它证明地下深处仍有东西在持续产能；那些在热岩中凿隧道的、汗流浃背的矿工，其实在不知不觉间，把手搁在了一座古老熔炉的炉皮上。

sentences.en: About half of that warmth is leftover heat from the planet's violent birth, some 4.5 billion years ago, when the collisions that assembled the young Earth released enough energy to keep the whole world glowing for an age.
sentences.zh: 这份热大约一半来自行星猛烈诞生的余温，那是大约四十五亿年前的事；当时拼装出年轻地球的那一次次碰撞，释放的能量足以让整个世界发光一个纪元。

sentences.en: The rest comes mainly from the slow radioactive decay of uranium, thorium, and potassium locked inside solid rock, a patient nuclear fire that has been quietly feeding the engine from within since the very first day.
sentences.zh: 其余则主要来自铀、钍、钾在固态岩石里缓慢的放射性衰变——一堆耐心的核火，从第一天起就在引擎内部安静地添柴。

sentences.en: Students of word roots will notice that therm appears in thermal, thermometer, and thermodynamics alike, three words that describe heat as it is felt, as it is measured, and as it obeys the strict rules of physics.
sentences.zh: 留意词根的人会发现，therm 同时出现在 thermal、thermometer 和 thermodynamics 之中：这三个词分别描述被感觉到的热、被测量的热，以及服从物理严格法则的热。

sentences.en: In geology the same root surfaces in geothermal, the word we use for heat drawn from the ground, and this is no accident of vocabulary, for the science of the Earth and the energy buried inside it were discovered together, shaft by shaft and borehole by borehole.
sentences.zh: 在地质学里，同一个词根又以 geothermal 的面目出现，专指从地下取出的热；这绝不是词汇上的巧合，因为地球科学和埋藏地下的能量，本就是一井一井、一孔一孔同时被发现的。

sentences.en: Physicists describe the rules of this energy flow as thermodynamics, the science of heat in motion and disorder, and their patient equations explain why a planet as massive as ours cannot simply hide its warmth forever.
sentences.zh: 物理学家把这套能量流动的法则称为热力学，一门研究运动与无序中的热量的科学；他们那些耐心的方程式解释了，为什么像地球这样巨大的行星无法把自身的热永远藏下去。

sentences.en: The deep planet cannot dump its heat all at once, because the overlying structure of rock works like a thick blanket; layer after layer of dense stone obstructs the escape, so the engine beneath us is forced to leak slowly, like heat through a feather quilt in winter.
sentences.zh: 深部地球的热无法一次性倾泻而出，因为上方岩石的结构像一床厚厚的棉被；一层又一层致密的石头拦住了去路，于是我们脚下的引擎只能慢慢地渗漏，像冬天透过羽绒被漏出的热气。

sentences.en: In the deepest South African mines, workers have measured rock temperatures near sixty degrees Celsius at three kilometers down, and the men who drill there labor in short shifts, drinking water without pause, cooled by pipes that carry chilled air into the dark.
sentences.zh: 在南非最深的矿井里，人们在三千米深处测到接近六十摄氏度的岩温；在那里打钻的工人只能短班轮作，不停地喝水，靠管道送进黑暗的冷风降温。

sentences.en: Down in those tunnels a laborer faces exhaustion and heatstroke, the exact opposite of the hypothermia that kills the unprepared climber on a freezing mountain; heat and cold wear different masks, but both are the faces of the same deadly physics.
sentences.zh: 在那些巷道里，工人面对的是虚脱和中暑，与冻死毫无防备登山者的失温症恰好相反；热与冷戴着不同的面具，却都是同一种致命物理的两副面孔。

sentences.en: To study the leak, scientists lower sensitive instruments into boreholes to measure the heat that escapes from the crust below us, and every thermometer they send down into the dark, week after patient week, comes back with a number that tells the story of the buried engine.
sentences.zh: 为了研究这股泄漏，科学家把精密仪器吊入钻孔，测量从我们脚下的地壳逸出的热量；他们一周又一周耐心送入黑暗的每一支温度计，回来时都带着一个数字，讲述那台被埋引擎的故事。

sentences.en: Their instruments reveal that the planet loses about 47 terawatts of power into space, roughly twice the total consumption of all humanity, a steady breath of energy that has never once paused in four billion years and cannot be switched off by any government or any engineer.
sentences.zh: 仪器显示，地球向太空泄漏约四十七太瓦的功率，大约是全人类总能耗的两倍；这口呼吸四十几亿年来从未停顿，也没有任何政府、任何工程师能把它关掉。

sentences.en: That steady leak is small beside the flood of the Sun, yet it is enough to move continents, raise mountains, and crack cities; the chapters that follow are the story of where that quiet, patient, invisible power goes, and of what it has built and destroyed here on the surface.
sentences.zh: 在太阳的洪流面前，这股泄漏虽小，却足以推动大陆、抬升山脉、震裂城市；后面几章讲的就是这份安静、耐心而看不见的力量去了哪里，以及它在地表建造过、又毁坏过什么。

questions.q: According to the chapter, where does Earth's internal heat come from?
options: Sunlight stored in the crust during summer months.
Leftover heat from the planet's birth and the radioactive decay of uranium, thorium, and potassium.
Friction between the ocean tides and the shore.
Fires left over from ancient volcanoes.
questions.explain: 第4句 “About half of that warmth is leftover heat from the planet's violent birth, some 4.5 billion years ago”，再加上第5句的铀、钍、钾放射性衰变，共同构成地球内部的热源。

questions.q: What is the geothermal gradient, as described in the chapter?
options: The rate at which temperature rises with depth: about one degree Celsius per forty meters.
The slope of an active volcano.
The speed at which continents drift apart.
The depth of the deepest borehole in South Africa.
questions.explain: 第2句 “the temperature rises by roughly one degree Celsius for every forty meters of depth”，这一规律即地热梯度。

questions.q: What have workers measured in the deepest South African mines?
options: Rock temperatures near freezing at three kilometers down.
Rock temperatures near sixty degrees Celsius at three kilometers down.
Steady temperatures of twenty degrees at all depths.
Temperatures higher than the surface of the Sun.
questions.explain: 第10句 “rock temperatures near sixty degrees Celsius at three kilometers down”，三千米深处岩温接近六十摄氏度。

questions.q: What can be inferred about why the planet's heat escapes so slowly?
options: Because the overlying structure of rock, like a thick blanket, obstructs the escape of the deep heat.
Because the heat is constantly swallowed by the oceans.
Because the engine below stopped working long ago.
Because the atmosphere reflects heat back into space.
questions.explain: 第9句 “the overlying structure of rock works like a thick blanket; layer after layer of dense stone obstructs the escape”，可推断层层岩石像棉被一样挡住了热，使它只能缓慢泄漏。

questions.q: The root therm appears in thermal, thermometer, and thermodynamics. What does this root mean?
options: Earth.
Structure.
Heat.
Motion.
questions.explain: 第6句 “therm appears in thermal, thermometer, and thermodynamics alike”，三个词都围绕“热”：therm 意为热，geothermal 即“来自大地的热”。

title: 《地壳下的引擎》· 大陆漂移

sentences.en: In 1912, a young German meteorologist named Alfred Wegener proposed an idea so strange that it made the geologists of his era furious: the continents, he argued, are not fixed in place but drift slowly across the face of the Earth like ships on a slow sea.
sentences.zh: 1912年，年轻的德国气象学家阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳提出一个让同时代地质学家愤怒的想法：大陆，他主张，并非原地不动，而是像慢海上的船，在地球表面缓慢漂移。

sentences.en: Wegener was trained in weather rather than in rocks, and the geological establishment dismissed him at once as a wandering amateur who had wandered into the wrong lecture hall; a man who studies clouds, they said, has no right to move continents.
sentences.zh: 魏格纳学的是天气而非岩石，地质学界立刻把他贬为一个走错了讲堂的游荡外行；他们说，一个研究云的人，无权去搬动大陆。

sentences.en: Yet his evidence was uncomfortably good: matching coastlines on the opposite shores of the Atlantic, identical fossils of the same plants and animals, and similar rock structure continuing from Brazil into Africa, as if the ocean had once been absent and the land unbroken.
sentences.zh: 可他的证据好得让人难受：大西洋两岸吻合的海岸线、同种动植物的相同化石，以及从巴西延续进非洲的相似岩石结构——仿佛大洋曾一度缺席，陆地曾连成一体。

sentences.en: Critics demanded a driving mechanism, some visible engine that could push entire continents, and his earliest answers, which imagined the landmasses plowing through the seafloor like icebreakers, satisfied almost nobody and gave his enemies an easy target.
sentences.zh: 批评者们要求给出驱动机制，某种能推动整块大陆的可见引擎；而他最早的解释——设想大陆像破冰船一样犁开海底——几乎无人买账，还把把柄递到了对手手里。

sentences.en: One hostile reviewer called the whole idea geopoetry rather than science, a beautiful dream dressed in numbers, and the textbooks of the era followed his lead, ignoring continental drift for nearly half a century while its author grew old, kept waiting, and kept answering his critics in letters that few of them bothered to open.
sentences.zh: 一位充满敌意的评论人把这套理论称作地质诗而非科学，一场穿着数字外衣的美梦；那个时代的教科书随声附和，对大陆漂移冷落了近半个世纪，而它的作者渐渐老去、一直等待，还不断给批评者回信——那些信几乎没人肯拆。

sentences.en: Wegener died in 1930 on a rescue expedition in Greenland, frozen on the ice far from his camp, still waiting for the proof that never reached him in his lifetime; a colleague wrote sadly that the man had been right about the Earth but wrong about his era.
sentences.zh: 1930年，魏格纳在格陵兰的一次救援远征中去世，冻毙在远离营地的冰原上，生前始终没等到那份证明；一位同事悲伤地写道：他对地球看得没错，错的是他的时代。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, survey ships mapping the floor of the Atlantic Ocean found something the old maps had never shown: a vast mountain chain running down the middle of the ocean, split lengthwise by a valley of cracked, fresh, and strangely young rock, young enough that no one could explain it away.
sentences.zh: 二十世纪五十年代，勘测大西洋底的测量船发现了旧地图从未画过的东西：一条纵贯大洋中部的巨大山脉，被一道裂谷从头到尾劈开，谷里的岩石破裂、新鲜，而且出奇地年轻——年轻到谁也无法把它搪塞过去。

sentences.en: Harry Hess, a geologist who had commanded a warship during the Second World War, reconstructed the seafloor in 1962 as a slow conveyor belt: molten rock rises along the ridge, freezes into new crust, and carries the continents sideways as it spreads.
sentences.zh: 曾在二战中指挥过军舰的地质学家哈里·赫斯，在1962年把海底重建成一条缓慢的传送带：熔岩沿洋脊涌出，冷凝成新的洋壳，一边扩张一边把大陆驮向两侧。

sentences.en: The engine, at last, had a name and a shape; it was convection, slow currents of hot rock creeping through the mantle, powered from below by geothermal heat, the same buried warmth that sweats through the deep mines of South Africa.
sentences.zh: 引擎终于有了名字和形状：热对流——在地幔中缓慢爬行的高温岩流，从下方由地热驱动，正是从南非深井里渗出来的那份埋藏的热。

sentences.en: Mantle rock flows only a few centimeters each year, no faster than a fingernail grows, but a current that slow, given a hundred million years of patience, is strong enough to construct an ocean and to tear a continent in half.
sentences.zh: 地幔岩石每年只流动几厘米，不比指甲长得快；但只要给它一亿年的耐心，这样慢的潜流也足以建起一片大洋，把一块大陆撕成两半。

sentences.en: By the late 1960s, plate tectonics had assembled a new picture of the surface from a dozen moving rigid plates, and the geometry of those plates explained earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain belts with a simplicity that geologists had been seeking for a century.
sentences.zh: 到六十年代末，板块构造用十几块移动的刚性板块，为地表拼出了一幅新图景；这些板块的几何以地质学家追寻了一个世纪的简洁，解释了地震、火山与山带。

sentences.en: The theory once mocked as poetry became the load-bearing structure of modern geology within a single scientific decade; professors who had instructed their students to laugh at Wegener now instructed them to memorize the names of the plates.
sentences.zh: 这套曾被讥为诗的理论，在一个科学十年之内成了现代地质学的承重结构；当年教导学生嘲笑魏格纳的教授们，如今教导学生去背板块的名字。

sentences.en: An English geologist of that generation admitted, years later, that the shame of the discipline was not the mockery itself, for science must argue, but the length of it; half a century is a long time for the truth to stand in the cold.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，那一代的一位英国地质学家承认：这门学科的耻辱不在争论本身——科学本就要争——而在于争论之久；让真理在寒风里站半个世纪，实在是太长了。

sentences.en: It is a lesson worth keeping: the evidence was on the table from 1912, but the community could not accept a fact it could not picture, and the picture arrived only when instruments finally reached the bottom of the sea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个值得铭记的教训：证据从1912年起就摆在桌面上，但学界无法接受一件它想象不出来的事实；直到仪器终于沉到海底，那幅图景才姗姗到来。

questions.q: What was Alfred Wegener trained in?
options: Meteorology, the study of weather.
Mining engineering.
Marine geology.
Classical poetry.
questions.explain: 第1句 “a young German meteorologist named Alfred Wegener”，他是气象学家出身，因此被地质学界视为外行。

questions.q: Which evidence did Wegener cite for continental drift?
options: Magnetic stripes on the seafloor.
Volcanoes erupting in straight lines.
Matching coastlines, identical fossils, and similar rock structure across the Atlantic.
Earthquakes occurring only on islands.
questions.explain: 第3句 “matching coastlines on the opposite shores of the Atlantic, identical fossils of the same plants and animals, and similar rock structure continuing from Brazil into Africa”。

questions.q: What did Harry Hess do in 1962?
options: He led a rescue expedition in Greenland.
He commanded a survey ship in the 1950s.
He reconstructed the seafloor as a slow conveyor belt.
He named the mid-Atlantic ridge.
questions.explain: 第8句 “reconstructed the seafloor in 1962 as a slow conveyor belt”，赫斯把海底设想为熔岩上涌、冷凝、扩张的传送带。

questions.q: What can be inferred about why Wegener's theory was ignored for so long?
options: His measurements were later proven wrong.
The evidence was too weak to survive debate.
The community could not accept a fact it could not picture, until instruments revealed the seafloor.
Geologists were forbidden by law from reading his papers.
