questions.explain: 第14句 “the community could not accept a fact it could not picture, and the picture arrived only when instruments finally reached the bottom of the sea”，可推断缺少直观图景与海底证据是长期被冷落的关键。

questions.q: In the word “reconstructed”, the root struct means the same as in structure and construct. What is that root's meaning?
options: To build — reconstruct means to build a picture again.
To heat.
To measure.
The Earth.
questions.explain: 第8句 “reconstructed the seafloor in 1962 as a slow conveyor belt”，词根 struct 意为“建造”，reconstruct 即在证据之上把图景重新搭建出来。

title: 《地壳下的引擎》· 造山

sentences.en: About fifty million years ago, India, then an island continent sailing steadily north across an ocean that no longer exists, collided with the southern coast of Asia, and the entire future geography of half the planet changed in that slow, silent, invisible moment.
sentences.zh: 约五千万年前，当时还是岛大陆的印度，穿过一片如今已不存在的大洋一路向北，撞上了亚洲的南缘；半个星球未来的地理，就在那个缓慢、无声而看不见的瞬间被改写。

sentences.en: The collision did not destroy either landmass, for continents are too light to sink; instead the impact crumpled their edges like sheet metal folded in slow motion by a giant's patient hands, and the folds themselves, pushed higher and higher, became the bones of the highest mountains on Earth.
sentences.zh: 碰撞并没有毁掉任何一方，因为大陆太轻，沉不下去；冲击反倒像巨人用耐心的手以慢动作折弯钣金那样，把两侧边缘挤皱；那一道道被越推越高的褶皱，本身就成了地球上最高山脉的骨架。

sentences.en: That impact has constructed the Himalaya, the highest mountain range on the surface of the Earth today, and the construction is not finished: the range is still rising, still thickening, and still writing its own geometry into the sky above Asia.
sentences.zh: 这场撞击建造了喜马拉雅，今日地球表面最高的山脉；而这项建造尚未完工：山脉仍在抬升、仍在增厚，仍在把自己的几何写进亚洲上方的天空。

sentences.en: Mount Everest, measured at 8,849 meters, consists of rock that once formed the floor of an ancient sea, compressed and cooked and pushed upward until a piece of the ocean bed stood higher than any land on the planet.
sentences.zh: 珠穆朗玛峰测高八千八百四十九米，构成它的岩石曾是古大海的海底；它们被压缩、被炙烤、被向上推举，直到一块洋底站得比行星上任何陆地都高。

sentences.en: Fossils of ocean creatures appear near the summit, small shells and sea lilies of extraordinary beauty, and every climber who reaches the top stands upon a quiet instruction written in stone about where these mountains actually began their long journey upward.
sentences.zh: 峰顶附近能找到海洋生物的化石，那些美得惊人的小贝壳与海百合；每一个登顶的人都站在一句写进石头里的无声教诲上，它讲清了这些山开始漫长上行的真正起点。

sentences.en: Under sustained pressure, flat sediment layers bend into long folds that a trained geologist can read like a diagram; the structure of the folds records the direction of the squeeze, much as a dent in a car door records the direction of the crash.
sentences.zh: 在持续挤压下，平直的沉积层弯成一道道长褶皱，受过训练的地质学家能像读图纸一样读它们；褶皱的结构记录着挤压的方向，正如车门上的凹痕记录着撞击的方向。

sentences.en: Fold by fold, the crustal structure shortens sideways and thickens vertically, until the crust beneath Tibet is nearly twice the normal thickness, a doubled slab of light stone supporting the highest plateau on Earth, a roof of stone standing two miles above the sea.
sentences.zh: 一褶又一褶，地壳结构横向缩短、纵向增厚，直到西藏下方的地壳接近正常厚度的两倍——一块加倍的轻质石板，托举着地球上最高的高原，一面高出海面两英里的石顶。

sentences.en: Where stress exceeds the strength of rock, the layers snap instead of bending, and the destruction arrives as an earthquake; the same pressure that patiently builds a mountain over ten million years can flatten a city in ten seconds.
sentences.zh: 应力一旦超过岩石强度，岩层便不再弯曲而是断裂，破坏以地震的形式到来；用一千万年耐心建起一座山的同一种压力，能在十秒钟里夷平一座城。

sentences.en: Nor is the work finished: India still drives north at about five centimeters every year, like a patient ram leaning into a wall, and the wall, being made of stone, answers every push with a shudder.
sentences.zh: 造山也并未完工：印度至今仍以每年约五厘米的速度向北推进，像一头耐心的公羊抵着墙；而那堵墙既然是石头做的，便以每一次颤动回应每一次抵撞。

sentences.en: GPS instruments anchored to bedrock show the range rising a few millimeters annually, slightly faster than erosion can destroy it, so the mountains are winning their slow race against the glaciers and the monsoon rains, at least for the next few million years.
sentences.zh: 固定在基岩上的GPS仪器显示，山脉每年抬升几毫米，略快于侵蚀对它的破坏；至少在今后几百万年里，这些山仍在赢下它们对冰川与季风暴雨的那场慢赛跑。

sentences.en: Erosion attacks the peaks from above with glacier and river, while construction pushes from below with heat and pressure, and the endless balance between those two patient opponents shapes every landscape the way a sculptor's two hands shape the wet clay.
sentences.zh: 侵蚀从上以冰川与河流削减峰顶，建造从下以热与压力托举；这两位耐心对手之间无休止的平衡，塑造着每一片风景，一如雕塑家的两只手塑造湿黏土。

sentences.en: The deep roots of the range sink, heat up, and release geothermal springs wherever the structure cracks, so that pilgrims in the high valleys have bathed for centuries in the warmth of the collision without ever knowing the buried engine that heated the water or the ancient crash that lit its fire.
sentences.zh: 山脉的深部根带下沉、受热，凡结构开裂之处便涌出温泉；于是高谷里的朝圣者几百年来一直沐浴在碰撞的暖意里，却从不知道加热这水的地下引擎，也不知道点燃这台引擎的那场远古相撞。

sentences.en: Modern geologists have reconstructed the entire collision in computer models, frame by frame across tens of millions of years, instructing the machines with the laws of physics and then watching, in patient animation, as the Himalaya rises again, slowly and convincingly, inside the screen.
sentences.zh: 现代地质学家已在计算机模型中逐帧重建整场碰撞，前后数千万年；他们用物理定律教导机器，再在耐心的动画里，看喜马拉雅在屏幕中缓慢而令人信服地重新升起。

sentences.en: Their reconstructions match the folded rocks so closely that a student can now watch mountains rise on a laptop in a single afternoon, and the match itself is quiet proof that the story geologists tell is very nearly the true history of the world.
sentences.zh: 重建结果与褶皱岩层吻合得如此之好，以至于如今一个学生能在一个下午里，用笔记本电脑看山脉长起来；这份吻合本身就是安静的证明——地质学家讲的故事，已非常接近世界的真实历史。

questions.q: What is Mount Everest made of, according to the chapter?
options: Granite from ancient volcanoes.
Rock that once formed the floor of an ancient sea.
Lava from the collision itself.
Sand blown from the Gobi Desert.
questions.explain: 第4句 “consists of rock that once formed the floor of an ancient sea”，珠峰的岩层本是古大海的海底。

questions.q: How fast does India still drive into Asia today?
options: About five millimeters a year.
About half a centimeter a year.
About five centimeters a year.
About five meters a year.
questions.explain: 第9句 “India still drives north at about five centimeters every year”，印度至今以每年约五厘米的速度北进。

questions.q: What happens when stress exceeds the strength of rock?
options: The layers fold into gentle arches forever.
The layers snap instead of bending, and the destruction arrives as an earthquake.
The rock melts quietly into magma.
The crust floats upward as pumice.
questions.explain: 第8句 “the layers snap instead of bending, and the destruction arrives as an earthquake”，应力超过强度时岩层断裂，破坏以地震到来。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the ocean fossils found near the summit of Everest?
options: That ancient climbers carried shells to the top as offerings.
That the sea once lay far above the land everywhere on Earth.
That the rocks of the summit were lifted from an ancient seabed, so these mountains grew from the floor of a vanished ocean.
That Everest was once a volcano in a shallow sea.
questions.explain: 第5句 “Fossils of ocean creatures appear near the summit, small shells and sea lilies of extraordinary beauty”，可推断峰顶岩石来自古海底，山是从消失的洋底长起来的。

questions.q: In the phrase “the structure of the folds”, what does the root struct mean?
options: To fold.
To heat.
To build — structure is the way something is built.
The sea.
questions.explain: 第6句 “the structure of the folds records the direction of the squeeze”，词根 struct 意为“建造”，structure 即某物被建造而成的方式。

title: 《地壳下的引擎》· 冰岛现场

sentences.en: In the southwest of Iceland, the mid-Atlantic ridge itself climbs out of the ocean and walks across dry land, so that a visitor can stand with one foot on the North American plate and the other on the European one, straddling two continents and two geological futures in a single step.
sentences.zh: 在冰岛西南，大西洋中脊亲自爬出海面，从干燥的陆地上穿行而过；游客可以一脚踩在北美板块、一脚踩在欧亚板块上，一步跨立两大洲和两种地质未来。

sentences.en: At Thingvellir, visitors can walk down into a rift valley and see the structure of two continents pulling apart above them, walls of cracked basalt on either side, the newest stone in Europe splitting quietly like a loaf being torn.
sentences.zh: 在辛格维利尔，游客可以走进一条裂谷，抬头看见两大板块把彼此拉开的结构：两侧是龟裂的玄武岩壁，欧洲最新的石头正像被撕开的面包一样安静地裂开。

sentences.en: The plates there separate by about two centimeters per year, roughly the speed at which your fingernails grow, an amount so small that no eye can catch it, yet the valley widens, the cracks deepen, and the cliff walls crawl apart century after century.
sentences.zh: 那里的板块每年分开约两厘米，大约等于你指甲生长的速度；这个量小到肉眼无法捕捉，可裂谷在变宽，裂缝在变深，崖壁一世纪又一世纪地缓缓爬开。

sentences.en: The island exists because a hot spot sits beneath the ridge, and the doubled heat constructs enough lava to build land that should by rights stay under the sea; Iceland is a country standing on the seam of the planet, warmed, lit, and in part built out of the leak itself.
sentences.zh: 这座岛之所以存在，是因为中脊之下坐着一个热斑；翻倍的热造出足够的熔岩，堆起本该待在海面之下的陆地——冰岛是一个立在行星接缝上的国家，靠这道泄漏取暖、照明，甚至在一定程度上就是用这道泄漏建成的。

sentences.en: The geology is so young and so active that geologists can study a plate boundary without a submarine, and they come from every nation on Earth to watch, in real time, a continent being born in front of their instruments.
sentences.zh: 这里地质年龄轻、活动强，地质学家不必乘潜水器就能研究板块边界；他们从世界各地赶来，在仪器前面实时观看一块大陆的诞生。

sentences.en: The people who live there have made an energy bargain with the ground: roughly nine out of ten Icelandic homes are heated with geothermal water piped straight from the volcanic rock beneath the farms, warm, mineral, and free of any fuel bill.
sentences.zh: 岛上居民与大地达成了一笔能源交易：大约十分之九的冰岛家庭，用管道直接引自农田下方火山岩的地热水取暖——水是温的、含矿的，账单里没有任何燃料。

sentences.en: Power stations at Krafla and Hellisheidi turn thermal energy into electricity for a nation of about 380,000 people, and the turbines spin on steam that no furnace was ever required to boil, for the Earth itself supplies the heat.
sentences.zh: 克拉夫拉与赫利舍迪两座电站把热能变成电，供约三十八万人使用；汽轮机靠蒸汽旋转，而那蒸汽从不需要任何炉子去烧——供热的是地球本身。

sentences.en: The infrastructure is unusual by world standards: instead of importing coal and gas across the ocean, the country runs its heating on steel-cased boreholes, kilometers of insulated pipe, and the patient labor of engineers who listen to the volcano.
sentences.zh: 以世界标准看，这套基础设施不同寻常：国家不用跨洋进口煤和气，供暖全靠钢套管钻孔、数公里长的保温管道，以及一群愿意倾听火山的、耐心的工程师。

sentences.en: Those engineers lower instruments into the wells to watch temperature, pressure, and the quiet movement of magma below, because a field that draws its power from a live engine must keep watching that engine, and a thermometer in the right borehole is worth a thousand theories argued in a comfortable office.
sentences.zh: 工程师们把仪器沉入井中，监视温度、压力，以及地下岩浆的细微动静；因为一个从活引擎身上取电的油田必须时时看住这台引擎——放在正确钻孔里的那支温度计，抵得上一千条在舒适办公室里争论出来的理论。

sentences.en: At Svartsengi, water too cool for generating electricity was dumped into a field of old black lava, and the silica-rich runoff turned milky blue where it gathered, so that the basin became the famous Blue Lagoon spa of today.
sentences.zh: 在斯瓦特森吉，用来发电嫌不够热的水被排进一片古老的黑色熔岩地；富含硅质的排水在积聚处变成乳蓝色，水塘便成了今天举世闻名的蓝湖温泉。

sentences.en: That lagoon is a byproduct of construction, a world-famous bath assembled from the leftovers of an engine, and the bathers who float in its warm blue water are, quite literally, swimming in the waste heat of the planet's interior.
sentences.zh: 那座湖是建造的副产品：一座世界闻名的浴场，由引擎的边角料拼装而成；漂浮在那温暖蓝色水面上的泡浴者，不折不扣是在行星内部的废热里游泳。

sentences.en: Thermostats in every school and office hold a steady warmth through the polar winter without burning one ton of coal, and children in Reykjavik have grown up never having seen the smoke of a heating fire.
sentences.zh: 每所学校与办公楼里的恒温器，让整个极地冬天稳稳的暖，不必烧一吨煤；雷克雅未克的孩子们长大成人，却从未见过取暖炉的烟。

sentences.en: An old engineer who had worked in the coal ports of his youth once told a young colleague that Iceland had simply plugged itself into the place where the planet leaks, and that every nation on Earth lives above a similar leak if it is patient enough to drill.
sentences.zh: 一位年轻时在煤港干过的老工程师曾对年轻同事说：冰岛不过是把自己插进了行星泄漏的地方；而地球上的每一个国家，只要有足够的耐心去钻，脚下其实都躺着一条类似的泄漏。

sentences.en: Iceland teaches the central lesson of geology better than any textbook: where the engine under the crust shows itself, a patient society can construct its whole infrastructure around the leak, and live warm and lit upon the waste of the world's making.
sentences.zh: 冰岛比任何教科书都更好地讲明了地质学的中心一课：凡地壳下的引擎露出身影之处，一个耐心的社会就能围绕这道泄漏建起整套基础设施，靠世界的造物之废热，活得又暖又亮。

questions.q: What can visitors see at Thingvellir?
options: An erupting volcano with rivers of lava.
A rift valley where the structure of two continents pulls apart.
A field of geysers and mud pots.
A bridge across a glacier.
questions.explain: 第2句 “walk down into a rift valley and see the structure of two continents pulling apart above them”，辛格维利尔可以看到两大板块拉开的裂谷结构。

questions.q: About how fast do the plates separate in Iceland?
options: About two millimeters per year.
About twenty centimeters per year.
About two centimeters per year, roughly the speed at which fingernails grow.
About two meters per year.
questions.explain: 第3句 “about two centimeters per year, roughly the speed at which your fingernails grow”，板块每年分开约两厘米。

questions.q: What share of Icelandic homes are heated with geothermal water?
options: Roughly nine out of ten.
Roughly one out of ten.
About half.
Almost none, because coal is cheaper.
questions.explain: 第6句 “roughly nine out of ten Icelandic homes are heated with geothermal water”，约十分之九的家庭用地热水取暖。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the Blue Lagoon from the chapter?
options: It is an ancient volcanic crater filled by rain.
It was dug as a swimming pool for tourists.
It is a byproduct of power production — a bath assembled from the leftovers of the engine.
It is a harbor flooded by the sea.
questions.explain: 第11句 “a byproduct of construction, a world-famous bath assembled from the leftovers of an engine”，可推断蓝湖并非天然温泉，而是电站排水的副产品。

questions.q: A thermostat keeps a school at a steady temperature. What does the root therm in thermostat mean?
options: Stone.
Heat.
Structure.
Water.
questions.explain: 第12句 “Thermostats in every school and office hold a steady warmth”，词根 therm 意为“热”，thermostat 即让温度保持稳定的热控制器。

title: 《地壳下的引擎》· 地震与预警

sentences.en: An earthquake begins as slow arithmetic: stress accumulates along a fault for decades while the surface above stays silent, and the people who live there build their houses, plant their fields, and raise their children through the long years of invisible loading, unaware.
sentences.zh: 地震始于一种缓慢的算术：应力沿断层积攒几十年，地表却保持沉默；住在那里的人盖房子、种庄稼、养大孩子，在看不见的漫长加压岁月里一无所知。

sentences.en: The two sides of the fault grip each other like a man gripping a rope, and elastic strain builds until the structure of the rock fails; the rope snaps, the grip releases, and the stored energy of half a lifetime leaves the rock in a single violent second, with a noise like distant cannon.
sentences.zh: 断层两侧像抓着绳索的手一样彼此咬合，弹性应变不断累积，直到岩石的结构失效；绳断了，手松了，半辈子积攒的能量在一记凶猛的瞬间倾泻而出，伴着远处炮声般的巨响。

sentences.en: In April 1906, the San Francisco earthquake destroyed most of a great city and killed about three thousand people, and the fires that followed the shaking burned for three days and nights what the shaking had spared, until the ruin of the proud young city was complete.
sentences.zh: 1906年4月，旧金山大地震摧毁了一座城市的大半，约三千人遇难；震动过后燃起的大火烧了三天三夜，把震动所饶过的部分也烧了进去，直到这座骄傲年轻城市的废墟凑齐为止。

sentences.en: Studying the ruptured ground afterward, the geologist Harry Fielding Reid reconstructed the mechanism now called elastic rebound: the fault's sides, bent slowly out of shape for decades, snap back like a stretched rubber band, releasing the stored energy within seconds.
sentences.zh: 事后研究破裂的地面，地质学家哈里·菲尔丁·里德重建了今天称为弹性回跳的机制：几十年间被慢慢拉歪的断层两侧，像绷紧的橡皮筋一样弹回，几十年的储能几秒内释放一空。

sentences.en: The energy travels outward as waves: fast P-waves jolt first, a sharp initial kick, and the slower S-waves follow with the destructive shaking that topples walls, and the gap between the two waves is where every warning system lives.
sentences.zh: 能量以波的形式向外传播：快的P波先来一记猛烈的初颠，慢一些的S波随后带来推倒墙壁的毁灭性摇晃；两波之间的时间差，正是每一套预警系统安身立命的地方。

sentences.en: Early-warning networks exploit that gap, turning a grid of sensitive instruments into a nervous system that feels the first kick, and instantly computes where the rupture happened, which cities the destructive waves will reach, and in exactly how many seconds they will arrive.
sentences.zh: 预警网络利用的正是这段时差：它把一排排灵敏的仪器连成一副神经系统，第一时间感知初颠，随即算出破裂发生在哪里、毁灭性的波将到达哪些城市、还剩下整整多少秒。

sentences.en: When the fast wave trips the seismometers, computers locate the rupture and warn the cities farther out, and the warning, however brief, travels faster than the shaking, because it rides on light instead of stone.
sentences.zh: 快波一触动地震仪，计算机立刻定位破裂点，向更远的城市报警；预警再短也跑得比摇晃快，因为它骑在光上，而不是骑在石头上。

sentences.en: Japan has run such a system since 2007, and in the great earthquake of 2011 it warned millions of people before the strongest shaking arrived; phones buzzed, television anchors spoke over the alarm, and trains were already braking when the waves reached the rails.
sentences.zh: 日本自2007年起运行这套系统；在2011年的大地震中，它在最强摇晃抵达前向数百万人发出了预警——手机嗡鸣，电视主播的声音压过警报声，而波浪抵达铁轨时，列车已经在制动。

sentences.en: The warning usually buys only five to thirty seconds, but that is enough to stop trains, to halt operating rooms, to open the doors of buildings so that jammed exits do not trap the frightened, and to let fire crews roll their engines out of the station and ready their hoses.
sentences.zh: 预警通常只换来五到三十秒，但足够让列车停下、让手术室暂停、让大楼的门自动打开以免慌乱的人群被卡住的出口困住，也足够让消防队把车开出站、备好水龙。

sentences.en: In 1985, an earthquake born far off the coast destroyed hundreds of buildings in Mexico City, which stands 350 kilometers from the sea, on the soft mud of an ancient lake bed that shakes like a bowl of jelly when the waves arrive.
sentences.zh: 1985年，一场源自远海的地震摧毁了墨西哥城数百栋建筑；这座城距海三百五十公里，坐落在古湖床的软泥上，波浪一到便像一碗果冻般晃动。

sentences.en: Mexico then constructed a network of sirens and sensors along that coast, and because the distance is long, the capital now receives up to a minute of notice, enough time for children to leave their classrooms and stand in the open air.
sentences.zh: 此后墨西哥沿海岸建起了警报器与传感器网络；正因为距离够长，首都如今最多能提前一分钟得到通知——足够孩子们走出教室，站到空旷的露天里。

sentences.en: Building codes share the same logic: engineers construct structures that bend and sway instead of snapping apart, and a well-designed steel frame survives the destruction that flattens a brittle one, absorbing energy the way a tree absorbs the wind.
sentences.zh: 建筑规范遵循同样的逻辑：工程师建造的是会弯曲摇摆而不折断的结构；设计良好的钢架能挺过足以压扁脆房子的破坏，像树吸收风一样把能量吸收掉。

sentences.en: The engine under the crust cannot be switched off, the plates will keep moving, and the earthquakes will keep arriving for as long as the Earth stays warm inside; no instrument, no building code, and no policy can end that.
sentences.zh: 地壳下的引擎无法关停，板块将继续移动；只要地球内部还是暖的，地震就会一次次到来——没有任何仪器、任何建筑规范、任何政策能终结这件事。

sentences.en: But instruments and honest infrastructure can hear the engine's warnings first, and a society that listens — drilling, bracing, teaching, rehearsing — turns a sudden catastrophe into a survivable event; that, in the end, is the whole instruction this book has tried to give.
sentences.zh: 但仪器与诚实的基础设施能最先听见引擎的预警；一个肯倾听的社会——去钻井、去加固、去教导、去演练——能把骤然的灾难变成一场可幸存的事件：归根到底，这就是本书试图给出的全部教诲。

questions.q: What did Harry Fielding Reid reconstruct after the 1906 earthquake?
options: The first plate tectonic map.
A tsunami warning system for the Pacific.
The mechanism now called elastic rebound.
The epicenter of every Pacific quake.
questions.explain: 第4句 “reconstructed the mechanism now called elastic rebound”，里德在震后重建了弹性回跳机制。

questions.q: What is the difference between P-waves and S-waves?
options: P-waves only travel through water.
Fast P-waves jolt first, and the slower S-waves follow with the destructive shaking.
S-waves are always stronger but slower than P-waves in water.
P-waves arrive days before S-waves.
questions.explain: 第5句 “fast P-waves jolt first, a sharp initial kick, and the slower S-waves follow with the destructive shaking”，快P波先颠，慢S波随后带来毁灭性摇晃。

questions.q: Since when has Japan operated its earthquake early-warning system?
options: Since 1906.
Since 1985.
Since 2007.
Since 2011.
questions.explain: 第8句 “Japan has run such a system since 2007”，日本的预警系统自2007年起运行。

questions.q: Why does Mexico City receive up to a minute of warning?
options: Because the capital has its own fault directly beneath it.
Because the threatening coast lies about 350 kilometers away, so the long distance gives the sensors time to fire first.
Because Mexican buildings are extremely tall and slow to shake.
Because the government banned construction near the coast.
questions.explain: 第10句 “which stands 350 kilometers from the sea” 与第11句 “because the distance is long, the capital now receives up to a minute of notice”，可推断远距离换来提前量。

questions.q: In the sentence about building codes, what does the root struct mean in “engineers construct structures”?
options: To shake.
To warn.
To build — construct means to build, and a structure is something built.
To measure.
questions.explain: 第12句 “engineers construct structures that bend and sway instead of snapping apart”，词根 struct 意为“建造”：construct 即建造，structure 即被建造之物。

title: 《流行病简史》· 雅典瘟疫

sentences.en: In 430 BC, in the second year of the long Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta, a disease that no one could name slipped into the crowded city of Athens, and within weeks it was moving through the packed lanes like fire through a dry summer forest.
sentences.zh: 公元前430年，雅典与斯巴达之间的伯罗奔尼撒战争进入第二年，一场无人能叫出名字的疫病溜进了拥挤的雅典城；不出几周，它便像野火烧过干燥的夏日森林一样，在塞满人的街巷里蔓延开来。

sentences.en: Pericles, the city's most trusted general, had ordered the whole rural population of Attica behind the long walls, betting that a crowded democracy could outlast a Spartan siege, and nobody in the assembly guessed that the crowding itself, in that thirsty summer, would become the killer.
sentences.zh: 城中最受信赖的将军伯里克利，早已下令把整个阿提卡的乡下人口迁到长墙之内，赌一个拥挤的民主政体能耗赢斯巴达的围城；而公民大会上没有一个人猜到，在那个干渴的夏天，拥挤本身会成为头号杀手。

sentences.en: The Spartan army, a disciplined corps of farmer-soldiers, camped among the smoking farms of Attica but kept a careful distance from the walls, so the sickness stayed a purely Athenian guest while the refugees watched their own villages burn from the ramparts with their own eyes.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达军队这支由农夫组成、纪律严明的军团，在冒烟的阿提卡田野间扎营，却始终与城墙保持谨慎的距离；于是疫病成了雅典人独有的客人，难民们只能从城墙上，亲眼看着自己的村庄化为灰烬。

sentences.en: Inside the walls, thousands of refugees passed a season of horror in the crowded huts of the summer heat: skin so hot that no linen could touch it, endless vomiting, a thirst that whole jars of water could not calm, and sleepless nights stacked upon sleepless nights.
sentences.zh: 高墙之内，成千上万的难民在夏日酷热里挤在棚屋中熬过一段恐怖的时光：皮肤灼热得连亚麻布都无法触碰，呕吐不止，喝下整罐的水也压不住的干渴，还有一夜接一夜、无休无止的失眠。

sentences.en: Thucydides, a young general who would later write the history of the whole war, caught the sickness himself and survived it, which gave him both the courage to watch the dying closely and the strange, calm authority of a man with nothing left to fear.
sentences.zh: 修昔底德，这位日后要为整场战争撰写历史的年轻将军，自己也染上了疫病并活了下来；这既给了他近距离注视垂死者的勇气，也给了他一种无所畏惧之人特有的、奇异的平静与权威。

sentences.en: He described the plague with the cold precision of pathology rather than the tone of pity, setting down the burning skin, the red inflamed eyes, the bleeding gums, the failed sleep, and the memory loss that shadowed the survivors, in the exact order in which the symptoms appeared.
sentences.zh: 他以病理学般的冷峻精确、而非怜悯的腔调描述这场瘟疫：灼热的皮肤、红肿发炎的眼睛、出血的牙龈、无法入睡的长夜，以及纠缠幸存者的记忆衰退——而且严格按照症状出现的先后顺序记录。

sentences.en: He explained his purpose in his own words: the account was written “so that men would recognize the disease if it ever returned”, and in that single sentence he founded a whole tradition of epidemic reporting that health officers with their daily bulletins still follow today.
sentences.zh: 他用自己的话解释了写作目的：这份记录之所以写下，是“为了让人们在疾病卷土重来时能认出它”；凭这一句话，他便开创了卫生官员至今仍以每日简报沿循的疫情记录传统。

sentences.en: He also recorded, with a historian's sadness, the failure of sympathy: men dared not visit their sick friends, the dying were left alone by relatives too frightened to come close, and even the humble rites of preparing a body were abandoned, because every act of kindness had become a risk of death.
sentences.zh: 他还带着史学家的悲哀，记下了同情的失灵：人们不敢探望患病的朋友，垂死者被吓得不敢靠近的亲属独自留在那里，连为遗体做最基本的安放仪式也被放弃了——因为每一个善举，都变成了拿性命去做的冒险。

sentences.en: Corpses piled up in the streets faster than the rites of burial could be performed for them; some families slipped their dead onto other people's pyres by night, and the whole city smelled of smoke, of burning flesh, and of the long summer that would not end.
sentences.zh: 尸体在街头堆积的速度，快过下葬仪式能为它们一一举行的速度；有些家庭趁着夜色，把自家的死者悄悄放到别人家的柴堆上；整座城市都弥漫着烟、焦肉，以及那个迟迟不肯结束的漫长夏天的气味。

sentences.en: The demographic shock was severe beyond anything the city had known; scholars still estimate that between a quarter and a third of the crowded population eventually died, and Thucydides, counting the unburied, concluded that the plague was the most lethal thing the Greek world had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 人口冲击之惨重，远超这座城邦此前经历的一切；学者至今仍估计，城内拥挤的人口最终死去了四分之一到三分之一；修昔底德清点着无人掩埋的死者，断言这场瘟疫是希腊世界见过的最致命之物。

sentences.en: Pericles lost both of his legitimate sons to the plague and then died of it himself in the following year, and the democracy lost the one leader whose patience and prestige might still have steered the exhausted city through the war with some honor.
sentences.zh: 伯里克利的两个婚生儿子先后死于瘟疫，次年他本人也染病身亡；这个民主政体失去了唯一一位凭耐心与威望，或许还能带着这座精疲力竭的城邦体面走出战争的领袖。

sentences.en: Thucydides noticed a deeper rot as well: watching death so closely, many citizens fell into a flat apathy about the laws of their city, spending their savings on quick pleasures, because honor and gold and fine words suddenly looked like pathetic shields against a plague that took no bribes.
sentences.zh: 修昔底德还注意到一种更深的溃烂：日日近距离注视死亡之后，许多公民对城邦的法律变得麻木冷漠，把积蓄挥霍在即时的享乐上——因为荣誉、黄金和漂亮话，在一场不肯收买的瘟疫面前，忽然都成了可怜的挡箭牌。

sentences.en: Modern doctors read his pages with a professional empathy that crosses twenty-five centuries, and they still argue about the pathogen; typhus, typhoid, and smallpox each have scholarly defenders, although no modern diagnosis quite fits every detail of his careful account.
sentences.zh: 现代医生怀着跨越二十五个世纪的职业共鸣阅读他的书页，却仍在争论病原体：斑疹伤寒、伤寒与天花各有各的学者拥趸，只是任何现代诊断，都无法完全吻合他细细记录下的每一个细节。

sentences.en: He wrote for future readers, and the future keeps answering him; whenever a new epidemic or pandemic enters a crowded city, his description of fear, fever, and failed burial still reads as if the ink were barely dry, which is the highest compliment a witness can be paid.
sentences.zh: 他为未来的读者而写，而未来也一直在回应他；每当一场新的流行病或大流行进入某座拥挤的城市，他笔下那些恐惧、高烧与无人下葬的描述，读来仍像墨迹未干——这正是一位见证者所能得到的最高礼赞。

questions.q: When and where did the unnamed disease first strike in this chapter?
options: In 430 BC, inside the crowded city of Athens during the Peloponnesian War.
In 404 BC, when the war finally ended.
In a Spartan army camp, before the siege began.
In 430 BC, in the open countryside of Attica.
questions.explain: 第1句 “slipped into the crowded city of Athens”——疫病于公元前430年、战争第二年溜进拥挤的雅典城，斯巴达军队刻意远离城墙，故B、C、D均与原文不符。

questions.q: Which symptoms did Thucydides record, in the order he gave them?
options: Bleeding gums, then burning skin, then memory loss.
Burning skin, red inflamed eyes, bleeding gums, failed sleep, and memory loss.
Vomiting and thirst only.
Cough, fever, and rash.
questions.explain: 第6句 “setting down the burning skin, the red inflamed eyes, the bleeding gums, the failed sleep, and the memory loss”——他按症状出现的先后顺序逐一记下，选项B完整对应原文。

questions.q: How much of the population may have died, according to scholars' estimates?
options: About one in ten.
Between a quarter and a third.
More than half.
Only the soldiers.
questions.explain: 第10句 “between a quarter and a third of the crowded population eventually died”——学者估计全城最终死了四分之一到三分之一的人口。

questions.q: What can we infer about the crowded-city strategy from the chapter?
options: It worked exactly as Pericles planned.
By packing refugees behind the walls, it unintentionally gave the disease perfect conditions to spread.
It forced the Spartans to retreat quickly.
It was abandoned before the plague arrived.
questions.explain: 第2句 “betting that a crowded democracy could outlast a Spartan siege”——把全体乡民塞进长墙之内，本为拖垮围城，却“无人猜到拥挤本身会成为杀手”；由此可推知，这一策略反而为疫病传播创造了理想条件。

questions.q: The word “democracy” in sentence 2 contains the root “dem”. What does this root mean?
options: City.
People.
Disease.
Body.
questions.explain: 第2句 “betting that a crowded democracy could outlast a Spartan siege”——dem 意为“人民”，democracy 即“人民的统治”；同根词还有 demographic（人口学的）、pandemic（涉及全体人民的疫病）。

title: 《流行病简史》· 黑死病

sentences.en: In October 1347, twelve Genoese trading ships reached the harbor of Messina in Sicily, carrying a cargo that no manifest had listed and no doctor knew how to treat: plague, which came ashore with the rats, the rags, and the dying sailors, before the year was out.
sentences.zh: 1347年10月，十二艘热那亚商船抵达西西里墨西拿港，运来一件舱单上没写、也无医生知道如何医治的货物：鼠疫——它随老鼠、破布与垂死的水手一起登岸，年底之前便蔓延开来。

sentences.en: The Black Death became the second great pandemic of plague, and within five years it had killed between a third and a half of Europe, perhaps twenty-five million people, a mortality that no war on that continent has ever come close to in all its history.
sentences.zh: 黑死病成为鼠疫的第二次大流行，五年之内杀死了欧洲三分之一到一半的人口，约两千五百万人；此后欧洲历史上任何一场战争，都从未接近过这样的死亡率。

sentences.en: Chroniclers recorded the mortality parish by parish, which makes this the first epidemic in history with detailed archives; in Siena, Agnolo di Tura wrote, “I buried my five children with my own hands”, and added that so many died that everyone believed it was the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 编年史家逐教区记录死亡人数，使它成为历史上第一场留下详细档案的流行病；在锡耶纳，编年史家阿尼奥洛·迪·图拉写道：“我亲手埋葬了我的五个孩子”，并补充说死者太多，人人都以为世界末日到了。

sentences.en: In Florence, the population fell from about one hundred and twenty thousand before the plague to fewer than fifty thousand after it, and even the banking families, some of them corpulent with generations of easy profit, could no longer hire enough hands to bury their neighbors properly.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗伦萨，人口从瘟疫前的约十二万跌到之后的不足五万；连那些世代坐享其成、身躯肥硕的银行世家，也再雇不到足够的人手，去体面地埋葬他们的邻居。

sentences.en: Giovanni Boccaccio, who watched the outbreak from inside Florence and lived, opened his Decameron with the plain facts of the city: every morning the carts collected the corpses, brothers abandoned brothers, and the great marble tombs of the rich were dug open for the poor.
sentences.zh: 亲眼看着瘟疫席卷佛罗伦萨并幸存下来的乔万尼·薄伽丘，在《十日谈》开篇写下了这座城市的真实景象：每天清晨推车收走成堆的尸体，兄弟抛下兄弟，富人家的大理石墓穴被掘开，用来安葬穷人。

sentences.en: His ten storytellers, seven young women and three young men, flee the dying city for a country villa and swap a hundred tales across ten days, because Boccaccio believed that in a plague the sensible plan is to escape it, and to keep one's spirits as light as possible.
sentences.zh: 他笔下的十位讲故事的人——七位年轻女子和三位青年——逃离这座垂死的城市，躲进乡间别墅，在十天里交换了一百个故事；因为薄伽丘相信，瘟疫之中明智的计划就是逃开它，并让心情尽量轻松。

sentences.en: He described how fear split the city into two camps: some citizens, deciding that no medicine could save them, drank deep and gave way to pleasure, while others lived soberly indoors, stepping out with bunches of flowers and herbs to cover the smell of the dead.
sentences.zh: 他描述恐惧如何把城市劈成两派：一些市民断定任何药物都救不了自己，索性纵酒寻欢；另一些人则闭门克制度日，出门时手捧成束的花草香草，以盖过死者的气味。

sentences.en: Ordinary feeling seemed to die with the sick; in one story Boccaccio watches pigs root among the rags of a poor dead man, tumble over, and die on the spot, an early and grotesque hint that whatever the killer was, it clung to bodies and clothing.
sentences.zh: 寻常的情感仿佛随病人一同死去；薄伽丘讲过一个故事：几头猪在一名穷死者的破衣堆里拱食，随即翻倒毙命——这是一个早熟而怪诞的暗示：无论凶手是什么，它都附着在身体与衣物上。

sentences.en: City governments answered with the first public-health measures that Europe had ever seriously attempted; councils incorporated the new plague boards into their statutes, orders were issued to clean the streets of the towns, and for once public policy and public sympathy pointed in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 各城邦政府拿出欧洲有史以来第一次认真尝试的公共卫生措施：议事会把新设的瘟疫委员会写进城邦法令，清洁城镇街道的命令接连颁布；难得有一回，公共政策与公众的同情心指向了同一个方向。

sentences.en: Venice appointed a small corps of officials to board incoming ships, inspect the cargo and the crew, and isolate sick sailors on islands in the lagoon, and with that order the modern practice of organized isolation became, for the first time, an instrument of state.
sentences.zh: 威尼斯任命一支小小的官员队伍登上来船，检查货物与船员，把患病的水手隔离在潟湖中的岛屿上；凭这道命令，有组织的隔离第一次成为国家治理的一件工具。

sentences.en: In 1377 the port of Ragusa ordered every arriving traveler to wait thirty days on a nearby headland before entering the town, trusting the delay more than any drug or prayer, and other ports along the Adriatic copied the rule within a few years.
sentences.zh: 1377年，拉古萨港命令所有抵达的旅客先在附近的海岬上等待三十天，方可进城——他们对这段延时的信任，胜过对任何药物或祈祷的信任；几年之内，亚得里亚海沿岸的其他港口纷纷效仿。

sentences.en: The period was soon stretched to forty days, quaranta giorni, and that is where the word quarantine comes from; it was a quiet triumph of policy over pathology, because nobody had seen the pathogen or understood it, yet the delay alone starved it of its chance to pass on.
sentences.zh: 这一时限不久便延长为四十天，意大利语称 quaranta giorni，“隔离检疫”（quarantine）一词便由此而来；这是政策对病理学的一次安静胜利——没人见过病原体，更无人理解它，但仅仅靠拖延，就断送了它继续传播的机会。

sentences.en: The epidemic still returned in smaller waves for three centuries, walking the trade routes at the pace of a merchant, but never again with the force of 1348, and the parishes learned to count its coming as they counted the harvest and the taxes.
sentences.zh: 此后三个世纪，这场流行病仍以较小的规模反复回潮，沿着商路以一名商人的步速行走，却再没有1348年那样的威力；各教区学会了像记录收成和税收一样，记录它的到来。

sentences.en: The demographic break proved durable: labor turned scarce, wages rose, and landlords lost their ancient grip on the survivors; by 1381 the workers of England were marching behind Wat Tyler, and historians still argue how much of that new spirit the Black Death had planted.
sentences.zh: 人口断层的影响经久不散：劳动力变得稀缺，工资上涨，领主对幸存者古老的钳制松了手；到1381年，英格兰的工人已追随瓦特·泰勒上街游行——这场瘟疫究竟播下了多少那股新精神，历史学家至今仍在争论。

questions.q: How did the plague arrive in Europe in 1347?
options: On Genoese trading ships that reached Messina in Sicily in October 1347.
With a Spartan army marching overland.
On river barges sailing down the Rhine.
With pilgrims returning from Rome.
questions.explain: 第1句 “twelve Genoese trading ships reached the harbor of Messina in Sicily”——鼠疫随热那亚商船于1347年10月抵达西西里，与老鼠、破布和垂死的水手一同登岸。

questions.q: What did the Sienese chronicler Agnolo di Tura write about his own family?
options: That he had fled the city with his children.
That he buried his five children with his own hands.
That his village was spared by the plague.
That he became rich selling herbs.
questions.explain: 第3句 “I buried my five children with my own hands”——阿尼奥洛·迪·图拉亲手埋葬五个孩子，并补充说死者太多，人人都以为是世界末日。

questions.q: Where does the word “quarantine” come from?
options: The Latin word for ship.
The name of a Venetian island.
The Italian quaranta giorni, meaning forty days.
A famous plague doctor's surname.
questions.explain: 第12句 “The period was soon stretched to forty days, quaranta giorni, and that is where the word quarantine comes from”——隔离时限从三十天延为四十天，quarantine 得名于意大利语的“四十天”。

questions.q: What can we infer from the fact that later waves of plague never matched the force of 1348?
options: The disease disappeared from Europe completely.
The delay-based measures and parish counting probably gave the cities some protection.
Europeans had become fully immune to plague.
All trade routes were permanently closed.
questions.explain: 第13句 “never again with the force of 1348”——回潮从未再现1348年的威力；结合上文威尼斯的隔离与拉古萨的三十天等候，可推知这些以拖延为核心的措施为城市提供了部分保护。

questions.q: In sentence 4, “corpulent” comes from the Latin root “corp”. What does this root mean?
options: People.
Feeling.
Body.
Ship.
questions.explain: 第4句 “some of them corpulent with generations of easy profit”——corp 意为“身体”，corpulent 即“身体肥硕的”；同根词还有 corpse（尸体）和 corps（队伍、军团）。

title: 《流行病简史》· 天花与牛痘

sentences.en: Smallpox killed an estimated three hundred million people in the twentieth century alone, more than all the wars of that century combined, and for thousands of years before that it had been a pandemic disease without cure, without season, and without mercy for rich and poor alike.
sentences.zh: 仅二十世纪，天花就估计夺走三亿人的生命，比该世纪所有战争加起来还多；在此之前的数千年里，它一直是一种无药可医、不分季节、对贫富一视同仁毫不留情的大流行疾病。

sentences.en: The disease spared no rank: it killed Louis XV of France in 1774 and Queen Mary of England in 1694, along with millions of ordinary children in every village of Europe, whose names were never written down in any parish book at all, only counted among the dead.
sentences.zh: 这病不挑身份：1774年它杀死法国的路易十五，1694年杀死英格兰的玛丽女王；还有欧洲每个村庄里数以百万计的普通孩子，他们的名字从未被记进任何教区簿册，只被算进死者之数。

sentences.en: In the London of 1796, nearly every adult face carried the pitted scars of the disease, blind survivors begged at the church doors, and the small corpses of children went out of the houses each morning on the common carts, so hardened had the city's sympathy grown.
sentences.zh: 1796年的伦敦，几乎每张成年面孔都带着天花的麻疤，失明的幸存者在教堂门口乞讨，孩童的小小尸体每天清晨随公用推车被运出家门——这座城市的同情心，早已磨出厚茧。

sentences.en: Doctors had long practiced variolation, inoculating healthy people with matter taken from a mild case of smallpox, a method that English merchants had learned from the healers of Istanbul; it worked often enough, but it killed perhaps one patient in every hundred, and could even start fresh outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 医生们早已实践人痘接种：把轻型天花病例中取出的物质接种给健康人，这一方法是英国商人从伊斯坦布尔的医者那里学来的；它常常有效，但大约每百人中会死一人，甚至可能引发新的疫情。

sentences.en: Families gambled anyway, because the odds still looked kind next to the epidemic itself; a mother of the time might well have said, “Better the needle's small risk than the pox that takes the face”, and many a spring the wager rolled over the whole parish.
sentences.zh: 人们仍愿赌上一把，因为和疫病本身相比，这点胜算已算仁慈；那个年代的母亲很可能会说：“宁冒针头的小险，不赌毁容的天花。”许多个春天，这场赌局都会在整片教区轮转一遍。

sentences.en: A country doctor named Edward Jenner had noticed while training in the countryside that dairymaids who had recovered from cowpox never caught smallpox; one of them told him, “I cannot take the smallpox, for I have had the cowpox”, and the pathology of his day could not explain why that should protect anyone.
sentences.zh: 名叫爱德华·詹纳的乡村医生早在乡间学医时就注意到：患过牛痘的挤奶女工从不染上天花；其中一位对他说过：“我生不了天花，因为我得过牛痘。”而他那个时代的病理学，完全无法解释这为何能保护一个人。

sentences.en: In May 1796, Jenner took fresh matter from a cowpox sore on the hand of a dairymaid named Sarah Nelmes and scratched it into the arm of a healthy eight-year-old boy, James Phipps, the son of his own gardener, and the boy barely flinched.
sentences.zh: 1796年5月，詹纳从挤奶女工萨拉·内尔姆斯手上的牛痘疮里取了新鲜物质，划进一个健康八岁男孩——他自家园丁的儿子詹姆斯·菲普斯——的手臂，那孩子几乎没缩一下。

sentences.en: The boy felt mildly unwell for a day or two and then recovered; six weeks later Jenner challenged him twice with matter from a fresh smallpox sore, and Phipps showed no fever, no eruption, and no susceptibility whatsoever, as if the cow had quietly trained his blood for the duel.
sentences.zh: 男孩只轻微不适了一两天便恢复了；六周后，詹纳两次用新鲜天花疮中的物质向他发起挑战，菲普斯却全无发热、无疹、无任何易感迹象——仿佛那头母牛早已悄悄训练过他的血液去赴这场决斗。

sentences.en: Jenner called the method vaccination, from vacca, the Latin word for cow, and although the Royal Society politely refused his first paper, he published the evidence himself in 1798; within a year, pamphlets describing the new protection had crossed most of Europe's borders and the Atlantic as well.
sentences.zh: 詹纳把这种方法命名为 vaccination，取自拉丁语的 vacca（母牛）；皇家学会虽然婉拒了他最初的论文，他仍在1798年自行发表了证据；不出一年，介绍这种新防护法的小册子便越过了欧洲大部分国界，也跨过了大西洋。

sentences.en: The idea was not guesswork but the seed of immunology: a mild pathogen borrowed from a cow taught the human body to recognize a killer without ever risking the full disease, and the body remembered that lesson for years, which is exactly what doctors now call immunity.
sentences.zh: 这个想法绝非瞎猜，而是免疫学的种子：从牛身上借来的一种温和病原体，教会人体识别一名杀手，却不必冒罹患重症之险，而且身体会把这个教训记住多年——这正是如今医生所说的“免疫力”。

sentences.en: The medical corps of the day split down the middle: London cartoonists drew vaccinated patients growing horns, udders, and little cow faces, while quieter country doctors simply copied the method, and within a decade the vaccine had crossed the ocean into the Americas, without asking anyone's permission.
sentences.zh: 当年的医学阵营从中间裂成两半：伦敦的漫画家画出接种者长出犄角、乳房和小牛脸的模样，而更沉得住气的乡村医生则默默照搬这套方法；不出十年，疫苗便未经任何人许可，越过大洋传入了美洲。

sentences.en: Napoleon, though at war with Britain, had his own soldiers vaccinated by his army corps; when Jenner later wrote to him asking mercy for an English prisoner of war, the emperor reportedly answered, “I can refuse that man nothing”, and set the prisoner free.
sentences.zh: 与英国交战的拿破仑，也让自己军团的士兵接种了疫苗；后来詹纳致信为他求情一名英国战俘，据说这位皇帝回答：“这个人要什么我都没法拒绝。”随后便放了那名战俘。

sentences.en: Where parishes incorporated vaccination into the routine registration of newborn babies, child mortality fell sharply, the pathetic sight of blinded and scarred orphans grew rarer in the streets, and the old demographic fear that every outbreak season brought slowly faded from the cities of Europe.
sentences.zh: 凡把疫苗接种并入新生儿常规登记的教区，儿童死亡率都急剧下降；街上那些失明带疤的孤儿——那副可怜景象——越来越少见，而每逢疫病季节便要发作一次的旧日人口恐慌，也慢慢从欧洲的城市里退去。

sentences.en: In 1977 the last natural case appeared in Somalia, and in 1980 the World Health Organization, after a corps of vaccinators had hunted the disease through every remaining village and market, declared smallpox eradicated: the first disease, and so far the only one, that human cooperation has ever erased from the earth.
sentences.zh: 1977年，最后一例自然病例出现在索马里；1980年，在一支接种员队伍追遍每一个残存村庄与集市之后，世界卫生组织宣布天花已被消灭：这是人类合作有史以来从地球上抹去的第一种疾病，至今也是唯一的一种。

questions.q: What material did Jenner use for his famous 1796 experiment, and on whom?
options: Matter from a mild smallpox case, given to a dairymaid.
Fresh matter from a cowpox sore on Sarah Nelmes's hand, given to eight-year-old James Phipps.
Crushed herbs, given to his own gardener.
Matter from a dead calf, given to a London orphan.
questions.explain: 第7句 “Jenner took fresh matter from a cowpox sore on the hand of a dairymaid named Sarah Nelmes and scratched it into the arm of a healthy eight-year-old boy, James Phipps”——他用的是萨拉·内尔姆斯手上牛痘疮的新鲜物质，接种对象是园丁之子菲普斯。

questions.q: Where does the word “vaccination” come from?
options: Vacca, the Latin word for cow.
Vacuum, meaning empty space.
A French village called Vachon.
The Greek word for protection.
questions.explain: 第9句 “Jenner called the method vaccination, from vacca, the Latin word for cow”——vaccination 得名于拉丁语 vacca（母牛），因为最早的防护物质来自牛痘。

questions.q: What was variolation, and what was its risk?
options: A surgical removal of scars; the risk was blindness.
A forty-day isolation; the risk was starvation.
Inoculating healthy people with mild smallpox matter; it killed perhaps one patient in every hundred.
A prayer ritual; it had no risk at all.
questions.explain: 第4句 “it killed perhaps one patient in every hundred”——人痘接种用轻型天花物质，约百人中死一人，甚至可能引发新的疫情。

questions.q: What does the Napoleon anecdote suggest about vaccination at the time?
options: That Napoleon hoped to weaken the British army.
That its value was recognized even across enemy lines in the middle of a war.
That Napoleon had invented a better vaccine himself.
That Britain had banned vaccination everywhere.
questions.explain: 第12句 “I can refuse that man nothing”——与英国交战的拿破仑不仅让自己的军团接种，还尊詹纳为恩人；由此可推知，疫苗的价值在战争敌对的双方之间都得到了承认。

questions.q: In sentence 6, “pathology” contains the root “path”. What does this root mean?
options: People.
Body.
Suffering or disease.
City.
questions.explain: 第6句 “the pathology of his day could not explain why that should protect anyone”——path 源自希腊语 pathos，意为“感受、痛苦”，pathology 即“研究疾病之学”；同根词还有 sympathy（同情）和 pathetic（可怜的）。

title: 《流行病简史》· 西班牙流感

sentences.en: In March 1918, a cook at Camp Funston in Kansas reported to the infirmary with headache and fever, and within days the sickness was running through the crowded barracks like a grass fire, filling the wards faster than the camp's small medical corps could empty them.
sentences.zh: 1918年3月，堪萨斯州芬斯顿军营的一名炊事员因头痛发热前往医务室；不出几天，疫病便如燎原之火烧遍拥挤的营房，病床被填满的速度，快过这支小小的军医队伍腾空它们的速度。

sentences.en: Within months, regiments of the American army corps were boarding the crowded troop ships that crossed the Atlantic for the Western Front, carrying the invisible virus in their lungs to every port between Halifax and Brest, while the war made stopping the traffic unthinkable for a single week.
sentences.zh: 几个月内，美国军团的各个团正挤上横渡大西洋、开赴西线的运兵船，肺里带着这种看不见的病毒，把它带到哈利法克斯与布雷斯特之间的每一个港口；而战争让这股人流连一周都不可能停。

sentences.en: By autumn a second wave had turned far deadlier: strong young soldiers turned blue in the face, bled from the nose and ears, and sometimes died within a single day, and their doctors, helpless at the bedside, found the sight almost too pathetic to record in their letters home.
sentences.zh: 入秋之后，第二波凶残得多：健壮的年轻士兵脸色发青，鼻耳出血，有时一天之内便死去；守在床边束手无策的军医们，觉得这惨状可怜得几乎无法写进寄回家里的信里。

sentences.en: The 1918 influenza eventually infected perhaps five hundred million people, roughly a third of all humanity then alive, from the trenches of France to Inuit villages in Alaska, some of which were wiped out within a single week and left empty behind their dogs and their sleds.
sentences.zh: 这场1918年大流感最终感染了大约五亿人——约占当时全人类的三分之一——从法国的战壕到阿拉斯加的因纽特村庄；有些村庄一周之内被整个抹去，只留下空屋、狗和雪橇。

sentences.en: It killed somewhere between twenty and fifty million people, a total that exceeded the four years of the Great War's own slaughter; in India alone, twelve to seventeen million died, and in some villages the corpses lay waiting for days because there was not enough firewood left to burn them.
sentences.zh: 它夺走两千到五千万条生命，超过了大战四年屠杀的总和；仅在印度就死了一千二百万到一千七百万人，一些村子里，尸体一连几天躺在原地等待，因为连火化它们的柴火都已不够。

sentences.en: The demographic signature was strange and cruel: instead of the very old and the very young, the disease cut down healthy adults between twenty and forty, exactly the workers, nurses, and young parents that families, farms, and armies could least afford to lose.
sentences.zh: 它的人口学印记奇特而残酷：倒下的既不是老人也不是幼儿，而是二十到四十岁之间的健康成年人——恰恰是家庭、农场和军队最赔不起的工人、护士与年轻父母。

sentences.en: Wartime censorship hid the epidemic in every belligerent country; editors were forbidden to print anything that might hurt morale, so the newspapers promised a mild three-day fever while, outside the printing houses, the hearses stood in queues and the gravediggers worked in shifts day and night.
sentences.zh: 战时审查在每个交战国都掩盖了这场流行病；编辑被禁止刊登任何可能打击士气的消息，于是报纸把病说成“三天即愈的轻症”；而印刷所门外，灵车排着队，掘墓人昼夜轮班。

sentences.en: Neutral Spain had no censors, so when the young king Alfonso XIII fell seriously ill, his fever made honest headlines around the world, and the pandemic was misnamed the Spanish flu almost as a punishment for reporting the disease truthfully in the middle of the war.
sentences.zh: 中立的西班牙没有审查制度，于是年轻的国王阿方索十三世病重的消息，诚实地登上了全世界的头条；结果这场大流行竟被误称为“西班牙流感”——几乎算是对它在战争中途如实报道疫病的惩罚。

sentences.en: In Philadelphia, the newspapers repeated the official promise that the disease was no more dangerous than ordinary flu, and on 28 September 1918 a parade of some two hundred thousand people marched down Broad Street in the sunshine, singing as they collected war bonds for the government.
sentences.zh: 在费城，报纸不断重复官方的保证：这病不比普通流感更危险；1918年9月28日，约二十万人的游行队伍在阳光下列队走过宽街，一边唱着歌，一边为政府募集战争债券。

sentences.en: Within six weeks the city had dug about twelve thousand graves; hospitals ran out of sheets, coffins, and gravediggers, the dead were buried in plain trenches, and public sympathy, stretched past its limit, slowly hardened into the flat apathy of people who had seen too many carts.
sentences.zh: 六周之内，全城挖出约一万两千座坟；医院的床单、棺材和掘墓人都用尽了，死者被草草埋进普通壕沟；公众的同情心被拉到极限之后，慢慢硬化成人人见过太多运尸车之后那种麻木的冷漠。

sentences.en: Science moved faster than ever before: within months the bacteriologist Richard Pfeiffer isolated a small bacillus from flu patients and confidently named it the pathogen, an honest mistake that sent the whole medical world chasing the wrong killer, and the pathology textbooks repeated the error for years.
sentences.zh: 科学的反应比以往任何时候都快：几个月内，细菌学家理查德·法伊弗便从流感病人体内分离出一种小杆菌，并自信地宣布它就是病原体——这个善意的错误让整个医学界追错了凶手，病理学教科书把这一谬误重复了好几年。

sentences.en: The true agent was a virus far too small for any microscope of 1918; nobody could see it, grow it, or photograph it, and the truth was not finally confirmed until the new electron microscopes, decades later, opened the invisible world to human eyes at last.
sentences.zh: 真正的凶手是一种病毒，小得连1918年的任何显微镜都看不见；无人能看见它、培养它或拍下它，直到几十年后新型的电子显微镜终于替人类打开了那个看不见的世界，真相才尘埃落定。

sentences.en: Then the pandemic burned itself out by 1920, taking much of its mystery with it; a world exhausted by war buried its millions of dead and, at the same time, buried the memory of them, and the worst demographic shock of the century was largely forgotten by 1925.
sentences.zh: 1920年前，这场大流行自行燃尽，也带走了它的大部分谜团；被战争拖垮的世界埋葬了数百万死者，同时也埋葬了对他们的记忆——这个世纪最惨重的人口冲击，到1925年已大体被人遗忘。

sentences.en: The story survived only in the private letters of doctors and nurses, in the memoirs of a few pathologists, and in the silence of widows and orphans; historians now rank the Spanish flu beside the plague of Athens and the Black Death in the grim family of humanity's worst pandemics.
sentences.zh: 这段往事只活在一些医生护士的私人信件里、少数病理学家的回忆录里，以及寡妇孤儿的沉默里；如今历史学家把西班牙流感与雅典瘟疫、黑死病并排，列入人类最惨烈大流行病那个阴森的家族。

questions.q: Where did the first recorded American case of the 1918 flu appear?
options: At a navy yard in Boston.
At Camp Funston in Kansas, where a cook reported sick.
On a troop ship in mid-Atlantic.
In a Philadelphia hospital.
questions.explain: 第1句 “a cook at Camp Funston in Kansas reported to the infirmary with headache and fever”——最早有记录的美国病例出现在堪萨斯州的芬斯顿军营，患者是一名炊事员。

questions.q: Why was the pandemic misnamed the “Spanish flu”?
options: Because the virus first appeared in Madrid.
Because neutral Spain had no censors, and the king's illness made honest headlines.
Because Spanish doctors discovered the virus.
Because Spain suffered the highest death toll.
questions.explain: 第8句 “Neutral Spain had no censors, so when the young king Alfonso XIII fell seriously ill, his fever made honest headlines”——交战国都有战时审查，只有中立的西班牙能如实报道，于是疫情反而被冠上了西班牙的名字。

questions.q: What happened in Philadelphia within six weeks of the parade?
options: The war ended in Europe.
The city had dug about twelve thousand graves.
The parade organizers were arrested.
The epidemic quietly disappeared.
questions.explain: 第10句 “Within six weeks the city had dug about twelve thousand graves”——游行之后六周，费城挖出约一万两千座坟，医院的床单、棺材与掘墓人全部用尽。

questions.q: What can we infer about why two hundred thousand people marched in Philadelphia?
options: They knew the danger and accepted the risk.
The reassurances in the censored press had hidden how dangerous the disease really was.
They had all been vaccinated that spring.
The parade was ordered by the army to spread the virus.
questions.explain: 第7句 “the newspapers promised a mild three-day fever”——在审查之下，报纸把疫病说成轻症；结合第9句费城报纸“不断重复官方保证”，可推知民众正是被这种安抚性报道蒙蔽，才会在疫情中列队游行。

questions.q: In sentence 10, both “sympathy” and “apathy” contain the root “path”, which means feeling. What does the prefix “a-” in “apathy” do?
options: It strengthens the feeling.
It negates the feeling, so apathy means lack of feeling.
It turns the feeling into a disease.
It means body.
questions.explain: 第10句 “public sympathy, stretched past its limit, slowly hardened into the flat apathy”——path 意为“感受”，前缀 a- 表示“无、缺”，apathy 即“无动于衷、麻木”，与 sympathy（同感）相对。

title: 《流行病简史》· 现代：从SARS到新冠

sentences.en: In 2003, a strange pneumonia appeared in the markets of Guangdong province and then traveled by airplane and elevator to some thirty countries within a few weeks, taking the hospitals of Hong Kong, Toronto, and Singapore completely by surprise before the world had even agreed on its name.
sentences.zh: 2003年，一种奇怪的肺炎出现在广东的市场里，随后乘着飞机与电梯，几周之内便扩散到约三十个国家，令香港、多伦多和新加坡的医院猝不及防——那时全世界甚至还没就它的名字达成一致。

sentences.en: The SARS epidemic was strangled in about eight months, with fewer than eight thousand cases and around eight hundred deaths, a victory that the World Health Organization and its corps of epidemiologists won through old-fashioned isolation and patient contact tracing without any vaccine at all.
sentences.zh: SARS这场流行病在约八个月内被扼杀，病例不足八千，死亡约八百；世界卫生组织与其流行病学队伍靠老式的隔离和耐心的密接追踪赢得这场胜利，压根没用上任何疫苗。

sentences.en: SARS was slow in one useful way: patients became infectious only after the fever and the cough announced them, so thermal cameras at the airport doors caught them one by one, and for once quarantine could actually outrun the virus instead of chasing it.
sentences.zh: SARS在一个关键处慢：病人要等发烧和咳嗽先“自我宣告”之后才有传染性，于是机场门口的热成像摄像机一个个把他们筛了出来；难得有一回，隔离跑在了病毒前面，而不是在后面追赶。

sentences.en: Seventeen years later, at the closing of 2019, another coronavirus slipped quietly out of the winter markets of a crowded city in southern China; this one spread from person to person before any symptom appeared, and the old playbook of fever screens lost its first page overnight.
sentences.zh: 十七年后，2019年将尽之时，另一种冠状病毒悄悄溜出中国南方一座拥挤城市的冬季市场；这一次，它在任何症状出现之前就人传人，旧剧本里“测体温筛查”的第一页一夜之间失灵了。

sentences.en: Yet science itself had accelerated almost beyond recognition: in January 2020, a pathology laboratory in Shanghai published the complete genome of the new pathogen online free for anyone to read, and within days laboratories on every continent were building tests from the same string of genetic letters.
sentences.zh: 但科学本身已快得几乎认不出来：2020年1月，上海一家病理学实验室把新病原体的完整基因组公布上网，供任何人免费阅读；不出几天，各大洲的实验室都在用同一串基因字母制造检测试剂。

sentences.en: For comparison, the pathogen behind AIDS, first noticed in 1981, took researchers roughly two years to isolate, and the virus was not clearly photographed until years after that; the difference of speed between the two epidemics measures how much the world's laboratories have changed in a single generation.
sentences.zh: 对比之下，1981年首次引起注意的艾滋病病原体，研究者花了约两年才分离出来，而清晰拍下病毒还要再等好几年；两场流行病之间的速度差，恰好量出了一代人的时间里世界实验室的变化。

sentences.en: Test kits, vaccine platforms, and public dashboards incorporated that sequence almost immediately; pharmaceutical corporations, with governments paying the bill and the risk, compressed a process that normally takes a decade into a single year, and the first vaccine doses followed before the following winter was over.
sentences.zh: 试剂盒、疫苗平台与公开数据看板几乎立刻把这条序列纳入自身；制药公司在政府兜底买单并承担风险的情况下，把通常需要十年的流程压缩到一年之内，第一批疫苗在次年冬天结束前便已就位。

sentences.en: The demography of the disaster was urban: more than half of humanity now lives in cities, packed apartments share corridors, water taps, and elevators, and density has been the oldest friend of every epidemic since the refugees crowded behind the walls of Athens two and a half thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 这场灾难的人口学是城市的人口学：如今人类过半住在城市，挤塞的公寓共享走廊、水龙头和电梯；自两千五百年前难民们挤进雅典长墙之内起，“密集”就一直是每种流行病最老的朋友。

sentences.en: On 11 March 2020, the World Health Organization finally declared the outbreak a pandemic, a word it had delayed using for weeks, partly for fear of the political alarm the label would sound, and partly because no official ever wants to be the person who closes the world.
sentences.zh: 2020年3月11日，世界卫生组织终于宣布这次疫情为大流行，这个词它已迟迟数周不肯使用——一半是怕这个标签敲响的政治警报，一半是因为没有哪位官员愿意成为“关闭世界”的那个人。

sentences.en: The pandemic exposed every weakness within its reach: overflowing morgues and refrigerated trucks in the rich capitals, uncounted corpses in the care homes, health workers writing wills before their shifts, and official statistics that quarreled with each other from country to country throughout the first year.
sentences.zh: 大流行把它触得到的一切弱点都暴露出来：富国首都里溢出的停尸房与冷藏卡车、养老院里无人清点的尸体、上岗前先写好遗嘱的医护人员，还有第一年里各国官方统计数字之间没完没了的互相打架。

sentences.en: By 2022, the officially reported mortality had passed six million people, while excess-death estimates ran several times higher still; the demographic gap between nations that had vaccines early and nations that had none became one of the quiet scandals of the age, quietly recorded and rarely debated.
sentences.zh: 到2022年，官方报告的死亡人数已突破六百万，而超额死亡的估计还要高出数倍；早拿到疫苗的国家与一支疫苗都没有的国家之间的人口落差，成了这个时代静悄悄的丑闻之一——被默默记录，却很少被争论。

sentences.en: Vaccine corporations moved at record speed and with real courage, but the distribution of doses argued with geography and money from the first month to the last, and some nations were fully protected before others had received a single sealed vial through no fault of their own doctors.
sentences.zh: 疫苗公司以创纪录的速度行动，也拿出了真正的勇气；但剂量的分配从第一个月到最后一个月都在与地理和金钱争吵，一些国家已被完全保护之时，另一些国家连一支密封的疫苗瓶都还没收到——而这并非他们医生的过错。

sentences.en: As the emergency faded, public sympathy faded with it; a comfortable apathy returned to the rich world, preparedness budgets were quietly cut once again, and the memory of the millions of dead grew softer with each passing season of normal weather and reopened restaurants.
sentences.zh: 随着紧急状态退潮，公众的同情心也一并退去；一种舒适的冷漠重新回到富裕世界，备战预算再次被悄悄削减，而那数百万死者的记忆，随着一季又一季的正常天气和重新开张的餐馆，越变越淡。

sentences.en: The next pathogen will find the same dense cities, the same twenty-four-hour airports, the same short human memory, and much faster laboratories waiting for it; whether it also finds a ready world, with honest statistics and stocked supply rooms, is now a political choice rather than a scientific one.
sentences.zh: 下一种病原体将遇到同样密集的城市、同样全天候的机场、同样健忘的人类，以及比它快得多的实验室在等着它；至于它是否也能遇到一个备有诚实统计和充足库存的准备就绪的世界，如今是一个政治选择，而非科学问题。

questions.q: Why could SARS be contained within eight months, without any vaccine?
options: Because warm weather killed the virus.
Because patients became infectious only after symptoms, so thermal cameras and isolation could catch them.
Because everyone was vaccinated in secret.
Because the virus vanished on its own.
questions.explain: 第3句 “patients became infectious only after the fever and the cough announced them, so thermal cameras at the airport doors caught them one by one”——SARS病人症状出现后才有传染性，机场测温能筛出他们，隔离因此跑赢了病毒。

questions.q: What did a pathology laboratory in Shanghai do in January 2020?
options: It invented the first vaccine.
It published the new pathogen's complete genome online for anyone to read.
It hid the pathogen from other laboratories.
It isolated the AIDS pathogen after two years.
questions.explain: 第5句 “a pathology laboratory in Shanghai published the complete genome of the new pathogen online free for anyone to read”——2020年1月病原体全基因组被公布上网，数天内各大洲实验室据此造出检测试剂。

questions.q: What did the World Health Organization do on 11 March 2020?
options: It declared the end of the emergency.
It announced a global ceasefire.
It finally declared the outbreak a pandemic, a word it had delayed using.
It ordered every airport to close.
questions.explain: 第9句 “On 11 March 2020, the World Health Organization finally declared the outbreak a pandemic, a word it had delayed using”——世卫组织在拖延数周后，终于宣布疫情为大流行。

questions.q: Why does the author mention “the walls of Athens” when describing modern cities?
options: To suggest that modern cities should build walls like Athens.
To show that crowding has helped epidemics spread since ancient times, and modern cities repeat the pattern.
To prove that Athens was the largest city in history.
To argue that country life is dying out.
questions.explain: 第8句 “density has been the oldest friend of every epidemic since the refugees crowded behind the walls of Athens”——作者回扣第一章：从雅典长墙内挤塞的难民到今天共享电梯的公寓，密集始终是流行病最老的朋友，可推知现代城市正在重演古老的模式。

questions.q: In sentence 12, “corporations” comes from the Latin root “corp”. What does this root mean?
options: People.
Feeling.
Money.
Body.
questions.explain: 第12句 “Vaccine corporations moved at record speed”——corp 意为“身体”，corporation 字面即“结成一体的团体”；同根词还有 corpse（尸体）、corps（队伍）和 corpulent（肥硕的）。

title: 《光线讲义》· 影子与直线

sentences.en: A proper lecture on light should begin in the dark, because darkness was humanity's first laboratory; in a cave, with the last fire dying, our ancestors noticed that a hand placed before a flame threw a sharp-edged copy of itself upon the stone wall.
sentences.zh: 一份正经的光学讲义应当从黑暗开始，因为黑暗是人类的第一间实验室；在洞穴里，当最后一堆火渐渐熄灭时，我们的祖先注意到，一只手挡在火焰之前，会在石壁上投出一个边缘清晰的自身影像。

sentences.en: The earliest students of light noticed the simplest of facts: a shadow always has sharp edges, and sharp edges mean that light travels in straight lines, a truth so plain that children confirm it every afternoon with nothing but their own fingers and the sun.
sentences.zh: 光的最早研究者注意到一个最简单的事实：影子总有清晰的边缘，而清晰的边缘意味着光沿直线传播——这个道理如此浅白，孩子们每个下午都能用自己的手指和太阳加以验证。

sentences.en: Around 300 BC, the Greek geometers formalized this observation into exact theorems, giving the study of light the vocabulary of geometry; from that moment on, every question about rays could be answered with a ruler, a compass, and the patient rules of proportion.
sentences.zh: 公元前300年前后，希腊几何学家把这个观察整理成精确的定理，让光学从此继承了几何学的词汇；从那一刻起，关于光线的每个问题都能用一把直尺、一只圆规和耐心的比例法则来回答。

sentences.en: Euclid treated rays exactly like the lines of geometry, and optics was born as a daughter of mathematics; legend says he instructed a doubtful king with the famous words that there is no royal road to geometry, and the king, like every student after him, had to walk it.
sentences.zh: 欧几里得把光线当作几何里的直线来处理，光学于是作为数学的女儿诞生了；传说他曾用那句名言教导一位心存怀疑的国王——通往几何没有皇家大道——而这位国王，和他之后的所有学生一样，只能一步一步走下去。

sentences.en: When a wall obstructs the sun's rays, the region behind it receives none — no ray, however eager, is granted an exception — and a shadow is the visible record of that simple arithmetic; nothing mysterious hides in the darkness of a shadow, which is merely the place where the straight lines of light were not permitted to land.
sentences.zh: 当一堵墙挡住阳光，墙后的区域便什么都收不到——无论多么急切的光线都不曾获准例外——影子就是这份简单算术的可见记录；影子的黑暗里没有藏着任何神秘，它不过是那些不被允许落下的光线原本要占据的地方。

sentences.en: Straightness also explains why eclipses can be predicted, for they are shadows doing arithmetic on a cosmic scale; a Babylonian priest could warn his king, “The moon will be swallowed tomorrow at the third hour,” and the prediction always came true, because geometry never lies about where a thrown shadow will fall.
sentences.zh: 直线性还解释了日食为何可以推算，因为蚀影是影子在宇宙尺度上做的算术；一位巴比伦祭司可以警告他的国王：“明夜第三个时辰月亮将被吞掉”，而这预言总会应验，因为几何从不说谎，从不说错一道投下的影子会落在哪里。

sentences.en: The camera obscura, a dark room constructed with one small hole, showed that light keeps its geometry even through a narrow gap; a traveler in Cairo called the experience standing inside an eye, with the busy street painted upside down upon the wall.
sentences.zh: 暗箱——一间只开一个小孔的暗室——证明光穿过窄缝时仍保持它的几何；开罗的一位旅行者把这种体验称作“站进一只眼睛里”，喧闹的街道被倒着画在对面的墙上。

sentences.en: On the wall of such a room, an inverted image occupies exactly the space where light is permitted to land, and the structure of that image is so faithful that observers could count the buttons on a passerby's coat; the world had accidentally built a machine for copying reality.
sentences.zh: 在这样一间屋子的墙上，一幅倒立的影像恰好占据光被允许落下的那片地方，影像的结构忠实到观者能数清过路人外套上的纽扣；世界就这样无意间造出了一台复制现实的机器。

sentences.en: Artists later used the darkened room to trace scenes, accepting its upside-down world as the honest price of geometry; one Venetian painter reportedly told his apprentice, “Draw what the hole gives you, not what you remember,” and the apprentice learned that memory bends a line while the hole never does.
sentences.zh: 画家们后来利用暗房描摹实景，把这颠倒的世界接受为几何诚实的代价；据说一位威尼斯画家曾对徒弟说：“洞给你什么就画什么，别画你记得的”，徒弟由此懂得，记忆会弄弯一条线，而小孔永远不会。

sentences.en: Astronomers perceived a quieter lesson in all this: carefully done geometry could describe a sky nobody could touch, and an instrument as cheap as a stick and its shadow was enough to measure the height of a pyramid, the depth of a well, and eventually the distance to the moon.
sentences.zh: 天文学家从这一切中察觉到一个安静的启示：认真做的几何竟能描绘没人摸得着的天空；一根木棍加它的影子这样便宜的仪器，就足以丈量金字塔的高度、一口井的深度，乃至最终到月亮的距离。

sentences.en: Early opticians liked to say that no eye could deceive you about where an edge falls, if the line was drawn correctly; they trusted the shadow because a shadow is honest, and they trusted the straight line because its predictions survive every test without suffering destruction by any rival theory.
sentences.zh: 早期的光学研究者常说，只要线画得对，任何眼睛都无法欺骗你边缘落在哪里；他们信任影子，因为影子诚实；他们信任直线，因为它的预言经得起每一次检验，从未被任何对手理论毁掉。

sentences.en: Nor was light's gift only for the eyes, for every patch of sunlight carries thermal warmth that a bare cheek can feel; ancient builders understood this well enough to construct houses with windows facing the winter sun, letting straight rays warm a room in one afternoon.
sentences.zh: 光的馈赠也不只给眼睛，因为每一片阳光都携带着脸颊能感觉到的热；古代的建造者深谙此道，他们造房子时让窗户朝向冬天的太阳，让直进的射线用一个下午就暖起一间屋子。

sentences.en: From shadows, humanity received its first scientific instrument: the straight line, free to anyone with a wall and the morning sun; no laboratory was ever needed, no royal permission, no expensive glass — only the patience to watch where the light stopped and the honesty to write it down.
sentences.zh: 人类从影子那里收到了第一件科学仪器：直线——凡有一堵墙和一轮晨光的人都能免费使用；不需要实验室，不需要御准，不需要昂贵的玻璃，只需要耐心看光在哪里停下，并诚实地把它记下来。

sentences.en: Every later chapter of this lecture — reflection, bending, color, and finally the human eye — will lean on that first straight-line concept, because however far the argument climbs, it stands on the plain observation that a shadow's edge is sharp, and that sharpness is the signature of straightness.
sentences.zh: 本讲义后面的每一章——反射、弯折、颜色，直到人眼本身——都倚靠着这个最初的直线概念，因为无论论证攀得多高，它都立在那个朴素的观察之上：影子边缘锐利，而锐利正是直线的签名。

questions.q: What does the sharp edge of a shadow prove?
options: That light travels in straight lines.
That light can bend around corners.
That shadows are alive.
That the sun moves irregularly.
questions.explain: 第2句 “sharp edges mean that light travels in straight lines”，影子边缘锐利正是光沿直线传播的证据。

questions.q: What is a camera obscura, according to the chapter?
options: A polished metal mirror.
A sealed box for storing paintings.
A dark room constructed with one small hole.
A lens ground in northern Italy.
questions.explain: 第7句 “a dark room constructed with one small hole”，暗箱就是只开一个小孔的暗室，光穿过后在对面墙上投出倒立影像。

questions.q: What does the author call humanity's first scientific instrument?
options: The telescope.
The pocket mirror.
The camera obscura.
The straight line, free to anyone with a wall and the morning sun.
questions.explain: 第13句 “humanity received its first scientific instrument: the straight line”，直线是人人可免费取用的第一件科学仪器。

questions.q: Why did the Babylonian priest's eclipse predictions always come true?
options: Because the priests had secret telescopes.
Because geometry never lies about where a thrown shadow will fall.
Because the moon changes its path to match prophecy.
Because eclipses happen at random times.
questions.explain: 第6句 “because geometry never lies about where a thrown shadow will fall”，可推断蚀影遵循可推算的几何规律，所以预言必然应验。

questions.q: The word “geometry” contains the root geo. What does this root mean?
options: Light.
Earth — geometry began as the art of measuring land.
Shadow.
Glass.
questions.explain: 第4句 “Euclid treated rays exactly like the lines of geometry”，词根 geo 意为“大地”，几何学最初就是丈量土地的学问。

title: 《光线讲义》· 反射之镜

sentences.en: The oldest law in optics says that the angle at which light strikes a mirror equals the angle at which it leaves, a rule so exact that it has survived twenty centuries of testing; every mirror in the world obeys it, from a king's silvered glass to a puddle on the road.
sentences.zh: 光学里最古老的一条定律说：光射向镜子的角度，等于它离开的角度；这条规则精确到经得起二十个世纪的检验，世上每一面镜子都服从它，从国王的镀银玻璃到路面上的一个水洼。

sentences.en: Hero of Alexandria proved the law with plain geometry in the first century, and no experiment has broken it since; he instructed his students to test it themselves with any polished surface they liked, insisting that a truth this simple belonged to everyone, not only to philosophers with libraries.
sentences.zh: 公元一世纪，亚历山大里亚的希罗用朴素的几何证明了这条定律，此后没有任何实验推翻它；他要学生们用自己喜欢的任何抛光表面亲自检验，坚持说这样简单的真理属于所有人，而不仅仅属于坐拥藏书楼的哲人。

sentences.en: With a pin and a small plane mirror, a patient student can reconstruct Hero's proof on a kitchen table: mark where the pin's image appears to sit, swap the mirror's position, and geometry will quietly confirm that both angles agree to the width of a fingernail.
sentences.zh: 用一枚大头针和一小块平面镜，耐心的学生就能在厨房桌上重演希罗的证明：标出针像所在的位置，再挪动镜面，几何会悄悄向你证实，两个角度的吻合可以精确到一枚指甲的宽度。

sentences.en: Long before glass, craftsmen constructed mirrors from disks of polished bronze and copper, rubbing the metal for days until a face floated up out of the darkness; the Egyptians, the Romans, and the Chinese all left such mirrors in graves, as if a reflection were worth carrying into the next world.
sentences.zh: 在玻璃出现之前很久，工匠们就用抛光的青铜和铜盘来制作镜子，把金属连日打磨，直到一张脸从暗色里浮上来；埃及人、罗马人和中国人都曾把这样的镜子放进坟墓，仿佛一件映像值得带往来世。

sentences.en: The moon is the mirror we all share: it makes no light of its own, only returning what it receives, and on a clear night its borrowed brightness is enough to walk by, though it carries almost no thermal warmth, which is why moonlight feels beautiful but never warms a cold hand.
sentences.zh: 月亮是我们共享的那面镜子：它自己不发光，只是把收到的东西送回来；晴夜里它借来的光亮足以照人走路，却几乎不带一丝热，所以月光显得很美，却永远暖不热一只寒冷的手。

sentences.en: The lunar surface reflects only about twelve percent of arriving sunlight, yet that little is enough to read by; an astronaut standing on the moon would notice that the ground beneath his boots behaved like pale dust rather than glass, and the numbers confirmed what any shepherd already knew from the gentle light.
sentences.zh: 月球表面只反射约百分之十二的到达阳光，但那一点点已足够供人读书；站在月球上的宇航员会发现脚下的地面更像浅色的尘土而非玻璃，而这些数字也证实了任何牧羊人从那温柔光亮里早已知道的事。

sentences.en: Calm water does the same work for free, laying a second, trembling sky beneath the trees; fishermen have watched herons mistake a reflected fish for a real one, and each confusion is proof that the law of reflection is obeyed as faithfully by a lake as by the costliest laboratory instrument.
sentences.zh: 平静的水面免费做着同样的工作，在树影之下铺开第二片微微颤抖的天空；渔夫见过鹭鸟把水里的倒影错当真鱼，每一次这样的小误会都证明，一面湖对反射定律的服从，不亚于实验室里最昂贵的仪器。

sentences.en: A smooth surface gives a clear image because every ray obeys the same rule, while a rough wall scatters light into fog; in microscopic structure every bump obstructs some rays and throws them in new directions, so polished metal shows a face but concrete shows only a pale glow.
sentences.zh: 光滑的表面能给出清晰的像，因为每条光线遵守同一条规则；而粗糙的墙会把光散成一片雾——在微观结构里，每一个凸起都会挡住一部分光线并抛向新的方向，所以抛光金属照得出脸，混凝土只照出一片灰白微光。

sentences.en: Reflection also turned inward on language: we say a thoughtful person reflects, turning ideas over as a mirror turns light, and in that borrowed word lies a whole philosophy, for to think well is to send a question out into the dark and wait patiently for what comes back changed.
sentences.zh: “反射”这个词也向语言内部转折：我们说深思的人在 reflect，像镜子翻转光那样翻转想法；这个借来的词里藏着一整套哲学，因为好好思考，就是把一个问题送进黑暗，再耐心等待它带着改变归来。

sentences.en: The reflex is the body's own reflecting mirror, an answer wired in before thought can participate; a hand pulls away from a hot stove long before the brain could reconstruct a sentence about danger, because in an emergency the body cannot afford the slow luxury of thinking.
sentences.zh: 本能反射是身体自带的镜子，一个在思考来得及参与之前就接好的答案；手从滚烫的炉边缩回，远早于大脑能重构出一句关于危险的话，因为在紧急关头，身体负担不起思考这种缓慢的奢侈。

sentences.en: Not every shiny surface is honest, for a bent or deceptive curve can stretch your face into a stranger; a scratch across the glass causes a local destruction of the image, and the famous mirrors of amusement halls prove that a surface built to amuse can also be built to mislead.
sentences.zh: 并非每个发亮的表面都诚实，一条弯曲而具欺骗性的弧线能把你的脸拉成一个陌生人；玻璃上一道划痕会造成影像的局部毁坏，而游乐场里著名的哈哈镜证明，为逗乐而造的表面同样可以为误导而造。

sentences.en: Seeing yourself as others see you remains impossible; the mirror, our one exception, still reverses left and right, and when a barber once asked why his reflection parted its hair on the wrong side, an old customer laughed that the mirror is honest about direction but silent about identity.
sentences.zh: 像别人看你那样看自己，仍然不可能；镜子是唯一的例外，可它连左右都反了。一位理发师曾问，为什么镜子里的像把头发分到了错误的一边，一位老顾客笑着说：镜子对方向很诚实，对身份却保持沉默。

sentences.en: Keep a pocket mirror handy, for this chapter asks you to verify every claim with your own eyes; a concept you have tested yourself is yours forever, and a mirror is the cheapest scientific instrument most people will ever own, and unlike a telescope or a microscope, it waits for you in every handbag, every bathroom, and every quiet puddle after rain.
sentences.zh: 请随身带一面小镜子，本章要求你用自己的眼睛验证每一个论断；自己亲手验证过的概念将永远属于你，而镜子是大多数人能拥有的最便宜的科学仪器，而且不像望远镜或显微镜，它在每个手袋、每间浴室、每场雨后的安静水洼里等你。

sentences.en: A reflection, finally, is light telling the truth about its own direction; the angle that comes in is the angle that goes out, and this stubborn fairness is the reason engineers trust mirrors inside telescopes, periscopes, and lighthouses, where a wrong angle would send ships onto the rocks.
sentences.zh: 说到底，倒影是光在陈述自己方向的真相：进来的角度就是出去的角度，这种固执的公正是工程师敢把镜子装进望远镜、潜望镜和灯塔的原因——在那里，一个错误的角度会把船送上礁石。

questions.q: What does the oldest law in optics say about a mirror?
options: The angle of arrival equals the angle of departure.
Light stops at the surface.
The angle doubles after reflection.
Every mirror reverses up and down.
questions.explain: 第1句 “the angle at which light strikes a mirror equals the angle at which it leaves”，入射角等于反射角。

questions.q: About how much arriving sunlight does the lunar surface reflect?
options: Nearly all of it.
About half.
About twelve percent.
Nothing at night.
questions.explain: 第6句 “The lunar surface reflects only about twelve percent of arriving sunlight”，月球表面只反射约百分之十二的阳光。

questions.q: Why does a smooth mirror give a clear image while a rough wall does not?
options: Because polished metal is darker in color.
Because mirrors are made of silver.
Because every ray obeys the same rule on a smooth surface, while every bump on a rough wall obstructs some rays and throws them in new directions.
Because rough walls absorb all colors.
questions.explain: 第8句 “every bump obstructs some rays and throws them in new directions”，光滑面上每条光线遵守同一规则，粗糙面的凸起则把光线散向四面八方。

questions.q: What does the burial of bronze mirrors in graves suggest about how ancient people viewed reflections?
options: That mirrors were worthless to them.
That a reflection was thought worth carrying into the next world.
That mirrors were used only by priests.
That bronze was cheaper than glass.
questions.explain: 第4句 “as if a reflection were worth carrying into the next world”，可推断古人珍视映像，视其为来世也需要的物件。

questions.q: In the word “destruction”, what does the root struct mean?
options: To shine.
Heat.
To build — destruction is the un-building of something.
An image.
questions.explain: 第11句 “a scratch across the glass causes a local destruction of the image”，词根 struct 意为“建造”，destruction 即“毁掉已建造之物”。

title: 《光线讲义》· 弯折的玻璃

sentences.en: Light does not always travel straight; when it crosses from air into water, it bends at the boundary, and the bend is so obedient to law that a fisherman who aims his spear at a visible trout will always strike too low, because the eye reports the fish where it is not.
sentences.zh: 光并非永远走直线：当它从空气进入水中，会在边界处弯折；这种弯折对定律服从到如此地步，以至于渔夫把鱼叉对准看到的鳟鱼时，总会扎得太低，因为眼睛报告的鱼的位置，并不是它真正的位置。

sentences.en: The bending is called refraction, and a spoon in a glass of water displays it at every breakfast table; the handle appears broken at the surface, yet nothing is broken at all, and the apparent destruction of the spoon is only an honest report of bent light arriving in the eye.
sentences.zh: 这种弯折叫折射，一杯水里的一把勺子在每张早餐桌上都演示着它；勺柄在水面处像是断了，其实什么也没断，勺子表面上的“毁坏”不过是折弯的光进入眼睛后的一份诚实报告。

sentences.en: The beam deflects toward the slow side, much as a marching band turns when one flank hits a muddy field; the analogy delighted the scientists who first taught it, and it still instructs beginners today, because the mind perceives the whole rule at once in the turning band, and feels a truth that the eye can only watch.
sentences.zh: 光束向较慢的一侧偏转，很像行进中的乐队有一翼踩进泥地时的转弯；这个类比让最早讲它的科学家们大为欣喜，它至今仍在给初学者上课，因为头脑能从转弯的队列里一眼察觉整条规则，摸到一条眼睛只能旁观的原则。

sentences.en: Grind glass into the right curve and the deflection can be aimed: parallel rays are focused to a single point, and the geometry of that curve can be calculated as exactly as the orbit of a planet, which is why lens-making became half craft and half mathematics.
sentences.zh: 把玻璃磨出合适的曲面，偏转就可以被瞄准：平行光线被汇聚到一点，而这条曲面的几何可以像行星轨道一样被精确计算，这就是磨镜术之所以一半是手艺、一半是数学的原因。

sentences.en: A strong lens can also focus the sun into a spot of thermal heat fierce enough to light a fire, a trick known to the ancients; the light is unchanged in nature, merely gathered, yet concentrated it can light a fire or, in old stories, burn the sails of a fleet.
sentences.zh: 一块够强的透镜还能把太阳聚成一个灼热的光斑，烈得足以生火，这个把戏古人早就会；光的本性没有改变，只是被聚集起来，却就能点燃火绒，或者在老故事里烧掉一支舰队的帆。

sentences.en: That humble trick, performed by a shaped piece of glass, is the entire concept behind the lens, and every lens since — from reading glasses to camera phones — is a constructed descendant of that first curved surface, ground by patient hands long before machines existed to do the work.
sentences.zh: 这个不起眼的把戏——一块有形状的玻璃——就是透镜背后的全部概念；此后的每一枚透镜，从老花镜到手机摄像头，都是那第一块曲面的建造出来的后裔，由机器出现之前无数耐心的手磨出来。

sentences.en: Around 1290, craftsmen in northern Italy mounted such lenses in frames, and eyeglasses were born; a monk who had squinted at manuscripts for forty years could suddenly read again, and he wrote with astonishment that the little glass was worth more to him than a horse.
sentences.zh: 1290年前后，意大利北部的工匠把这样的透镜装进框里，眼镜诞生了；一位对着手稿眯眼四十年的修士忽然又能读书了，他带着惊奇写道，这枚小小的玻璃对他比一匹马还值钱。

sentences.en: For the first time, aging scholars did not have to accept failing sight as the end of their reading lives; a Venetian guild soon regulated the making of spectacles, and masters instructed their apprentices in secret methods of grinding, passing on instruction that a family guarded as jealously as gold.
sentences.zh: 年迈的学者第一次不必把衰退的视力接受为阅读生涯的终点；威尼斯的行会很快管起眼镜的制作，师傅们把研磨的秘法传授给徒弟，这种传授被各个家族像金子一样严密看守。

sentences.en: When printing arrived a century and a half later, a spectacle-wearing public was ready to receive it; the two inventions locked together like gears, for cheap books demanded reading eyes, and reading eyes demanded cheap lenses, and together they restructured the intellectual life of Europe.
sentences.zh: 一个半世纪后印刷术到来时，一个鼻梁上架着眼镜的公众已经准备好接收它；两项发明像齿轮一样咬合，因为便宜的书需要阅读的眼睛，阅读的眼睛需要便宜的镜片，二者一起重塑了欧洲的智识生活。

sentences.en: Some suspected the new lenses were deceptive instruments that distorted the world; preachers warned that seeing through glass was seeing through a lie, and one old senator reportedly asked whether a tool that changed his vision might also change his memory, his judgment, and his soul.
sentences.zh: 有人怀疑新透镜是歪曲世界的欺骗性工具；传道士警告说，隔着玻璃看就是隔着谎言看，据说一位老参议员问过，一件改变了他视力的工具，会不会也改变他的记忆、他的判断和他的灵魂。

sentences.en: Galileo later turned a better lens toward the sky, and the heavens were drawn into focus for the first time; with an instrument no longer than a child's arm, he saw the moons of Jupiter, and he understood at once that the old structure of the universe would have to be rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 伽利略后来把更好的透镜转向天空，天体第一次被拉进了焦点；用一件不比孩童手臂长的仪器，他看见了木星的卫星，并立刻明白宇宙的旧结构必须重建。

sentences.en: The eye itself, we came to understand, is a lens of flesh, flexible and self-adjusting, older than any glass; its internal structure adjusts its curve thousands of times a day without any conscious order, doing quietly and for free what the finest watchmaker's mechanism could never do at all.
sentences.zh: 我们后来明白，眼睛本身就是一枚肉做的透镜——柔韧、自动调焦，比任何玻璃都古老；它的内部结构每天上千次地调整曲率，不需要任何有意识的指令，就安静而免费地完成了最好的钟表匠的机械根本做不到的事。

sentences.en: A rainbow in a garden hose is the same law at play, each droplet bending sunlight by its own measure, so that an ordinary spray on an ordinary afternoon quietly reconstructs the full arc of colors; the garden becomes a laboratory, and the child holding the hose becomes a natural philosopher.
sentences.zh: 花园水管里的小彩虹是同一条定律在上演：每颗水滴按自己的分寸弯折阳光，于是一个普通的午后、一蓬普通的水雾，就悄悄重建出完整的彩色弧带；花园成了实验室，握着水管的孩子成了一位自然哲学家。

sentences.en: Refraction is thus light persuaded rather than light stopped, the flexible middle path between shadow and mirror; where a wall obstructs and a mirror commands, water and glass merely negotiate, bending each ray gently on its way and returning it to the world slightly changed.
sentences.zh: 折射因此是被说服的光，而非被挡住的光——影子与镜子之间那条柔韧的中间道路；墙负责阻拦，镜子负责发令，而水与玻璃只负责协商，把每条射线在途中轻轻弯折，再把稍加改变的它送回世界。

questions.q: Why does a fisherman aiming at a visible trout always strike too low?
options: Because the fish moves faster than the spear.
Because water pushes the spear upward.
Because the eye reports the fish where it is not.
Because trout are nearly transparent.
